name: Kimberly R. Kelly
text: This review is for a complete and utter flouting of COVID-19 restrictions and the unbelievable unprofessionalism of the host/owner. It's important to note that, as of this review date, Riverside County prohibits indoor dining and permits only outdoor dining. My partner and I attempted to go to Idyology for a drink and an appetizer on Saturday night. I called ahead to ask if there was outdoor dining available and whether I needed a reservation. The answer was "Yes, there is outdoor dining but it is wet and cold." (It had been snowing for the better part of the last 24 hours.) I asked if there were heaters and a covered patio, and the person on the phone assured me that there were heaters and umbrellas for the patio. I was satisfied with that answer, so my partner and I walked the 1/2 mile to the restaurant. When we arrived we were greeted by a hostess, who appears to be the owner/manager of Idyology as her picture is posted all over the restaurant's website, who was visibly intoxicated. We were unsettled to see that there were about 5 to 6 parties of 2-4 people each eating INSIDE the restaurant, despite Riverside County restrictions. We requested to be seated outside. Once outside we were seated at a wet table with minimal effort spared to dry it off. We were not offered a heat lamp and we were placed under an umbrella that was dripping cold water on us. The intoxicated woman asked why we wanted to sit outside (as if there is not a pandemic happening). Eventually a plate of bread and two waters were placed in front of us. After witnessing the intoxicated staff member take her mask off multiple times inside the restaurant, I peeked into the kitchen and saw the chef wearing his mask below his nose and one staff member in the kitchen without a mask at all. At this point, I felt that the restaurant was being very unsafe, so we politely left a tip for the really nice and hard-working busser (Chance) and got the heck out of there. This kind of behavior is unprofessional, unacceptable, and unsafe.

I had:
Pollo Asado
Carne Asada
(2) Al Pastor

Hubs had:
Pollo Asado
Carne Asada
Chorizo

We both agreed hands down Pollo Asado was the best. I found this shocking, I don't usually order chicken at taquerias because I try to choose something I wouldn't make at home (we make a lot of chicken at home). Normally, Al Pastor or Carnitas are my go to. I wouldn't order the Carne Asada, Chorizo or the Al Pastor again. But I would definitely get Pollo Asado and try some other choices.

Cantaloupe Aqua Fresca was amazing (we took 3 to go), Hibiscus Aqua Fresca was good but too sweet for me to order again.

It's a cute (not cozy) interior with lots of murals to look at. Lots of tiled tables with benches.

Next time, I'm getting corn with mayo and queso and a bunch of tacos. We'll be back.

The ceviche is served with tons of red onion, boiled yucca and yam, and corn. It's definitely very traditional and authentic Peruvian ceviche. Definitely one of the best I've ever had. The dish will run you about $15 though.

Their lomo saltado is, however, a little disappointing. The meat was a little dry and the dish was quite expensive for the portion. The flavor was okay but I wouldn't order it again.

The restaurant is usually pretty quiet. The service was good. They give you bread with butter and a very spicy dipping sauce with your meal. Be careful with putting too much of that sauce since it packs quite a punch.

name: Kevin Gaines
text:
First time visitor . . . certainly will be back.  Tired of taking Mom to P.F. Chang every time I visit L.A.  This joint is a short drive from her place.  Pretty simple; a limited menu, featuring various popular types of seafood, fried or grilled, with your choice of garlic butter sauce or cajun seasonings.  Add a choice of sides . . . brown or white rice, cole slaw, fries (sweet or regular potatoes).  I had the cajun salmon dinner, which featured 2 generous fillets.  Mom had the jumbo shrimp, with garlic butter sauce, which probably undid all the healthy choices she's made over the last couple months to drop almost 20 lbs.  Super delicious, though; both entrees.  If you'd rather go the baja route, a la Baja Fresh or Wahoo's, they do the fish taco/burrito thing too.  Their salsas taste really good

The atmosphere is big, casual and noisy . . . the restaurant interior kinda reminds one of a Chipotle store.  You order from the counter and have a seat.  You get your dish(es) very quickly after paying.  The best part of the experience, though?  $33 out the door, and that's only because Mom ordered the most expensive thing on the menu!

Good food, done fast, and pretty cheap.  Doesn't get much better.  Kudos, and see you again.

name: Jennifer Hunker
text:
WHAT IT IS
A FULL Italian deli. They stock BOARS HEAD MEATS (!!!), so there's a source of them in West Covina! Get the Everroast Chicken--your taste buds will love you. In addition to the meats, they have various salads and the ubiquitous Italian cookies.

They also have a restaurant section where they serve "Broasted" chicken, sandwiches, pizza, and soups. Please note--it's tucked away on Shopper's Lane, so it can be a little hard to find if you aren't used to the area.

WHAT YOU SHOULD ORDER
Sandwiches, deli meat

AMBIANCE
5 stars
I really like the look of this place. When you enter, you're standing in the deli portion of the store (which is partitioned from the dining room by a shelf). They have the full line of Boar's Head products including their flavored mayonnaise and mustard. The deli counter is to your right--the bar to order food is directly ahead. There's also a little dessert case right next to where you order your food to tempt you.

The dining room is nice and open and features a salad bar--a rarity in this day and age. This location is relatively new and it shows--everything is clean and lovely looking.

FOOD AND DRINKS
5 Stars
I am in love with their chicken salad sandwich. I've never had a chicken salad so good--I usually don't like chicken salad because I hate celery--but they ground everything up so finely that it comes out more like a delicious spread than a chunky salad. They serve that sandwich on a kaiser roll complete with poppy seeds, which just makes the east coaster in me super happy. I've never tried the chicken, but it smells quite good. I've also not tried the pizza.

NICE SURPRISES
Fruit tarts! One of my favorite little dainty desserts, and yet it's so hard to find outside of the Mexican super markets. And they're good, too!

OVERALL
A fantastic little deli for West Covina!

name: Jennifer Hunker
text:
WHAT IT IS
Sushi restaurant and bar. They also have your typical bento combinations and "kitchen" meals. A tip: Parking is behind the restaurant.

WHAT YOU SHOULD ORDER
Sushi!

AMBIANCE
4 stars
It's a fairly basic Japanese restaurant. When you enter from the street you, will be in a small foyer with tables all around you. To your right you will see the sushi bar. They have a few TVs on the walls as well. The music both times I've gone in is American, which is sort of unique for these sorts of places.

FOOD AND DRINKS
4 Stars
Both times I've been here I ordered the Nigiri plate which comes with a california roll and 8 pieces of assorted nigiri. The sushi here is fairly good. It's nothing that will blow you away, but it's fresh and doesn't commit any "cardinal sushi sins". I prefer a bit more vinegar in my rice.

The nigiri have a good fish to rice ratio. The fish cuts are thick, so you get a good amount of fish for your buck.The rice is sticky and holds up well. None of my nigiri fell apart upon being picked up. This is hugely important in a western sushi restaurant as I'm embarrassed to eat the nigiri properly (with my fingers) and opt to use the chopsticks instead. Nothing is worse than watching as the rice falls apart when you try to pick up your nigiri!

There was a good assortment of nigiri as well--8 different flavors! They were all delicious.

The California Roll was the lowpoint--the filling lacked flavor and there was a bit too much celery. It wasn't awful, but it was nothing to write home about.

The meal also comes with miso soup and a small salad. The salad is good. I don't know what's in their dressing, but I like it. Aside from that it's just your basic salad--iceburg lettuce and some red cabbage. The miso soup was another nice surprise--it was so flavorful! The tofu in it was wonderful too--soft and fresh. I've had SO many bad tofu cubes in miso soup over the years, so it's awesome to find a place that puts fresh tofu in their soup!

NICE SURPRISES
The assortment of Nigiri with the special is a nice touch, especially because many of the places around here limit you to 4 varieties of fish with these types of combos (opting to give you two of each instead). The miso soup was also a delight.

OVERALL
This is a great place for lunch. The service is quick--both lunches took me just under 40 minutes (and both times the restaurant was crowded.) You can call ahead and pick up your order too.

text:
I don’t often order an omelette. For me, that’s usually only the safe choice when I can’t find anything truly appealing. 99% of omelets are scrambled eggs with mediocre ingredients. But for some reason, I was intrigued by the offering at Petite Madeline.

First off, to set the stage, I was ravenous after just completing a long run. Sunday morning post-run breakfast for me is more like an attack by a wild animal than typical human dining. So apologies to the staff if I left a mess ;)

The omelette arrived and immediately it appeared different than what I’m used to. The egg was delicately folded - more like the dough of a croissant than the typical globular mess of most omelettes. There was a generous portion of the ingredients atop the whole thing and more within. The sausage was absolutely perfect. Full flavored and moist but not the typical acrid assault on the taste buds from cheap breakfast sausage. The goat cheese was perfectly tart and prolifically distributed. Add in spinach and onions, and this was one delightfully flavorful (and filling) meal.

The coffee was also excellent. My girlfriend had a delicious oatmeal bowl that I envied in silence.

Why 4 and not 5 stars? I reserve 5 stars for mind blowing experiences. This was very good and highly recommended. But it’s not in my top three favorite breakfast places, and I have to draw the line somewhere.

Jist is only for lunch and when I arrived on a Sunday about 40 minutes before closing time, the place was pretty empty. They have a few inside seating and a pretty big seating area outside. Their patio is dog friendly.

My friend and I ordered the Chashu Hash Skillet with rice and the French Toast to share. Both were excellent and reasonably priced for the portion. The food came out very quickly as there wasn't that many patrons in the restaurant.

I recommend getting the Chashu Hash with rice. The pork belly is heavenly and cooked perfectly. The flavor is great. The dish itself though is too sweet without having rice to offset it.

If you check in on Yelp, they give you a free cookie. I didn't quite care for the cookie since it's not soft-baked but free is free after all.

Parking can be hard to find. I was able to find free street parking several blocks down after circling a few times. There are a few paid lots in the area too if you don't want to look.

text:
Short version: it's good, it's expensive.  It might not be entirely fair to call it out as expensive, since what really made it more expensive than other similar places is that we got a lot more wine than we usually do.  But the restaurant is especially known for its wine, and they offer excellent pairings, so if you're not going to get the wine, why go?

Great food, great friendly, attentive, but unobtrusive service, nice semi-fancy, semi-rustic atmosphere.  And the wine was great.  It's always eye-opening for me to have wine well paired with food. I ordered a 2005 Rioja when we sat down, and we thought it was OK.  Later in the meal, the same wine came paired with my husband's entree (braised pork, polenta, maple-glazed delicata squash, orange-pecan gremolata) and it was 10 times better.  And with dessert we had a 2011 Jurançon Uroulat that was fantastic.

If we were in the mood to have someone hand-hold us through some excellent wines that can't be easily had other places.  But otherwise, for the money, we'd go to Blue Plate or Serpentine.

text:
First visit impressions. Not a large restaurant and that's positive. Nicely decorated. The staff are all very friendly, in fact I was pleasantly pleased that the number of wait staff servicing at the 6pm hour was 5 or so and the overall service was prompt.

The portion size of the edamame appetizer was huge, the soybean pods were fresh, a tad bit over salted, perhaps a fluke, delicious nonetheless. The salmon skin hand roll had a decent amount of crispy skin, and overall much more satisfying than what other local sushi restaurants serve. Ordered the Chirashi entree, all the sashimi were fresh, none were sinewy, the rice was served in a large tea leaf roll which was unique to say the least.

I'll definitely return to check out other dishes.

name: Nalani Ngoon Warde
text:
Once upon a time this restaurant was Liberty Cafe, then it was a not so good version of Liberty Cafe. Now, it's Bernal Star. It is reminiscent of Liberty when it was good, but it is new, and it is it's own little restaurant.

We've been for brunch, and I've been for dinner with friends.

Brunch was ok. Pleasant patio, lackadaisical service, average food. Brunch is tricky for restaurants, everyone in the world wants to eat at the same time, and there are only so many cooks. Even when this restaurant was Liberty brunch service was not the greatest, partially I think that the restaurant's unique layout has something to do with it (front, patio, back). The crispy chicken sammie started off great, but the sour slaw was just too much by the end, and I love slaw. The enchiladas were gorgeous, but they were only ok.

Dinner... was great! A party of six of us were wandering down Cortland, looking for somewhere to eat without a reservation on a Saturday night. I was a little hesitant a first, I wanted our out of town guests to have a special dining experience in our neighborhood... and based on brunch, I thought it might be hit or miss. It turned out wonderful. The front of the resto was packed with families (no thanks- we were a heard of moms having a night out on the town sans hubbies and kiddos), it was a little too chilly the patio, but the back was fairly empty. The burger was one of the better burgers I have had (so surprised, you never know when you're going to meet a great burger), mushroom pizza was good, corn side was delicious, veggie burgers were good, fish tacos were fresh and tasty, and the arugula salad was a fresh. The banana cream pie was AMAZEBALLS.

Bernal Star is fairly new, they're working out the kinks. They're off to a good start. They fill a need in Bernal for an 'affordable' (by San Francisco standards) cozy neighborhood spot for dinner. Even though we didn't want to be sitting with all the families that one particular night, I was really happy to see the restaurant filled with families. We'll be back especially for that burger!

text:
I'm pretty sure our waiter's crazy Italian accent was fake but I put up with it and still enjoyed my meal at Maccheroni Republic. We were seated outside surrounded by heat lamps. The patio is beautiful and I really liked the ambiance.

The great thing about this place is you can BYOB. They also don't charge a corkage fee so we were able to enjoy the Chianti my friend brought at no extra charge.

We ordered the carpaccio, which I somewhat enjoyed. It was a nice and light dish so it worked well as a starter, considering we both ordered pasta for our entrees. I would probably not order it again though when I go back. The flavor was too light and the dish could have used a little bit of salt.

My friend had one of the rigatoni dishes and didn't like it. To me, the tomato sauce that comes with the rigatoni has some sort of weird burnt taste and smell to it. I ordered the squid ink pasta with fish ragu and fell in love with my dish. The pasta is cooked perfectly, the nuggets of fish really compliments the dish, and the cream sauce is simply delicious. I could have eaten that sauce with a spoon.

The portions for pasta is pretty generous here. We shared the 2 dishes and didn't finish. I was stuffed by the time I left. Everything is reasonably priced. My squid ink pasta was on the expensive side of the menu and even that was only $13.95.

I found parking on the street, which is free after 8pm otherwise there is a 2 hour meter. The area is not the best so be careful walking over to the restaurant.

name: ben der
text:
WHAT DID I GET:  The Bold Ramen and the Wagyu Ramen Burger.

HOW WAS IT:  The Bold Ramen was...adequate.  It wasn't terrible but it wasn't great, and to be honest, I have no idea what everyone's talking about when they say this place is 'one of the best ramen places in LA.'  It's okay, but it's far from being 'the best.'  Truthfully, I've had packaged ramen with more flavorful broth and noodles.

The Wagyu Ramen Burger was just terrible.  Bad, bad, bad.  First of all, it doesn't look anything like the picture on the menu; the ramen noodle patties are super thin, and the burger is drenched in this kind of weird overly-powerful BBQ sauce.  As for the taste, it was so unbelievably salty, I had to send this thing back.  It was seriously like biting into a big pile of salt; after one bite, I had to down two whole glasses of water.

HOW MUCH DID IT COST:  Including tip, it was $16.15.  They took off the price of the burger, because I sent it back.  But still, $12 for a medium-sized bowl of mediocre ramen is just way too overpriced.

WOULD I COME BACK/RECOMMEND THIS PLACE:  No and no.  The food was mediocre to terrible, and the service wasn't too great either.  The guy who 'helped' me with the refund had no idea what he was talking about and he made the whole refund process ridiculously complicated.

If they had any integrity at all, they would've comp'ed the whole thing to make up for my terrible experience with their food and service.  SMH.

If you're craving ramen in LA, you're seriously better off making your own at home rather than coming to this place.  I really don't understand how this place has gotten so many positive reviews; my only guess is that the people who raved about this place were so drunk and hungry at the time, anything would've tasted amazing to them.  But if you're NOT drunk or starving, you're probably not going to have a great time here.

text:
My favorite Burmese restaurant in the city: the waits are not as crazy as the other places and the food has always been deliciously dependable.

My favorite (and therefore always ordered) items:
1.  Rainbow Salad: there are twenty ingredients in this thing, and together they make a divine dish.  I could eat this for a meal alone if it were just me.
2.  Mandalay Special Noodle:  normally I'm not a huge coconut fan, but it works in this dish.  The cooked noodles and the crunchy noodles complement each other in texture, and the chicken is always tender and nicely flavored.
3.  Mango chicken:  the sauce on the chicken is so delicious.  The mango chunks aren't always the sweetest, but that's not always a bad thing given it's a savory dish.
4.  Dry pan-fried string beans with tofu: just get them.  Seriously.
5.  Also have tried the tea leaf salad, which is also good, but I still prefer the rainbow salad.  Will order if I want to change it up.

True, the portions do leave something to be desired, but I suppose it prevents me from eating too much to the point of bursting.

Feels like walking into a tropical forest. Everything is lush, green and growing.  I love the plants everywhere. There are communal tables as well as small intimate tables. They use an eclectic mix of mismatched flatware and plates to give it a hipster vibe.
The food is so-so... Nothing is a standout, but the ambiance is fantastic. I love dining with friends and just taking in the atmosphere... Maybe it's all the plants, maybe it's just psychological... But the air seems better in there.

name: Natalie K
text:
The new Roy Choy restaurant has quite a different concept than his others. The focus on seasonal ingredients is really done quite well here. Because of this, their menu changes often. We were looking forward to trying their famous grilled corn but since it's not in season, it was off the menu.

The menu is quite...interesting? Each menu item is described by just one main ingredient. Our waiter explained that it is that way so that we have to ask the waiter and they will go over it with us. We ended up asking about a lot of the dishes so the ordering process was quite time consuming.

Most of the dishes though were quite good. We tried the bok choy, clams, burger, cauliflower, brussels sprouts, and the fish. My favorite dishes were the clams, bok choy, and cauliflowers. The fish and the burger was just alright and the brussels sprouts were my least favorite out of everything.

We heard that their cocktails were good and tried a few of their cocktails. All of them were quite delicious but a bit pricey for the size.

The restaurant itself is on the 2nd floor of the LIINE hotel in ktown. They have valet parking but we were able to easily find street parking that's not too far away. POT is on the first floor.

I loved the ambiance. The restaurant itself is inside a green house style structure on the 2nd floor patio. It is quite beautiful. I would definitely recommend this place for a date.

name: Mandy Irvine
text:
It's no wonder South is on the tips of everyone's tongues here in Sacramento. Food is flavorful, delicious and an update on what you may think of as southern cuisine. We had the fried chicken, salmon sandwich, mac and cheese, and cornbread. I can't wait to go back over and over again so I can try everything in their menu. (Especially those delicious dessert items!)

We enjoyed our dining experience on the patio and found the staff friendly, attentive and polite. The cornbread and biscuits were 100%. Throw in that honey butter and you've gone straight to heaven! In addition, the Kale doesn't look like anything special, but they have somehow how made it packed with flavor without making it greasy, overcooked or soggy. We both raved for the rest of the day about the juicy fried chicken and the spice mixture on the salmon sandwich- so we definitely left full and happy.

Disappointing, especially given some of the good reviews here.

Ordered the chicken taco salad with sour cream and guac. While waiting, salsa and chips came. Salsa was dreadful, and most of it seemed from a can; with only bits and chards of fresh tomato or onion, spiced with dry ingredients instead of fresh peppers, and not a hint of cilantro.

Salad arrived sans sour cream and guac. I reminded the server, and she then brought a small side bowl that contained both. The guacamole tasted mostly of lime juice. The salad itself was mostly flavorless, with dry, under seasoned chicken, beans, and rice. The lettuce was mostly dark, limp green leaf; not the cool, crisp, shredded iceberg I have come to associate with Mexican food.

The grated cheese seemed of the packaged type, with an all too consistent look, perfectly round, shiny and smooth, and it was cheddar instead a a mild Mexican queso. In fact, the whole salad was so tasteless, it was overpowered by the small amount of cheddar that was there. I am not used to describing a taco salad as dry and tasteless, but this one was.

The presentation and service were good, but not having the 'basics' even close to right gives me no reason to return. Mexican food is all about the basics, exploding with flavor. None of that here.

name: myna nacare
text:
Great local place to eat for a treat!

Popular so make a reservation or prepare to either eat outside or wait. For the same reason be patient when parking. There are many tasty selections and specials, live music, and newcomer discounts (hint: email list) so it's a low-risk venture to try.

The Friday night we dined we were spared a 20 minute wait and seated immediately outside since we had no reservations, passing by fresh food preparation on the way. Staff was friendly, attentive without being overbearing, and quite accommodating. Lots of good teamwork noted with service.

The atmosphere is fresh and light despite activity, unpretentious but stylish, and in true California mode is appropriate for the casual dresser to the gussied up romantic date. Not really a kid place, unless you're with a big party but they also do banquets.

The manager let us know there are 22 different kinds of (mostly non-vocalist) musical groups there on Friday and Saturdays. The volume was just right as backdrop music. On Wednesdays they have a myriad of specials and shenanigans offered.

Our dishes were superbly done, with clear but subtle flavors and gently sauced. They make nearly everything from scratch and are more than happy to customize your meal. I had Salmon with Polenta cake and mixed squash. It was delicious! (And I don't usually like squash) My friend had beautifully done Pork Chops served with a creamy butternut squash. Kinda made me wish we could trade. Or eat both :] Plus they made me a killer Old Fashioned with my favorite Woodford Bourbon, thanks to our fabulous server, Amy!!

If the prices were a little lower here it'd become dangerous for me! LOL
Even after just one visit, I declare this one a total win!

text:
Delicious tacos. Not street tacos. They're closer to gourmet. The pork taco ($3) was my favorite, with a tie for second for the "Media Luna" shrimp and scallops taco ($6) and the beef skirt steak taco ($4). You may be surprised by the price to size ratio, but taste them and them make your judgement. I'm sure you'll agree that they are tasty.

They came with a small cup (about 2oz) of black beans, a small cup of soup (also, about 2oz) which was flavorful and had the right amount of spicy heat, and two lime wedges.

The pork and beef tacos came in thick blue corn tortillas which were delicious, and the meats had a generous amount of fatty juices (some people might think 'greasy', but it was a treat and I hope the restaurant doesn't change that!—lean this and lean that has no character!). The "Media Luna" had a spice cream sauce which packed a bit of a spicy punch without it being overwhelming. All of the tacos were tastefully topped with a micro-greens meddly.

I washed it down with two Topo Chico's mineral water ($3 each—which is pricy, but I'm willing to overlook because of the ambience and the good food).

Order at the window and pick it up, but the service was slow. I'll chalk it up to it being a new place and they're feeling their way, but hopefully this will improve.

I will be returning and will continue to return assuming the service improves over time. Again, I'm giving them the benefit of the doubt and I hope they read this!

Spicy city is located on the 2nd floor of the plaza with 99 ranch in San Gabriel. Parking is a nightmare on the weekend so we ended up having to park far away in the huge parking lot and walking.

We were seated right away but our server wasn't very nice or attentive. We ordered the cold dishes, which were okay but the bean thread noodle that this type of Chinese food is known for was quite good. After eating that first, I had high hopes for the rest of the the dishes we ordered but I was sorely disappointed.

We had the hot pot dish with meat and vegetables. The sad part is there was way too much potatoes and too little of everything else. The dish wasn't cheap so I felt a little jibbed. The worst dish was the Tasty Frog. It was huge and had tons of huge frog legs but the meat was overcook and tough. The sauce was also too oily and not tasty. I ended up not eating a whole lot of it.

Although the bean thread noodle is better than Chendu taste, their entrees didn't impress me. It's also a little too pricey so I probably won't be coming back any time soon.

Just opened mid July 2015! It is an acai bowl spot! One of the few in the area! They have a large selection of acai bowls, a selection of different smoothies, some panini sandwiches if you want something more filling, and even grilled cheese for the kids!

If youre going there for the acai bowls for breakfast, the 20 oz should be enough for a single person. If you want to share i would recommend going for the larger size.

You can add extras of any fruit for an additional cost or even replace any of the toppings with anything you want

We had vitality bowl and the power bowl (which has broccoli!) Both were very good! The acai bowls are served in metal bowls which is pretty neat and sustainable if you eat in. If you take it to go it will be served in a paper bowl.

They were a bit pricey I'll admit $9-$13 depending on size and choice,  but i guess it makes sense for Palo Alto where things are a bit pricey. You can definitely get a cheaper bowl at a place like Nekter where they charge about a couple dollars less.

Seating is a bit limited i think about 20 people can sit in the place, which makes sense because people are just in and out anyway. You may have to group tables for groups larger than 4

But overall i enjoyed the bowl and the spot is a decent place to catchup with a few friends!

I'd come back to the place if I'm in the area and craving an acai bowl!

text:
We took a party of 12 to dine-in for my sons 7th birthday today. We called in ahead of time (probably only about 15 min) to place our order for 4 large pizzas. as we walked in, they were just pulling them out of the oven, the timing really was perfect. We were able to sit at a large table in the middle of the restaurant to eat and overall had a really great time. The place was clean and even more importantly the staff was fantastic.
I didn't get an opportunity to get the blonde woman's name that was working the register today, but she was my favorite. Her customer service was quite possibly the best I have ever seen in my life. I also had a couple brief run-ins with the GM (who's name I also did not get) and he was fantastic as well. Its clear that he really cares about the place.
The Pizza, which is really what we went for was killer! the bread/cheese/sauce/topping ratio was perfect, and they all tasted great.
Lastly, they also had a small arcade in the back for the kids(and adults), and even though some of the games cost a dollar to play, everything was working and in good order.
All things considered, we will certainly be returning to Jerseys the next time we find ourselves in a pizza deficient state.
Thanks for a great experience guys!

We also got tacos de birria which came with three beef corn tacos. The meat was tender and juicy but lacked a bit of flavor that we needed to ask for hot sauce. They brought it out and it was super spicy!

Last we got pescado zarandeado which is grilled sea bass with masa dumplings and corn cake which looks like mash potatoes. After drinks some appetizers were in order, so we ordered the blue cheese chips and fried pickles. Both were excellent especially the fried pickles. I also ordered some more drinks. This time I ordered "Owl Night Long" which is gin, fresh kiwi, lemon, passion fruit, and a mist of absinthe. It was a good flavored drink but I thought there was too much foamed topping. After that drink, we decided to get a pizza specifically the "Gotta Have My Meat." It has pepperoni, fennel sausage, bacon, marinara, and fontina cheese. It was delicious and I would recommend it.

Finally, I decided to get a dessert drink and I noticed they had a drink called the "Hedwig." This drink had Screwball whiskey which is peanut butter flavored and I have wanted to try it since I heard of it. The drink was delicious and the peanut butter whiskey was not overpowering. It had a nice subtle flavor. I would get the drink again.

Overall, this place is a great place with a nice atmosphere and good staff. I would recommend this place to anybody looking for a good night out or even breakfast as they server breakfast all day.

text:
Small, minimalist Japanese "izakaya" in the Mission. I put the "izakaya" in quotes because it's nothing like a normal izakaya (no grungy, underground feel; no large menu of grilled meats; no fun environment where it's socially acceptable to do sake bombs). It's more like a toned-down, mature Japanese restaurant that serves a few izakaya-like items at quite-expensive price points.

But damn are those items delicious. The food is excellent here, no doubt -- the grilled squid, the uni-slathered yaki onigiri, the white shrimp tempura with matcha salt, the tender wagyu beef tataki, the uni steamed egg; everything was good.

I'm a bit mixed on Izakaya Yuzuki, because even though everything was delicious, it falls a bit short with its compact menu and high prices.

Wherever you get your LA pizza now, if it isn't Brooklynz, do yourself a favor and get yourself a fresh pie here. The crust has the right New York chew, with a thin "handle" and gentle crisp. The sauce is the right amount of salty and the cheese has that perfect tan. Toppings were on point. We split a pie, artichoke and Brooklyn. It's back to indoor dining, but decided to do lunch take out. The inside is very colorful with cute characters on the wall. They also sell hand crafted face masks and have a huge inventory of Lee Kum Kee soy sauce bottle for sale. This place is also owned by a Vietnamese family. (This is the third Japanese restaurant in Grantville that I've been to that's Vietnamese owned).

The on-line menu does not show lunch specials. When we arrived, I saw the banner and poster. Make sure you ask for lunch specials if ordering take out on the [phone. There's a $9.95 two item special and a $7.99 two hour special.

Baked cali roll (6pc) $5 - Baked rolls take about 20 minutes but since it was slow, it was ready when we got there in 15 minutes. Note that these are tiny pieces of 6.

Shrimp tempura roll $8.95 - This was nothing special. I was expecting crunchy roll and didn't specify so it's basically just coated panko.

Mixed tempura, 2 shrimp, veggie $6.95 - Can't go wrong with tempura but the breading seems a bit chewy like it was left out not freshly made.

Kawaii lunch special $9.95 - Came with 4 pieces of garlic chicken wings, one cup rice, salad, miso soup, and edamame. This is worth the money and the garlic chicken wings was very tasty.

Chicken Katsu curry rice $8.95 - Having more spice would make this better otherwise the flavors are mediocre.

Overall, the food here is neither great or bad. I would come back for the lunch specials only because it's a great price for all the sides.

The service was great. The staff were all SO friendly and were very helpful since it was our first time here. They even gave us a free cornbread loaf (possibly because the cornbread was taking a little long, but we didn't mind) and a free side of pickled onions and jalapeños.

Even without the free sides we received, $40 for two meats, two sides, and a cornbread loaf is a really good deal, and more than enough for two people.

My one wish is that they should offer Mac & Cheese as a side. It was a bit strange to see a barbecue restaurant not offer it. 😅

I would recommend making a reservation at 530PM, and grabbing a seat at the sushi bar and ordering their Chef's Omakase! You won't regret it. Sitting at the sushi bar when you do this is key in my opinion. You get the best and most attention when you do this. The tea may LOOK expensive, but it definitely is worth getting. Why you may ask? Because, they rotate and refill your cup everytime they notice your cup is low OR if it's been sitting too long and is no longer hot. That to me was totally worth it, I never had to ask :)

The chefs were entertaining and had a great time serving their wonderful creations to us.

They ship a good deal of their fish straight from Tsukiji Fish Market in Tokyo! And it's probably the best sushi I had in SF. I even enjoyed their Uni, and I don't even enjoy Uni!

I really had an amazing time, and the chef and the staff were awesome! This is seriously my new favorite spot in SF!

This is our go to poke place, and it's nice that it's closeish to home. The staff is nice, and the fish is usually pretty fresh. I also really appreciate the option of spicy tuna as the base protein, since most places only offer "crab", and I'm not a fan of that.

Ordering during covid is pretty similar to ordering before covid. You walk in and go through the different steps (base, proteins, sauces, toppings).

Getting there can be a little tricky if you don't know what you're looking for. I find that the most convenient way to get there from Winton is to turn right at the Chase (before the stop sign) and then turn left on the first parking area you can turn left at. I usually park in that area and then walk over, as there's very limited parking by the front unless you need handicap parking.

Definitely recommend for poke if you're looking for a poke fix! It's not the same as true Hawaiian poke, but nothing I've had in the bay area is.

text: While this opinion is not objective I can flatly state that this is the best Taco Bell in California. They have moved across the street to a stand-alone site a few years ago, but the same Taco Bell quality has been retained. While some people look down on Taco Bell as not real Mexican food, they are missing the point. If you need a quick bite and you are sick of hamburgers, then Taco Bell is the place to be. All the usual menu items are available and the employees here are super friendly and the whole establishment is spotless. The bottomless drink station is a plus too for those thirsty travelers. If you are venturing either north or south on Highway 101 in central California, be sure to stop and and give this fine restaurant a visit.

name: Benson Wong
text:
It was a busy Labor Day weekend when I walked in looking for a bite. The host informed me they were busy and that it might be a while before I can get seated at the bar. He suggested Milligan's as they had more bar seating. I moseyed across the street to Milligan's but returned to Cantinetta as I'm not a fan of English food. This was only several minutes later.

The host said I was in luck as someone just left. I sat down at the bar at 8:30 in the evening and ordered a Cappuccino as I was feeling tired and sleepy. I probably looked a little worse for the wear, having just gotten off the boat from whale watching and feeling seasick.

Moments later, the host asked if I would like to be seated at the other bar by the kitchen and the wood-burning stove to watch all the activity in the kitchen which was open. I accepted.

Expect the hostess was seating someone else at this point. Now I was in a conundrum. The seat I had just given up went to someone else.

The host apologized and said that it looked like someone else at the bar was leaving soon and asked if I would be ok with waiting.

He got me some sparkling water and a menu while I waited. During this time, my cappuccino showed up but I didn't have a free hand. So the lady said she would make me a new one once I got seated.

I waited some five minutes for the seat. The others patron left and I wondered if I should just sit down at the dirty bar. So I did just that. The host came back and shooed me away, saying they'll need to clean off the area first.

After several minutes, I sat down and my cappuccino came back, too. I watched the activity in the kitchen and the pizza chef make pizzas and how they used the wood burning oven to make meals. It was fascinating.

I was impressed by the overall level of service. I typically never tip 20% but did so this one time because Cantinetta more than earned it.

The food was also delicious. I had the steak in the cast iron pan. I have to say this is the second best steak I've ever had. The first would be Iron Chef Michael Symon's Roost in Detroit.

I went back in November, this time at 5:30 pm on a Sunday. Though the place was not at all busy when I arrived and I was seated before this couple, the hostess forgot to give me a menu. When the waiter finally arrived to take my order some ten minutes after I was seated, I mentioned that before I do a menu would be nice.

It's times like these that are telling of a restaurant's full capability. The inability to maintain consistent service, this at a time when the restaurant was not at all busy, was disappointing to me. For this, I removed a star.

I still recommend this place but buyer beware.

Second, they have two locations so make sure you’re ordering from the Westminster location on Bolsa and Buschard.

No dine in so we did take out. It came in a brown paper bag with chop sticks, soy sauce, wasabi and ginger packets. The wasabi paste is product of Japan, I didn’t like the ginger, it was wet, thin, and mushy.

I got two rolls: The Crunchy Cali and Yoga Fire. Both had shrimp, avocado, cucumber but with different texture, sauce and toppings.

Crunchy Cali roll was extra crispy with the panko. The end pieces were the best! The sauce made it sweet and the whole piece was like creamy Mayo.

Yoga Fire had the AF sauce which was a spicy kick that made my lips tingle. Had the creaminess from the avocado. To resemble tuna on top, it was made with some type of soy like tofu.

The best way for me to describe the shrimp is that it taste like Loving Hut shrimp. If you’re vegan, you know what I’m talking about.

name: Uncle Buck
text:
Jerseys Pizza... Wow, what a place! This location has been a staple of the community for decades, offering what is arguably some of the best pizza period. Family owned and operated, Jerseys is a local favorite.

Located in the heart of downtown, Jerseys is conveniently placed right at the edge Orange St. and Redlands Blvd. Featuring an unbelievable collection of local memorabilia and paying tribute to hometown heroes, Jerseys has a full bar with many local brews being made right in the city and choice chilled wines. Seating is not as robust as many other locations offering similar foods, however locals know that it may be worth the wait to get a table if you are craving excellent pizza. This location can get really packed during dinner time, so plan accordingly.

With the taste of pizza being subjective to individual taste and preference, my family can honestly say that we have been enjoying Jerseys pizza for over 15 years. The crust is always perfectly soft yet flaky without being dry and brittle. Their sauce is on the sweeter side while being full flavored and not overbearing. Having over 30 toppings to choose from helps keep things interesting and offers a chance to try different combinations on return visits. Again, this is all subject to taste, but locals will tell you these are just some of the reasons they continue to come year after year.

If you happen to be in the area, or are just looking to venture out and try a new place, please stop by and give Jerseys a try, I'm sure that you stomach will thank you.

We ate and drank:
Weihenstephan: unfiltered hefe
Staropramen Dark: Crisp, light, rich beer
SMALL PLATE - GERMAN SPICY SAUSAGE: the sausage was so good, just the perfect amount of spicy
CHICKEN PAPRIKASH: sweet, savory, delicious
SZEGED GOULASH: my favorite, tangy, sour, rich, and awesome
HOMEMADE APPLE STRUDEL: The dessert was delicious, it did not need the chocolate and strawberry drizzle, and would have been perfect simply served with whipped cream

We'll definitely be back. The food was wonderful and a breath of fresh air on the SF restaurant scene. The prices were just right.

name: Roy Chi
text:
I love restaurants that do good for society. Problem is, on a completely objective level, these types of restaurants don't provide a great dining experience, so it feels more like donating to charity rather than having an enjoyable dinner.

Old Skool Cafe completely destroys this misconception. Had I not been told by our waiter that it was designed for at-risk youth to stay off the streets and learn valuable business skills, I would've thought that it was just a wonderful soul food restaurant with an incredible ambiance for a great night out. What they are doing is phenomenal for these kids, but even more, what they are doing is phenomenal for the dining public.

It's dark and intimate, with a incredible singer and pianist performing random (but great renditions) of popular pop songs. It really gives Old Skool its charm and made dinner that much more enjoyable. We even made a song request to the singer and although she didn't know all of the words, she performed something similar and gave us a warm shoutout.

-------------------------
FOOD: (Best to worst)

BBQ Ribs:
What amazing BBQ Ribs. They were tasty and fall-off-the-bone tender. Loved every bite of these.

Gumbo:
Delicious gumbo that went very well with the rice.

Sweet Potato Fries:
Addictive as hell. These sweet potato fries were sprinkled with some sugar and cinnamon, which gave it a nice salty and sweet taste explosion. Although a bit too sweet at times, most of the ones I had were awesome.

Peanut Butter Stew:
A bit like Thai masamun curry, the peanut flavor was definitely the star of the show. It was good, but was missing some more kick.

Shrimp and Grits:
The shrimp was nice and tender, but grits were missing some more cheesy or buttery flavor. The grits were cooked well, just wasn't really that tasty.

Fried Chicken:
The fried chicken here included a few small drumsticks, each were nice and moist in the inside, but a bit over-fried on the outside. There was also a bit too much rubbed on, so the exterior taste was a bit too overpowering. The gravy could've also used some more saltiness.

Blackened Catfish:
The one truly disappointing dish of the night. The catfish was too rubbery and the spices didn't kick at all.

-------------------------

The very few food disappointments aside, Old Skool Cafe is undoubtedly an amazing establishment. Even if it wasn't for an incredible cause, it would still be a great joint for tasty, homestyle soul food. I'm definitely coming back.

In this modern world, we often forget to take a breath of fresh air and we forget to step outside. Maria’s provides that. Although know for their tacos, the burritos are handcrafted with ingredients you can choose. They even take the next step in excellent burrito crafting by toasting the burrito over a buttered grill. It doesn’t just stop at authentic Mexican food. Maria’s also offers hot dogs wrapped in crispy well cooked bacon. My go to for Maria’s is a bacon wrapped hotdog with grilled onions with two “Asada Tacos”. The only thing preventing me from leaving a perfect review is that the condiments and extras are left outside and that ultimately attracts flys and what not. This is also a plus because you get to choose what you want to put on your tacos and other foods.

text:
WHAT DID I GET:  I got a custom three-scoop bowl with avocado and a bottled water.  For my bowl, I got salmon, tuna and albacore.

HOW WAS IT:  It tasted very fresh and vibrant, and I could taste all the different ingredients and toppings and sauces that went into it.  But after I was finished, I was still so damn hungry.  Though the poke bowl was delicious, it wasn't very filling or feel substantial.  I ended up having to go get a sandwich from next door.

HOW MUCH DID IT COST:  With tip, it cost a little under $19.

WOULD I COME BACK/RECOMMEND THIS PLACE:  I want to say yes, but I have to say no, I won't be coming back or recommending this place to others, simply for the fact that I was still so damn hungry after I left this place.  And having to pay almost twenty bucks to still be hungry just seems like an absolute waste to me (delicious as it was).  I guess eating here makes sense if you're trying to be more healthy or if you're on a diet, but I just wish they found a way to make these things more filling.

Also, a note of constructive criticism, I wish they would use larger bowls.  The bowls are so small and filled to the brim that it's hard to kinda dig through the ingredients, and get a little bit of everything in one bite.

The staff was very friendly and helpful, though.

PS, The bathroom door lock was kind of weird and confusing, and it was hard to be sure if I had really locked the door or not.  <--Second note of constructive criticism about the location.

The Protein Roll was a bit of a mixed bag for me, as it tasted fine, but it had the consistency of chewing on uncooked ground beef.  Visually, the rolls were somewhat colorless and bland, especially the Protein Roll.

HOW MUCH WAS IT:  Including tip, it cost a little over $52.

WOULD I GO BACK/RECOMMEND THIS PLACE:  No, I think there are better sushi places out there for the same price.  That's not to say that this place is bad (it's not), but it's just....an okay place.  Service was pretty friendly.

text:
This is a rare find and gem in South El Monte! If you're looking for vegetarian/vegan Vietnamese food, this is the place for you. Super affordable, fresh quality, and delicious.

I ordered the popular dish Bun Bo Hue, Shredded Pork Spring Rolls, and a sugarcane drink. Total was $21.30. My thoughts:

Bun Bo Hue ($7): yum! I'm not an expert on this dish but the broth was yummy, great seasoning, enough spices (not too spicy), and big portion. Great amount of veggie meats, bean curd, mushrooms, and comes with a separate bag of shredded cabbage, bean sprouts, lemon, and basil. Amazing quality and value

Shredded Pork Spring Rolls ($7 / 4x): really yummy and comes with what seems to be a vegan fish sauce along with pickled carrots and radish as a side. Very fresh and filling

Sugarcane drink: I was most excited for this because it has been a long time since I've had sugarcane juice. It was very light, refreshing, not sweet at all and was infused with kumquat! My first time having it like this and was a good mix! When I first saw the portion, thought "wow. $5 for such a big cup!" Only to find out that they fill the cup with ice MORE THAN halfway. Bummer but still delicious.

Overall, YES PLEASE ORDER FROM VEGGIE LIFE. Very yummy. Please note: they speak limited English so cannot be too detailed or ask too many questions over the phone with them.

name: My Le
text:
My parents generation was Phuong Trang which still exist until this day. While PT Eatery is my generation that’s like the quick modern simplified version of Phuong Trang while keeping all the quality of foods the same.

The menu is all in English with no Vietnamese translation. Traditional seven course beef is not offered at this eatery and neither were the fried fish or exotic dishes that you’re used to at the original Phuong Trang. What to expect at PT Eatery are the basic categories like rice, vermicelli noodles, pho, vegetarian, meat, sandwiches, and appetizers.

We got pho, vermicelli grilled pork with egg rolls, garlic butter ribs and garlic butter wings, wrapped grilled shrimp (banh hoi).

My favorite were the garlic butter ribs because they were deep fried and the batter was crunchy delicious. The wings were the same fried battered but the ribs were 10x better because it was different.

I normally get egg rolls as an appetizer but decided to get it with the vermicelli noodles along with char grilled pork. The pork was very tasty, it was thin flat rectangle shaped. The portion was huge and I only ate half.

The grilled shrimp wrapped in lettuce looks familiar because it’s the shrimp that you get at dim sum wrapped around a sugar cane. The banh hoi is like weaved vermicelli noodles.

All the staff wore masks. No dine in available but the interior is being remodeled with new hand painted murals based on real life photos from the owner’s visit to Vietnam.

text:
We've eaten both at the restaurant and had delivery.  We've always enjoyed the food. The food is like Indian food but not (I know, that was not a great description)... let's try: wonderful sauces full of flavor, but not as heavy, oily or creamy.

Tonight's meal was the best we've eaten from Little Nepal so far.  We always order the Lamb Chhoila (so, so, so good) and we try to order something we haven't yet had. The lamb Chhoila never disappoints, melt in your mouth, busting with flavor cubes of lamb (in the future, I plan to order 2 lamb Chhoilas and a veg curry combo, and that will be plenty with leftovers to spare). Kukhurako Pakuwa was awesome too, chicken in a tomato sauce full of spices.  We ordered the chicken as a combo, so it comes with naan, rice, potato, lentils and a spicy sauce situation. And last but not least, Saagko Tarkari.  We both looked at it and said 'looks meh,' but it was delicious, Indian greens meet Southern greens.

For two, the lamb Chholia, Kukhurako Pakuwa combo and the Saagko Tarkari  was more than enough.  We like leftovers.  I lied, I like the idea of leftovers and pretend to eat them, while my hubs actually eats the leftovers.

They quoted us 45 minutes for delivery, it was literally here in 15. AWESOME.  Thanks Little N!

name: Roy Chi
text:
Jasmine Garden is definitely one of the best Vietnamese restaurants in SF, just as long as you're NOT eating pho.

The Pho here has way too much cinnamon. It was like an apple cider broth. The beef slices were tough and the broth just isn't hot enough. Everything about this pho was lackluster and not even worth serving at what is otherwise an amazing Vietnamese restaurant.

-----------------------
FOOD:

Catfish Sweet & Sour Soup =
Incredible. A perfect blend of sweet and sour that goes extremely well with white rice.

Banh Xeo =
Crispy and flavorful, I loved this Banh Xeo.

Raw Beef Slices =
Delicious. The mixture of the cilantro, peanuts, and fish sauce made these tender raw beef slices amazing.

Chicken & Shrimp Salad =
This was okay. There wasn't much flavor in this dish -- had to drench it in fish sauce.

Shaking Beef =
The Shaking Beef here was tender, but the flavor was a bit off. It was still good, just a bit sour from the vinegar in the sauce.

Deep-Fried Shrimp w/ Garlic Noodles =
Shrimp should have been a bit more deep-fried, but the garlic noodles were EXCELLENT here.

Sea Bass over Glass Noodle =
This dish was just okay. The sea bass was a bit TOO flaky and the glass noodles were too garlicky. It went pretty well with white rice (since there was so much pungency from the garlic), though.

Roasted Quail =
Excellent quail. It came out bursting with flames (from the Bacardi 151 that it was doused in) and had tons of flavor.

-----------------------------

Jasmine Garden is one of the more authentic Vietnamese restaurants I've been to in SF. With the serious exception of their horrible pho, Jasmine Garden is an amazing Vietnamese restaurant that will guarantee a great experience.

name: Roy Chi
text:
Oyaji has always been on my list of must-try restaurants for a while now -- so I really wish I could say that I loved it, or even liked it -- but honestly, it was just okay.

---------------------------

FOOD:

Chicken Karaage = Highly recommended by Yelp, but was way too tough and too bland for me. The chicken tasted a bit old, giving it that jerky-like toughness that is every fried-chicken-eater's nightmare. One slice of lemon was not enough to bring any memorable flavor whatsoever.

Asparagus Beef Skewer = Pretty horrible. The beef was way too tough and overcooked. The tiny asparagus was engulfed by the disproportionate amount of tough, chewy beef.

Chicken Yakitori Skewer = This was okay. The chicken was cooked to a medium -- not too dry, but not really that moist either.

Braised Pork Belly = The one redeeming dish of the night. The braised pork belly here is pretty damn phenomenal. Extremely tender and flavorful, with plenty of fat to go around.

Ankimo = Good, but nothing great. Pretty average ankimo -- I wish it had more of the rich liver flavor. The spicy sauce on top took away from the ankimo's natural umami.

Miso Steamed Cod = Decent flavor, slightly overcooked.

Albacore Nigiri = Good -- a little tougher than that at better sushi joints, but still had a lot of the fatty flavor.

Scallop Nigiri = Good -- soft and tender.

Hamachi Nigiri = Decent -- nothing special.

---------------------------

Oyaji is mostly just an average, forgettable experience -- the sushi was okay and the robata grill items were quite horrible. If not for the braised pork belly, I'd probably consider Oyaji as one of the worst Japanese restaurants I've had in SF.

text:
Thanks to my friend, ex-wife and fellow local guide Hanae K, I had the opportunity to feast on an amazing array of izakaya dishes at Torihei. I am definitely a fan of Torihei and will be returning again for more.

Pretty much everything is good from the various items that we ordered. The ones that stood out the most were the chicken meatballs (OMG so good seriously), fatty pork, beef tongue, and chicken with green onion. Those items are all on the grill menu for you to fill in the number of items you want.

I also ordered a chadzuke with beef collagen. The flavor was good but the broth was a little too heavy for my preference. The meat was tender and delicious though. They also serve 20 orders to chicken broth shoyu ramen daily. We didn't try it but it's a great deal at only $5.

They have apple shochu that comes with frozen apple cups. It was so cute but not very practical as it was a complete pain to drink out of. There was too little alcohol and too much apple juice so the whole thing was very sweet.

I highly recommend their fried kabocha dessert. It's Japanese pumpkin slices covered in corn flakes then fried. It's served with a scoop of vanilla ice cream with blueberry sauce on the side. It was super delicious.

The service was pretty good. We ordered too many orders of a particular dish for the amount of people we had. The server was nice enough to come back and warned us about the portion size. We ended up reducing the order from 5 to 2 orders and it was perfect.

I had heard that the wait on weekends can be pretty bad here and I can see why. The place is tiny. They did open the Tsujita Annex diagonally across the street but I have yet to peek in there. Since it was a weekday, we were able to grab the last 2 spots at the counter.

I had the Tsukemen while my boyfriend had the char siu ramen. I didn't care for the broth on their regular ramen too much. I prefer richer darker broth.

As for the Tsukemen, when I had the first bite, I was a little overwhelmed by the intense bonito flavor of the broth. It was very seafood-y. However, after I added lime to the noodle as recommended, the flavor balanced out extremely well. I thoroughly enjoyed my ramen to the last bite.

The restaurant is cash only. Parking used to be a pain but they have free valet parking with validation now. It's located behind the building.

name: Natalie K
text:
Original Hoyka Noodle moved and is now in a bigger location with more parking in the back. It's not far from the previous location but the restaurant is much nicer inside. The service was also a little better.

Hoyka means dangling legs. The name came from the noodle place they purchased the recipe from in Thailand. There too, you sit and dangle your legs while eating. The new location has these high tables that allow you to get that experience.

The Hoyka noodle is a clear broth that has a sour and spicy flavor. I love this dish and also the boat noodle, which is a dark beef broth. We also order the crispy pork with basil. They have a small bowl of noodle for under $4 and a large for under $6. The portions are fairly small here so I suggest getting a small bowl of noodle per person then get some rice dishes or appetizers to share.

They have some homemade dessert items and traditional Thai drinks here. They also will have a lot of your traditional Thai favorites. If you just are not Thai food savvy, they definitely have Pad Thai for you.

The restaurant is cash only just like the previous location and every other restaurants in Thai town. Make sure you have cash.

I counted them, 2 plastic bowls for noodles, 2 containers for soup, and 2 other plastic bags outside the soup containers. 2 plastic bags for sprouts, 1 plastic bag for raw beef, and 5 small plastic containers for sauces. Then, all of them in a large plastic bag. They are total 15 plastic bags or containers for this order. I feel guilty for this.  I will never order to go again in here.

text:
Being from the San Gabriel Valley part of time, I've had my share of Taiwanese cuisine. So when I heard of a new Taiwanese place opening up west of the SGV, I was (and am always) bias about the quality / authenticity of a place before even trying.

Nonetheless, I finally tasted Pine & Crane this past weekend and was satisfied, although I've had better. The flavors and spiciness was all a bit tamed down for the community.

The DAN DAN NOODLES could have used a bit more spice and peanut flavoring. The noodles were done well, though.

The SPICY WONTONS could have been more spicier.

The BEEF ROLLS could have used a bit more beef and hoisin sauce. Too much veggies in the wrap.

The TAIWANESE STICKY RICE was a tad too sweet for me. The balance of savory was lacking.

The SCALLION PANCAKES were probably the best tasting dish compared to what my taste buds are used to and were my favorite. So glad they didn't mess this one up!

Great alternative for community if you're lazy to travel to SGV for the tastier, better quality choices.

name: Natalie K
text:
I should have known that despite having good reviews, getting Taiwanese good in Silverlake wouldn't ever really measure up to the SGV experience. I stopped by Pine & Crane for dinner on a weekend. Parking is a little tough. I ended up finding meter parking and walking.

The restaurant is a self-seating arrangement where you order first, get a number, and then find a table. There's several smaller tables and one big communal tables in the middle. There were also 3 tables outside. The restaurant is on the smaller side.

We ordered the three cup chicken, spicy shrimp wontons and sweet potato leaves to share. We also had a slice of "heirloom" watermelon, which is another fancy word for yellow watermelon. It was decently good but very pricey at $2.75 for a tiny slice. You can get yellow watermelon at a Chinese grocery store for like $1 per whole watermelon.

The food was fairly good but expensive. The portion sizes were pretty small compared to other Taiwanese restaurants and they definite charge a lot more. I did like the sweet potato leaves and shrimp wonton but didn't care much for the three cup chicken. I love the three cup dishes at Uncle Yu's in San Gabriel a lot more.

I would say skip this place and drive a little further to one of the many amazing Taiwanese restaurants in the SGV instead.

text: We took the Gourmet Express lunch train for my birthday and had a great experience. We had mimosas at the station bar while waiting to board with a huge crowd. The train itself was impressively well-maintained, a treat for anyone into locomotive machinery! Chef was able to accommodate our dietary restrictions flawlessly and the food was impressively well prepared considering it was made in a train car. We had a complimentary glass of wine from a selection of local wineries. Our dining experience continued in the dessert car for the trip back home with a flour-less chocolate cake which I liked in particular, a brulee and coffees. I also enjoyed a wine flight of selected reds. The observation deck was a pretty cool experience as well. I want to do a Murder Mystery dinner next time!!

name: Chris Good
text:
Overall it was a really disappointing experience.

When I called the Napa Wine Train to make a reservation the guy I spoke to recommended the Napa's First Wine Tour and talked me out of picking a different option. We arrived to get on the train and instead they put us on a bus where we sat for 25 minutes. Raymond Winery was great, I've been there before, but it seemed like they were dragging the tour out to fill up the hour tasting that they promised. We then got on the same bus and drove another 15 minutes to the train where we had a decent lunch and headed back to the station.

I was really unhappy with the fact that I paid $180 a person to ride a train and taste wine, and instead we spent half the time on a bus which neither the person I talked to nor the website said anything about. I felt like the guy who sold me on that tour conned me because they wanted to fill up all the tours. I definitely would not recommend the wine train, you can get a lot more for your money going wine tasting on your own. The only reason I gave it two stars is because the lady who guided us on the bus and winery was really nice and entertaining.

name: Jonathan Marinaro
text: "Ramen The Place" is billed as Japanese Fusion, but comes off as an upscale ramen joint over on the border between Santa Clara and Cupertino/Sunnyvale. The ramen itself is tasty, the wife and I had the Spicy Miso Tonkotsu and the Duck Shoyu ramens. Of the two, the Duck Shoyu really stood out. The broth is very flavorful and tastes like a duck consomme with large pieces of perfectly cooked duck to adorn it. The Spicy Miso Tonkotsu was a good showing, but if you've got a hankering for miso specific I'd recommend Misoya up the street. Service was good, especially since there was only one person on front-of-house, and the appetizers looked good, but the wife and I weren't hungry for more than ramen this time. Next time, we'll make sure to try the Kaarage Chicken and the Miso Minced Pork Rice Bowl!

text:
We went to Dumpling Kitchen today because I desperately wanted dim-summy food... dumplings. This was my first Shanghainese restaurant experience (I think)?

We put our names down, and were told 10-15 minutes. A few minutes later we were asked if we were okay with sharing a table. "Sure!" was our answer. We sat with two women, they had ordered a ton of food, so there was no need for any food ordering shame for me.

We ordered:

XLB Shanghai-style steamed pork dumplings (10pcs) - they were DELICIOUS!!!
Shanghai-style pan-fried pork buns (8pcs) - Meh, would not order these again
Pork dumplings in chili oil (10pcs) - YUM. Wontons in sesame chili oil.
Shanghai-style green onion pancake - YUM! Crispy, onions, light, fluffy!!!
Beijing-style sweet buns (4pcs) - Meh. We ordered steamed but got fried. Even still, just meh.

This is a good place for 4 or more people to come and dine with portion sizing. We ordered way too much food so that we could try a bunch of things. We'd definitely share a table again, just hopefully not the round table at the back (my hubs had to get up 3 times so the food delivery hand truck could make it to the kitchen). Parking wasn't too bad, we found a spot a long block away (and definitely needed the walk after our big meal).

name: Mike Shaheen
text:
As a newcomer 3 years ago to "real" Chinese food (you other midwest transplants probably know what I'm talking about) I made it my quest to try xiao long bao (the steamed dumplings with pork & soup) at every Shanghainese restaurant that offered it.

My wife's is Cantonese and grew up in the bay area with a restaraunt loving family, so over the years I have collected a list of dumpling rating criteria.

The ratios are arguably the most important criteria  to me.  If there is too little soup, there is less flavor.  If the dumpling is too thick, it can mask the flavor.  If there is not enough pork...well you see where I'm going with this.

Other xiao long bao issues:
- Served in a tiny foil tin that almost invariably sticks to dumpling
- Very salty broth
- Tough and/or dense port

This is turning into a food theory post, so I'll get to the point.

The Shanghai Dumpling Shop consistently serves delicious Xiao Long Bao.  I know the ratios preference is matter of opinion and maybe you like really salty soup, but I think these are the BEST.

And, maybe the highest praise I can offer in our hyper-critical Bay Area dining market:  "I have never heard anyone say anything bad about these wonderful dumplings."

text:
Fresh Corn Grill is easily one of my favorite lunch spots for many reasons. It's also very popular (for those reasons that I'll dive into in a bit) among many locals and businesses during lunch time so please be warned - you'll be greeted with a long line.

1. Their staff is SUPERB - always nice and polite with a smile.

2. Ordering steak with your salad, bowl or sandwich is always a tricky decision with any eatery - whether it's fancy sit-down or a fast food joint. There's always a concern with the meat being too dry, which happens all too often. Fresh Corn Grill have mastered the art of cooking steak just right. The tender slices on my favorite KALE ROOT BOWL are always perfect and plentiful. I crave their steak!

3. If you're like me and don't like to overeat, there's always an option to get a HALF SALAD for any of their options, which also helps to save some change in the wallet. My favorite salad is their BEETS SALAD either by itself or you can add extra protein for a few more bucks.

4. I've always been a big, big fan of their CAPRESE SANDWICH (fresh buffalo mozzarella, tomato, fresh basil with balsamic vinaigrette and olive oil), which comes with their delicious panini bread with a side salad. It's really delicious and is a BIG portion. You can split half the sandwich with someone else and it'll cost less than $5/person. Another yum sandwich is their GRILLED CHICKEN, which comes in a choice of cajun or citrus sauce.

Always a great choice for lunch or dinner and extremely delicious and affordable!!!

name: Sam C
text:
The fine city of San Francisco is a mecca for diverse dining. Burma Superstar needs to be on your list of places to eat.

If you decide to have a bite, be sure to come early for lunch (opens at 11:30AM) and grab a table before the waits could exceed your lunch hour. If you happen to be waiting, they have complimentary tea for your patience.

On to the menu:

Tea Leaf Salad - a MUST! With a list of 10+ fresh ingredients this is the most unique salad I ever had. The server will dress it for you.

Lamb Burmese Style Curry - tender chunks of goat in a rich curry stew. Not too spicy. On the side a scoop of their famous coconut rice.

Nan Gyi Dok (Coconut Chicken Rice Noodles Curry) - similar presentation as the salad. A very mild curry flavor.

I guess they decided that they needed something for the non Cajun food eaters. Me and the wife sometimes are just looking for a great burger, who thought it would be here. High quality meat and bun, WOW. I was addicted to the Shrimp Po Boy before and Cajun Chicken and Sausage Chowder. I have to admit I still am crazy about that.  I have to tell you the Brisket looked really good. Someone next to me had that and they said it was wonderful. I have to admit I've been there a couple of times before but didn't write about it. Went to the Blues Festival they had and it was fun. Look for the Crayfish Festival in April.

UPDATE:  7/29/2018. Had the steak tonight, man was that good and potato salad. Wife can't stop ordering the bisque. Finally ordered something different, then the blacken shrimp Po Boy, wasn't cheap, but steak was first class, ate everything except the plate.   Been back a number of times for Lunch, but like to update every once in a while.   UPDATE: 12/19/2017   This time I went with my wife and friend. I was sitting next to a couple and asked them about their meal. I told him I am confused about the reviews I've read. They stated that they are  from Louisiana and they tried to explain that people who aren't from Louisiana and are from California just don't understand the food correctly and that this is the only restaurant they come across out here that tastes exactly and the closest to the food they grew up with. He explained that he knows the  the restaurants history and has a choice,  but the choice he makes is to be at this restaurant and I said thank you.  Please read through the reviews and decided what's  real.   Having friends bash a restaurant to promote your restaurant is not the right Forum for food reviews.   Seriously I don't see this happening to other restaurants.                                       Update 6/10/2017- I can't believe the reviews with one star and calling the Chief a Mexican and not enough bread and I like the Old Place better and watered down drinks.  The Chief is the same Cook from the old place. Only difference is the old owner and his family seem to have a beef going on.. All of a sudden hateful reviews showing up. I understand sometimes longer waits, cold food, not spicy enough or too spicy reviews. Sadly these review sites can now serve as bases of hurting others.
I would read through the reviews and make your own decision on what is real. When I went there last week, the guy sitting at the bar next to me said this is the closes to the food his Mother made and when he comes out here this is where he eats all week.  * By the way my new favorite is the Shrimp Po Boy*

So far everything I've had there is great. The Bartenders are all nice and the service staff is fun. Not sure what one other person was talking about as far as un-happy workers, I thought all workers are happy. I love the Blacken Steak and  Shrimp Fettuccine, my wife likes it with chicken and sausage. I've been there about 10 times with different groups of people. For my: I eat like a five year old friends,  They can make the food not spicy and they do have vegetarian options, just ask. Try to go there when they have the shrimp and crayfish boils going on. The new owners Steve and Lisa are great people and they try their hardest to insure everything is done right. All I can say is everyone that I know loves the food. By the way the Bartenders shake my hand and welcome us when we show up.

text:
This review is for Republique's dinner.

3.5 stars towards their food | 5 stars towards their customer service

Upon arriving, expect parking to be limited but valet is available (small parking lot, though). Otherwise, metered street parking is available as well.

I was looking forward to finally trying Republique last night. Their customer service is great. The staff was helpful in educating us first-timers on their house favorite dishes and personal favorites as well. We ended up ordering a all starters and skipping the fish, pasta and meat sections.

Popular hors d'oeuvre EGGS ON TOAST was a favorite amongst our group as it is topped with a creamy and plump uni.

Starters ordered:
MEDITERRANEAN OCTOPUS - splendid dish and well cooked. Would order again! Lots of Vietnamese flavors in this one.
HAMACHI CRUDO (house favorite) - Thai influenced dish with refreshing flavors. Would order again!
BEEF TARTARE (house favorite) - very rich served with potato chips. Our group didn't care for it. I would not order again.
BRUSSEL SPROUTS - looked delicious but after breaking and mixing the egg yolk, it took the crispiness away from the charred leaves and just made the dish soggy altogether. Would not order again.
ESCARGOT - was well cooked and flavors were on point but would not order again.

DESSERT:
Popular SALTED CARAMEL CHOCOLATE CAKE - size-able dessert that had really good chocolate cake quality. However, the salted caramel drizzle made it a tad too sweet. The alcohol-infused milk that accompanied this dish was a nice taste to offset the sweetness. Would order again but maybe with salted caramel on the side.

I would love to come again for dinner to give it a second shot and to try out their brunch, which I heard great things about. It is also a completely different menu from dinner.

text:
I got a recommendation for the Sanguchon at Takatis so I decided to order it to go during a work day. They said it would take about 20 minutes but we ended up waiting so it took about 30 minutes total.

The sanguchon was really delicious. It's a messy sandwich with chicken, egg, veggies, sauce, and a thin slice of sweet potato. I would recommend that you keep the wrapper on as you eat. They give you these green and orange sauces. The orange one is spicier but didn't have great flavor. I really enjoyed the flavor on the green.

One of my coworkers tried their chicken and said it was delicious. The chicken was well-seasoned and the meat was very moist. They just weren't too crazy about the sauces. They give you 2 sides for a half chicken. The plantain was especially good. If I could, I would order a big order of plantain by itself.

They have Peruvian sodas and I always get Inca Cola when I eat Peruvian food. You can get a big bottle here or just the can.

text:
This place had me entertained! It’s a club turned restaurant/event space, and truly I wish it was still a dance club! There is a floor to ceiling TV screen that was oddly playing sports. Really out of place here. The menu was designed eclectically with different element themes matching each of the restaurant’s rooms -water, earth, fire, air. We joked that maybe we would rotate to the appropriate room corresponding to our next entree!

The food is good, however. It was just such a waste to have such an awesome place be just a restaurant. I had the unagi roll and my coworker had the salmon lemon roll. Both were very good and fresh. We also shared shishito peppers! Dinnerware was also very upscale and unique. They have actual chopsticks (not wooden ones wrapped in paper).

Our waiter was super nice and gave us a tour of the space after our meal. There is a special hidden room you can rent for a steep price to sing karaoke. And the bathrooms were really cool- the men’s room was Tiffany’s themed and the women’s room had a lip chair and lots of glitter.
