text:
Located in the same plaza with 99 Ranch and Starbucks, this restaurant is a hidden gem. My husband and I, we were planning to try this restaurant the weekend before, however, it was closed during dinner time due to private party. It was noted on Google, but we didn't check it, so it was our bad not them. Lol.
Didn't discouraged, we came back the following weekend. Boyz, this restaurant didn't disappointed us at all. From ambiance to service and what else? Food, of course.
We tried 2 appetizers which were chicken satay that came with sticky rice cakes and cucumber served with peanut dipping sauce. Chicken was tendered and peanut sauce was creamy and tasty. Next one was Roti Canai with chicken curry dipping also came with pan toasted flat bread. Very authentic and delicious. For entre, I chose Char Kwey Teow rice noodles. It was a combination of stir fried flat rice noodles with Chinese sausage, shrimp, egg and bean sprout. Kinda Pad Thai, however, I like this version better because it wasn't oily at all. Oh so tasty and yummy. My husband ordered its famous Nasi Lemak which was steamed rice in coconut juice served with curry chicken, roasted garlic peanuts, boiled egg, fried anchovies and sambal (a kind of mixed tamarind sauce). It got 2 thumbs up from him. Don't forget to choose medium spicy level for a kick. Last, but not least, a Happy Roti for dessert. Very unique. It was a blend of hot and cold, you'll get one scoop each of coconut pandan and jackfruit cashews ice cream on pan toasted flat bread sprinkled with coconut flakes. OMG!!! Soooo delicious, especially, jackfruit ice cream. Not sweet at all. Love it.
- Service was friendly and attentive. The 2 ladies servers were frequently checked on customers and refilled our water quickly.
- Most items on menu were under $10 and generous portions too.
Good food, good service, affordable price. We'll definitely be back to try other dishes soon.
- Do come on off peak hours to avoid waiting.

name: Roy Chi
text:
Kiraku is one of the most exciting and innovative Japanese restaurants in the Bay Area. It's completely unassuming and the decor is pretty plain, but you can instantly tell from the constantly out-the-door lines that there's something special here. I love everything about Kiraku -- the service is phenomenal (the owners are such sweet people), the ingredients are incredibly fresh, and the dishes are wildly inventive yet somehow seems to maintain such a strong sense of authenticity that they should definitely not be considered "fusion fare."

I've been to Kiraku so many times now that my list of favorite dishes extends much longer than I'm able to type, but just know that it's really hard to go wrong here. The sashimi is unbelievably fresh, so make sure you throw in some sashimi slices into your order (Amberjack, Black Throat, Salmon, Toro, etc.). The Braised Kurobuta Pork is incredibly tender, the Amberjack Kama (Collar) is delicious, the Tempura Corn is perfectly crispy, and it really just goes on and on. The more you eat here, the more you'll be able to pick out your personal favorites, since there are just so many items on the menu.

My personal addiction here is their Fried Chicken Cartilage. It's super simple, but they just cook it so perfectly. It's seasoned and breaded so well that it's tough to imagine that something so easy could be so addictively delicious. Of course, you'd have to love the crunchy-meets-rubbery texture of chicken cartilage to really appreciate this awesome dish.

Make sure you end your meal with Kiraku's subtly-sweet, perfectly-textured Sweet Potato Creme Brulee.

With all of the incredible restaurants in the Berkeley area, Kiraku stands out because it has fresh, delicious Japanese food that's genuinely innovative and prepared so intricately. It's definitely one of the very best restaurants in the Bay Area.

Nutshell: tasty overpriced food in a good atmosphere.
I've dined at Forage twice, once for dinner, once for lunch. Surprisingly the pricing and food selection was largely identical. Closed on Sunday?
For dinner I had the protein+2 side combo for about $17 which included tri-tip, brussels sprouts and a kale salad, all very flavorful and well prepared and an appropriate portion size.
Lunch was a surprise coming out to $18 for their grass fed burger and a small market lettuce salad. Both the salad and the burger were good but unremarkable (the heirloom tomato was the star of the burger). One of my fellow diners ordered a sandwich which they had to make fresh and the wait was much longer than we were told.
For locally sourced and sustainable ingredients, i suppose the price is not outrageous, but I think it's closer to $$$ than $$

text:
I typed in “hu tieu” in Yelp and this place popped up.

There’s plenty of parking to the left of the building, while the right side was reserved for outdoor dining.

I walked in the front door and said I wanted to dine-in. The guy said have a seat at the table and call him when ready to order.

So we went to seat ourselves and on the table, had a little note that said when you’re ready to order, please call this phone number. That the menu could be viewed electronically on Yelp, inside on the wall, or printed paper menu at the entrance.

We weren’t satisfied with the paper menu so we went back inside. The official menu on the wall had more pages with photos. The first page showed the types of noodles offered like large or small rice noodles, thin or thick egg noodles, and other types.

We then proceeded back out to take a seat and then the food was brought to us in a bag with take out containers. I thought it was odd that the broth was in a separate container and you pour in the broth yourself into to the bowl. Condiments, garnishes, and veggies were all in sandwich bags. Oh prior to food coming out, we got served Chinese long doughnut.

The portions were huge! My mom and I shared one soup broth container between the two of us.

My mom got the hu tieu combo plus liver and I got mi (egg noodles) with char siu and wonton. My mom loved her meal and said it resembles Vietnam and how much she enjoyed it that she finished it all. For me, I enjoyed it. The broth was clear, not too sweet or salty, didn’t taste any msg. The portion was too much for me and I had to take the rest home.

After we finished, we went back inside to pay the bill. I would think people have dine and dashed if payment is not taken beforehand since everything is in take out containers.

Chemango! It's the best kind of Raspado there is. For those of you who don't know what either of those 2 items mentioned is, let me explain. Raspados are Mexican shaved ice with fruit and syrup. They come in tons of flavors like mango, pineapple, coconut, strawberry, etc.

I love coconut but Chemango is my favorite. It's a combination of mango, chemoy (which has tamarind and some other things mixed in), and chili. It's sweet, sour and spicy. Raspado Xpress makes seriously delicious Chemango.

Although you can buy much cheaper Raspados from a questionable cart in a park, getting it from Raspado Xpress is better. They have a wider variety of flavor and is much cleaner. It is pretty pricey though at $6 each. The size of the Raspados here are really big.

text:
If you’re looking for authentic, homemade Filipino food, Zarlitos is it. My friend and I ordered takeout, and eating this reminded me of going to a friend’s house and trying their parent’s delicious food.

Disclaimer: if you are health conscious and do not like to eat pork, this review may not be for you, but don’t worry, as they have other options available!

I always get the lechon combo from Zarlitos. You get pancit bihon, garlic fried rice, lumpia, and a generous serving of lechon kuwali. The lechon is crispy, melts in your mouth, and tastes great with the garlic fried rice and mang tomas sauce. This is Filipino soul food at its very finest, and I never leave Zarlitos feeling dissatisfied.

The sisig plate is crispy, juicy, and has the right amount of zest and spice that makes this sisig great. This is a lot of pork to eat in one sitting, so I definitely recommend eating a portion of the meal and saving the rest for the next day. Zarlito’s generous servings, tasty food, and homey customer service always bring me back for more.

This place on the outside looks like some hole in the wall place and very small. If you don't have a reservation, expect to wait 40 min to an hour. Once you get a seat, everything else is quite easy and fast! At each table, there is a 10" tablet for you to choose what you want, even if you want to just get the waitresses help. Once you pressed the order button, everything comes quickly. You can order a small amount, order, decide what else you want, then order again! name: Uncle Buck
text:
Fuego Cravings in Beaumont, CA is, well... en Fuego!

This new restaurant to the Pass Area, located at the border of Beaumont and Banning, is truly a delicious take on classic/traditional Mexican snack/street food with a modern twist, combining established flavor with unique and current cultural favorites.

Let's talk about the menu... street tacos, burritos, mulitas, elote, hot dogs and desserts, oh my! Everything is either traditional or offered with a covering/mixing/dusting of a flaming hot chip of choice (Cheetos/Doritos). To say that this spot caters to it's customers is an understatement.

When you're done with all of the main foods, save some room for a dessert of choice. Fuego Cravings offers sinful choices such as Mangonadas, fresh churros (authentic Mexican style - from the little man on the corner, by the church on Sunday, in TJ) and a wide variety of Tostilocos style (in the bag and smothered with greatness) chips for your enjoyment.

The restaurant is clean and well maintained, along with an inviting layout showcasing more than (8) TV's and a large sectional couch for watching the game with friends and family. Did I mention that they also serve alcohol? What better way to eat this food than with an ice cold beer... for the little ones or folks that don't drink alcohol, there's plenty of bottled Mexican favorites (soft drinks, Jaritos) and agua frescas.

Wendy, one of the owners, was delightful and helpful with ordering and making sure that we got all of our items, in a timely manner.

As this location is new, be prepared for a wait during lunch and dinner times. As with all great things... it's worth the wait!

When in the Pass Area, stop by and give Fuego Cravings a try... tell them Uncle Buck and the Madonna family told you to, "Come on in!"

Then I noticed that there was a $0.99 fee charged, which is not cool that she didn't tell me at all, much less before she ran my card. Upon getting my food she said here is the $2, even though she was supposed to give me a little over $2.50 back. I was over it at that point. No receipt showing exactly how much change I should have been given, didn't tell me about the fee, didn't let me know before she ran my card that she didn't have the change right then, and then shorted me my physical change. It isn't really about the money for the fee and missing change as much as it about that all being unethical business practices. Needless to say I will not be returning. The food wasn't bad, not amazing either, but I would rather give my money to a business that will treat me with respect and not just hope I don't care because it is a small amount of money.

text:
Gomez's Snap-E-Tacos has been the best taco stand in the Covina area for over 30 years! You cannot find a more authentic taco stand with such a local following anywhere else in the area.

Snap-E-Tacos is not an imitation Mexican street taco spot. Instead they offer crunchy hard shell tacos, burritos, gorditas, street tacos, sopes, taco burgers, hamburgers,  chili cheese fries etc. With many specials offering 1-2 items (or more) and a drink, this spot will save you money and get you full.

Located at the intersection of Vincent and Badillo, Snap-E-Tacos is in the heart of Covina. Family owned and operated, you get top notch service (from an actual family) that cares about the city and has made a commitment to stay in it and serve the people with pride.

Next time you are in the area, stop by and give 'em a try. Word of mouth is their primary form of advertising, so if you like the food and the service, please support them in whatever way you can.

I was extremely confused when I walked into Tsurumaru Udon Honpo. You have to order cafeteria style and even bring the tray back, which is all fine and dandy. The issue is the ordering system is just confusing. You go up to the first guy and ask for the udon you want then you have to ask someone else for the fried topping you want in your udon.

Finally after you pay, there is no clear instruction of where you wait. We ended up going back to the udon guy to get our udon and then waited a while for our fried items. Our noodle was getting cold while we were waiting for our fried items.

I ordered the kake udon, which is just plain udon and broth, and I got a side of kakiage. The udon isn't bad. The noodle was a little undercooked for my liking but the broth had deep flavor. I wouldn't say that it's as good as Marugame Monzo by any means but it's edible. Their fried kakiage is also fairly good.

The restaurant is located on the 3rd floor in the little tokyo plaza. You can park inside the plaza with a 2 hours validation from here. There is also an arcade and karaoke room on the 2nd floor in case you need something to do after your meal.

name: Roy Chi
text:
*3.5 stars*

I knew I was in for something special when I came to Atelier Crenn. Two Michelin stars, molecular gastronomy, one of the most talked about chefs in Dominique Crenn -- it had to be amazing. And it really was. The food here is wildly creative, uniquely flavorful, and presented so beautifully that to eat it would be a tragedy in the art world.

There were so many incredible things going for it: (1) The food was delicious, (2) the sommelier was enthusiastic and knowledgeable, and (3) the ambiance was intimate and refined. Dominique Crenn is an absolutely genius when it comes to her food.

Unfortunately, the disappointments came with the service. Now, the service was good in the sense that they were attentive (water & wine always filled) and the dishes were brought and taken away simultaneously. For a Michelin-starred restaurant, those are givens. However, the servers (except for the awesome sommelier) were all emotionless robots. Monotone and quiet, they all seemed like they hated their jobs. There wasn't even an iota of friendliness in their voices whatsoever, and it kind of dampened the experience drastically. When each dish was served, it would be served silently and then with a brief and boring description -- completely making us unexcited about whatever we were about to eat.

The worst part was that they completely didn't do anything for my friend's birthday. Now, I mentioned to them TWICE before the dinner (when I was making the reservation and again, when I confirmed the reservation) that the dinner was to celebrate "Alice's birthday." On the phone, the receptionist even said: "Oh yeah, I have that written down. Don't worry, we'll have something nice for her." During the actual dinner, however, nothing. No candle, no "Happy Birthday" written with chocolate, not even a verbal "Happy birthday." For a two-Michelin starred restaurant of this caliber, such negligence should NEVER occur. Unfortunately it did, and we had to have a depressingly anti-climatic "yeah.... so... happy birthday, I guess" moment outside. I wouldn't come back solely for that part of the experience.

Also, from my friends' experiences with Atelier Crenn, Dominique Crenn always comes out to say hello to the guests. Definitely not this time.

Now the food itself was excellent for the most part -- the "adult cereal" (seeds & grains) and the mixed mushroom dish were delicious. The "beet" dessert (beet sorbet w/ chocolate "root") was incredible. The squab was well-cooked, but lacked a powerful flavor that made it dissolve into the background of our meal. Every dish was beautiful and creative, and I believe it really was worth the price.

The service, however, just disappointed me so much that even the greatest food in the world couldn't make it worth it, especially at this price point.

text:
I used to live in the area about 4 years ago, we visited family for the holidays and decided to get some food on our way home. I was upset to see that a lot of my favorite places closed down or no longer existed. I am extremely pleased that this place was still here. I would come for the xiao long bao alone, but noticed they expanded their menu quite a bit from what I remembered all those years ago.

The xiao long bao is still exceptional. It takes a bit to get to your table, but it's worth the wait every time.

The pork belly with preserved vegetables is a traditional dish that my chinese born husband remembers fondly and their version made him and myself very happy. It's melt in your mouth delicious!

The XO sauce noodles we ordered were scrumptious, easily the best noodles of its type I've ever had.

We were sadly too full for the clay pot curry, but that was absolutely delicious too. We took it home and had it the next day.

Thank you for the delicious food and good memories. :)

We got there and it was a slightly busy Friday night. I understand it was going to be a little slower due to amount of people. But I nor my wife were prepared to sit there for 1 hour and 30 minutes for our food to come out. The bar tender was friendly enough but there was no obvious communication in between the kitchen and FOH. It got to the point of having to leave because we had to get our child from the babysitters. As we were getting up to leave, still very hungry, out comes out food. I asked for it to be boxed up as we didn't have time to eat and wanted to take it with us. The food was taken back to the kitchen and we started the waiting game......again. It took 10 minutes to put our now very cold food into a a take away container. It was only after I enquired about the missing food did it come back out.

text:
Tony's Spunky Steer has been a beloved steak house in the Redlands, CA area for over 20 years. They offer a full stake house experience without the drastically high prices that generally come with "premiere" restaurant offerings.

Located right off of the 10 freeway, The Spunky Steer has an easy to find location with upfront and side paring lot access. This spot is a local favorite with the lunch rush happening between 1-3 pm and the dinner rush between 5-7 pm. Everyday of the week sees heavy traffic during these hours so plan accordingly.

Food offerings are vast, with everything from Rib-eye to Prime Rib. They not only have steak, but offer chicken and fish items as well. Appetizers are generous and I recommend the sauteed mushrooms, they are excellent! There is a kid's menu with 8+ choices so the little ones won't feel left out if they don't want a steak. By far the most budget friendly and overall favorite of most visitors is the "Small but Mighty" special that includes your choice of a salad or soup, an 8 oz. steak cooked to order, mashed or baked potato or french fries, and a piece of "Texas Style" toast. The Spunky Steer has a bar offering beer and wine choices and also a full variety of the usual soft drinks.

If you are craving a "premium" steak lunch or dinner, but want to stay close to home and not break the bank while dinning out, the Spunky Steer should be your ultimate destination. Give them a try and see what locals have been raving about for over two decades.

The kids enjoyed the simple cucmber, tuna, and octopus rolls.  I was surprised the kids liked the octopus roll as much as they did.

name: KimnLee 7591
text:
It's been a while since the pandemic that my husband and I, we returned here to enjoy its famously baked catfish and seafood hot pot. Boyz, it didn't let us down at all.
- First of all, here are some updates as of today, you now can dine-in (with limited seating per state - law, of course). From my observations, restaurant has re-arranged its tables approximately 6' apart including surrounding glasses dividers for each table (the amount of tables have been reduced in half compared to pre-pandemic) so we feel more safe and comfortable to eat-in. They tried to seat customers as far as possible from one table to other tables. All employees were wearing masks, and they cleaned up tables and chairs thoroughly with sanitizer after each used.
- As usual, we ordered our favorites baked catfish and a seafood hot pot. The balance of the sweet, sour and little spicy of the broth was perfect. There was a variation of seafood such as fish, shrimps, clams, jelly fish, squid, snails and quail eggs for you to dip in broth. It served with rice vermicelli and vegetables. I'm still salivating when thinking about it. Lol. We couldn't finish it because we still have to make room for the baked fish. Wow. The fish was perfectly baked. It was golden brown, crisp and fresh. Beautifully decorated with its trimmings such as lettuce, carrot pickle, cucumber, crushed peanuts. So yummmmy. It served with rice paper, a full plate of various mints, lettuce, more carrot pickle and slices of cucumber dipped in anchovies or mixed fish sauce of your choice. It's so good. Worth an hour drive to get here. Lol.
Service was nice, attentive, and friendly. Expected to wait a bit longer for the food, which was understandable. Perhaps, kitchen personnel down-size due to the Covid-19 situation. However, foods had same taste as before pandemic.
Overall, we would definitely return again.

It was true genuine Korean BBQ that wasn't packed with sugar to adjust for American tastes. They also have these wonderful turtle-shaped plates. The second time my group of friends and I went to eat at this restaurant it was no longer located in the original spot so we thought the place closed and we were a bit sad.
We thought we found a new Korean BBQ spot on this block but as soon as we saw the turtle-shaped plates we were delighted to find out it was the same BBQ restaurant, just located in a different spot. Great food, a bit pricey but for good reason.

My friends and I came here during HH and on an off hour for a whiskey flight special. WOW. What a great choice to trying different types of whiskeys. I definitely appreciate this as a whiskey drinker.

Their HH flatbread is great, wings are great, burger is great. Pretty all of the HH items are great.

There is a parking lot for during the day and FREE valet for early evening-late timeframes.

text:
This is a solid Thai restaurant a little bit off to the corner of Thai Town area. They specialize in Northern Thai food but will have pretty much all your Thai favorites to select from. The restaurant is small so I would not recommend coming with more than a party of 4 because there will be no way for everyone to sit together.

The restaurant is cash only. They do have an ATM inside. Parking is free since it's not on the main strip of Thai town. The service is pretty good.

We ended up ordering Tom Yum shrimp, Pad Thai with shrimp, and grilled beef with sticky rice. I didn't try any of their Northern dishes this time around. Everything we got was delicious. I especially enjoyed the grilled beef but will want to their try the grilled pork next time. It seems like they're known for that.

This restaurant is definitely not cheap. For the 3 dishes we ordered plus 2 drinks, we ended up paying $58 before tip. That is probably the most expensive meal in Thai Town for 2 I've ever had so I was very surprised considering this place is such a hole in the wall.

My favorite restaurant for regular Thai dishes in Thai Town is still Hollywood Thai. The price is more reasonable and the food is better.

text:
My mom and I had dinner here recently and had a good meal.  The place as not too crowded so we were able to order right away.  The food then came within a few minutes.  They deliver right to your table.  We both had the Pick Two.

I went with the Green Goddess Cobb Salad with Chicken - Chicken raised without antibiotics, arugula, romaine, kale and radicchio blend, vine-ripened tomatoes and pickled red onions tossed with freshly made Green Goddess dressing and topped with avocado, bacon, and cage-free hard-boiled egg (mom ate the egg). This was a really good salad.  Loved the bacon and avocado.  Good chicken flavor.

I also had the Vegetarian Autumn Squash Soup - A rich blend of butternut squash and pumpkin simmered in vegetable broth with select ingredients including: honey, apple juice, cinnamon and a hint of curry, then finished with sweet cream and topped with roasted and salted pumpkin seeds.  I really like this soup.  It has a good Fall flavor.  Love the pumpkin seeds on top.

Mom had the Vegetarian Creamy Tomato Soup - Vine-ripened pear tomatoes pureed with fresh cream for a velvety smooth flavor accented by hints of red pepper and oregano and topped with our homemade black pepper focaccia croutons. She really liked the soup. Good tomato flavor.

She also had the Heritage Ham & Swiss Sandwich - Artisan ham, Emmental swiss, emerald greens (mom skipped the greens) and maple mustard sauce on Country Rustic.

Ate the side of bread the next day and it was really good toasted.  And love the kettle chips too.

Overall a good dinner.  Love their food.

Men Oh Tokushima's ramen is pretty good but their Tokushima don is really delicious as well. They have 4 different options: Shoyu, Tonkatsu, Spicy Tonkatsu, and Tokushima. Tokushima is a combination broth between Shoyu and Tonkatsu. I personally enjoy the Tokushima style the most.

The Tokushima don is a rice bowl with pork that's been cooked in this delicious marinate. They serve it with some flavored bamboo shoots and lots of green onion. I got it as a combo with my ramen and it was way too much food but worth it.

The water there smells horribly like chlorine. I ended up having to order a green tea to have with my meal because I couldn't drink their water.

The service is pretty good and the food comes out quickly. They have a parking lot that is $5 flat fee but if you mention to the attendant that you're eating at one of the restaurants, parking is only $3.

name: alice chung
text:
Ramen Champ blew my mind.

Sure, the eatery is small but the wait wasn't horrible on a rainy Sunday evening around 7pm. We waited for about 10 minutes and was seated in front of the kitchen. I love the open kitchen where you can see the chefs do their magic.

My friend and I ordered two appetizers - the karaage (fried chicken) and fried mushrooms. Both were superb! Fried chicken never tasted so moist and juicy.

Now for the tonkotsu ramen - broth was so thick and creamy, I couldn't believe the flavor that was coming from JUST the broth. The noodles weren't as abundant as your regular ramen place but it was the perfect portion size for me, a 5'5 Asian gal. The semi-cooked egg was amazing. When opened, the yolk was of a thick orange hue and so packed with flavor I couldn't understand how it could have been so flavorful from the inside. Mind blown.

Thank you ramen champ. Looking forward to trying other dishes when I return!

High end mall, and worth a visit.

Stores either are always running a sale, or about to run a sale, so patience is awarded. The mall is outdoors, and can be confusing to navigate, but unlike some other malls it's compact enough that a wrong turn won't get you completely lost.
Store variety is amazing. Lego store, Macy's, Express, and Nordstrom are great stores.

Parking is amazing. Large parking lots with a leniant two hour grace period, and only two dollars per hour after that. Occasionally bottlenecks at the entrances, and the entrance coming from La Jolla Village Drive often holds up traffic due to bad signal timing.

I recommend coming from Executive Drive or Nobel
Drive if driving.

Food is higher priced. Good variety around the mall, but expect around 10 dollar meals.

name: Wesley Chen

The only concern I would have is if the weather is bad, but it seems that here the weather is never bad. Interestingly, people stay and browse around from morning until night, and there is very rarely a nonbusy time on the weekends.

I went to the bar and got up close with the group monopolizing his attention, but I was not acknowledged either. A lady came from the outside, walked straight to him and asked for a refill. I went where she was and loudly stated I guessed we had been standing in the wrong places. (BTW, the carbonation was down in the bar as well.)
We wanted to get tshirts and take pictures and post that we were there and loving it.... We didn't.
Up side.... An hour later, at home, our food was DELICIOUS!

text:
WHAT DID I GET:  The Fried Chicken Sandwich, the Key Lime Pie (small), and a Coke.

HOW WAS IT:  The sandwich was pretty solid; nothing mind-blowing, but it hit the spot.  The Key Lime Pie (small), while good, was more of a tart; it came in this little tinfoil cup instead of as an actual slice, which was disappointing.  I've seen other places do this as well with cakes and pies (serving them in little cups instead of as actual slices), and I really don't like it.  If you're going to sell pie, I want an actual slice, not two bites of a slice of pie in a little cup (the large pie was also in a slightly larger tinfoil cup).

HOW MUCH DID IT COST:  Including tip, it was a little under $19.

WOULD I COME BACK/RECOMMEND THIS PLACE:  Maybe.  I wouldn't say no, because the food was satisfying and the staff was pretty friendly.  I also wouldn't say yes, because my table was wobbly and I feel like I got let down with the pie (again, I was really hoping for a slice, not tinfoil cups, of pie).  Also, for what I got, I feel the price was a little too high.

text:
It's not often I have the inclination to visit the first thing Yelp recommends in the morning. This time I did. From the looks of it, Gastropig has the makings of a family friendly hipster haven, equipped with fresh coffee, homemade baked goods filled with bacon, and canned sauvignon blanc or hard cider.

The menu items are kitchy and different enough to spark curiosity. I went for the breakfast tacos. Pulled pork, eggs and salsa sounded great. Something I had never seen is waffle hash browns. When I  asked the server bringing our food where they were, she pointed at the plate to my surprise. They literally look like waffles.

Up until now everything looked very promising. The taste: bland. So many ingredients would generally gleam complexity, but lack of spices and salt make for a filling snack instead of a savory meal. It was served room temperature with the tortilla hardly toasted. Given the saucyness of the pulled pork and salsa, a structured tortilla would have prevented the taco from splitting in half, which is what it did.

I took a break from the broken tacos and went for the waffle. When I crave hash browns, it's for the crispiness. The image I got from these was as if I left a defrosted waffle out overnight and took a bite of it in the morning because it's what required the least amount of effort. The cemented slice of cold cheese on top added rubbery to the criterion.

A few bites of one of my companion's flattened sausage, starchy seasoned potatoes, the unassuming bacon nutter butter, and bacon chocolate chip cookie sounds cool to say, but the memory of it lays fickle.

I'd give it another go to check for consistency. Though, sometimes execution of a concept means forgoing lasting flavor impression, which is why I took a refill of the best tasting item I had--coffee--to go.

text:
I was dying to have a waterelon juice with lychee. On the way home I stopped at Eggettes. There was one poor fella working the counter, and a long line, but that guy was making bobba, eggettes, and chicken as fast as fast can be!

I didn't know what to expect. I have a love hate relationship with bobba, the tapioca is so good, but so weird. So when a friend recently brought me a 'bobba' with lychee jelly, all of the bobba pieces of the bobba puzzle came together.

WATERMELON JUICE WITH LYCHEE JELLY - watermelon juice super good, lychee jelly ok (I liked the jelly from Tapioca express it had better texture and more flavor)

THAI TEA WITH TAPIOCA - Thai tea was a little weaker than traditional Thai teas from Thai restaurants, tapioca was good (I think I'd try a different tea next time)

HONEYDEW EGGETTES - OMG WTF AMAZEBALLS. I was standing in line trying to decide whether or not to get these, and I am SO glad I did. They look like giant bubble wrap, or alien cookies if you have an overactive imagination like me. I was wondering if they were going to be eggy, they're not. They're light and crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside.

ORIGINAL CRISPY CHICKEN - lightly floured, then deep-fried, then re-heated in an oven. They were really good. Next time, I will ask for them plain without the cheese and green stuff. And I'll also ask for some sauce.

I imagine that it will take me several trips to find my favorite juice/tea situation (so many choices: tea, juice, frozen, tapioca, extra tapioca, fruit/tea combo). I think at Eggettes I will stick with tapioca. I will definitely be back for Eggettes, and the chicken.

I was sad to see they had fin soup... until I read more carefully and realized it was imitation. Good on ya Eggettes, for serving imitation shark fin :)

Minus 1 star... the interior of Eggettes needed a little refreshing (new paint on the walls and a good cleaning).

The service was nice. The staff wore masks and our waitress was very honest about the wait time for our food to go to our table. If you order the wings it’ll take longer to make so that might come after your pho gets to you!

Let’s get to the food. It was all right! The price:size ratio of the pho was a bit underwhelming, but the broth was good, typical of most pho restaurants. I like how we got to pick which meats we wanted in our pho because other restaurants just give you a set option. I wish there were more noodles because there wasn’t enough. It was just a lot of onion and herbs and not enough noodles to balance the dish.

The chicken wings were ok. I personally thought that these wings were a little on the dry side (both in cook and in flavor). These definitely needed some sweet and sour fish sauce (nuoc cham) because it didn’t really have a lot of spice. I definitely thought it could have used more imagination in the way this was made and presented.

Overall, I liked the food and service. The staff were great, but I think the food could be better, especially if you’re paying that much for pho and garlic chicken wings. Granted, this location is by Disneyland, so food will probably be priced higher.

name: Her Majesty Ms Freeman Her Royal Highness Freeman
text: Excellent parlor! Been frequenting this one for years and years. Had a few birthdays and family get together. I long for the days when after a long hard day at work, when it’s too darn hot to cook as Chico temperatures soared up in the 110 degree range. Piling the family up into our 1982 Gremlin with sweat dripping from each of their tiny heads, as their faces gently planted on the huge panorama back window. Without air conditioning it was a blessing to have this neighborhood pizza parlor so close to home. This has been a staple to many of us old Chicoans. The place was packed with ball players galore, with new teams coming in with each new hour. Finding a seat was somewhat difficult at times, but always expected from us locals. The pizza was that yummy and the social hour was even more appealing to us parents raised up in the seventies. Handing the kids a bucket full of quarters in an exchange for a few minutes of bliss, was well worth my contributions of blood sweat and tears I donated to my work at Thriftys scooping ice cream the previous week. The kids played games for a half an hour before my peace was destroyed by the screaming of my youngest because he didn’t get his tickets he felt he deserved from a game he was Way too young to understand the concept of stopping the light on the ticket number that was the highest. Nevertheless at that moment as I sat in my chair with the cool air conditioner blowing my previously sweat soaked hair into a dry crispy texture, my inner self was smiling. The table of softball players drowning out the cry’s of a kid done wrong. I acted as if I was once again I was in the height of my hey days as a local college student with the only care in the world was pondering where we could party in the upcoming weekend, or if my tube was still holding the air after las weeks blackout. This nostalgic pizza parlor brings it all back like yesterday.

text:
Yet another food-truck-turned-brick-and-mortar restaurant popping up in LA. This new addition to Ktown is a great place to stop for some Korean fusion eats.

I stopped in for lunch and the whole place was mostly empty. They have a parking lot about 2 doors down that they share with a Korean catering company, which is nice. They have menus up on the counter and you order before seating.

They have several side dishes but I was mostly there to try the buns. My favorite was the spicy pig bun. I also enjoyed the pork belly bun. The kalbi bun was just alright to me. You can get it was a 1, 2, or 3 buns combo. We chose to have ours with garlic fries and sweet potato fries.

We also tried the bacon cheese corn. It was really delicious and had tons of bacon and cheese in it. The dish was enough for a few people to share because it's pretty rich.

They serve beer and wine as well. They had a few beer selections on tap, which I liked. I had one of their hefeweizens and enjoyed it. They also serve your Korean favorites like soju, makgeolli, and korean beers.

The service is okay. The food does take a little bit to come out. The atmosphere is very casual.

text:
From the atmosphere and customer service to the quality of the food, Skaf's Lebanese Cuisine was a superb experience for me.

I dined here a few nights ago for the first time and was really impressed with the customer service. A man, who seemed to be the manager, genuinely wanted to know my friend and I liked our specialty drinks. I ordered the rose water beverage and my friend got the blueberry juice beverage. I thought both were too watered down but still tasty. I let him know and he took it with a smile and told us his favorite, which was the blueberry one.

We shared the SPICY POTATOES ($7) appetizer, which was great. The manager gave us a free side of GARLIC SPREAD (normally $5) to go along with the potatoes. It was such a perfect (and generous) combination.

I ordered the LAMB KEBOB ($16) entree - medium rare - and came with rice (or fries), their famous cabbage salad, hummus & pita bread. Oh, it was delicious. Everything was great.

My friend ordered the COMBO PLATE ($19) because she wanted to try a little bit of everything. Her dish was delicious as well.

I will definitely come back again. Loved everything and cannot wait to try other dishes.

They have a small parking lot available for you or there's always street parking.

text:
I love indian food, it's hard to find good authentic fare, I was in hollywood not too long ago and had some but was left wanting. I've had some good places in the Inland Empire, but hadn't had any luck since moving down here.

My husband surprised me with this little gem of a place for my birthday, and it's a small innocuous hole in the wall, but inside I had what was quite possibly the best indian meal of my life.

The curries were exploding with aromatic spices and flavors, the rice was scrumptious and fresh and our tandoori chicken and lamb arrived to our table sizzling hot and was cooked to absolute perfection.

The naan bread was fresh off the oven and absolutely delicious, their chutneys and sauces are so flavorful and tasty, I could have eaten nothing but the naan and I would have left happy.

At the end they surprised me with a lovely rice pudding dessert. I was so happy, and our waitress was always so sweet and was happy to suggest dishes to my husband!

I'm very happy I've found an amazing place to satisfy my indian food craves. If you're in the area, you must give this place a shot and have it change your life.

PS the Mango Lassi is to die for.

text:
My mom and I recently had dinner here.  The restaurant recently moved from a smaller location around the corner and I wanted to try the new location.  The place is large and spacious.  Love the chandelier in the lobby.  They give you a basket of garlic breadsticks.  These were so good.  Not too garlicky.

Mom had the Gamberi as vino Bianco - jumbo prawns sauteed in white wine sauce served with a side of penne pasta.  She really liked this.  Lots of big prawns.  Nice light sauce.  Not heavy at all.

I had the Vitello al Marsala - Veal sauteed with mushrooms in a Marsala wine sauce, with a side of veggies instead of pasta.  This was so good.  Lots of mushrooms, tender veal, good flavor.  Veggies were cooked nicely, not mushy.

For dessert, mom had the salted caramel gelato.  She loved this.  Very tasty.  Large portion.  I had the cannoli.  This was really good.  Crisp shell that was easily cut with a fork.  Flavorful cream inside.

A great local Italian restaurant.  I will be back.

text:
My friend frecommended this place for lunch after our hike by saying that it's healthy. I just finished working out and wanted something delicious, not healthy so I reluctantly followed along. I have to say that I was surprised by how delicious their healthy selections were.

It was Sunday so the restaurant was very busy. Luckily we found some metered parking on the street almost right in front. We waited less than 10 minutes for our table.

I ordered the veggie sandwich, which was really amazing. The cheese and the spread they use really gave the sandwich a lot of flavor. The mixture of veggies was just right for the texture and the bread was grainy and delicious. I have ordered veggie sandwiches at other restaurants but none have measured up to the one here yet.

My friend had their breakfast burrito and really enjoyed it. They also have fresh juices and smoothies. I saw a lot of people who came just for the juice. I didn't get to try any since I really needed coffee at the time.

The service was great and our waiter was friendly. We got our food fairly quickly. I would definitely come back again when I am in the Palisades area.

I ordered the medium size PB bowl.  It was beautiful, tasty and huge!  The bottom was and acai peanut butter blend, then a layer of crunchy grains, then a layer of bananas and then strawberries, artfully arranged.  It was topped with raspberries, coconut shavings, and a little honey.  The restaurant was spotlessly clean. The assortment of ingredients for salads and bowls was ample. I didn't check the restrooms. The service was fast, friendly, and informative. We found out they have two locations open now with two more expected this year.  Vegan, organic, clean, and healthy, and for those who crave meat conveniently located right next door to Subway. What's not to love?

name: Chevelle Macndough
text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐[ EBT ALERT!! ]⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Left In The 💙 Of My Hood! This Burger King accepts EBT food stamp cards! If only they all did! 🤔😞😒...
I remember when there was a large spike in acceptance of EBT food stamp cards by various restaurants and it was exciting to watch in wonder who was going to accept EBT cards next!! When you think about it, the possibilities are endless! Although we now we have some pretty good choices, it seems like the widespread growing acceptance of EBT cards by food chains has come to a screeching halt; and in all honesty, when you look at the immense possibilities and the bigger picture, the truth is, very few restaurants accept EBT cards! They're spread all over and very far apart. (We definitely need more!) + its another way/avenue restaurants can receive more money than they've already been getting by accepting an alternate way of being paid; and in this situation, all money is good money, as well as the more the merrier!
The only bad thing is, for some reason, their EBT system is usually often down! 😞 I don't know what causes this, or why this is, but it's so upsetting to drive across town just to get there and run into a sign that says "EBT not working"! What a waste of gas and time!
I've also noticed that food chains that accept EBT tend to treat people who are in possession of one a little different and less than their average customers! (?) I've never understood that!
I've been to this location hundreds of times and can't really remember too many bad experiences that's noteworthy. I feel they treat us pretty fair. Also, this location has a lot of hard customers, and I have to say, as employees, they deal with that pretty well! They keep it clean and stay professional. Out of all the Burger King's that accept EBT, this is one of the best ones!
It looks like it's been through some rough times though! Just needs a little remodeling.

text:
Located on the corner of Newland and Westminster. Even has a drive-thru and walk up window. The double glass door is locked and indoor seating is closed due to the pandemic.

Drive-thru line was long so we parked to order at the walk up window. The menu is taped to the window.

We got four different banh mi’s.
1. Dac biet (The Classic) $4.99
2. Xiu Mai (Meatball) $4.39
3. Thit Nguoi (pork belly) $4.39
4. Heo quay (crispy skin pork) $6.49

It’s on a baguette and I prefer French bread over baguette because it tends to get hard. Well, no need to worry because their baguette is very soft with a slight crunch. It’s also a 12inch baguette where you get the two ends not like a middle piece of the yard long baguette. I could only eat half because it’s massive.

The fillings inside are very generous with meat to veggies ratio. The price is average for the quality. The sauce is different than traditional banh mi. It’s not the Mayo but like a creamier texture mixed with the pate and I taste a bit of soy sauce. Very good.

The crispy skin pork is super crispy and had a lot of meat pieces. The xiu mai was no a typical round meat ball but like in a shape of a hot dog. It’s not saucey like how I prefer it but it had a lot of bold flavor.

I love that each banh mi is carefully wrapped and labeled with a sticker.

Overall, I would return here for future banh mi craving. They also serve spring rolls, egg rolls, drinks, fried rice, noodles like bun rieu.

name: Marty West
text:
I've been dining at the Korea House BBQ Buffet for at least 30 years.  I was introduced to it by Korean American friends who lived very nearby. It is my go to place for out-of-town guests who can't find Korean food at home.  I prefer buffet style for Korean bbq for the variety it allows although I mostly eat kalbi.  The service is always courteous and some of the staff I remember from decades ago (and they recognize me).  There are a dozen or so different proteins from land and sea to choose from, many marinated.  An ample, very fresh, Western salad bar is flanked by typical Korean pickled/marinated veggies: kimchi, namul (spinach & bean sprouts), daikon and lettuce for wrapping meat the traditional way.  In addition there's fried rice, and some tempura style vegetables: onions, pumpkin, carrots and etc. Of course there are numerous condiments, and on request, white rice and ice cream.

I would have given it 5 stars but over the years the selection & quality have diminished a bit, probably to keep prices down.  In the past there were raw oysters for grilling, raw salmon sushi, and the chap chae had a little meat, shiitake mushroom slivers and more vegetables in general.

text: I have to preface this with the fact that there are very few Bolivian restaurants in Southern California. So an extra star was added off the top for that reason. Now when it comes to the food, I would say it was just ok. It was tasty and flavorful, but not very authentic. I've been to Bolivia many times and I also have made it a point to try any Bolivian restaurant I can find, so I have a pretty good idea of what I'm talking about when it comes to the food. I've been here many times as well and the quality of the food varies. Today the silpancho and the falso conejo were good, but not great. The rice was not the typical Bolivian rice I'm use to, instead it was regular white rice. The saltena was good but small, easily the best part of my meal though. The service was fairly prompt and the restaurant has a nice Bolivian decor and ambiance. The restroom could use a little more attention...but that's not something to skip this place over.  Overall, I would recommend this place if you want Bolivian food (mostly due to the lack of other options). The one server was nice and the restaurant is pretty clean.

name: Wayne Christensen
text:
To me, the key to making a judgement about the essence of a restaurant, by extension, whether it’s worth a visit (in person, by takeout, or delivered) with high expectations, is what percent of the dishes you order are exceptional. Are the presentations eye popping? The flavors delightful. The textures sublime. The temperatures just right. Your day-after recollections of the entire meal deeply pleasant. If all the dishes you tried—every one of them!—measured up, you’ve discovered a gold mine. The restaurant becomes one of your absolute favs. Just half the dishes pass these tests and you’ll no doubt return again and again. Maybe one dish amazes enough to bring you back when the spirit moves you.

This is, far and away, the best East Bay restaurant I’ve enjoyed in many years and in many dining out adventures here. Among its honor-worthy, carefully crafted worth-a-visit delights are lamb shanks with scrumptious polenta, headily flavored beef short ribs with baby carrots and unctuous mashed potatoes, and a dense caramel-and-pistachio-bedecked chocolate cake.

text:
Giardino's is a quaint little place in Lemon Grove and provides another option to Lido's restaurant. You would pass this restaurant if you didn't know it was there because it can be a hard to see the location and an even harder place to park. There is additional parking in the back of the restaurant but, honestly, not much. The restaurant itself is small but cozy. It has a nice relaxing ambiance with writings on the wall that help build the atmosphere.
The food here is classic Italian and very delicious. My girlfriend and I have been here twice once for brunch and just the other night for dinner. She had the eggplant parmesan, and I had the Americana pizza with bruschetta as an appetizer and truffle fries for a side. Both helpings were huge and filling, and she had plenty of leftover spaghetti the next day. The Americana pizza came with sausage, pepperoni, salami, bacon, red onion, bell pepper, and mozzarella and parmesan. It is then all baked inside of a brick oven. The bruschetta was flavorful and very delicious. The truffle fries were delicious. They were traditional home fries flavored and fried to perfection.
The pricing of the food is very reasonable. For both of our dishes, we only paid $43, and this did not include wine or beer. Which they do have a selection of but it is not the largest I have seen in the past.
The brunch we had was also very well done. My girlfriend had a veggie omelet and I had the meat lovers omelet. Both were flavorful and delicious.
I would recommend this place for brunch or dinner.

text:
I never thought to go to Eagle Rock for amazing French food, but after a recommendation from another yelper James S., I had to check this place out. I brought my dad and brother for a belated family birthday celebration for both my brother and I. I must say that I'm definitely a fan and will be back again in the near future to Cafe Beaujolais.

There are plenty of street parking even on a Saturday night. They don't have valet parking. I tried to call ahead for a reservation and learned that they don't do reservations on Fridays and Saturdays. I arrived at 6:45pm and was told that the wait would be 20 minutes. We were seated 2 minutes later.

All the staff speak French to each other...a great sign that you're getting seriously authentic food. The place is small and dimly lit. It's definitely not quiet though. There were a lot of hearty conversations going on. Patrons take a long time to dine the traditional French style so don't come here if you are in a hurry.

They have this 3 Monts beer directly imported from France. It's seriously good beer. My dad and brother went through 2 large bottles and my dad even took a picture of it so he can remember to order it in the future. Their entire wine list consist of French wines. Most selections are reasonably priced at less than $10 a glass. They do charge a $15 corkage fee if you bring your own. I had the Bordeaux Merlot and loved it.

My dad had the French onion soup and really enjoyed it. It was extremely cheesy. We also shared an order of escargot. It was delicious and only $9. The garlic, butter, and herb mixture that they have with the escargot is great for dipping your bread in.

For entrees, we had the Maitre D'Hotel steak (basically steak and fries), seafood pasta, and the lamb chops. The lamb chops was highly recommended by the waiter and by far my favorite entree out of the three. The seafood pasta was also delicious. The steak and fries were pretty good and the portion was huge. All entrees including steaks are under $25.

They have about 6 types of French desserts at a little under $7 each. We didn't get too adventurous and had the creme brulee. It was delicious and a great way to end the meal. I will try the Profiteroles or the Tarte Tartin next time.

text:
So..the bad with this one goes back years. Used to come on my lunch when I worked evenings, had a friend that would give me discounts, till one of her food prep coworkers caught on (and was pretty obvious with his reaction) and from then on I always got scraps and fat instead of good cuts....so I swore off for a few years.

More recently, the other location has been slipping, so tried coming back here. Both times have been during the takeout only covid times. Both times I ordered online, but ended up having to wait through the line of indecisive people that didn't order ahead, both times my order wasn't actually put together till I was there.  This time, they were helping the deliver app pickups and other online orders that just decided to skip the line and cut to the front. Ended up waiting extra because by the time they prepped my order, they'd run out of some of the sides I ordered. Checked my email and they'd marked my order as ready 15 minutes after I ordered; I arrived within a couple minutes of the predicted ready time when I ordered (~30 mins), and basically spent another 30 waiting. Actual pickup time was over an hour from when I ordered.

On the good side (and why it's 2 stars and not 1) is that the food was good, and the order was 100% correct.

Everything else about the experience says I wasted my time ordering online and should just order in person, since that way I won't go in with any expectation of it being ready and probably wait about the same, if i come to this location again. Might have to give the other one another try, or write them off entirely.

Second. We were told there was a section we could sit while we waited to be seated. I sat in the section which might I add had no sign saying not to sit due to social distancing which I’m all for. Someone came up to me and told me I can’t sit there and need to move. Ok. So I got up and moved. But still. For one person to say u can sit there and another to say move. Clearly there’s lack f communication and the customer feels it. I love eating out and I love this place so I tried to put it past me. But the one thing that got me was the servers lack of attention to us. I made sure to watch and sure enough our waiter passed us multiple times while attending other customers next to us. Finally. I spent more time waiting on the bill than I did waiting to be seated. It took about 20 minutes for our waiter to be advised we were ready for our check before he came back with it. Now I’m not one to complain or write reviews but today’s service was just terrible. And it hurts to say because I used to love this place.

WHAT DID I HAVE:  I had the miso ramen with corn, eggs, and pork.  I had them make my ramen spice level 'impact' or '3,' which I guess was supposed to be pretty spicy.  I also had the shumai dumplings.

HOW WAS IT:  The ramen was mediocre.  The broth was not spicy at all, and they are really stingy with how much stuff they put in your ramen.  My ramen was like....90% broth, and then like 5% noodles and 5% other stuff (corn, mushrooms, pork, etc.).  Seriously, it was basically just a big bowl of soup with a little bit of actual noodles and toppings.

The dumplings tasted like they were frozen/pre-made.

HOW MUCH WAS IT:  With tip and everything, it was like $28.  I tipped pretty generously because my waitress was friendly.  But the manager guy (or at least I think he was the manager) was really unfriendly.  He has like a permanent scowl on his face and he looks like he just hates his job and his customers.  Why is he doing this job if he hates it so much?  I have no idea.

WOULD I COME BACK/RECOMMEND THIS PLACE:  No and no.  The food is really mediocre and some of the servers are cool, but the manager is not.  I've been to many other ramen places in LA, and NONE of them have been worth the money.  They've all be mediocre or just flat out bad.

At this point, I'm convinced that LA has NO good ramen places at all.  If you live in LA or you're visiting, making your own instant ramen at home and adding some of your own toppings you get from the grocery store would be a much better deal/experience than going to a ramen restaurant.

If you're looking for noodles in hot soup, you're probably going to have a better experience at a pho place.  LA has lots of good pho restaurants.

name: Kimberly R. Kelly
text: As a native Texan, Home State tugs at the heartstrings. They very deservedly won best flour tortilla in Southern California from the KCRW Masa Madness competition, For which they probably displayed a plaque at the store entrance. For my money and taste buds, their breakfast tacos with or without eggs beat out their anytime tacos. The Guadalupe (chorizo, eggs, and cheese) reminds me so much of the spicy delicacies found at little taco carts in Austin. Home State's breakfast tacos are well balanced, wrapped in perfectly fluffy flour tortillas, and a nice portion. Their queso approximates authentic Texas queso, but I find it a little runny compared to the thick, creamy (admittedly derived from processed cheese) staple of east and central Texas. The charro beans Cowboy Cup is EVERYTHING. I was really impressed with all of the textures and flavors achieved, but not muddled, by topping beans with pickled onions, guacamole, jalapeños, and pico. Don't skip on the frozen margarita for an even more authentic experience. Seating is pretty limited, as you might be relegated to the patio on a breezy cool day.

text:
I had the most perfect birthday celebration here!

This review is for the Navio weekend brunch. I was here last Sunday on the exact day of my birthday and Sam, our wonderful server took care of me and my husband (Simon). We were here to celebrate my birthday as newlyweds and the experience was perfect from start to finish. The ambiance, food, service were all excellent.

Upon entering the Ritz Carlton in Half Moon Bay, the valet fee (weekend rate) to pass the gate was $45 and you can pay this with your restaurant tab. We were seated within minutes after checking and sat at a table facing a large window, staring into the beautiful view of the beach as we watched the waves crash back and forth. It was so relaxing and we were offered complimentary mimosas before the feast began.

Lunch was $199 per person for 2 hours and it's basically all you can eat, where we selected from a list of 20 dishes with a curated mix of land and sea options. Each person was able to order 2 dishes at a time, and Sam would periodically check in on us to take our subsequent orders.

As I scanned the menu, I love how there were more seafood options, which felt very appropriate for the location. I was very strategic about how we were going to tackle this menu. I wanted to try every item if possible and started with the most expensive dishes in case I got too full. We ordered 4 unique dishes at a time and worked our way down the menu from top to bottom. Once we reached the end of the menu, we double backed to our most favorite dishes. We ordered 17 out of 20 dished on the menu. If you have the stomach to try all 20 dishes, good for you!! Definitely come hungry or you'll have FOMO.

THE MENU: 2-hour luxury brunch experience

The very popular Döner Kebab from Berlin has also found its place in Los Angeles, where Berlin, located near the Beverly Hills, offers this specialty to its customers.

name: Roy Chi
text:
Burger Bar is a burger restaurant from a gourmet chef (Hubert Keller) at gourmet prices (~$20 a burger) that serves painfully-mediocre food.

On the list of well-known, superstar chefs, Hubert Keller has always been the one that I always scratch my head about -- I thought Fleur de Lys was all presentation with mediocre taste. But a burger joint shouldn't be too difficult for a renowned, experienced chef, right? Maybe for Keller it is.

The Le "Frog" Burger, with brie cheese, shaved asparagus, sprouts, and garlic aioli, was just okay. The flavors weren't very strong, so it didn't have anything special going for it. The thick meat patty wasn't cooked enough for a "medium," so it was just an unseasoned, mushy burger. I've also had the Hubert Keller burger, which I had at a "medium," but was strangely too well-done, so it was just an unseasoned, dry burger.

The one redeeming factor? Burger Bar has some pretty killer fries. Both the regular and sweet potato fries were delicious -- perfectly crispy. The view of Union Square is also a good reason to come up for a drink or two.

As for the main star of the show, Burger Bar's burgers just aren't good enough for the outlandish prices. In fact, if you just walk a few blocks down, you'll hit Pearl's Burgers, which has burgers that are phenomenally better at 1/3 of the price.

There are so many delicious burgers in SF that Burger Bar should only be considered if: (1) you're shopping at Macy's and your lazy ass is too hungry and tired to leave the Macy's building, or (2) you are a tourist who doesn't know any better.

text:
This is It!

The MOST authentic Mexico-style Street tacos in 'West' L.A.!  Period!

This is a truck literally parked on the steet, a taco cart and only 3 guys who operate this well oiled machine:

One guy warms up the little tortillas and assembles the meat into the tacos.

Another guy slaps fresh, thin sirloin steak filet cuts, real cabeza, buche, lengua, carnitas, chicken and 'al pastor' trompo meat onto this Mongolian style grill/deep fryer of sorts, filled with (you can only imagine) a mixture of the juices, greases, fats, oils, and 'au jus' from all the cuts of meat, into which, these guys (who offer the lucky taco treasure hunters a unique experience), drop, sink and drench both the tortillas and the meats! (secret's in the sauce)

Last but not least the 3rd guy puts together the relishes, free cucumbers,  radishes, lime wedges & assortment of salsas, plus collects the money and serves the soft drinks!

Be prepared: this is no fancy place but it is the realest, most 'Púro Mèxico' taco stand I have found in L.A. so far.

I highly recommend it!
You're going to love it!

I love coconut but Chemango is my favorite. It's a combination of mango, chemoy (which has tamarind and some other things mixed in), and chili. It's sweet, sour and spicy. Raspado Xpress makes seriously delicious Chemango.

Although you can buy much cheaper Raspados from a questionable cart in a park, getting it from Raspado Xpress is better. They have a wider variety of flavor and is much cleaner. It is pretty pricey though at $6 each. The size of the Raspados here are really big.

- Damn, it's like everything I dream of when I think of a cheeseburger. The meat was juicy, the egg yolk was runny, and the guacamole gave it a delicious kick. It's a messy ass burger, but every bite was delicious. It's not a perfect burger (the bun could be more sturdy), but it's a delicious one nonetheless.

(Note: Do NOT get the Tillamook cheddar substitute with your burger -- it's not sharp enough to give it the cheesy flavor you need to make it pop.)

Cali Steak Zapatos =
- This is like a Taco Bell grilled stuffed burrito, but with real ingredients (as opposed to whatever it is they put into Taco Bell burritos). It's delicious.

Fried Chicken Sandwich =
- Moist chicken, well-fried. The only thing is that the bun was a bit too thick and tasteless, so it was too much fluff that overpowered the chicken. I doused this puppy with some good old Crystals Louisiana Hot Sauce and it was glorious, though.

----------------
I've been here a number of times and each time it gets better and better. Wash everything down with an ice cold Idiot IPA and you're good to go.

text:
I came to Sushi Gen for their lunch sashimi platter for my sister's birthday. It was supposed to be a great deal at $15 during lunch. The wait for a table was insane and we both had plans after lunch so we opted to sit at the sushi bar. I did end up paying more but I don't regret it at all.

When you sit at the bar, everything is a la carte and you have to order a minimum of 4 items per person. We didn't have any problems going over that minimum that's for sure. You also are not able to order the lunch special menu.

Our sushi chef was friendly. They give you a paper menu but you don't mark anything. You just go ahead and tell the chef what you and he is the one that keeps track of it.

We had all the expensive stuff including toro, hamachi toro, amaebi, and uni along with the regular items like salmon, albacore, and yellowtail. There was no price listed so I thought I was going to get slammed with a huge bill but I paid $95 for 2 including tax and tip. It was a much cheaper than I thought it was going to be.

The fish is very fresh. I would say it's one of the best sushi I've had in a while. My sister can be a little picky about sushi as she is also a big foodie but even she was impressed. We definitely want to come back again soon.

Their parking lot can be kind of a nightmare. You can try to find street parking. The restaurant will validate so that you only pay $2 for the lot but be aware that the lot does fill up during busy times.

text:
*3.5 stars*

If you're in the mood to drink a ton of German beer with some of your buddies, Suppenküche damn near guarantees a great time. It feels like you're at home, just hanging out and kicking back more beer than is good for you. The star of the show is the Das Boot, a huge 2+ liter glass boot that is guaranteed to induce speech impediments and balancing issues. As a German beerhouse with a great selection of German beers, Suppenküche is as good as it gets in SF.

As a restaurant, however, the food just isn't that great. I mean, you'll get tons of deep-fried, sausagy, starchy goodness, but overall it's just average German food.

-----------------------
FOOD:

Braised Beef w/ Cranberries & Red Cabbage = This was just average. The braised beef was decently-tender, but tasted a bit like canned beef stew. The gravy was bland and unexciting.

Appetizer Plate w/ Blood Sausage & Head Cheese = This tasted like your run-of-the-mill deli meats and offal that you find inside those pre-packaged deli platters at Safeway. It was okay, but nothing special.

Spaetzle = The spaetzle here is too dry and too overcooked.

-----------------------

Suppenküche is definitely a must if you're looking for a fun German bierhaus. The beer is the main star of this venue; the food is the lackluster supporting cast.

And the country potatoes that came with it looked boiled and pale unlike before they were crunchy and brown and before it had fresh peppers and onions too.

4. Smoking was allowed which is still banned due to covid in most casinos.

Naan was good - crispy in places but also a bit pita dough tasting and thick in others.
Mint/cilantro sauce was the watery type and very Spicey but it was still good. They forgot to put it in my to go bag. I’m glad I double check things before I left.
Rice was ok...no cardamom pods, and cooked acceptably well but not amazing.
No one answers the phone...at all. It’s literally there just for show. They should put a message on their voicemail at the very least to refer people online.

Chicken TiKa Masala was amazing though. Holy heck. I’m going back tonight.
Prices are pretty reasonable too. Love this place! I’ve found my spot

text:
Short version: the food was alright but overpriced, the (supposedly) owner made fun of us without being in the position to do so.

Long version: We found ourself quite late in the Big Sur area, as this was the only option for dining past 9 p.m. we decided to stop. We ordered our food with the awareness It was gonna be overpriced, but without any problem about this (even if three soggy Ambrosia burger and a beetroot salad weren't worth the price). However, the fact that the owner made fun on us in a mean way, and only because we didn't accepted to sleep in a lodge owned by a friend of his for $399 dollars per night for 4 people (his comment was that this amount should have been representative of how we valued our time).
When we told him that we already made a reservation for that night he warned us with a "pay attention to the road at night" laughing with the waiters and left making pointless sarcastic comments for the rest of the night.

It's obvious that this place lives in a bubble that survives only because there are no alternatives, and hopefully you will keep living in this bubble because outside you wouldn't survive a day. In our (extremely) long and diversified road trip this was the only place that was able to upset and disappoint us.

So, greatings from King City from those customers that value their time, enjoy diving, but despise arrogance.

text:
We went to celebrate my husband's birthday. Spent $142 (including tips, taxes, etc.). We arrived at 7 pm and left at 10 pm - had a 4 course dinner. My husband did "The big Night Out" and I selected "Pork and Poultry" (on the bottom of the page)

Thistle cocktail - good flavour, but low concentration of alcohol (for my taste) - 4 stars.

Cheese fondue (the one with bacon) - excellent. Best part of our dinner - 5 stars.

Salad (with Gorgonzola cheese) - okay. Exactly what you would expect - 4-5 stars.

Meat - The Duck is The Meat here. Not what you would normally expect. Better than filet mignon, falls apart in your mouth while full of flavour. I was surprised. Every other meat - good, tasty, usual. Overall - 5 stars.

Desert - this is where all was lost after I saw a nice and hairy mold growing on the bottom of the little container with strawberry. To make things more interesting I saw it after I ate a piece of strawberry. Fingers crossed. Of course, they brought us a new plate, but that didn't make me "unsee" what I saw.
However, other than this unpleasant event, the desert was not worthy (we selected the one with dulce de leche). The reason for that is because the bites they give you to dip into chocolate are sweet by themselves and when combined with sweet chocolate a sickening over-sweet combination is created. The only piece of desert I liked was pineapple. Maybe we should have selected a different chocolate. Overall for desert - 2 stars.

Overall we enjoyed our dinner and would return in the future.

What hasn't been said about this establishment? It is the One Stop Shop for everything delicious and carby.

From the amazing coffee, perfect pastries, decadent cakes, to the perfect savory sandwiches and dishes, this place is a dream come true. Not only that, it is extremely affordable. We're talking a sandwich, a coffee, and a cookie/pastry for $10, give or take.

Some of my favorite pastries that are also their popular items: guava roll, cheese roll, guava & cheese strudel, dulce de leche kiss, peanut butter cookie (with actual chunks of peanuts), meat pie, empanadas, and dulce leche Napoleon. They are also known for their potato balls, but this item is not my favorite.

This place gets packed during the holidays but is pretty decent in terms of waiting time during lunch on the weekdays. It is a huge space with ample seeding indoors and limited seating Outdoors.

Parking is also very cheap and available everywhere. They have a parking lot in the back for $1/hour.

text:
Tacos & Beer is a staple of the local community of Beaumont. Here you can find great Mexican food and a laid back family atmosphere. The food is delicious and the prices are very fair. The staff is courteous and the restaurant in general is kept very clean.

The menu has something for everyone, from meat eaters to vegetarians. Tacos, burritos, sopes, enchiladas, chilaquiles, cocktail de cameron etc. You can find many great specials through the week offering a variety of tastes and experiences. Taco Tuesday... Check. Thursday night is a great time to visit for dinner as there is a live Mariachi band singing and entertaining the entire restaurant. Friday beer specials are sure to get the weekend off to a good start.

The restaurant is CASH ONLY... however, the owners do provide a surcharge free ATM in the entry way. Although the restaurant does not charge a fee to use the ATM, your bank may... Keep in mind, this is not up to the owners but YOUR bank.

Overall, Tacos & Beer is a gem in the city of Beaumont that almost all can find agreeable with quality food and fair prices.

text:
I really want to give Colori Kitchen at least a 4 star rating but my entree was so disappointing that I just can't. I will be back again eventually though so hopefully I enjoy my food more on my next visit.

First of all, I love the BYOB with no corkage fee. The service was great. I love their bread and also most of the dishes we had, including the mushroom risotto and the lasagna. I especially loved the salad that was on their specials menu. I could eat 5 plates of that salad and be happy.

It all goes wrong with my Linguine alla Vongole or Linguini with Clams came out. The dish was crazy salty to the point where I could barely eat it. I ended up splitting the dishes around the table with the rest of the table and stole my boyfriend's mushroom risotto. Several of the clams had a lot of sand in them too so I was unpleasantly surprised after chewing into them.

Parking is tough since it's DTLA. You may get lucky and find street parking. Otherwise, I would just suck it up and pay $5+ to park at one of the downtown lots.

I do wish they had some better sauce like at Manna or Jeong Won, but the one provided wasn't bad. (EDIT: The ponzu sauce they use now is DELICIOUS!) Also had to ask for a side of white rice, surprised they didnt really provide that without asking. I guess it's ok since not everyone eats it. My only true complaint is that they don't have refills for your drink, if you ordered soda you get a can and that's it. No fountain drinks! Despite all of the above, service is great, meat was delicious, and I think at 20$ all you can eat, it was a bargain.

Update: I've easily redeemed 2 punch cards, and I just love coming here; my 5 star review stands, though I've amended that the ponzu sauce they use now is perfect. I would like to add as a nitpick that the tongue and beef belly in particular can sometimes be the absolute best, and others I will stay away from the rest of my visit because they are tough and chewy, particularly saddening as they are my favorite cuts to order.

Again, at 20 - 25 all you can eat, it's still a damn amazing deal, and I will continue coming here often.

text:
We live in a face- paced world where we even have drive- thru for banks and dry cleaners. Needless to say, I find apps that are designed to expedite ones life, such as Postmate and Instacart, very handy. I'm perpetually in a hurry and I find myself relying on these apps as they allow me to keep track of the order process in real time.

I placed the order on Postmate at 3:41pm and it showed the estimated time of delivery at 3:51pm, which is very acceptable. I checked to make sure that the app showed that Anny's confirmed the order before I even left the house. I arrived at 4pm - just to give them a few extra minutes - and walked up to the counter.

There were two young workers at the register: a guy who seemed to be in his late teens and a girl with red and black hair. They were talking animatedly and it was a few moments before they even acknowledged me (actually, the guy had to motion towards me with his eyes before the girl even looked my direction). I advised her that I was there to pickup an order, but she seems completely baffled. I tell her helpfully that it's via Postmate. She says, "Ohhh..." and checks a different screen and JUST THEN prints out the order. She then proceeds to lie to me and tell me that it'll just be a few minutes as she sticks the order on the rail.

I try my best to hide my frustration as time slowly passes. There is absolutely no sense of urgency with any of the staff. They take their time, they joke, they laugh, and I seethe.

It's 4:13pm by the time I receive my order; a full 22 minutes later than I was promised. What really upset me enough to write a review is that there was never an apology or even an update until I asked.

Thanks to the staff's laziness and not checking for incoming orders as well as the kitchen staff's inability to expedite an already- late order, I arrived at work full six minutes late, which has never happened before.

As for the food, it's good. Anny's always had good burgers and I like their Buffalo Chicken burger (which reminds me of Zaxby's) and the perfectly seasoned waffle fries.

However, good service at a restaurant is so very important to many people. I mean, how else can you explain Applebee's and Hooter's staying in business with their subpar cuisine?

Needless to say, I won't be returning to this one.

text:
There is a reason this restaurant has been open for a hundred years. We had a magnificent experience here for my birthday.  I ordered the New York Strip, perfectly cooked.  Potatoes au gratin (excellent) and a vieux carré.  The cocktails here are dynamite and served with a side of more cocktail in a small ice bucket.  Its kind of two drinks for the price of one.

On to dessert.  They were all great but they gave me a little brownie with ice cream and a candle which was my favorite.  The brownie was molten chocolate gooey paradise topped with smooth and rich vanilla ice cream.

If you look at my reviews you'll notice I gave a LOT of five stars.  Partially because I have champagne taste, but also because giving a low score for something unless it is terrible strikes me as whiny.  I'd rather not review a place than rip it a new one for having a dish that was good but not great.

That said, if I could give Musso and Frank six stars I would.  Old style hollywood charm that stands the test of time.
