text: I've had a mix of service there but overall, its a pretty casual place with fresh food and friendly service. I've tried the rotisserie chicken with french fries and grilled veggies, carne asada plate with house salad, tacos, churros, and agua frescas. And of course they have a salsa bar with green tomatillo salsa, pico de gallo, onions, cilantro and radishes. Their rotisserie chicken was tender and not very seasoned but the salsa took care of that. This order was to-go so my french fries were soggy since they came in a plastic container full of condensation (which probably is a good sign since that means the fries were hot and probably fresh out of the fryer when they were put into the container). The grilled veggies turned out to be julienned zucchini, yellow squash, and bell peppers. The carne asada was pretty flavorful, but mostly average. The house salad consisted of chunks of cucumber and tomatoes on a bed of chopped romaine lettuce with sliced red onions. I tried their tacos on a Tuesday and the cashier informed me that they have a Taco Tuesday deal $5 for 3 tacos (chicken, pork, or beef). I have tried the lengua, carne asada, carnitas and al pastor. They were all pretty average, except the carnitas wasn't as pull-apart tender and was rather dry for me. It also came with chips and sometimes a little chopped up lettuce and tomato. I often find that this place has problems with consistency--service wise and food wise. Sometimes they leave off the chips, sometimes they leave off the lettuce and tomato. The churros were filled with cream and still warm when I got them. I tried their agua frescas and the lemonade one was quite good. The waiters/waitresses were friendly and attentive, considering it's a "order at the counter and your food will be brought to you" place. The cashier that I picked up my order from was detailed-oriented enough to pick out the staples on the handle of the plastic bag (they stapled the receipt to the bag) so I wouldn't stab myself. They have a couple parking spots and there's meter spots in front.

The best part of the meal was the meatballs. The meatballs were tender and moist and the marinara sauce was quite amazing. We also ordered a salad to share but that did not arrive until after our entrees. That was really horrible.

For the main dishes, we had the lobster ravioli and the clam linguini. They brought out the clam linguini with red sauce even though we had asked for the white wine sauce. We had to send it back and wait for some time before the new one arrived. It was a good thing that we shared our dishes because otherwise, the ravioli would have gone cold.

The flavors of the entrees were good but the linguini was overly salted. I actually think the meatballs could have used less salt as well.

I heard their pizza is really good but didn't get a chance to try it yet. I may come back again next time to try the pizza and enjoy the meatballs.

text:
Amazing Chinese fusion restaraunt on the border of Mountain View and Palo Alto! This place had everything!

My favorite part of the place was the ambiance! It has a nice mix of indoor and outdoor seating! And the setup was very attractive. It looks much larger inside than it does outside!

We went there for the happy hour! Pro tip: If you want to enjoy the happy hour you have to sit in the exterior part of the restaraunt. Everything was fairly priced! We got one of everything from the Happy Hour menu!

My light and fresh personal favorites were the Peking Duck Roll and the Spicy Tuna Cucumber Bites

My heavy flavorful favorites were the Pork Belly Quesadilla, Kimchi Kalbi Fries, and most importantly the San Tung Chicken Wings!

We paired all this with the red sangria which was amazing, and served in an interesting tall skinny pitcher!

We topped off the meal with an amazing toffee lava cake and a waffle! Both of which were amazing!

I'm definitely coming back here to enjoy both the atmosphere and the amazing meal!

Only downside is that parking can be difficult, there are two spots in the front and limited parking in the back of the restaraunt. Other than that, this is one of the hidden gems of Palo Alto!

text:
My wife and I were looking for a new beach to explore and happened upon Tomales deli + cafe. It was mostly a bathroom break by plan. Though, there wasn't much for food along the way to where we were going so we started looking at the menu.

This deli has Mexican flare in its colorful decor and menu. Out of sheer curiosity I ordered the Carnitas sandwich. I rarely order this at taquerias but I wondered what a pit stop carnitas fare would be like. It's my kind of  combination of adventurous and reckless.

The pay off was substantial. Not only was the meat flavorful, but the bread and salsa held their own too. We wished we had ordered something else, but we were miles out by then. This is the kind of food I'd expect in SoCal's trending alternative takes on Mexican.

It has a mom and pop charm with a friendly staff. Have an open mind and try something new. Chances are it will pay off for you too.

text:
You know, I'm beginning to not like McDonalds more and more these days. Have not had very good experiences w them lately.
1st off. I was at the hospital ALL day. I had 2 appts. & some testing I needed to have done. I am not saying this for anything other than to explain my physical shape. I am handicapped and walk w a cane, but have severe back issues that render me unable to stand upright. I'm not that old but I m extremely exhausted by the end of the day if I have to get around by myself. So, after everything was finished I found a nearby McDonalds, ordered online, picked it up, parked in their designated parking lot, ate, and unfortunately, fell asleep. I was tired.
I was awoken by the tapping of the glass by some teenager manager who stated that if I do not move off the premises w/in 15 minutes, he will call the police and have me towed for loitering on the property.
I have never been to this or any other McDonald's in months. I fell asleep because I ate and was exhausted. I ecplained to him what happened, showed him my handicapped plaquard that was clearly hanging, explained to him, apologized to him profusely,  and he then gave me 10 minutes to leave or he would call for a tow truck and the police. He wasn't anymore than 18 I don't think.
I did not intend to fall asleep. I was not loitering, littering, making noise, or causing any problems.
I think he was throwing his newfound managerial weight around to look good. To please someone. I am old enough to be his grandmother for sure. I've worked w the oublic. You do not treat your customers like that. It wasn't crowded when I was there nor was it when he woke me up.

text:
We normally go to the other competitor but Paradise has an advantage because they offer outdoor dining while other dim sum places are take out only.

We got here 10 minutes before they opened at 11. So the dining area was not yet completed with decorations to make it look more inviting.

I love that the tables were lined with paper and disposed of after. Each table is a square shape but can extend to become round and seat more. The first cart that came were the basic items that you normally see such as har gow, shu mai, and chicken feet. They were steaming hot.

I asked for the flat rice noodles stuffed with bbq but she said not yet and only had shrimp in this second cart along with baked bbq buns. So we got the shrimp. Then the next cart of egg tarts, bean curd, and steamed bbq bun came. We got bbq bun and egg tart.

Overall the food was mediocre. The chicken feet must have been steamed for an infinite amount of time because it fell off the bone so easily that it was weird! The har gow was decent, good ratio of shrimp and it didn't have a fishy smell. It also didn't detached from the shell so easily. My favorite was the shrimp flat rice noodle. It's a whole shrimp but beaten where it's flat and clumped together. The rice sheet wasn't as thin as I'm used too.

The servers wore masks and gloves. They refilled my water without touching my cup, which is how I think it should be for less contact. What I didn't appreciate and it's common at Asian restaurants, is that they can't seem to be patient and wait until you leave to clear out the damn plates! They weren't even seated to capacity. We're in a middle of a pandemic and I would sure feel more comfortable of they kept their distance until customers are gone. Here I am, unmasked and putting left overs in a box, then I have a presence on the side of my shoulder reaching over to grab plates and asking if I was done? How rude.

We ordered salted fish fried rice the next morning as take out. It was a Saturday morning and boy they were busy! Indoor dining was open and they had more carts offered.

text:
If your idea of a party is the 6am crowd at IHOP, you'll feel right at home at Keungama. I walked in on a Friday night with my Korean friend who suggested the place and other than a table of 3 Chinese girl, we were the youngest people in the room. I would go to say that at least 70% of the patrons are currently receiving social security checks and the rest are mostly getting there. To top it off, a Korean funeral party came in a little after we sat down and took up over half of the restaurant. They were all eating and watching the Dodgers game but the atmosphere was still fairly grim.

Keungama is known for their soups and stews. If you walk through the back area to the parking lot or the bathroom, you can see the humongous vats that they cook the soups in. Most people either order the Gamjatang, kalbitang, selleongtang, or the jungol.

My friend and I ended up ordering a combo for 2 that's written in Korean. It's actually an amazing deal at $26.99. For that price, we get a big plate of Bossam (lettuce wrap with pork belly and radish kimchi), Gamjatang (spicy pork bone and potato stew), one hot stone rice per person and your choice of either a bottle of soju or makgeolli.

The bossam was pretty good but I didn't like that the pork belly had cartilage left in. It was a pain to pick it out but I guess some people enjoy chewing on the cartilage so they just eat it like that. The soup was also very disappointing. The flavor wasn't very strong and I didn't think that it was spicy enough. The meat was tender but most of the pot is mostly the neck bone.

The service is fairly good. They have a call button, which I love. They also have many large flat screen showing the game.

name: Jennifer Hunker
text:
My new favorite hangout in downtown Covina. :)

WHAT IT IS
The B&B is really a sports bar. Their offerings include the basic sports bar fare (burgers, onion rings, ect), but there are some surprises. True to its name, they have some pasta dishes (with meatballs, of course).

WHAT YOU SHOULD ORDER
Hamburgers and beer.

AMBIANCE
5 stars

Wonderful. When you enter, there will be a chalkboard menu to your left that lists current specials. The bar will be in front of you, and the dining room to your right. We usually sit near the windows.

It's nice and dark and cool inside during the summer, and at night they light little candles on the tables so it has a rustic flair that goes well with the old building it's in. It's open concept so it can get a bit loud inside, and they have live music on the weekends. If you're not a fan of live music they have a pretty decently sized outdoor patio.

FOOD AND DRINKS
4 Stars

The first time we visited, my husband was craving pasta. He ordered their basic spaghetti with marinara and meatballs. I ordered the "Big Poppa", a burger topped with egg, avocado, prosciutto, and garlic aioli. We also ordered a starter, the pictured "carnitas fries"

The fries were a LOT like the super nachos you see at Mexican restaurants, except with fries! Delicious, and way more filling than we were expecting them to be!

The spaghetti was *okay*. I'm Italian and am pretty snippy about my marinara, and this had a bit too much heat for my liking. The meatballs were a bit dry. Not my bag, but then I make my own meatballs from scratch at home, so why would I want to order them from a restaurant?

As for my burger? Ah-maze-ing.

The Big Poppa is complex, but the flavors work. The salty sweetness of the prosciutto goes is wonderfully balanced by the garlicy bite of the aioli and the creamy avocado and the richness of the egg.  Now that I've experienced it, I far prefer prosciutto over bacon for hamburgers. It's less overpowering and lets the patty shine through. My patty was cooked perfectly to medium and was plenty juicy without ruining my bun. My only complaint is that they don't mash the avocado--avocado is so slimy that it has a tend to slide out of the burger as you eat, so this is a messy one! Once the yolk popped I pretty much gave up on being neat, since it was impossible! Absolutely delicious, though.

As my side, I had their seasoned fries, which blow chain restaurants out of the water. I have since had their shoestring fries, garlic fries, and onion rings and they're all winners as well, though I felt the garlic fries were still not quite on the level as the normal seasoned ones.

Ah, but I haven't mentioned drinks! The Brew and Meatball takes FULL advantage of all the wonderful microbreweries we have in the San Gabriel Valley and as of this writing has 16 craft beers on tap. You have your blonds, your IPAs, your darks, and then you have fun things like Phantom Carriage Strawberry Muis or Dogfish Head Punkin Ale. The list  updates all the time, so they cycle new beers in. The last time I was in I had a vanilla cream beer that was out of this world, but it's not on the list for September.

NICE SURPRISES
They have papas rellenas on the menu! They call them "papas balls", but you can't fool me! For the uninitiated, papas rellenas are meat stuffed potato balls that are fried. Your meat and potatoes in one package. :) The grocery store in my hometown (which was a Publix in Deltona Fl) used to carry these alongside their fried chicken and I used to grab one every time we went to the store (and I MISS THEM). The papas at the Meatball aren't quite what I remember (these have sauce, and are much smaller. Also they're filled with chorizo), but it was nice to see them again!

OVERALL
A stellar lunch spot if you stick to the burgers. Granted, we didn't roam their pasta menu much after that initial sitting, but we've since combed over their burger menu and those burgers are just out of this world. Stop going to Chilis and start coming here. Your taste buds will thank you!

name: Kevin Gaines
text:
Great food.  Abysmal service.  They sell sliders and sides.  Huge variety on the burgers...beef in several flavor/spice combinations, chicken, a beef/lamb mashup, turkey.  You have a choice of a few standard burger recipes (western, for example, onion rings, cheese and bbq sauce).  Or you can build your own slider.  Sides include fries that look like potato chips, onion rings, sweet potato fries, and other options.  You can order "half & half" sides, too.  I ordered 2 sliders, a half fries/half onion rings and a regular fountain drink... that set me back $ 13.  Delicious, as I said.  Just don't call it fast food.
It took 20 minutes to get it... then my order was wrong; I received all fries instead of the halIf & half.  When I went back and received "the right" side dish, it was more like an 80/20.... a huge portion of fries, and 5 onion rings sitting on top.  That sucked, because both the fries and onion rings were awesome, with an optional cajun seasoning.

I would have been pissed, but instead was amused watching the shenanigans in the kitchen.  There were a bunch of teens and twenty-somethings working on top of each other.  On the other side of the counter was a young lady pulling the food from the kitchen, checking for accuracy, then shouting customer names.  I'm glad she wasn't shouting at the kitchen staff, but she clearly wanted to, because of having to prod them to hurry. And several orders were returned inaccurate and had to be redone, not just mine.  She was very clearly, but to her credit discreetly, in conflict with the kitchen lead. There was an older gentleman hovering behind the order counter and in the middle of the mess in the kitchen... and did nothing to help, from what I could see. Problem was, you could tell he was in charge because everyone was @ least trying to look busy, except for him.

Like I said, it was funny to watch, but frustrating because they were wasting so much time...my time.  That's what happens when you're new, I guess.  I'll definitely try going again in a few months, after they've had a chance to get their act together.

Something Healthy is a great local alternative to good and affordable eating in the city of Monrovia.

It's conveniently located next to a 24 Hour Fitness and have ample parking in and around their lot.

If you order a 1/2 sandwich, it usually comes with a side salad.

text:
I was really excited to try Night + Market Song because 1) they were really close to my apt and 2) I had learned about their fried chicken sandwich.

I had dinner here with some friends last week and immediately noticed the weird attitude of our bearded male waiter. He lacked enthusiasm and clearly didn't care to help us with the menu when we asked about his recommendations.

Throughout the day, his service was getting worse. Not only did forget to bring a cup of water (clearly a very minor mistake), he never stopped by to ask if we wanted to refill our alcohol, to ask us about our food or if we need anything. We didn't see him stop by until THE VERY END when all of our food was finished.

We actually had to look to see if it was just US he had a problem with or everyone and it was clear his bad service was given to EVERYONE. A waiter with such attitude should not be in customer service.

If I were to come here again, I would request to avoid this particular waiter.

NOW TO THE FOOD: We ordered the FRIED PAPAYA SALAD, which was very yummy. The CRISPY RICE SALAD was TOO SALTY for me and my friend's tastes. The FRIED CHICKEN SANDWICH was OKAY. It was TOO HARD to bite and kind of hard to eat. Thus, making the chicken not very moist or tender. MEH.

text:
Range is a great example of San Francisco cuisine -- not the best -- but definitely good. The dishes are fresh and delicious, with a (slightly) creative twist on your everyday boring flavors. It wasn't wildly inventive and nothing really blew my mind, but it was all fresh and well-made.

-------------------
FOOD:

Roasted Chicken =
- The dish that everyone talks about does not disappoint. It's your everyday roasted chicken, but incredibly moist and tender. It wasn't that exciting, but it did make me nod my head and mutter: "hmm... that is pretty damn good."

Cauliflower Soup =
- Well seasoned, but nothing incredible. It was just a good bowl of pureed cauliflower soup.

Seared Yellowtail w/ Uni Broth =
- The yellowtail could have been a bit less seared to bring out the fresh hamachi flavor, but it did pair pretty nicely with the uni broth.

Pea & Mushroom Corn Cakes =
- These were actually surprisingly flavorful. Nicely crisped with a good texture.

Chesapeake Bay Soft Shell Crab =
- Crispy and delicious.

Poppyseed Strawberry Shortcake =
- The poppyseed flavors definitely shine in this dessert, which was great. It wasn't overly sweet and had a nice fluffiness to the shortcake.

--------------------

I'm a bit torn with Range because it was like having boring food, but really good boring food. Nothing was really that exciting, but it was delicious nonetheless. Unfortunately their coffee-rubbed pork shoulder wasn't on the menu that night, so I may have to come back and try that before I really call it "boring".

The beansprouts were crispy on the outside like they'd been tanned on a tropical beach all day but firm on the inside. They had a little kick that was just right. The Crab cakes tasted like they used fresh crabs and the tarter sauce that came with it was a little spicy too which was with the accompanying salad.

name: My Le
text:
Wanted to support local business nearby and picked this place.  They allowed dine-in but we sat outside because we brought our dog. It’s blocked off using graffiti heart shaped concrete barricades.

We saw people who sat inside got their order taken at the table. But we sat outside so we placed our order first and paid before sitting down.

I love how their menu offers a variety of options like omelettes, French toast, specials, Benedict’s, their menu is organized but not overwhelming which lets me know that they are specialize in what they serve. Being on Restaurant Impossible in 2011 surely helped and I’m glad to see they are thriving today.

I started off with a mimosas flight that was served in a muffin tin. Four flavors, orange, strawberry, pineapple, and POG (passion fruit, orange, guava).  It’s about a 6 ounce glass each and I got tipsy after two glasses, took a sip of the third and fourth but I couldn’t finish.

We got the crab cake benedict and meat lover omelette, both served with home fries. Home fries are basically potato slices. Be sure to ask for extra crispy or well done or else it’ll be slightly on the uncooked side.

I usually eat half a benedict but I ate it all!  The crab cake patty was thick, crispy, not fishy and just enough crab. The omelette had a lot of meat and not as much cheese (I don’t like cheesy omelette). I would think the meat would make it salty but it was a bit bland. So adding a bit of hot sauce brought all the flavors out to a 10/10.

name: Ryan Bauer

My girlfriend got the chocolate covered bacon pancake and her friend got some pumpkin pancakes. They both looked delicious and got rave reviews from both of them. I, myself, had the crab cake eggs benedict. It was delicious. Mimosas were also offered during brunch with a few different flavors: orange, mango, and pineapple. The service was very good and the place had a line out the door when we left. I would recommend this place to anybody.

text: Grab & Go subs was a quick stop for my brother and I before catching a flight. I must say, I was pleasantly surprised. The bread, which I'm extremely picky about, was fresh with just the right level of "toastiness". I'm a sucker for Pastrami so I decided to give their Hot Pastrami a try. WOW. The flavors found inside were everything you could ask for ! The Pastrami meat itself was fresh, salty, smoky and had Italian all over it. Washed it all down with a delicious Lemon San Pellegrino, and for a brief moment of my day, I felt as if I was sitting at an Italian eatery as authentic as it gets. Can't forget I had a bite of my brothers Tuna Swiss and remember nothing but deliciousness, location was superb and surprisingly they have parking as well! Thanks Grab &Go!

After the meal, she offered to make a burrito out my leftovers, did not have the heart to say no. My wife took home the pozole, out politeness when she offered her to box it to go.

text:
My girlfriend and I went for Sunday brunch and were greeted with an open and bright atmosphere. There was a big sign for the "Resident Brewing Company" on the back wall. A vast beer selection is offered here, and all of the beers are broken down into their respective category from stouts, ales and to ciders.
The food menu has an excellent selection of food and offers a separate brunch menu, but both lists are provided to you when seated. My girlfriend had the chicken and waffles while I had the fire birdy.
The fire birdy is a spicily seasoned piece of ground chicken topped with pasilla peppers, pepper jack cheese, roasted serranos, chipotle mayo, tomato, avocado, and fried onion strings. This sandwich was ample and delicious and traditionally served with fries, but I got a side salad with ranch.
The chicken and waffles was a large helping. The chicken was large. My girlfriend couldn't finish all of it.
The server was attentive and responsive to all of our needs whenever we needed something. I would recommend this place to anybody looking for a good beer and some great food.

Visited during soft opening.  Staff was very friendly.  Kids meals didn't have menus yet.  Kids meals were way too big for our children, 2 full size tacos, beans and rice sides had us taking home piles of leftovers.  Hard shell tacos were too spicy for kids.

I really liked the specialty beans. They had a good amount of spice to them.  Kids not so much, should probably make black beans the standard for kids meals.

The Spanish rice seemed a bit on the bland side.  Was hoping for more flavor there.

Blended margarita had no flavor.  They were kind enough to take it back.  On the rocks margarita had good taste.  I suspect they took the same recipe from on the rocks and put it in is blender.  If they plan to continue offering blended as an option, I'd recommend they review the recipe, as the ice in a blended will make things taste more bland.

Prices on the menu were all over the place.  Like $15 appetizers mixed with $70 appetizers.  Same thing with entrees.  It felt like the order of items was haphazard.  It was also a bit of a shock to see the first appetizer as expensive as it was.  The lunch as a whole ended up a bit on the pricey side, but not as bad as initially feared.

Kids loved looking out the window at the harbor.  It is a nice venue.

name: Dan Broadhead
text:
The food, the service, and the ambiance were all excellent. And the price was relatively inexpensive. I got the Meli-Melo entree, which my server described as a Creole jambalaya, and two red stripe beers, plus tip, for under $40. Not bad. And the portion size was just right. I left full, but not stuffed. The entree comes with two plantains and you can get the green plantain or the sweet yellow plantain. I wasn't sure which to go with so tried one of each. The green one was smashed flat and sort of looked and tasted like a potato panckake. Not a lot of flavor, and kind of dry and flakey like a biscuit. The sweet yellow plantain was succulent, sweet, and full of flavor. It was the clear winner for me.
What island is sort of isolated from most of the other restaurants in Downtown, but not by too far, and it's pretty easily seen once you're on Eureka. It's just a 10 minute walk from my house, so I'll be back for sure.

text: Truth be told I'm not a buffet guy. I think they're disgusting. I always wonder what they do with all the left over food. Do they reuse it the next day? Am I eating fresh food or day old food? The other issue with buffets, can I eat my money's worth? The answer usually is no. I'm a constant eater not a single meal kinda person. Buffet and beverage here is $23. I was forced to eat here on this day because of a birthday party. With an open mind I went. When you enter there is a Koi pond in the lobby. Lots of fish but not the greatest presentation. The restaurant is huge. Plenty of seating. The food options are emense. I walked around a bit and wasn't excited about much until I saw the Mongolian BBQ area. Bingo, if nothing else this was my jam. Loaded my plate with fresh veggies, noodles and beef (cut in little steaks rather than chunks). I passed on the chicken cuz the presentation of raw chicken was disgusting. Handed my overloaded plate to the cook and watched him cook up my meal. I was pretty full but wanted to get my money's worth. Tried some black pepper chicken, California roll and salad. Last 3 items were OK but nothing spectacular. Again I think buffets are best for those who can eat a ton at one sitting. If you can you will find this place a decent value. Others at our table had crab legs, desserts, cooked veggies, and many more items. Some loved it others were like me. Waiters were friendly. name: Natalie K
text:
Move over Sushi Stop. Kula is the new cheap sushi competition in town. At a cheap-as-dirt price of $2 a plate, it's no wonder that there's already quite a wait for this newly opened revolving sushi restaurant.

I used to go to Sushi Stop and paid $2.75 per plate. I would rather come to Kula for cheaper and better sushi. The slices of fish here is thicker and the service is better. The best part is being able to pick up what you want to eat right off the conveyor belt so you don't have to wait. If you don't see what you want, you can always place an order with a waiter.

They even have amaebi, uni, and toro for just $2 a piece. They even fry the shrimp's head and serve it with the amaebi order. That is really amazing. I definitely get my money's worth by loading up on the normally expensive items.

At the end of your meal, they will count your plates in order to figure out how much you ate. It's kind of daunting seeing the plates stack up and realizing that anyone can look over and notice what a pig you are. But as you look around, you'll notice that pretty much everyone else also has an absurd amount of plates stacked up right next to them as well.

The restaurant is located in the same plaza as Nijiya and Daiso. There is a parking structure underneath that you can park for free in.

They have interesting flavors of ice cream as well but I haven't tried it yet. The pineapple coconut sounds good.

The restaurant itself is smaller with a few seats inside and a few tables outside. The service is good and fast. The guy who helped me was friendly.

My husband and I ordered a medium sized hazelnut gelato, thinking they would barely give us any like at most places. We were wrong! It was so much, we could not finish it, but we wanted to. text:
I've had Ink bookmarked for quite some time after hearing that the winner of Top Chef Masters opened this restaurant in Los Angeles. Finally, for my birthday, I had the opportunity to check Ink out and I am definitely impressed.

My boyfriend had no trouble getting a reservation on a weekday. I heard though that weekend reservations can be a little tough to snag. We were seated right away when we walked in and the restaurant was pretty full. The ambiance is fairly casual for a $$$$ restaurant.

The waiter suggested 2-3 dishes per person as they are a little smaller in size and meant to be shared. We ended up with 5 dishes but I felt like it was a little too much for us. We didn't even have room for desserts.

My favorite dish of the night was the flat iron steak. The steak was tender and flavorful. It's served with a seaweed mashed potatoes. At first I thought thi sounded like it would be disgusting but it's seriously one of the best mashed potatoes I've had. We received that dish last and I was stuffed but still somehow found a way to eat it.

I really loved the lollipop kale dish. This dish really surprised me. The kale wasn't tough to eat and I really enjoyed the flavor and texture of the dish. The crispy-fried pig's ear really gave it a nice crunch. The sauce that the kale is served in has a nice tart flavor that really complimented the dish.

The hamachi dish was delicious and the sauce was pretty amazing. We ordered 2 other dishes that I enjoyed but didn't truly blow me away: the Octopus and the Gnocchi.

The grilled octopus itself was delicious but I would have liked more of that than the green pasta that it was served with. The dish was also a little too salty for my taste. The gnocchi was interesting indeed. The center of the gnocchi was filled with gooey egg yolks. As a connoisseur of egg yolks (no such thing really but I really like egg yolks), I should have gone crazy for this dish but I didn't feel like the mushroom sauce complimented the gnocchi very well.

Overall though, the experience was great and I really enjoyed both the food and the service. There are several dishes that I read rave reviews about that we didn't get to try this time so hopefully I'll be back to try them at some point.

name: Nalani Ngoon Warde
text:
We came here for our anniversary dinner. It was a wonderful experience. This is a special occasions restaurant. Set menu, your one possible option is to add wine pairing. The experience was full of thoughtful touches, the reservation name was on our menus. The kitchen is open and right up front, which was near where we were sitting. For us, especially me, it was nice, I love to watch people cooking.

The food was fantastic. the restaurant was intimate. Plates were as beautiful as they come, and the food was as delicious as it was beautiful. They serve as a team, with a lead, all of the staff who came to the table were wonderful. An especially nice touch: the cornbread was amazing and something I felt I could make at home... we asked if it might be possible to get the recipe... and Chef made it happen. Now he'll probably curse me, as the requests start rolling in, but I felt I had to mention it as it was such a nice gesture.

Super local-focused and seasonal, much of what they serve comes from their own gardens nearby.

We're on a quest to go to one or two Michelin rated restaurants a year. Sometimes we make it, sometimes we don't. This doesn't mean that the experience wasn't totally wonderful, but if money were no object, this would still be a special occasion restaurant because of the several course fixed menu...

But I'll get to that... I want to start from the beginning.

I would not have guessed from the rather plain exterior that this place has a nicely decorated and pretty spacious interior. The hostess was very nice and welcoming as she seated us right away. Our server (Jessica) wasted no time coming to our table to see what we would like to drink. She was very pleasant and informative about food and drink options. She recommended several menu items for the both of us. We ended up starting with the garlic puffs and hause salad. Then I got a penne pasta with grilled chicken and spicy red sauce and my wife got Fettuccine Primavera, both meals were amazing. I found myself trying very hard to stop eating before I was too full. The portions are pretty generous. My wife felt the same way.

Jessica was very attentive throughout our whole meal. She also remained pleasant every time she came by our table...even as the restaurant started getting very busy.

We took our leftovers home and they were still delicious the next day.

We will definitely be coming back.

The service was horrible here. Our waitress rolled her eyes at us more times than I could count and practically threw our plates on the table. I was getting kind of pissed off but my anger quickly subsided when my cold dish arrived.

Ding's Garden offers a variety of noodle, rice, and dumpling dishes. The thing they're best known for though is their cold plate. My friend and I got the basic cold plate for $8.50 and it came with tripe, pig's ear, and bean curd. It's seriously the most delicious cold dish I've ever had. We ordered it extra spicy.

My friend and I also shared a spicy beef noodle soup and a stir-fried yu choy (vegetable dish). Both were alright but I would have rather ordered 2 cold dishes and nothing else. They have several kinds of dumplings but we didn't try it this time around.

The portions are large and everything is pretty cheap. The restaurant has a sign that says cash only but we overheard the waitress telling someone they accept debit cards.

text:
If you are a local or a visitor, this is a cool place to get good Thai food fast in Santa Monica. I've been here twice and both times I ordered and was out the door in less than ten minutes. With a nice patio to eat or to-go options (the beach is two blocks away) there is no reason not to stop and get good food.

Another reason I love this place is the selection. The variety of food allows a great choice of the best foods and if with a friend, you both can appreciate the different items. The tastes are authentic so expect to really get the traditional flavors.

Finally, the prices on the menu are definitely reasonable. The food tastes good, you won't be burning a hole in your pocket for lunch and the beach is less than a skip away. How can anyone beat that?

name: Andy Mars
text:
Overall, the food has always been delightful and delicious at Shojin, but the service at this Culver City location was not at the stellar level as at the DTLA location.  While I was the only customer in the restaurant around 6-7pm on a Thursday night, they rudely rushed me from course to course.  While I still was savoring the last couple of bites of one course, they brought the next pressuring me to hurry - this was this disappointing reality at each course's almost completion.  The lack of professional customer service was gravely disappointing.

As to the food, the best parts to me were the especially authentic classic components of the renkon, the hijiki, and the umeboshi.  Those, while excellent, were just mere touches to the dishes of which they were part.  In particular, I was disappointed at the couple of bites of renkon in the salad as I had let the waitress Hitomi know that I was considering that dish in particular as I so love renkon.  Had she let me know that there were only a couple of bites of renkon in that dish, then I would not have ordered it.  The renkon sushi roll, though, was much better.  In fact, it was the best of the items I had there this evening.  What a magnificent blend of flavors and textures!  The creamy yet nutty avocado and edamame top was a beautiful contrast to the genmai-hijiki base.  The renkon in between, though, was again my favorite. The ume was a bit too subtle for my taste as I enjoy that so much, but it worked rather nicely in this artful maki masterpiece.  The vegan "scallop" roll, though, was not as impressive.  I had explicitly asked Hitomi if they would be actually scallop-like, and she said yes and encouraged the order.  They, however, tasted nothing like scallops.  The mushrooms from which they were made did have somewhat of a scallop-ish texture, but the flavor was pure basic mushroom.  At least had they used lobster mushrooms, that would have been better as those naturally have a seafood-ish flavor.  Using the trumpet mushrooms, though, did not work as well.  Had they added to them some seaweed powder, perhaps yamahide aosa or some form of aonori, that would have much improved the dish.  Still, each of the culinary creations I have experienced from Shojin are quite creative and enjoyable to some degree.  I am not so disappointed in those in the kitchen as I am with the waitress who heard my questions and did not rightly clearly respond to them as to lead to a more satisfying dining experience.  I used to more enjoy the DTLA location, but I no longer live in the area.  I, though, am back in the area this weekend to speak at the SoCal VegFest and treated myself to this belated special birthday dinner as soon as I left LAX, and it was not as much what I desired or expected it to be. Hitomi's service was greatly lacking.  Not only did she not answer my questions well and guide me poorly on my ordering, but her general demeanor was not the especially respectful positive customer service I have experienced from Shojin.  In stark contrast, though, Elena who seemed to be working for Hitomi was a much better representative of Shojin.  Elena was particularly positive and pleasant and better answered questions after the fact than did Hitomi.  Had Elena been my waitress fully from the start, I get the sense that my dining experience would have been much better overall.

We were told by the counter person that our party of 4 would be seated within 15 minutes. He asked my wife her name and then she repeated it 2-3 times. We watched parties of 4 being seated for 22.5 minutes before we got up and went and asked the young lady who was seating another party of 4 what was going on. She looked through my wife giving her the thousand yard stare and her smile immediately disappeared: "I'll be with you in one moment...Ma'am."
So when she came back the same guy who had taken her name was hunched behind the computer at the front desk and she ignored my wife. Going instead for the woman buying macaroons for her 2 children. "I'll be with you in one moment Ma'am." She repeated and then looked at my wife after fulfilling yet another customer's order and said: "How may I help you?"
My wife told her what was going on and that her name was never called. The girl looked at her and said: "We called your name on multiple occasions. I'll seat you now." It was just a bold faced "'f-ck you" to my wife. All these other people walked in and were seated immediately and she decided that we were garbage. So they sat us at the long table next to a bunch of other families who were already eating. My wife was angry because of the way she was being spoken to by this server and she said: "You guys didn't call our name but whatever. We're very hungry now." The server rolled her eyes and then looked at my wife and said: "We called your name a few times. Here's your table. Have a nice meal."
I'm a pretty quiet person but when we're hungry we're still going to spend good money on food the service doesn't have to be perfect- but ffs she could at least be polite. I've eaten at other Korean BBQ places in Sacramento and this place has the worst service ever. Their wait staff are entitled, rude and could learn a little bit from old school waitresses and waiters.
The young lady's shameful approach to waiting tables was an embarrassment to her establishment. If I were to have eaten here I wouldn't have felt comfortable as she probably would have spit in our food.
Good luck everyone who is reading this. Buyer beware.

text:
Admittedly, I was a bit wary of going out to dinner so soon after the Shelter- in- Place was lifted, but I know the owner so we figured we'd give it a try.
We arrived and there's a barrier blocking the entrance so that each person has to have his/ her temperature checked before being admitted in.

Then you are seated one table away from each other in a staggered formation so that no one group is sitting near another, and they've actually revamped the dining process so that there is no central area where they keep all the veggies but brought to you in a tray and each person has his/her own tongs.

I actually felt better about eating here vs other restaurants since nothing is cooked in the kitchen before being brought out, which means less human contact, therefore less chance of contamination. Plus, any ingredients that are brought out to you is literally boiled in scalding hot soup before consumption.

We ate for an hour and half, going through seven trays of veggies and FIFTEEN trays of meat. We stuffed ourselves, and the total was barely $60.

Good, healthy, wholesome food. Fantastic service by safety- conscious employees. Amazing price. Yes, please.

text: This review is for a complete and utter flouting of COVID-19 restrictions and the unbelievable unprofessionalism of the host/owner. It's important to note that, as of this review date, Riverside County prohibits indoor dining and permits only outdoor dining. My partner and I attempted to go to Idyology for a drink and an appetizer on Saturday night. I called ahead to ask if there was outdoor dining available and whether I needed a reservation. The answer was "Yes, there is outdoor dining but it is wet and cold." (It had been snowing for the better part of the last 24 hours.) I asked if there were heaters and a covered patio, and the person on the phone assured me that there were heaters and umbrellas for the patio. I was satisfied with that answer, so my partner and I walked the 1/2 mile to the restaurant. When we arrived we were greeted by a hostess, who appears to be the owner/manager of Idyology as her picture is posted all over the restaurant's website, who was visibly intoxicated. We were unsettled to see that there were about 5 to 6 parties of 2-4 people each eating INSIDE the restaurant, despite Riverside County restrictions. We requested to be seated outside. Once outside we were seated at a wet table with minimal effort spared to dry it off. We were not offered a heat lamp and we were placed under an umbrella that was dripping cold water on us. The intoxicated woman asked why we wanted to sit outside (as if there is not a pandemic happening). Eventually a plate of bread and two waters were placed in front of us. After witnessing the intoxicated staff member take her mask off multiple times inside the restaurant, I peeked into the kitchen and saw the chef wearing his mask below his nose and one staff member in the kitchen without a mask at all. At this point, I felt that the restaurant was being very unsafe, so we politely left a tip for the really nice and hard-working busser (Chance) and got the heck out of there. This kind of behavior is unprofessional, unacceptable, and unsafe.

name: Layla Habahbeh
text:
There are several great Mexican restaurants in Montrose, but La Cabanita is hands down my favorite!

The interior of the restaurant is cozy with colorful murals and festive decor. The volume is typically moderately loud, but in the way it gets at a large family gathering.

On a week night, we're usually seated right away. On the weekend for dinner, the wait is 10-20 min on average for 2 people. It's a good excuse to sit at the bar and have a margarita though! Their house margarita is great and the bartender has a heavy pour. They normally cost $8, but on  Wednesdays they're $5!

When you're seated, they serve complimentary chips and 2 types of salsa: a mild, tangy salsa verde and a brown salsa with a bit of a kick. Both are authentic and delicious!

My favorite menu item is the cheese enchilada de mole They're $4.25 a la carte. I get it almost every single time because the mole is to die for! It's rich, chocolately, and unlike any others I've tried. It's definitely different than the usual mole sauces out there, so if you try it expecting it to taste a certain way, you'll be surprised - hopefully in a good way like me, but it seems like you either are obsessed with it or you hate it.

I'd also recommend their taco de cochinita if you like pork. They're $3.75 each.

The service is fantastic 95% of the time. The waiters are attentive and always friendly. I go often and there have only been a handful of times where we had slow service - it's definitely atypical.

Parking is street only, but ample (curb your tires - this part of town actually tickets for that!)

Overall, I'd highly recommend La Cab - there is a reason I keep coming back!

I've been going to this Wingnuts since 2006, but it seems I won't be returning due to their lack of food quality combined with exorbitant prices. I made my order online of the 'ribs and wings' combo, which unfortunately took two attempts at guaranteeing my order was correct.

The pickup was easy, with little waiting, even though I arrived early so my food would still be hot when I got home. It was lukewarm, so I had to use the microwave to heat it back up (I still don't think 20 minutes would make the food that cold).
The wings had very little meat on them, and what little meat was there was extremely dry, although the chipotle BBQ sauce was good.
The ribs were the worst I've ever had, and that's saying something since this place has ruined ribs for me in the past. The meat was very dry, very tough, and the charred whiskey BBQ sauce tasted awful. While eating a rib, I was reminded of drinking a nasty protein drink, with all the chalky lack of flavor. I, honestly, have had better ribs from Boston Market.

Either this place knows it has terrible food and just doesn't care to do anything about it, or they have no clue and need to be told to do better.

The homemade chips that come with every sandwich are divine. Seasoned beyond anything that comes in a bag, crispy and perfect, these chips deserve honor and awards. Bring on the medals!

text:
Quick, delicious, authentic Mexican cuisine. Located on Highland Ave/state route 43, between Nebraska and Mt. View Aves. I'm not sure of their hours, but I know that they are usually open well after the bars close(still true, even post-Covid).
In a short stretch of road, there are 4 or 5 taco trucks, but what makes this one my favorite is the dish that they serve that none of the others do - Pupusas. It's kind of like a cheese frybread loaded with your selection of meat - asada, lengua, pastor, tripas, possibly even cabeza, and served with a couple fresh slices of avocado and tomato, some shredded cabbage, and a little touch of creamy sauce. Had never heard of it before, but now I'm hooked on Pupusas.
All of their other dishes are excellent as well, and I've been pleased with every variation of every dish I've tried. They cook it up right on the spot, so sometimes you have to wait a bit, but it's well worth it.
They also have a large selection of beverages, including jarritos in multiple flavors, horchata, coke, a couple flavors of agua frescas, and I'm not sure what else.
Travellers might appreciate that they do have a port-a-potty available on site.
The prices are reasonable, the people are friendly, and the food is delicious. Definitely worth the short trip off the 99 as you pass through Selma.

text: Happy to sit down and enjoy a meal in a restaurant. 1st one in over 2 months. We chose Lucille's because they were open and we were craving BBQ. They're doing their best to comply with the restrictions such as extreme table separation and sanitizing everything. We ordered the dinner for 2 which include BBQ chicken, 2 types of ribs and a choice of burnt ends, tri tip, pulled pork and a couple of others. We chose burnt ends which were my only complaint. They were fatty and some were just gristle. Their BBQ sauce is terrific and I am a huge fan of any of their ribs. You get an additional 2 sides with the meal and we chose veggies and mashed potatoes. Both were very good. We also had a choice of appetizer or salad and we chose the salad. Nothing spectacular but the ranch dressing was good. Finally you get a choice of several desserts and we chose the carrot cake. Good but not great. A little dry. All in all a very good meal and the the service was friendly and efficient. BBQ is never cheap, 2 cocktails and the meal for 2 with tip was $100.

text: Had no clue what this place offered but boy am I glad I walked in. What an awesome concept and very good food. It's similar to a Cafe Rio or Chipotle. You pick your base which could be multiple types of salad combinations (I picked super greens) and/or a grain (I picked Saffron Basmati rice) then you'll pick a dip (I picked Crazy Feta & Tzatziki), next is a protein (I picked grilled meatballs and grilled chicken), then there's the toppings (I picked fetta and romaine lettuce) and finally the dressing (I picked lemon herb tahini). My selections made for an amazing Mediterranean food experience which I highly recommend. I paid extra for 2 full servings of protein but that was overkill, I would have been fine with just one serving. They have multiple juice and tea options that are all very good and healthy. They also offer a soda fountain that dispenses naturally sweetened sodas with some unique flavors such as blueberry. Put this down for your next food experience.

text:
If your memory serves, there was a Vallejo's here once, but now it is a small cafe, 1 block from the capital. As you are seated, butcher paper is your tablecloth, and there is a huge roll of it in the condiment corner.  "Take as much as you want," the proprietor (you assume) says.  Each table is stocked with a full deck of crayons and/or colored pencils.  The walls are lined with cool drawings from previous diners.  At this point, it doesn't matter that the breakfast menu is awesome (lemon ricotta pancakes, scones baked on site, cream stuffed french toast, home fries with zucchini).  As a set of grandparents dining with 2 boys under 5, you say to yourselves with complete confidence... WE. WILL. BE. BACK.

Notwithstanding the proprietor's offer to take your order at the table, standard procedure is to order and pay at the counter....which you do.  Is chocolate milk available?  "I'll work something out," she says.  While the 4 y.o. is  sketching a dragonfly, Proprietor steps to the table with a 16 oz. mason jar of milk with chocolate syrup...and a huge dollop of whipped cream on top.  Score.

Breakfast is delicious and, after paying at the counter afterward, you turn your back to grab the 11 mo. old, then return to the counter to see your your 4 y.o. conversing liberally with Proprietor.  The hungry new patron behind the little boy patiently waits for the chat to end.  It takes a while.

name: Jeanne Lam
text:
I tried Marugame for the first time ever last night and loved it!

This location is quite new and since it has opened, I've only seen lines out the door since I work nearby. I recently heard they currently also open for lunch so that's exciting!

If you're planning to come for dinner, come by 5pm! We arrived about 5pm and just beat the rush by a couple of minutes. There was already a short line inside and we just made the cut off of having to wait outside in the cold. Brrrr! At 5:07pm when we turned around, the line grew by 30+ people and it was basically remained that long by the time we left.

HOW TO ORDER

- Get in line quick!
- Review the menu and figure out what you want to order
- Grab a tray
- A staff member will take your order and prepare your fresh noodles, wait for 2 minutes and your bowl will be handed to you
- Continue down the line to the tempura station and select your huge pieces of fried goodness. There are so many to choose from!
- Next is the musubi station and there are a variety to choose too
- Then you arrive at the cashier to pay for everything you just grabbed
- Last stop, head to the sauce and toppings station which is just a few steps form the cashier. You will find 2 types of tempura sauce (traditional) and a saltier one similar to katsu sauce on one side of the cart. The other side has fresh scallions, cilantro, tempura battered crisps (I call it crack), and a ginger paste. Top yourself off!
- And then find a table! It's open seating so grab whatever you see.
- You know what's next after you get settled at your table. Slurp, slurp, slurp!

WHAT WE ORDERED

- #1 seller Nikutama Udon, served hot regular size ($9.90) - the portion was reasonably generous and there was a heaping amount of beef inside my bowl. And that runny poached egg was pure perfection. The broth was flavorful and a bit on the salty side. My tiniest complaint is that I wish there was more broth in my bowl so overall this was excellent!

- An assortment of tempura: 2 shrimp, crab, fish cake, tomagoyaki, vegetable ($1.70 - $2) - between 2 people we ate 6 pieces of tempura. The size of the the tempura is huge and they all cost under $2 a piece. I love the variety and I tried to choose the less commonly served pieces. My only complaint is that some pieces were cold and I was expecting all the tempura to be hot. So some improvement here is needed.

- 1 fish roe musubi/onigiri ($1.60) - this was yummy, nothing earth shattering but for $1.60, served fresh, and it's staring you in the face, why not! I'll make room for it :)

I walked past Marugame today on my way to work, and all I have to say is I WANT MORE!

Contrary to the name, Hole in the Wall Burger Joint is not quite a hole in the wall. Apparently their previous location was really cool but their new location is just a regular store front located on the first floor of an office building.

The restaurant is cash only. Once you enter, they have order sheets on the counter for you to make your own burger combination. You can also select the sides and drinks right on the order sheet. When you're done, take it to the counter and they will call your name when your order is ready.

I had the beef patty with egg, onion mayo, pepper jack cheese and veggies in a pretzel bun. The burger was oily yet flavorless. I had to smother mine in ranch and ketchup. The burger was quite big and messy. I couldn't finish mine in one sitting.

I had their fried mac n cheese ball and the hushpuppies for my sides. The hushpuppies were quite good but the mac n cheese ball was over-fried so it was hard. I didn't quite care for the flavor either.

They have homemade ketchup, which I found to be too liquidy. I prefer the regular ketchup and luckily they have that. They also make their own ranch and it's pretty good.

I wanted to try their rice roll that's made with black rice since it looked good. I really wasn't impressed with it at all. The rice was too hard and the rice roll was too small. I enjoy the rice rolls at Yi Mei a lot more.]

What everyone orders here is the soy milk dishes. Some people get the sweet soy milk while others get the salty kind. The salty soy milk is really interesting. It has broken down tofu with pork sung and Chinese donut in the soy milk. It's a very interesting combination of flavors that a non-Taiwanese like me can't quite understand.

I ordered one of their sticky rice boxes to-go. It was not good. The rice was hard and the pork was too salty while the sticky rice itself lacks flavor.

text:
What stood out the most of my entire visit to Craft is the service. I made a reservation about a week ahead of time for my boyfriend's birthday on Opentable. They called me several days ahead to confirm that it was a birthday and asked for my boyfriend's name.

We arrived about 15 minutes early and they seated us right away. The menu had "Happy Birthday, Mitchell" printed on the top. It was such a nice touch and they even wrapped up the menu for us to take back. Several employees came by to wish my boyfriend a happy birthday after we sat down. I was quite impressed with the level or service they provided in making sure he felt special for his birthday.

I had Craft bookmarked for a long time since they're known for their steak. However, the birthday boy decided he liked the dineLA menu better so we tried that instead. Their dineLA menu is a little different where you don't select the desserts or first course. Everything listed comes out for the table to share. You simply pick one entree each.

The starters contained a kale salad, mushroom toast, and the beet and avocado salad. The kale salad looked plain and like it wouldn't have a lot of flavor but it turned out to be my favorite dish. The salad was packed with flavor. The mushroom toast was good as well. They also served bread from La Brea bakery with room temperature butter. I love their bread. Unfortunately, the beet and avocado salad was just okay to me.

Our entree choices were the pork belly with grits and the sole. The pork belly was really great. The meat was tender and the grits was so flavorful. The sauce that came with the dish was very good. Unfortunately, I can't say the same about the sole. The fish was rolled up and seared. It tasted citrusy but the whole dish really lacked flavor. It would have been better with a sauce. They gave us complimentary brussels sprouts for our side and it was amazing.

The desserts were good. We had the banana bread pudding, which was more like a banana nut muffin with some cream on top, and the sherbet. The sherbet was quite tart and refreshing. They also gave us a chocolate cake since it's a birthday celebration. The cake was very chocolatey. At the end, they give you granola to take home.

Our server recommended a nice wine to go with our dish for $15 a glass. Our dine LA for 2 plus wine and tax and tip came out to less than $200.

text:
*4.5 stars*

The Boiling Crab revolution has taken over, but I'd have to say that Rockin' Crawfish is better. Rockin' Crawfish has a much better broth/sauce (Rockin' Combo) that isn't overly-garlicky like Boiling Crab and the crawfish is much fresher. I've gone to Rockin' Crawfish over 15 times in the last few years (including the Oakland location), and although it has it's rare bad days, it's pretty consistently delivered. I went yesterday and the crawfish was the freshest it's ever been (and they had roe!!).

The waitresses are friendly, there's TVs, and the food is excellent. I love their fried catfish (fish 'n chips), buffalo wings, and fried oysters as well.

Hands down the best crawfish boil restaurant in SF (or at least much better than Red Crawfish, Craw Station, and Swamp).

text:
My wife and I were invited by friends to this acclaimed Dublin restaurant for dinner, the first visit for both of us. We met there early, about 15 mins before the dinner service doors opened and there was already a sizeable line of diners waiting. Luckily we were able to get a table in the first seating.

We tried the grilled edamame appetizer, the grilling smokie flavor really complemented the natural sweetness of the soybean and salt seasoning, definitely a dish I'd recommend.

I ordered the Katsudon entree and I enjoyed all of its flavors. The tonkotsu was lightly breaded and crispy, the pork was cooked well but still moist. The dashi taste was present but not heavy. Portion size was huge.

I plan to come back to try other dishes.

name: Wayne Christensen
text:
ALL ATWITTER! Dublin, Calif., folks are all atwitter about Amakara, a "contemporary Japanese" darling. I want on a Thursday night. It opens at 5 p.m. By the time the doors opened, there were some 40 folks in line to eat that night. In talking to someone else in line, I discover that it used to be that lines only formed on weekends. Now, it's every night Amakara is open.

One reason is likely that the chef here serves some highly imaginative food. For example, he grills edamame with olive oil (not steams) giving it an extra tasty dimension of flavor. He serves foie gras sushi, made with monkfish liver, which is a better idea than it is a fulfilling execution. How about an oyster shooter, with a quail egg yolk in sake or Kurobuta pork belly with kimchi?

There's much to choose from and I'm definitely headed back there.

Our friends booked their private banquet room and also had them cater the event. The room was a good size and the servers were very friendly and prompt. However, I suspected that I might be in a bit of trouble when we tasted the chips and salsa. On a positive note, the chips appeared to be home made. The salsa was also home made but lacked in flavor or heat.

When the meal was served, I always try the rice and beans first before anything else. The rice was overcooked and so wet it was still soggy. The refried beans were also disappointing because they were too loose (watery) and also didn't have any flavor. If I had to guess, I think that the person that catered this event was not their usual person because it had all the markings of someone who did not know how to scale recipes for larger groups.

I have heard that the food at this restaurant is usually very good so I will have to come back for an individual meal vs catered event.  I will post again when that happens.

The wings are JUST. SO. GOOD. So, so, so good.

I haven't tried all the Chinese wing places in San Francisco, but honestly... I feel I can stop at SO.

Tiny, a little bigger than a whole in the wall, this place is my favorite place for wings. If you come, you MUST get the wings. They are crispy, a little sweet, garlicky, spicy. Be prepared for sticky fingers and a runny nose. The best place to enjoy these would probably be in the comfort of your own home, where you could wash your hands when you needed to blow your nose, or just go savage and get messy... but I am getting off topic a little... the wings aren't as good by the time you get them home (trust me, I've tried)...

The Chipotle Fried Rice is delicious, smokey, a little spicy, savory (my favorite of all of their fried rices).

The String Beans are good. Dumplings have all been good.

The service is always friendly, it's a small place and I've seen the same friendly faces over the past year every time I come in.

PRO-tip, call ahead to make sure they're open (I've come by expressly to get lunch during their normal business hours and they've been closed with a funny note in the window, I was a SO sad panda). You can also order your wings if you're nearby, and they'll be ready when you get there (piping hot and delish).

text:
A true Izakaya, this is the original and still the best Japanese bar food you will find. While many will stick with what they know, be adventurous here as you'll always be rewarded! I personally never pass up the Tori Kawa  (skewered chicken skin) that's super crispy and tasty, the Okonomiyaki (Japanese pancake/omelette with everything in it) that'll fill you up and leave you wanting more, and of course their sushi.

Now, you'd ask, why not go to a proper sushi place? Well, while you might find a cheaper place that has marginally fresher fish, Izakaya has the best prepared nigiri in the US. The rice is warm, slightly sticky and fluffy with just the right dab of wasabi to match the delicious fish on top. While I always go for the hamachi or salmon, I haven't had bad sushi there, ever.

name: Jonathan Marinaro
text:
My wife and I are regulars here, and while we do love the Ramen, our usual to-go order is a big plate of their yakimeshi, Japanese fried rice, and the karaage, the fried chicken.

The rice is super supple and extremely flavorful, a great example of how it differs from Chinese or Thai style fried rices, but that chicken sings. First it's a massive portion and fried perfectly (just make sure to open the container ASAP when taking to go to make sure the steam is let out, otherwise it might get a little soggy) with each piece super crispy and full of flavor. Remember to toss the salt included on it and shake, that really opens up the flavor!

Every Plant Power menu is different. We are closer to SDSU location but we chose OB because they offer more items.

This location is right off the highway on Sunset across from Shell and Jack and the Box. It has its own building downstairs and parking lot. They even have 4 spaces designated for curb side pick up. Nice outdoor seating area and two restrooms outside that requires a code.

Oh they are also pet friendly! My dog was allowed inside. They said they love dogs. Thank you OB!

When you walk inside, there’s a touch screen stand, one on each side of the room for self ordering. Or you can go up to the counter.

We ordered the Fish Filet Sandwich and the Iconic Burger. Got a side of Iconic Fries which taste like In n Out animal style fries. We also got Buffalo wings. The wing sauce is on point, I wish I had celery! Boyfriend said they remind him of Loving Hut strips.

I tasted more bread than fish filet. Even though the patty appeared to be thick, I wished it was even thicker because it was masked by the two buns. Can’t go wrong with the Iconic Burger.

They have merchandise that you can purchase and even their own newspaper!
So cool!

Worth the trip in every way.  Every dish was exceptional, the staff make you feel at home, and the intimacy is unrivaled.  I had to make reservations two weeks in advance, so keep that in mind when planing your visit.  The menu changes approximately every 1.5 weeks, with the chicken arepa remaining as the staple dish for every menu.

First we had a tomato, burrata, and crouton salad with (olive?) oil and pesto.  Then the classic chicken arepa.  Next there were scallops resting on black garlic corn, covered in a Japanese citrus and jalapeño vinaigrette.  Finally a watermelon sorbet with sprinkled on top, which was refreshing without being too sweet.

(Translated by Google) INDIAN RESTAURANT IN THE HEART OF SAN FRANCISCO

Near Union Square is one of the city's best Indian restaurants, Punjab Kabab House, which we visited.

The decor is neat and authentic, while the service is very friendly.

We got to try the Tandoori Mix Grill, which contains chicken, lamb and sis kebab. In addition, we also got Rice and Naan Bread.

Prices are reasonable. In total we paid 53.61 USD for 3 people with drinks, which is equivalent to 328 DKK.

Punjab Kabab House is a highly recommended eatery which is close to being unique place. It is one of the best Indian restaurants that we have tried. Their food tastes really good, where both the service and the serving add the finishing touch.

text:
This location has the cleanest rest rooms anywhere that should serve as the Model for the Industry.

That said, it's an El Pollo Loco that despite a wonderful staff & tasty recipes, suffers from the same glaring symptom of shock as others in its chain.

The Universe's Absolute Worst Menu lives here. Menus in many joints are becoming hard to fathom, but here is the example of how ridiculously bad they can get.

Want soup? They have it...but it's not on the menu. Want only the entree part of a Combo Meal ala carte? Sure...but its price is nowhere to be found.

2021 review

My husband said, ‘how did you find *the* place in Orange County?’ And I couldn’t agree more! We were seated outside on their patio, and enjoyed the heat lamps and live music of Adam Lasher. He was incredible, and we ordered dessert partly because of him.

Our server was great (I think his name was Ronnie) and offered great suggestions and service. We started with their complimentary bread, and my husband ordered an amazing cocktail (can’t remember the name- but it had tobacco and chocolate bitters. It was amazing). He ordered the salmon and I ordered the scallops. Both were good, but my scallop entree was a little better.

I was ready to head out, but my husband convinced me to order dessert and I’m so glad he did! We got to enjoy Adam’s music a little longer, and their dessert and cocktails turned out to be the highlights of our dining experience. We ordered a red eye cocktail (it was an espresso martini) and couldn’t resist sharing both the apple pie and the pineapple butter cake after Ronnie recommended both. Apple pie was good, but the butter cake was one of our favorite desserts ever! I’m still thinking about it today, it was that good. We would come back here for sure! This restaurant is amazing for both brunch and dinner!

text:
KBBQ just tastes better when you wrap meat, garlic, and bean paste in a giant piece of lettuce then stuffing the impossibly large bite into your mouth all at once. Soot Bull Jeep will serve you with everything you need, including lots of lettuce, green onion salad, bean paste, and tons of garlic for you to have with your meat. I highly recommend asking for the garlic and sesame oil in a foil cup for your grill. The garlic becomes so tender and delicious after being slowly cooked in sesame oil.

This place is not AYCE so be prepared to pay a little more. We had 3 orders of kalbi or marinated short ribs, an order of tongue, and one kimchi stew for 4 people. It was a lot of food and we realized we could have been fine with just 2 orders of kalbi. The total was $165 with 2 large bottles of beer so it's a little pricey but not unreasonable.

The kalbi is definitely delicious. The grill is a combination of gas and charcoal and you can really taste the charcoal flavor, which really adds to deliciousness of the beef. The grill does have uneven head though because of the charcoal. The kimchi stew is a great deal at about $10. It's nicely spicy and the kimchi has been fermented long enough so it's pretty sour. Each order is huge.

The service is great even though their English is kind of spotty. We got everything we asked for quickly and our waiter was super nice. They have a free parking lot also, which is extremely rare for a Ktown restaurant.

Been wanting to try this place since it opened! Unfortunately it’s take out only, otherwise, they have a very cute outside patio.  Quite a few guests came to pick up their order. Proper stickers on the floor for six feet rule.

We waited outside in our car and they brought the food out to us. It was secured in a brown paper bag and the top was stapled. We brought it home and eager to open the bag. I was surprised to see utensils, napkins and even plates! Each dish was in a foil tin on top of a plate and that’s how it was stacked.

Pestofredo - It’s a mix of pestofredo and craft pesto. Craft pesto is just pesto green sauce and pestofredo is a mix of Alfredo and pesto. This dish has shredded roasted chicken with fettuccini and it’s super moist and tasty. Added broccoli as veggies. The sauce is light on the creamy side which I prefer.

Pasta & sauce - there’s 3 pasta choices and 5 sauce choice. We got penne with bolognese. You can tell the sauce is fresh because it has the tomato sour taste and a bit of sweetness from carrots!

Meat lasagna - This dish is same as the previous dish except it’s lasagna with each layer as cheese.

If you check into Yelp, you get two free garlic knots! It has a bit of saltiness,a blend of sweetness, soft and chewy, the center reminded of biting into a Cinnabon.

The garlic bread was amazing! It’s thin like bruschetta bread with melted garlic butter and with every crunch, the bread melts in your mouth! Taste great dipped in the red sauce.

My bf is picky and he actually approved of this place. Our favorite is the Pestofredo.

text:
Maybe it’s a better experience with better quality food for brunch?

We came here for dinner and sat outside on the top deck. Their heaters weren’t working, so we were a little chilly. The servers were understaffed, so I felt bad for our waiter. He did a good job, but we could tell he was really frazzled, and some other guests were complaining about missing items from their order or waiting too long for the bill.

We ordered the mahi mahi fish special (mine simply grilled with beurre blanc sauce and my husband’s macadamia crusted with brown butter sauce). The guy who delivered our waters decided to take our order to help our server, and then our server came back to take our order all over again and record it in their electronic system.

For sides, we ordered mashed potatoes and a side Caesar salad. Our server said ‘so no vegetables?’ But potatoes and salad are both veggies, so at first I was a little confused. The fish wasn’t the best quality, and not what I expected for a well-known top-rated restaurant in Newport Beach. The mashed potatoes were warm in some parts and cold in others, perhaps re-heated in the microwave or prepared in a rush. Overall, a good price and okay service given the understaffed situation, but there are just too many outstanding restaurants in Newport with a view like this one. Wouldn’t recommend.

text:
My friends threw me a surprise birthday party at the Stocking Frame and I had a fabulous time. I had never heard of this restaurant before but I can't wait to be back again.

Parking was a pain for most people in our party since there is no valet and the restaurant is located in downtown LA.  There is a pay lot across the street though if it's not full.

The dishes are small and can be a little pricey. They recommended 2-3 dishes per person but we ended up ordering almost everything on the menu and sharing. My favorite dish of the night was definitely the Hamachi on coconut rice. The sauce was nicely sour with lime and pickled Thai chili. I could eat like 10 orders of that by myself.

They have a decent drinks list. They also have several types of bottled apple cider. I didn't try any of their cocktails but some of my friends and they looked yummy.

The service was pretty good. It was a weekday and the whole place was almost completely empty. No reservations needed really, although as I understand, they accept reservations.

I will be back soon for more of the hamachi dish!

text: When I think of Giant Burger, I don't think of it as just your typical burger joint, or a pit stop on the way to or from Bear Valley and points beyond, rather I consider it an historical landmark, if you will. Restaurants have come, and many are now gone, but for those of us that grew up or passed through the small town of Arnold, Giant Burger has always been there. I can clearly remember as a young child more than 30 years ago just hanging out for hours enjoying a "Baby Burger", fries and a milkshake and playing the arcade games (things kids did before Nintendo, Xbox and PlayStation). I remember being so short I couldn't even reach the counter to order. Sure, over the years the menu has changed (of course you can still order the "Giant Burger" or its younger sibling the "Baby Burger") and so have the owners, but this establishment has been serving up small town charm to locals and passers-by since 1968 and I imagine it will continue to do so for many more.

name: CT Martin
text:
Went for a second time last night with my business partner... hadn't visited for a couple years (!!) and last night's meal was a reminder of what I've been missing -- really good food.

First, definitely start with the chips and salsa flight -- you'll get generous portions of SEVEN very distinct and delicious salsas, arranged from mild to spicy and all great.  It's a good deal for the price, which isn't much more than what you typically spend on chips & salsa, only you'll get a ton of variety.

On our previous visit, we had the octopus appetizer and the Sea of Cortez Kanpachi Sashimi, both are highly recommended as the place prides itself on its seafood (and rightly so). This time we tried the Pacifico beer battered fried crab appetizer and the vegetarian-friendly potato & broccolini-stuffed taquitos, and both of these were absolutely delicious.

Feedback about the crab appetizer: the cold salad (slaw of green papaya, green beans, red onion) which served as the bed for the crab was cold and refreshing, but maybe a little too cold. The plate itself was very cold, which suggests the slaw was already plated and sitting in a refrigerator, which is not a very appetizing thought.

For our entree, we both had the macadamia-crusted lamb chops. These were really yummy and cooked perfectly medium-rare.  They come with some roasted radishes, which I had honestly never had before and are delicious as a roasted root starch.  For sides, we ordered the corn esquites and the cilantro-lime rice -- both highly recommended as well.

For dessert, the churro & ice cream was a real keeper. The churros are so light and fluffy.
