text:
Akiko's had everything it took to become my favorite sushi restaurant in SF, but just failed miserably.

Now, I will definitely give credit where credit's due: Akiko's has some of the freshest, unique, and delicious fish that I've tried in SF. The Ankimo (monkfish liver) here is amazing, the Russian Uni was the best uni I've ever had, and Hamachi nigiri was perfect. The ambiance of the place was incredible -- the brick wall blended with pipes and stucco felt like I was in some cool underground bar, but the lighting and atmosphere felt like I was in a tranquil spa in Kyoto.

Where it goes miserably wrong, though, is with the service. Now, our server Ray was a nice guy -- I'll give him that -- but it really felt like he was pushing orders on us way too aggressively. We felt like we were being upsold by a Comcast representative and it just wasn't pleasant. After we put in our order, our drinks were forgotten and we had to ask a busboy twice to get us the beers that we ordered. They didn't arrive until our third dish had already come out. But honestly, even that's excusable.

What really pissed us off was that we ordered the Kuro Maguro (Chu Toro), since all of us really go to sushi restaurants for toro (everything else is a nice plus). First off, they ran out of every kind of toro, except for the Chu Toro, so we ordered that. Another server (not Ray) brings us our "Chu Toro" that obviously did not look like belly, so we asked him what it was. The server said it was the Chu Toro and we said "Are you sure? That doesn't look like Chu Toro." He says: "That's the shoulder cut, you ordered it" and walks away. It wasn't until after the dinner that our server (Ray) comes and says: "Oh by the way, we ran out of Chu Toro so we substituted it for the bluefin tuna shoulder cut."

The whole exchange was just extremely shady. If you run out of toro, then you come tell us that you ran out of toro and ask if we'd like to order something else instead. You don't sneakily throw something in there that we didn't order and try to trick us into thinking it's what we ordered. That whole experience really left a bad taste in our mouths.

And by the way, what sushi restaurant runs out of 3 different types of toro on Friday night at 8pm??

This place was very disappointing. Pho Ha is a chain that’s been around for decades with one of my favorites in San Jose and Pomona (eat there and you won’t be disappointed). By reputation, Pho Ha is very authentic but this particular day it went wrong. Owners of this franchise really need to go back on their service and chef training. It gives the other Pho Ha a bad name.

We left Palm Springs to head south and wanted pho. The next closest Pho heading South was Temecula. This was Thanksgiving weekend and combined with CoVId restrictions, this plaza was very dead. Pho Ha had six tables for outdoor dining on their sidewalk. Three on each side, five of them seat 4 and one seated two.

The first annoying incident was that we went inside and stood halfway between the door and register due to social distancing. There were others in there and at the time we thought they were customers but they were workers! No uniform so we couldn’t tell. Then they didn’t acknowledge us! At least say, “we will be right with you”. So we made a comment out loud like do we just stand here? A guy walks passed and said you order at the front then find a seat outside. We thought he was a customer leaving but that guy happened to work here!

So we finally placed our order, no apologies from the counter at all. My mother was already seated outside. We got 3 pho’s (seafood, dac biet, and rare streak) and banh khot which is Vietnamese savory mini pancake.

The seafood pho was not worth serving. One of the imitation crab was still frozen. Which means the fish balls, meat balls, shrimp probably all were frozen prior.

The broth tasted weird and at first, I couldn’t figure it out. It was like soupy. I got the rare steak and normally I love carbs and would eat noodles and save meat for last. This time the broth and noodles was so disgusting that I just ate the meat. I still couldn’t shake that smell and taste from the broth. Later, I figured it out, it’s not the broth, it’s the noodles that was over cooked and it’s like they didn’t rinse off the extra starch and just served it like that so it had a funky thick smell to it.

My mom and I can’t stand to waste food and we thought maybe taking it home and add some spice would be easier to chow down. So we asked for take out containers. My mom had the seafood and ended up tossing the noodles and keeping the seafood to make a new meal at home. I had the rare steak and when I took it home to heat up, It was worse so I had to throw it away.

On the flip side, they give a lot of noodles. So that take home portion could have been divided up into two meals.

The only item that turned out delicious was the banh khot. We thought they forgot about it because it should be an appetizer but it came out after we boxed our pho.

Banh khot was freshly made, the batter had to be mixed and fried. It came out crispy on the outside and glutinous chewy in the center with the friend shrimp on top and had tons of flavors when wrapped in lettuce and dipped with fish sauce.

I was aiming for 1 star but the banh khot redeemed itself to 2.

name: Uncle Buck
text:
Cuca's Mexican Food has been around since the 1990's, establishing itself in Redlands, CA as one of the premiere locations to get authentic Mexican fast food items without the high prices or long waits... The Yucaipa, CA location carries that same sentiment while going above and beyond.

The restaurant features a large dining hall, outside patio seating and a convenient drive-thru. They are open for breakfast, lunch and dinner. This location offers generous seating to accommodate large families as well as intimate booths for two. The inside of the restaurant has been redone with an updated interior offering a festive Mexican theme without being overdone. The dining area is kept clean and is well maintained as are the bathrooms and entire property.

Food offerings are plenty, with everything from burritos to tacos, sopes to enchiladas, and even going as far as to serve menudo and tamales. The daily special is a long time favorite among locals offering a "pick 2 items" approach while also including a medium drink. Cuca's also has a "day of the week" special that offers 6-7 different items that change for the given day ranging from a bean & cheese burrito, egg & cheese burrito, taco, tostada, quesadilla, cheeseburger etc. for only $1.39 per item with a limit of (5) per customer.

Cuca's has 6+ locations throughout the Inland Empire and continues to shine as an affordable solution for scoring great Mexican fast food that is sure to please the entire family! Stop by and check them out.

text: This place is like crack.  I brought one of my boys here as a birthday gift.  I'm back for the 3rd time in 2 weeks.  The cars really move for an indoor track (up to 40 mph, I hear), and the race is typically against time, not other drivers. However, large groups can actually race.  Results of each heat are delivered in writing following your race; conveniently, you can find a results sheet at the bar on the 2nd floor, where you can buy a soda or beer, and enjoy some snacks while you razz your friends.   A membership costs $6, and that provides you "free" helmet rental, face sock, and a free ride during your birthday month.  Races (14 laps in duration) start at $22 and go as cheap as $16 when purchased in a package of 3.  It's a totally immersive and addictive experience.  So think carefully whether you even want to start.  Once you do, stopping will likely require rehab.

The host did a great job of checking us (and everyone after us) in. We arrived at 7pm for a 7:15pm reservation. I just realized he never told us how long the wait would be... By 8:30pm we still hadn't been seated so we left. I tried to be kind and asked the person at the host station (whom at this point appeared to be the manager) to cancel our reservation to free up our spots for the next guests, but he just stared, pointed at the screen, and shook his head. I think he muttered something under his breath, but I'm not sure what. I just said thank you and walked out. The original host that checked us in held the door open and apologized, which was infinitely better than the reaction from the manager.

While we were waiting, I heard the host tell other irate people that OpenTable was to blame; that OpenTable keeps allowing reservations for the same times, and if Benihanas were to block that, they'd get in trouble. Seems to me that Benihanas should get rid of OpenTable. It's your restaurant that looks bad, not OpenTable. Also, you can't really put all the blame on OpenTable because we made the reservation over the phone. The lady asked if we wanted 6:45 or 7:15. If online bookings were really an issue, the lady should have said there were no more available reservations for the evening.

What's the point of making a reservation if you're still going to have to wait for over an hour? At least tell us that upfront so we can do something productive during that time. Or, maybe you can adopt some sort of text messaging service that texts the customer when their table is ready. I know they exist, because I've personally used one before.

There were SO many people that left unsatisfied... Definitely isn't good for business. Maybe hand out some discount cards, or free appetizer vouchers or something?

Apparently this issue isn't limited to this location, so I'm sorry to say that the Benihana's chain just lost a couple customers. This sucks because your soup and rice are so damn good! Unfortunately, not good enough to wait over 1.5 hours for on a Thursday night.

Wings themselves appear to be double-fried, which is great in my book as I’ve never had an undercooked or overcooked wing from this place unlike wingstop. The application and cooking quality for dry rubs and wet options seems to be consistent across fire wings stores...

There’s an attached poke bar (sushi salad) at this venue, unique from other fire wings place I’ve been.

They don’t take phone orders unless you’re willing to verbally give them your credit card information. So be forewarned if you want to just order conveniently, just use the online website options.

As usual, I was very hangry (hungry + angry for those who don't know) after my work out and wanted brunch. My friend and I came in and was told there was a 30 minute wait. I was contemplating leaving until a host offered me a complimentary sea salt chocolate chip cookies while I wait. I immediately planted my butt down and enjoyed the most delicious free cookie I've had to date.

The service is great. Out waiter was nice and attentive. We ordered 2 cups of coffee and they came in a French press. It was quite delicious.

My friend ordered the eggs benedict along with a side of grilled vegetables. She liked her dish but the side of vegetables was kind of a waste of money. Her small plate came with nothing but roasted squash and cost $4.

I had the brussel sprouts salad. It was light and healthy. It wasn't too flavorful but I did enjoy it. I also ordered a side of their homemade English Muffins. That was definitely the best part of my meal.

There is parking next to the restaurant in the structure. The first 90 minutes is free and it's $2 per hour after that.

What they call "burger" here doesn't really look or taste like burger. Even the basic ingredients, the bun and the patty, are low quality - beside they don't know how to cook the patty.
The meat was stale (it looked like frozen meat) it didn't taste good, and it was not cooked to order - we ordered medium rare  but the patty was dry.
This is not what a 14$ burger should taste like. There are plenty other places in LA that will give you "unique" "quality" in that price range.
The fries were salty and the sauces didn't taste right. Not even the ketchup.
I have a feeling that they have confused "Asian fusion" with adding extra salt and mixing seaweed in everything.

The waiter was not attentive; he forgot our order of wings (which I am okay with after tasting the burger - I could.imagine my disappointment​ with the wings) , he didn't apologize for it and when we complained about the food he shrugged it off.

name: Milo tG
text:
I came here seeking the Impossible Burger as I am a vegan and it interests me.  Though I do not personally eat much "fake meat" they are always nice to know about if you're going out to eat with meat eaters or trying to take someone out who wants a burger but you have to pay for it.

So I ordered the Impossible Burger w/ no cheese and some sweet potato fries.

AND HOLD THE PHONE WHY ARE THE SWEET POTATO FRIES AT UMAMI BURGER NOT NATIONAL NEWS!?

These sweet potato fries are top ten best things I have ever had at a restaurant.  I think they sprinkle them with brown sugar or something but it's very understated and perfectly executed.  Mad props to the recipe designers and especially the chef at this particular location!  Do not for a second imagine that you will share an order of this side with a friend or loved one, that will be a ruined relationship and a life of regret.  I am gonna get two for myself next time I go...

So about the burger though: I haven't eaten meat since 2014 so probably I am not the best judge, but it's a testament to the Impossible Foods Co (separate from UB) that when I was eating it I instinctively was comparing the burger to BURGERS of the past and not to other-veggie-burgers.  And it tastes like a burger!  A pretty good one too, though it's not a black angus tri-tip steak sandwich to be sure.  It's not trying to be.

I hate to sell UB short on the rest of the burger, it was quite good, but nobody should be surprised that they know burgers and I cheats them by nixing the cheese anyway.  Very satisfied and 10/10 service too.

Ooh and they have that Bunderberg ginger beer too, that stuff is too good!

name: Marcella Nichols Eastin
text:
3.5 stars, because some of the negatives outweigh the amazing positives.

Our room was the best part- luxurious king size bed with super plush bedding and wonderful pillows. Snacks in the room for a small fee, as well as other essentials you may have forgotten. Beautiful rain shower. We also had a little enclosed outdoor porch. And, they gave us a complimentary bottle of red wine! Surrounding hotel areas were also enjoyable. We liked the fire pit at night and listened to the music going on at two different weddings (we danced on the outskirts and had a fun time).

Negatives of the room were that the sink sprayed water all over the mirror each time we turned it on. The shower also leaked under the door, so a bath mat was a waste. The ledge/shelf to store your shower items was broken, so we had to place our things on the shower floor.

Customer service- mixed feelings here. The concierge was extremely helpful, friendly, and knowledgeable. The man who checked us in however, was not. We had to ask for a map and he did not explain to us the valet system. The valets let us park ourselves, so we thought it was unnecessary. Then we headed to our car to get our bags and they chased us and gave us the valet information. As we carried our bags, the front desk guy ran out and let us know that they would help us with it. So it wasn't clear all the luxuries we were afforded at this establishment until it was too late. However, the grounds were clean with staff everywhere to direct you if you were lost.

The gym- not impressed here. Tons of machines, but they are old and uncomfortable to use. It was also too warm in the gym, and I am someone who is always cold. There also is not any WiFi available, so plan your playlist accordingly.

Breakfast- it is no longer a buffet, sadly. You must order a la carte. I had to prompt them that it was complimentary also, so maybe that is changing. One person said they would deliver our food to the room, and then another said they were too busy. So mixed customer service here again. The almond butter toast was amazing and I would get it again. However, the American style breakfast (eggs, bacon, toast, pancakes, potatoes) was a disappointment. Bacon was limp, toast was served without jam, and the eggs weren't good. Pancakes were oatmeal and pretty tasty, but not what you might expect.

name: Chris Turpin
text:
3 stars because really I have no issue with the food by itself. I usually grab a barbacoa burrito. Tastes fine enough, certainly not the worst I've had.

But what gets my goat is the cost. I feel like in a place like Salinas with a rich selection of Mexican restaurants, paying $13 for a burrito is a bit of a tall order. And that's just the barbacoa with guac. Whereas I can go to a legit sit-in restaurant (Dona Ester's for example) and for a dollar more I'm getting a better burrito, avacado included, WITH free chips and salsa (that are bottomless, no less!)

If Chipotle were, say, in a vacuum where no other Mexican restaurants existed I could maybe see the appeal of it and the prices wouldn't be ridiculous. But this is Salinas, with a thriving Mexican population with Mexican restaurants all over the place that offer similar quality or better food for a cheaper price. In that case, it makes Chipotle a hard sell.

2 stars only bc the staff was nice. Got the Tandoori fish and goat biryani. Both were terrible.

The fish was so bland and flavorless, skin was crispy but inedible, picture on the menu cover shows a Whole fish and that's what the menu item says, but what comes is just 4 pieces of fish, and there were SO many thin transparent bones that it was a hazard to eat. I don't understand how anyone is recommending it unless they haven't had tandoori fish done right.

The goat biryani came with 4 pieces of bone with barely any meat. Complained to staff and they were kind to get us another goat biryani with a good amount of meat. Was not tasty to me but that's personal preference, others may like it.

Staff said the first biryani had less meat bc the goat purchased this time was covered by a cloth and turned out smaller than the chef expected. Umm...what?? That doesn't matter, you still give the same fair portion to customers and then say you're out when you're out. Not skimp around it with all bone pieces, saving the meat bc you can get away with it. Some people were picking up carryout too, they're gonna be disappointed at home for sure.

All in all the staff is nice and attentive, but food is just not up to par in taste or quality and they're being  oversmart in what they serve, but will quickly remedy the situation when called out. Will not return.

Also the decorations and atmosphere are great.

name: Jeanne Lam
text:
I made my first visit to Palette Tea House yesterday. It was definitely a fun experience and I loved the ambiance, modern/open decor, and the excellent customer service.

Between 3 people we spent $55 per person with plenty of leftovers. We thought it would come closer to $70 a person. I came with recommendations and ordered conservatively to start because, we can alway order more as we go. I didn't want our eyes to get bigger than our stomachs which was a good call.

All the food came out fast! I suggest ordering your desserts later, so your meal is more coursed out and everything stays hot. My favorite dishes were the lobster ha gow, soft shell crab, and blueberry sesame balls. Some dishes were kind of meh for the price point. They offer classic dim sum but most of dishes are made with elevated ingredients which is why we're here, right?

If it ain't fancy, I would suggest skipping the dish and getting it at a traditional dim sum restaurant because the prices are fairly steep and you should order something special. Don't skimp and make this trip worth your while!

They also serve cocktails for about $14 each but I preferred tea with my dim sum. The Chinese in me was keeping it traditional.

What we ordered:

- Jade Jasmine green tea ($9) - The first pot was light but after the tea steeps longer, the flavor becomes more fragrant and stronger. I love my green tea and it came in a huge pot.

- Roast duck congee ($16) - Good, but nothing earth shattering for someone that eats roast duck pretty often. My group really liked that there were kernels of corn in our congee so that added a nice crunch.

- Palette XLB ($12) - The different flavors were subtle: original, turmeric/crab (yellow), squid ink (black), beet/beef (red), spinach/kale (green). I thought this was good! Served hot and juicy but the skin could be thinner. There was also an edible lining on the bottom of the dumpling which was a bit weird.

- Lobster Ha Gow ($10) - Loved this! The syringe of lobster broth was also a lot of fun since you get to infuse your own dumpling for added juiciness.

- Jumbo scallop siu mai ($8) - Literally siu mai with a big scallop on top. Yum!

- Snow cap BBQ bao ($6) - Good. Came in 2. Nothing really special but we preferred this over the original steamed version.

- Soft shell crab crepe ($14) - One of my favorites! Crunchy soft shell crab rolled up in a rice roll is genius! I loved the texture and it was topped with the perfect amount of sweet/savory soy sauce.

- Iberico cha siu (BBQ pork) ($28) - Tender but underwhelming. For this price, I can get better BBQ at a traditional Chinese BBQ restaurant.

- Wagyu chow fun ($18) - Good. Generous slices of wagyu beef.

- Blueberry sesame ball ($6) - Loved this! Anything blueberry in a classic  dessert, I'm sold. The filling was amazing and the crunchy puffed rice exterior was equally awesome. Must get!

Other notes:

- Super easy to make reservations via Yelp
- Automatic 15% service fee on bill so need need to tip extra unless you want to
- Parking garage conveniently located at Ghirardelli Square. Palette validates!
- There is patio seating, bar seating, and a private room available at the restaurant
- Gender neutral restroom

Bring a large group of your bougie friends and enjoy!

Food Review: I ordered tacos and tried 4 different meats (pastor, asada, chicken and carnitas).  The carnitas and pastor had a bit of flavor but lacked authenticity.  The carne asada and chicken tacos had absolutely zero flavor other than that of unseasoned meat. Also, my soft shell tacos were topped with lettuce, tomato and cheddar cheese instead of the traditional cilantro, onions and optional pickled jalapenos, carrots and onions.  Personally, I didn't care for the salsa because it was over-powered by a strong flavor of oregano and not enough heat.  Maybe they have a hotter version.

Personnel Review: Everyone I spoke to there was very nice and eager to please.

Summary: The preparation of my tacos leads me to believe that this is not a traditional Mexican restaurant and that maybe the American dishes that I saw on the menu might be a better selection. I don't get out to that city too often but I'd I do, I hope to update this rating at that time.

text:
This place has incredibly delicious food; let's start with that.  I came here for lunch the other day and ordered the chicken shawarma plate and four pieces of falafel.  My meal came with a small plate of sides (a kind of slaw with red cabbage, pickles, beets and carrots), pita bread and hummus, a salad, and rice.  Suffice it to say, this was a SUBSTANTIAL meal.

To start, the falafel at Ta-eem was some of the best I've had in a long time.  The outside was nice and crispy and crunchy, and the inside was moist, soft, flavorful and had a great texture; not too grainy, but also not too mushy.

As for the side dishes, it wasn't that they were bad, but I just wasn't particularly fond of them (except for the red cabbage slaw).  The red cabbage slaw was delicious and I loved it.  Looking back on it now, if I knew how much I'd like it, I would've asked for more of it in lieu of the other sides.

The main meal - the shawarma with rice, salad, hummus and pita bread - had a great balance in terms of what was served on the plate.  Everything complimented each other very well.  The salad was vibrant and refreshing, the hummus was full of flavor and not too thick or runny, and the chicken was well-seasoned without the meat being overpowered by other flavors.

I only had two very minor criticisms of this plate, which were that the rice was a bit under-seasoned and a tad over-cooked, and that the chicken was just a little too dry and cut up into too small pieces.

Beyond that, the entire meal was simply delicious and very satisfying.  In total, including tip, the meal cost me a little under $25, which was a great bargain considering the amount of food they gave me.

Would I come back again? Yes.  Would I recommend this place to friends?  Definitely.  Not only was the food good, but the service was very professional and expeditious, and the environment was warm and welcoming to the customers.

I ordered the lobster roll with mac and cheese, and my fiancé ordered the same with coconut fried rice. And the presentation is so casual, you wouldn't think it's necessarily a 5 star meal. They serve it in a basket with paper. But wow, it's good.

Then we couldn't resist ordering dessert, after a meal so outstanding. We ordered the key lime pie, and let me tell you... I don't enjoy key lime pie. But this was phenomenal and changed my mind. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone in the area. We would return for sure!

text: Our family of four came during DineLA so we ordered 2 of the DineLA menus and 2 entrees since we're not that big on desserts. The DineLA menu came with half a dozen oysters so we had a whole dozen. The type of oyster was nothing special--I wished we had ordered off their menu instead. They were pretty fresh but not very well cleaned since every single oyster, except for one, had shell remnants. I really liked the lobster roll, only con was how short it was--even the one we ordered off the regular menu (the DineLA lobster roll was half the size of the one we ordered off the regular menu). The french fries that were served with the lobster rolls were heavily seasoned and thus very salty. The DineLA seafood pasta we ordered was good but nothing special/memorable and I noticed it's not on the regular menu. Our favorite dish was the branzino which was deboned and had crisp skin. It was visually stunning and even the vegetables it was served with (potatoes and cherry tomatoes) were scrumptious. I'd come back just for the branzino. For dessert, we had the strawberry shortcake and the key lime pie. The shortcake was a bit dense but the strawberries were very fresh. The key lime pie was not too sweet and had the right combination of creaminess and tartness, one of the better key lime pies I've had. Note that only the key lime pie is available on the regular menu. The atmosphere of the place was nice but the tables are so close together that you definitely hear everything your neighbors say and that makes it a little awkward. The staff was friendly but I guess they're short-staffed because it took 20 minutes for us to get refills for our water glasses after I flagged them down twice.

text:
Unfortunately, my latest experience at Daphne's left me beyond disappointed. I ordered the new Mediterranean salad, 1 gyro combo, 2 new california gyros, a side soup and a 5 oz. side container of tzatziki sauce. The total came to a little over $41. When I arrived home I discovered that my sauce was missing. Thinking, I'd call and pick it up tomorrow, I retrieved my salad to satisfy the reason for my visit to begin with. To my surprise, there was a tiny container of tzatziki, only 1/3 filled and another of balsamic dressing. What a jip!!! After paying $10 for a salad, your going to nickel and dime me over salad dressing? I only say this because I did end up going back and was told by one of the workers that they are instructed to do that by the managers, who gets their directive from corporate, which is an investment firm.

Well, let the truth be told. Long ago it was, when the founder George Katakalidis dreamed of opening a restaurant where people could get fresh Greek food for a reasonable price. Btw, Wendy's currently has a yummy Mediterranean salad for a few bucks less.

name: Cynthia Thai
text: I was pleasantly surprised by this place! I recommend the plates because you get more meat and I like my laffa bread on the side (best laffa bread I've had) that I can dip into the Tahini sauce. I've had the pita sandwiches with the 5 sides you can choose  which is tasty but I don't like how it's not evenly distributed--yes I'm the type of person that makes sure the last bite of my burger has a little bit of everything). I've tried the chicken breast plate, shawarma pita sandwich, ribeye steak plate, and the middle eastern beef kabob plate. I liked all of the above but I thought the chicken breast was too thin for my liking--thin has its pros since it cooks faster and allows for more seasoning but also tends to be dry. I love the ribeye since it's cubed and sauteed with caramelized onions. The middle eastern kabob was fantastic seasoning and are like little hamburger patties to me. The sides I like are the french fries (they're the fresh type--think thicker in-n-out fries), israeli salad (chopped persian cucumbers, onions, bell peppers, tomato, parsley), and the hummus (because who doesn't like hummus). I love the pickles they offer when you dine-in, they're on the saltier side but they're scrumptious! PS I also really like the picked lemons.

name: Kadir Türkyilmaz
text:
(Translated by Google) HUMMUS BAR IN SANTA MONICA

In Los Angeles, one of the most popular places is arguably Santa Monica with its beautiful beach and theme park Pacific Park.

In 3rd Street are many shops and eateries. One of the most prominent places is the Hummus Bar Express, which specializes in Middle Eastern delicacies.

The store is very popular where it can be difficult to find seating at lunchtime.

We order a Hummus with Mushroom, Olive Oil and Parsley served with homemade flatbread.

Prices are moderate. We paid 11 USD, which amounts to 73 DKK.

Hummus Bar Express is above average and close to being a recommendable eatery for hummus lovers. The price is a little too high for the quantity, but the taste is quite good. In addition, we were happy that the number of calories was added to the menu at each dish.

(Original)
HUMMUS BAR I SANTA MONICA

I Los Angeles er en af de mest populære steder uden tvivl Santa Monica med sin smukke strand og forlystelsespark Pacific Park.

I 3rd Street ligger mange butikker og spisesteder. En af de mest fremtrædende steder er Hummus Bar Express, der har specialiseret sig i den mellemøstlige delikatesse.

Butikken er meget populær, hvor det kan være svært at finde siddepladser ved frokosttid.

Vi bestille en Hummus med Champignon, Olivenolie og Persille serveret med hjemmelavet fladbrød.

Priserne er moderate. Vi betalte 11 USD, hvilket beløber sig til 73 DKK.

Hummus Bar Express er over middel og tæt på at være et anbefalingsværdigt spisested for hummus-elskere. Prisen er lidt for høj i forhold til mængden, men smagen er ganske udmærket. Desuden var vi glade for at antal kalorier var tilføjet på menukortet ved hver ret.

Had lunch here with a friend who lives in Half Moon Bay.  The weather was beautiful but we decided to sit inside as the outside tables were not covered.  But we had a great view of the ocean below.  Such a pretty place.

We started with the Fried Calamari with cocktail and tartar sauces.  This had good flavor.  Not greasy.  Loved both sauces.

For entree, we both had the Grilled Prawn Salad - Roasted delicata pumpkin, Asian pear, wild arugula, frisee, pumpkin seeds, ricotta salata cheese, maple vinaigrette.  This was so good.  There were about 6 nice sized shrimp.  Good grill flavor.  Loved all of the other stuff on the salad.  The pumpkin and cheese were so tasty.

We got a free dessert for my birthday.  We had the GLUTEN FREE Warm Apple Crumble - House-made vanilla bean ice cream and almond, GF oatmeal crumble.  This was really good too.  Nicely cooked apples, good ice cream.

Overall a great lunch with good food.

text:
Although Din Tai Fung is know for their soup pork dumplings, I would have to say that as a Chinese-American who was brought up on authentic Chinese cuisine and culture, this isn't the place to order "the best" soup pork dumplings. Go elsewhere where the soup and pork filling are actually flavorful.

But of course, I'm not saying don't dine at Din Tai Fung. Otherwise, why would I give them 4 stars? Other items on their menu are superb and, in my opinion, outshines the soup pork dumplings.

A few to consider: noodle with sesame sauce (amazing), any fried rice selection, any vegetable dish, spicy wontons, beef noodle soup and the dessert buns like black sesame.

I eat at Din Tai Fung for everything else outside of the soup pork dumplings. You should, too!

Side salad w/ blue cheese dressing were good too. There is a full bar, great friendly fast service, did congress out of the kitchen HOT much like when dining in Ireland! The prices seem very reasonable, we'd definitely return! 💯 Social distancing, and Covid cleaning is up to snuff and this place seems populate with regulars and they've been here for decades. Nice outdoor seating available. Lots of televisions rubbed to sports. This is a step above most pubs in the states and on par with the best in Ireland! 🤩🍻Thank you to Baily for the friendly, fun high caliber service!! 🥰 Tip your servers generously if you can afford to, these really are tough times for the industry!

name: Stephen Metrulas
text:
I am never disappointed with The Habit.  The burgers smell delicious on the walk over.  Burger patties there are hot off the grill and well-seasoned.  My goto burger is the teriyaki pineapple burger, no cheese, no mayo, with lettuce wrap.  Minus points because I have to ask for no mayo on a teriyaki burger, that should be given, but I'll let them slide because the burger is so good.

My personal favorite side dish is the tempura green beans.  They don't need a sauce or dressing, they are perfect when they are hot and salty right out of the fryer.  I feel much healthier when I order them over a side of fries.

I also like the variety of special offerings next to the drink machine.  Adding jalapeños or banana peppers to my burger can be nice.  I haven't been in the dining room lately to enjoy those offering though.

Operationally, The Habit also offers better service relative to most other fast food restaurants.  While the ordering process is similar, the pickup process is superior.  Their paging puck system informs you when your order is ready, no need to stand at the counter and wait for a number call, just sit and enjoy yourself at the table while you wait.

Restaurant is styled nicely and always clean.  Seating has good variety of options for single, small and larger parties.  Outdoor dining has always been available, so if you can get a table you can enjoy a sunny day properly.

name: Jennifer Hunker
text:
The best place for pizza fixin's!

I was making a calzone and needed some good marinara sauce and pizza dough. I was feeling lazy and didn't want to make my own, and then I remembered Capri!

WHAT IT IS
An Italian deli. When you enter, you're standing in their storefront. To your left is a case full of delightful cookies. :) Further down this case you have your deli meats and cheeses, and a sandwich ordering station. To your right is the rest of the store where you can buy anything you need to make pizza. There is refrigerated dough and marinara sauce, cheeses, ect. Lots of pasta. If you pass through the storefront you'll find a seating area for people who decide to eat in.

WHAT YOU SHOULD ORDER
Sandwiches, or pizza stuff.

AMBIANCE
3 stars
Not nice, but not bad either. It's dated, but not in a terrible way. This is a quick lunch spot.

FOOD AND DRINKS
4 Stars
Capri's sandwiches are pretty good. They're FAR better than the likes of Subway (which is the sandwich Gulag), and the bread is great, but they die for better meat. If this place upgrades to Boar's Head you'll see a real sandwich contender.

Their pizza fixins and cookies, however, are phenomenal. If you need stuff to make pizza and are weirded out by making your own dough or sauce, this is the place to go.

NICE SURPRISES
Their chocolate thumbprint cookies remind me of my Italian Nana. :) Also it was really cool to find sauce here. I had initially just come for the dough.

OVERALL
A great local spot!

text: I have eaten at Mimi's for years and never had any problems with service or the food. Restaurants have problems pop up from time to time. How they handle those problems says a lot about the restaurant. We came in at about 1:30pm on a Sunday. In all fairness,  they were trying to get back to near normal seating. The waitress came out to take our order. We informed her that my daughter had a dairy allergy. My daughter wanted to order a burger, so we asked the waitress if she could check if any of their buns or bread was dairy free. The waitress came back, said that all their buns and bread had dairy, and took our order. We told her absolutely no cheese on the burger. We also told her my daughter wanted the burger cooked medium. When the food was brought out there was cheese on my daughters burger! We told the waitress and all she said was OK. No apologies for messing up the order or possibly exposing my daughter to something she was allergic to. My wife's meal was supposed to come with bread and it didn't. We had to wait until the meal was over to get her bread. I ordered a salad with blue cheese dressing. The dressing was like water. My wife's potatoes were covered in oil. My daughters bacon was soft and not good. After the meal was over we talked to the manager. It was obvious that he had no idea about food allergies. The manager told us that all of his buns and breads contained eggs so they were not dairy free. We had to explain that eggs are not dairy. The manager apologized for the poor meal. We had already paid for our meal, so the manager offered to pay for our next meal. Hopefully they have things figured out the next time we go back. We were greatly disappointed.

text: Think you've had good falafels before? Well you haven't tried this place. Located off of Market Street in a small walk-up window, this place has some of the best vegan food that I have ever had. We usually order the half pocket falafel with all the fixings. I love how fluffy the pita pockets are and the sesame and spicy falafels are perfectly seasoned and cooked. The pocket is typically dressed with lettuce, tomato and tzatziki sauce. I always get and extra side of the sauce plus some spicy sauce. The other mind blowing item on their menu is the banana shake. This is no regular milkshake, it is a vegan shake. Dairy sometimes does me dirty, so this milkshake is perfect to indulge in. I wish the location is San Jose tasted as amazing as the SF location, but sadly the only thing that is the same is their name. Overall, if you're craving a falafel and a delicious banana shake then definitely check this spot out.

name: Layla Habahbeh
text:
Blazing Stone Pizza makes one of the best pizzas I've ever had in the Los Angeles area, and even just in general!

This place is family owned and operated and has a friendly small-town vibe about it. My boyfriend and I got to talk to the chef for awhile - he has been a pizza chef for 15 years and is super passionate about what he does and it shows in the quality you get!

The ingredients are fresh, there is plenty of delicious mozzarella cheese, and the dough is to die for. We tried the thin crust (which is not as paper thin as the usual thin crust, but thinner than normal), and the hearty crust (amazing.. they fold the crust over part of the pizza so that you get your toppings inside each bite of the crust).

We've only tried the rustic sauce so far, which is delicious, but can't wait to try the blazing next time. Update: Tried the blazing sauce - it's great and has a little kick, but I like the rustic by far.

They have a 12" and 18" pizza. Compared to other pizza places in town, it's a little pricey, but I really don't mind paying a few extra bucks for top-notch ingredients and flavor that is difficult to find in this area.

Other pros: Outdoor patio seating, accept credit cards, offer delivery.
Minor cons: Parking is street only

name: Jennifer Hunker
text:
WHAT IT IS
A fine dining Asian fusion steakhouse.

WHAT YOU SHOULD ORDER
Dry aged or wagyu steak.

AMBIANCE
5 stars
This place is BEAUTIFUL, as a fine dining establishment should be. Absolutely romantic, modern, and well thought out.

When you first enter, you'll be looking at the maître d'. There are some nice benches to your right where you can sit and wait until she's ready to seat you--the bar is across from this. The room is dark and very intimate. The seating areas are split up into smaller "rooms" which hold about six tables each. They were quiet, and intimate. All of the waiters and servers wear suits and ties, and the tables are neatly set. In between courses, the servers freshen up your silverware and plates.

FOOD AND DRINKS
5 Stars
Absolutely beyond phenomenal. The prices are high, but the quality is worth it. This is a fantastic place to go for an anniversary or birthday.

We started with a complimentary sparkling wine as it was our anniversary. It was delicious! While they have an extensive wine list, we opted for water after this. The waiter also brought us a tiny little surprise--a bit of tomato sorbet to whet our appetites!

For our opening course we opted for hamachi shooters. They're mentioned in practically every review for Alexanders and for good reason. They're refreshing, a bit acidic, and a wonderful start to the evening. The hamachi was incredibly fresh.

For our next course, we opted for the grilled pork belly with pears. This was by far the most adventurous thing we ended up getting, and was absolutely incredible. The pear cream and saffron pears just complimented the seared pork belly so perfectly--it just all melted in your mouth. My hubby is not a fan of fruit with his meat, and he was left speechless by this course. Ah-maze-ing.

Our next course was the complimentary bread basket. The breads they serve are interesting--squid ink, this delicious garlic thing, and japanese sweet bread. They come with three butters as well: a marrow butter, a sweet butter, and a salted butter. All of the breads were fantastic, but that garlic bread--my god. It was the most delicious garlic bread I've ever had in my life.

Next course was the steak course. My husband got the bone in dry aged new york steak, and WOW. I had a bite, and I will not even kid here--it was the most delicious steak I've ever tasted. I have never experienced texture like this in a steak--silky smooth, and absolutely amazing. I had opted for the filet mignon, but after tasting that dry aged steak, it paled in comparison. Still a delishious filet, but the new york strip was THAT good.

For the desert course, we opted for "Chocolate", the chef's take on a chocolate lava cake (deconstructed, of course). It was a spongy and delicious served with white chocolate coulant, a bitter chocolate cremeux, and cocoa nib ice cream.

It's important to note here that I am not a big fan of overly sweet things. I eat around cake icing. I prefer subtle, gentle tastes, and this desert was choc full of them. The varying textures, the almost custard-like marrow--it was absolutely phenomenal, and I'm honestly tempted to go back to Alexander's just for the desert alone!

But even after this, we weren't done. The chef sent us a complimentary piece of champagne cake for our anniversary (which we ate despite feeling like we were going to explode), and then out came more treats: Green Apple (freshly spun) cotton candy, delicious macaroons, and bon bons! It was all just incredible.

NICE SURPRISES
All the free things, and the personalized anniversary card signed by the head chef himself. This was the best anniversary we have had and was well worth the price of admission.

OVERALL
If you're looking for a place to have a REAL night out (and are sick of chain food), come here. It is expensive, but you'll enjoy a meal (and experience) that is well worth the cost. The dinner is LONG, too--we were there for three full hours and were never rushed. The food comes out at a great pace, and just makes the whole evening feel so intimate and special.

text: The pizza was pretty good, but the service was pretty bad. I ordered a large pizza with 2 toppings on half and 2 toppings on the other half. Not very complicated, and, I had her repeat the order back to me so I knew she had it right. It took a pretty long time, probably 20 minutes, for it to come out and when the cook hands it to her, I can see her open the box and realize that the cook made it wrong and start explaining to him why. At the end of the explanation she says this very sympathetic "I'm sorry" to the cook, because apparently she feels bad that he's mad because he messed up. She then goes about her business and never once stopped by our table to give us an update. Like nothing happened. So another 20 minutes goes by and out comes the new pizza. She looks at it again with the cook to verify if it's right. This time it is, but still, after verifying that it was right, she appologizes to the cook again for the inconvenience of having to make it twice. She brings it to us and says "Here you go." Not even a comment to us about why it took so long or even acknowledge that it took longer that it would have taken Dominoes to deliver. So, she apologized twice to the cook who screwed up, and not a single word about it to the customer who is paying for it. What she didn't know is that we aren't picky eaters, and we were starving, so chances are if she had just been honest and upfront, we likely would have eaten that first pizza in spite of whatever was wrong with it. Instead, she wasted a large pizza, a bunch of our time, and made a really bad impression. Mistakes happen. Trying to conceal them just makes them worse. I probably would not go here again, just because of that service.

name: My Le
text:
I’ve lived in Poway for three decades now and have tried many Thai restaurants in Poway but somehow missed this one when it’s the closest to where I live!

I ordered crab fried rice, duck pad see ew, and curry puff chicken on line. Not many places make crab fried rice so I had to try it. My go to for a new place is to try the pad Thai but this time I went with Pad see ew. For a protein, I was excited to see duck as an option.

The app said pick up in 30mins so when I got there my order was ready at the front door. Dine in options is closed at this place and only available for take out.

The containers were carefully lined in foil to keep the dish moist and from leaking.

The crab fried rice was average but it had lots of broken crab pieces. I got this as a level one and it was not spicy at all. I got the pad see ew with no spice and it was sweet. The duck was a great amount not stingy like most places. It was juicy not dry. Thai dishes tend to be sweet if not spicy. Still very good. The curry puff was delicious. Again, this was sweet. It came with a vinegar dipping sauce but I didn’t use it.

The portions were generous where I had left overs the next day. Looking forward to try other dishes.

name: Jonathan Marinaro
text:
For those Gastronauts willing to explore Bavarian culture through its food and drink, Teske's is your place.

Teske's Germania provides the atmosphere and cuisine found in the mountains and foothills of Germany, with the Chef picking exotic cuts like fresh wild boar to bring a slice of the Black Forest to your table. The menu is a little on the expensive side for both lunch and dinner, but many of the entrees should be shared as the Schweine Haxe's braised boar shank with schnitzel is enormous.

The bar fits the bill with an extensive bottle selection, a few standards on tap, and a couple rotating taps with something new. You can get your mug full of frothy pilsener or hefeweisen, but I recommend a look at their list of schnapps, little fruit and herb cordials that are quite varied. If beer is something you're there for particularly, choose something off their bottle menu or talk to one of the knowledgeable bartenders, they'll help you find something you didn't know you love!

text: This was our first visit to the Blue House. The hostess seemed annoyed when we asked her to explain how the menu worked. Maybe she was having a bad day. This is a Korean BBQ restaurant where you can choose to cook your food at your table or order off the menu. I was hesitant to pay the $27 per person price, at first, for all you can eat. You have a two hour time limit. You can order four items at a time. Once an item runs out you can order an additional item. The meal also comes with rice and sides like kimchi, cucumber kimchi, pickled dicon etc. We decided to go with the all you can eat. It just seemed like a better deal. I am glad we did because we got our money's worth. The food was excellent! My daughter really enjoyed being able to cook our own food. It sure made it so there was no reason to pull out cell phones or be distracted. Our family actually talked through the entire meal. Service was excellent! Our server was always nearby if we wanted our needed anything. The beef and chicken bulgogi were amazing! We weren't very impressed with the brisket since it had no kind of marinade on it. We dipped it in the soy sauce they gave us before putting it on the grill. It added a lot of flavor. The ribeye and ribs were also very good. We had a great overall experience! We will definitely go back! The prices are a little expensive, but well worth it for all the food you get.

text:
I've now eaten at Frances twice and can say it is definitely my favorite restaurant in the city. What I love about Frances is that the food is impeccably prepared but not overworked. All of Chef Perello's culinary decisions seem centered around letting each ingredient reach its fullest potential.

Many people will tell you that it is impossible to get a table at Frances, but if you are in the neighborhood they leave a few seats unreserved at the front of the restaurant and if you are willing to wait you can probably snag a table. It is a bit of a crap shoot, but definitely worth a try.

Highlights for me are the bacon beignets (a perfect combination of my two favorite things in this world) and the duck liver mousse, which may be the best appetizer I've ever had in my life. It was flawless!

name: liang xin
text:
My friend and I came to San Francisco for a work trip, and booked a special dinner at Frances based on the positive Yelp reviews--and we were not disappointed. The experience started upon entry into the tasteful but small restaurant, and every detail was accounted for right down to the lovely and simple wine carafe. The wait-staff were attentive and served every need with a smile. We had the applewood smoked bacon beignet's and the pasta with broccoli rabe, and both were simply prepared and delicious. The fish entree was very good but lacked a little bit of heartiness in the side dish, and the duck entree was even better with perfectly seasoned and cooked meat. We finished with the 'lumberjack' cake dessert that left us drooling for more.
Would definitely recommend Frances for an intimate and perfect dining experience.

Service at the bar was a bit slow, but everything else was fantastic. With the market shots (small cocktails) at $3, you can't lose. Bacon beignets are good, dungeness crab salad with satsumas even better. The duck leg was also awesome, and I enjoyed the unique desserts. Solid list of wines by the glass. name: Gregory Clift
text: The best part about riding through Marshall, CA on a bicycle is stopping for oysters. There's a few places along the water in town to get some but we just happened to stop here. Fairly pricey since the oysters come out of the water close by, but what you gonna do when you are hungry and ready to go?! There was a little bit of confusion about where customers could enjoy alcohol with their food. There is an indoor area, an outdoor seating area close to the store and a long table leading north away from the store. This long table is the only place where one can have beer/wine with food. Kinda silly, but whatever. There are also sodas and non-alcoholic drinks which I would have bought instead of the beer had I known that we were going to be shunted off to a crowded table. We grabbed the last two available seats and settled in. Our food was brought out by a server. The oysters were great and came with a vinegar/some sort of chopped green vegetable sauce that cut the saltiness of the oysters very well. I also enjoyed some hot sauce with mine. Overall, a perfect pit stop if you are traveling south down Highway 1 in the area of Tomales Bay.

name: Kimberly R. Kelly
text: The Marshall Store has certainly blossomed over the past decade. It appears the influx of tech money to SF has made its way north to Tomales Bay. The Marshall Store is busier and busier with every visit and the prices, which used to be a steal of a deal, are now a bit on the "whaaaa?" side. Still, THE BEST GRILLED OYSTERS PERIOD. It's always a nice treat when crab is in season and one can order the massive dungeness crab sandwich. And, I love the addition of the new(ish) large wine and beer case. So many options. Thank you for existing, Marshall Store. Please don't change (any more than you already have).

text:
I have mixed feelings after my first visit here. They may have had an off day as the joint was jumping at five o'clock on a weekday. Took about 20 minutes to get my order to go. Who goes out to eat at 5pm on a weekday?

Anyway... ordered to go; 2 meat plate w/2 sides (baby back ribs, brisket, cole slaw, and corn bread). This was a lot of food and half the brisket went into the fridge for maybe a sandwich tomorrow.

When I got home I took a quick sample of the brisket. I found it a little too fatty and a bit underdone for me. The ribs also 'looked' a bit the same. No problem, as I planned to reheat it a bit later and I just left the meat in the oven a bit longer (about 25 minutes at 350).

After a visit with the oven, both the ribs and the brisket were great. Ribs were fall off the bone tender, and the brisket was much more appetizing with a little more cooking time. Very tasty, but brings me to the conclusion that if I was served this there, I would have either had to send it back (something I rarely ever do), or just be pretty unhappy with my food.

The slaw and corn bread were OK, but nothing special. I will try the beans and/or potato salad next time.

On exiting the parking lot I saw a sign which may explain why this place was jumping on a weekday afternoon... "$2 Taco Tuesday". Nothing like cheap to get them rolling through the doors like oranges.

I will definitely try this place again (just not on a Tuesday), and ask for edge cuts if possible.

Update: Since my first visit here I am upping the place to 5 stars. Loving the baby back plate so much I order it almost every visit. The sides have been improved as well. Very tasty place

name: Allan Santiago
text:
Producing dishes that look just as difficult to prepare as they are to pronounce, the cooks at Dyafa make it seem effortless. The service certainly lives up to its Arabic namesake making you feel like you are being welcomed into a unique dining experience.

Geographically centered bites promise something you likely have never thought to have. Prime example is Kibbeh Nayyeh, a plate of flavored raw ground lamb with oil, a seven-spice blend (baharat), topped with pickled turnips and marinated red onions. Unless you have been to where it's originated, or had someone prepare it for you, you have never had this. It's beautiful, flavorful, and rivals any high-end sashimi in texture. A must-have.

The bread is memorable in and of itself, made in-house from dough that was produced the night prior, making this the most flavorful pita I've ever had. For those that do not mind the carbs, the pita serves as a perfect receptacle for all bites.

Every dish requires a moment to slow down and think about the flavors, textures, to the point you realize you've had nothing else like it. I knew the lamb shank was to be masterful judging by the 'wiggle' it had when placed. I mean a literal wiggle, indicating a gelatinous structure delivering a creamy, melt-in-your-mouth savory experience.

The fish didn't impress. Though well seasoned and cooked, its saltiness put an abrupt halt to the melds of flavors one had just experienced. Juxtaposed with the shank, the fish becomes shadowed and secondary.

Overall, you must come into this dining experience with a blank slate. To categorize this meal as "middle eastern" places a disservice to the finished product. Dyafa transcends what a home-cooked meal is, and finds a way to bring forth a modern dining experience with effortless traditional flair.

text:
If you love Taiwanese food, Yi Mei is the spot. The restaurant is fairly new and very clean. They're located in the same plaza as luscious dumpling in Monrovia.

My friend brought me here to have their Taiwanese rice rolls. I've had this at many other places in the SGV before but the made-to-order rice rolls here are definitely the best. I order the salted rice roll, which has the pork sung and Chinese donut. I also add a fried egg and Chinese pickles. For $4.75, the rice roll is very filling. You can also add a cold or hot soy milk to make it a combo for just $1 more.

Other than the rice rolls they're known for, Yi Mei has all your Taiwanese favorites of noodle and rice. They also have baked items and a cold fridge of prepared food. I haven't tried their Taiwanese tamales yet but it seems to be another popular item there.

The restaurant is cash only. You order at the counter and self-seat. The food come out quickly and the service is good.

text:
I’ve been here twice now. The first time was an ok experience. We did not use the paid playroom because my son was too young at the time. He did enjoy the sandbox.

Our second visit will likely be our last. We arrived and I asked how long the wait would be. The hostess was very evasive and wouldn’t actually answer this very basic question. I ended up talking to the manager and she told me it would be at least 30 min for the table currently being cleaned. Which didn’t make sense since no one else was waiting. I asked her to please check the waiting list so I could get an idea of the wait time. She said she would then proceeded to go do a bunch of other things and got annoyed when I asked her again. This is all just to answer the simple question of how long to wait for a table. There were quite a few visibly empty tables at this point.

Turns out there was no one else waiting and we did get that table. It would have been nice to just have been given a polite straightforward answer. Our service was terrible. We had to ask for things multiple times. The kids food came out last. We had to find our own napkins and silverware. We were not offered any drink refills. And we were overcharged on the bill.

Overall it was a very unwelcoming experience. And they did not appear to be adequately staffed not sure if that is due to competence or numbers.

The sand box area that used to be accessible to let you kids play was made less useful by having a giant outdoor tent. There was no longer a direct path and line of visibility to watch your child play so an adult had to get up to watch them.

This place seems like a great idea, but today’s visit showed that with such poor service it’s just not a place to take your family.

name: Ted White
text:
This space is a hidden gem.  Old school, cash only, single-page menu kind of gem.  They've been open in 1947, counter service only.  Hang out by the front until you see a space open up.

You really can't go wrong with anything on the menu, they say they're committed to doing a few things very well, and they knock it out of the park.  Order whatever you like, get some homemade pie afterwards.  Personally, I like ordering coffee, because it's the only thing served in an actual dish aside from the pie.

Go here!  It's one of my favorite spots in the world, let alone LA.  Perfect for friends or family visiting from out of town and well worth the trip.

BEST, BETTER, GOOD The Sunnyside setting on the western shore of Lake Tahoe is magnificent, what with the powerful beauty of the water and waves . . . the expansive views up and down the shoreline to the north and south . . . and the far-off 7,000 ft.+ snowcapped mountains to the south . . . it's hard to imagine another setting could best this one. Then there's the deck-to-die-for out back, adorned with colorful umbrellas and graced with cooling winds off the lake, always packed as this is a fan fav bristling with the energy of happy weekenders and vacationers. There's a new chef, too, Robb Wyss with some time under his belt here after the previous 25-year vet moved on. The new guy's from Chicago and has energized the menu to the delight of repeat customers. The lunch offerings are good, particularly the local wagyu burger, the short rib nachos, the carnitas torta, and the salmon rice bowl. Fried zucchini has been on the menu since 1965, for good reason.

At dinner Alaskan halibut, Nantucket scallops, Petaluma Moroccan chicken, elk strip loin, hanger steak, and house pappardelle with summer veg ratatouille are all offered. Sides include truffle garlic fries and bacon mac 'n cheese.

Then, they stopped selling the orange Hi-C. I loved that drink. No one else sells that drink. Who asked McDonalds to change it? Did they ask their customers before changing? I'm sure many would have said no.
Lets talk about their menu. What is up with that? This is good OLD McDonalds we're talking about. Not a fru-fru artsy drive thru that they are trying to change their image to appear to be. They have been around since the 60's. People, I'm sure, enjoyed their classic look and menu selection along with the prices. I do agree some things needed to change like adding another drive thru lane, pos, modernize it but not over do it. text:
Meh. Trying to impart what they think is a farm fresh image to ordinary but decent enough triteful food concoctions at exhorbitant prices better suited to a real restaurant with real table service & real cloth napkins.

The flippant yet adequately polite demeanor of the forward facing staff is consistent among locations, indicating a corporate molding whipped into those willing to feign politeness while covering an otherwise visible employee fear to not incur the wrath of supervisors beholden to what appears to be a very real & strict home office ideal of obedience.

This uncomfortable atmosphere is reinforced vis-a-vis a breathtaking choice of ambient audio pretending to be music but in reality is what amounts to be an unrelenting indelicate pounding into your brain of overt political screeds performed by unremarkable unknowns, just untalented enough to be ignored in the real world, even as amateurs.

Navigating their version of what many eating establishments offer in these dizzying digital days is not merely a chore of confounding curiousness, it presents an unusually amusing example of what *not* to design into any loyalty app, especially if it is to be at any time useful at all in any event at anytime anywhere for anything but pointed humor.

Finally, to have gone there to eat in the first place is to very definitely & very soon wish you had instead gone elsewhere for even just a cup of what they presume you will accept is coffee.

That's my 11 cents.

The cook probable thought blackened fish and blackened chicken are the same! No, its just burnt chicken. The whole sandwich had to be deconstructed on the plate and consumed scattershot with knife and fork. Eating it was a mess. Given the rising Ca. text:
Park Tavern is a welcome reprieve from the myriad Italian restaurants in North Beach. The food is excellent and decor is among my favorite in the bay area. It is modern while still feeling functional, and most importantly, you don't feel crammed into the space. I don't know why, but I am obsessed with the wall paper used in the back room and bathrooms. Everything just feels so well done.

As far as the food, it is a funny mix of a menu. There are some very southern things such as the best deviled eggs I've ever had and fried brussel sprouts, along with other high french fare such as a crab and lobster bisque. While eclectic, it doesn't feel gimmicky.

name: A Google User
text:
Park Tavern is designed to be perfect for any occasion -- birthdays, business meetings, catchups with friends, anything. It has a great atmosphere, thanks to the excellent design of the place.

The service was absolutely incredible. From the hostess to the bar server to our wonderful dining server, Emily, everything was on-point. We had to add 2 people last-minute to our table, and Emily graciously and happily helped us move to another table halfway through our meal. It really made our experience that much more enjoyable.

The food was a hit or miss for us. I'm a fan of Marlowe, so I was expecting the same level of excellence here, but it was just lacking a bit when compared to Marlowe.

----------------------------
FOOD:

Deviled Eggs = Delicious. Everything goes together perfectly.

Brussels Sprouts Chips = Addictive as always. Can't go wrong here.

PT Fries = Good, but nothing spectacular. The caviar wasn't salty enough to bring the flavors together between the egg yolk and the aioli. Half of the fries were overfried.

Grilled Pork Chop = Tender for the most part and had a pure flavor to it. It wasn't exciting, but it was definitely a well-cooked pork chop.

Mussels and Clams = This was good, but again, nothing exciting.

3 Variations of Duck = I had high hopes for this one, but again, it fell short. The duck breast was a bit dry, the duck confit was a bit overcooked, the duck skin wasn't crispy enough, and the duck liver mousse was too watery. The flavors were all there, it just could've been so much better. Plus, the beans didn't really add anything beneficial to the dish.

Venison Tartare = This dish was a great attempt, but was definitely lacking in execution. The beef tartare was good, but it was missing something with a bit more umami (for instance, it could've used some sesame oil or quail egg). The deep-fried bone marrow is an interesting idea, but was completely lackluster in execution. The bits of bone marrow were easily overpowered by the breading and it just tasted like fried oil.

Hamachi Crudo w/ Gin & Tonic = This dish wasn't good at all. There was no depth or excitement whatsoever -- it needed a couple of extra layers of flavor (something salty, something tangy) to really make the hamachi pop. text:
This is a long overdue review of Hillside Supper Club. We had our rehearsal dinner there in July of 2013 (I knooooooooow... a while ago, but I've been busy).

We were excited about the idea of having our rehearsal dinner just down the street from where we live at a restaurant opened by two young chefs who partially funded through kick-starter (my hub's secret addiction). We wanted to do most everything that we could locally for our wedding (this includes our rehearsal dinner). I worked in restaurants for a long time, so I think that this gives me a unique perspective about what is/is not reasonable to ask of a restaurant (especially a new one). Asking to do dinner for 15-20 people between 7 and 8 is not reasonable for most restaurants on a Friday or Saturday night, and if you do, you should be prepared for disappointment. So, we did an early dinner. 5:30pm. This was great because we had impromptu cocktails after dinner at Wildside West (which aside from their grumpy bartender, was AWESOME).

Our rehearsal dinner (like our wedding dinner) was family style, and honestly, I think this is the best way to serve a group of people (and keep them all happy). The food comes out at the same time, it's all hot, and if you want more it's on the table right in front of you.

I called and spoke with one of the chef's brothers, and then received an email from Tony (chef). I like corresponding via email. It's all in writing, and easily referenced. Plus I don't like talking on the phone.

The menu we decided on:
Market Salad
Chorizo Casoulette
Pork Shoulder with Peach Slaw
Assortment of current desserts

A leap of faith: we didn't eat at Hillside Supper Club until the week before the wedding. My husband was out of town a lot that summer, and it was the only time we could make it in. As we hoped, we loved our trial dinner. Phew!

The night before the wedding, parking was easy, even though it was a Friday night (BONUS, this is SF, and we had quite a few people driving). I got there early with flowers in vases (gifts for the women in the wedding party). Hillside had beautiful flowers on the table already. The table was set in an L-shape, which was perfect for conversation. Dinner came out at a great pace. The food was wonderful. It was a beautiful, low-key, rehearsal dinner. We couldn't have asked for anything more.

Thanks so much Hillside for coming through for us, and hosting an amazing rehearsal dinner!!!!

name: Ruiping Gao
text:
A phenomenal meal!

Came here with a group of 5 friends. We were able to request to be seated together at the communal table. We got in a few minutes late, so we were ushered upstairs to join the rest of the dining guests. We were served quite a few small tasters and offered drinks. After probably 20 minutes we took our seats and the actual meal started. If you are a drinker, would suggest getting the wine pairings to go along with the meal. The sommeliers was around explaining the wine after every plate. The chef also stops and discusses every plate and how it’s constructed. You have a little field guide to write down notes.

Diners are encouraged to walk around and meet the chefs who have created the meal. Everyone was very excited to talk diners through the process of where the ingredients came from and how it was cooked and plated. The night ended with another round of drinks/coffee and desserts.

(The bread and butter, ask for seconds!)

text:
One of the best food experiences I have ever had. It's quite the dining experience.

At first the sticker price was shocking but this was a special event. Well worth the price, the staff was very pleasant and the chefs we're very open to explaining everything they were doing.

This is a dinner experience with two long tables that seat everyone. They have it set like a family dinner encouraging you to meet and talk with others. The wine option was exceptional and they came by for refills during the meals. With the wine pairing they set a new wine with each dish.

Overall I want disappointed, or left hungry. I had feared that since this was my first coursed meal ever. My girlfriend and I still talk about it to this day. So treat yourself And/or someone special to a once in a lifetime experience!

name: Jeanne Lam
text:
For my annual birthday celebration with my friends, I booked Lazy Bear and it was everything I imagined it to be.

It was a magical 3 hour, well executed, unpretentious, intimate and delicious dining experience I won't forget. The best part was it wasn't one of those expensive meals where you left hungry. My contingency plan was to grab a bacon wrapped hot dog right outside in the Mission if I was still hungry, but I left the restaurant completely satisfied.

Our dinner before drinks was about $280/pp. We opt out of the regular wine pairing which was $95/pp and ordered a $17 signature cocktail instead. Altogether, we spent roughly $300/pp and it was well worth it. Our neighbors had the wine pairing and really enjoyed it, so I might splurge a bit more the next time I return.

Now, let's get to the food!

My ultimate favorite dishes were the lobster, lamb, salmon, kohlrabi, and matsutake respectively.

There were a total of 14 courses. We started with a glass of punch and 5 snacks upstairs. Once we got seated downstairs in the main dining hall, we were served a house roll, 7 more dishes, followed by a platter of 3 desserts.

SNACKS (served upstairs)

- Whipped Scrambled Eggs [bacon, maple, hot sauce] - we were instructed to dig deep with our spoons to get to the spicy maple syrup. This was a nice start to whet our palettes.

- Canterelle and Goat Cheese Tart [Lisa's "BoDacious", pickled pluot, sunflower] - light and crisp goat cheese over a tart

- Modori Gatsuo Tataki [preserved allium pancake, nasturtium flower relish] - fish over a thin pancake

- Broiled Shigoku Oyster [smoked pumpkin, wild fennel] - one of my favorite snacks. This was a cooked oyster and I had first pick from a tray. Yay!

- Duck Liver Mousse [mountain huckleberry, cornbread] - it looked like a truffle and I popped it in my mouth

DINNER - served in the dining hall (downstairs)

- Spelt & Rye parker house roll [cultured butter] - the 7 year old cured butter was the best part. I gobbled every bit of this and seconds were offered. The bread itself was soft and fluffy on the inside and crispy on the outside. It was well balanced and light.

- Kohlrabi [smoked sturgeon, vin jaune, Lazy Bear Reserve Caviar by Tsar Nicoulai] - loved the texture of the kohlrabi. It was fresh, with a light crunch and smothered in a creamy caviar sauce.

- SF Coast King Salmon [grilled cucumber, buttermilk, coastal greens] - the salmon cut like butter

- Fall Squash [lobster bay, carolina gold rice] - the combo of the lobster bisque and gold rice was something special

- Matsutake [conifers, shinko pears] - I loved the flavor of mushroom broth and the pears made it

- BBQ Rack of Lamb [brassicas, black olives, date barbeque] - this was decadent! The lamb was the perfect temperature and well seasoned. You'll have to pick this up with your hand to get every bit of morsel off the bone. It was paired with a salty butter pie which was rich in flavor and too intense for me to finish with the exquisite lamb. At this point, I was getting full.

- Green Goddess [apple, juniper, creme fraiche] - perfectly refreshing after the lamb

- Honeynut Squash [chicory, masa, palm sugar] - not very memorable but it could be because I'm full

TREATS
- Pluot Gummy Bear [olive oil] - one big plum gummy bear
- Cookies 'N' Cream Bon Bon [white chocolate] - delicious!
- Black Truffle Cream Puff [honey] - you can definitely taste the truffle

Thank you Lazy Bear for the amazing experience! The staff are pretty awesome and fun too :)

They were also the consistency of a kitchen sponge.  They were not the size displayed on their menu and they were just a poor excuse for what this place is know for.  So, for my first visit to this chain, I have to say that it was a complete failure.  I sent them back and ordered a croissant breakfast sandwich. text:
Brunch at Madera: We tried the eggs benedict with smoked salmon ($18) and the lump crab meat frittata ($21), along with a champagne mojito ($13). We asked for bread, which was a delicious, soft focaccia served with butter. The eggs benedict dish was overall excellent, but the eggs were poached a bit more than they should have been. The frittata was a disappointment, the crab meat was not very discernible and the dish just wasn't tasty, except for the tomato marmalade that came with it. The mojito was perfect. On this visit the wait staff could have been better; we had empty water and coffee ($5) cups for too long, and the restaurant wasn't full.

Madera Lounge: Complimentary bar snacks (olives, nuts, popcorn) are better than average, a nice touch. Good views, when its not so much of a scene you can't see it. Excellent Asian pear vodka cocktail. The burger is fine, while the accompanying fries were really good. On a separate visit, the fries ordered alone were a tad too crisp. The tuna tartare is a generous portion (though inexplicably few wonton chips come with it) and worth ordering.

We went there on Mother's Day. Instead of being a nice celebratory lunch, it was a nightmare. They had a pre fix menu at $30 per adult. In spite of calling ahead, it took a while to get seated (outside, without any umbrellas or shades). When I had called, I was told by the manager that they were restricting guests to 90 minutes. I thought, 90 minutes for a pre fix menu should work. The appetizers arrived about 60 minutes after we were seated. The soup and salad were delivered to the table approximately 30 minutes later. Main course didn't arrive. Desserts were brought in. I asked about the delay.

The manager started arguing and saying how he has 15 years of experience in the food service industry. Then, he started arguing with the guests on the next table. He started yelling at the guest saying how he was the only person who had a problem. I had to tell the manager that I had a problem with his attitude, the delay, and the food. The guest on the next table said that he would write on yelp, to which the manager said Go Ahead. The guest asked if he could speak with the owners and the manager said, no - they're busy. What a great way to run a new restaurant!

Oh boy! Never had such an experience in my life. I had a lot of respect for Sanjeev Kapoor, but if he's signing franchise deals with people like this, I feel sorry for him. It's pulling brand Sanjeev Kapoor down.

But I should have guessed. The Buena Park location has pretty bad reviews too. Mr. Kapoor, are you listening?

text:
Yelp kind of ruined the experience at Barton G for me. Specifically, all the photos that were uploaded for the restaurants. Barton G has decent food but the wow factor was supposed to be all the over-the-top presentation of all the dishes. I already knew what to expect for all the dishes we ordered from looking at the picture so I wasn't impressed when everything came out.

The first course was popcorn shrimp. It came in a giant popcorn machine that sat on the table. The dish was okay but there was just not enough space on a table for 2 for the entire thing. Our entrees were about the same in size and it was so hard trying to eat when there's no room.

I got to try 3 entrees: lobster mac n cheese, short ribs, and the cod. The fish was my favorite dish of the night. The fish was perfectly cooked and the butter sauce was delicious. The short ribs was very tender and flavorful. The lobster mac n cheese was pretty cheesy.

The desserts was absurdly large. The brownie sundae had 6 pieces of brownies, 3 giant scoops of ice cream and topped with a mountain of whipped cream and chocolate sticks, chocolate rice crispies, and gold chocolate leaf. It's enough to feed an army.

Their drinks are just okay. They do have a decent wine selection.The price was quite exorbitant for pretty much everything. The cost per person was anywhere from $100-$200 depending on if you end up drinking or not. The food tasted great but I don't think I would be willing to pay that much for it.

Oveall, I would say skip it. For that kind of money, I would rather go to one of the better restaurants in LA.
