text:
Small seasonal menus keep food delicious and priced well.  It's cute and funky inside, hand-written menus, aprons strung across the restaurant, booths along two walls.  Service is always great.  Food is delicious comfort food, portions are huge.

Garlic bread: buttered with herbs and garlic, crispy toasted.  Not smothered in cheese, but buttery, garlic-y and perfect.

Barry's Caesar Salad: 3 of us shared this, it was HUGE.  Dressed perfectly, with super crisp Romaine. It's a great salad to share between 2-4 people.

Spaghetti and Meatballs: Someone in another review mentioned the "meat boulders" which made me laugh... and then we saw the meatballs, they're HUGE.  I really enjoyed the tomatoe-y sauce.  The meatballs were delish too.  A meatier-style meatball, it didn't seem to have a lot of bread inside if any.

Fettucine with Spicy Italian Sausage, Roasted Cauliflower, Parmesan Cream Sauce, topped with Herbed Bread Crumbs: really, really yummy.  The cauliflower and spicy sausage balanced the richness of the dish.  The bread crumbs were added some crunch. Yum.

Doughnut: So good. So good. So good.

Orange Blossom Martini: very nice.  Not too sweet, citrusy and clean.

The High Roller: super nice. We could smell the vanilla, we could taste the lemon.

There were 3 of us: we ordered a small garlic bread and Caesar salad to share, 2 spaghetti and meatballs, one fettucine, and the doughnut to share.  We went home with half of the fettucine and a whole order of spaghetti and meatballs, which is fine if you like leftovers (which we do).

The only thing: it was way too loud for us inside. I've worked at restaurants for years and years, including ones that always have the music too loud (the result is that I'm a little hard of hearing, I swear, and it was still too loud for me in there!!!).  Maybe it was just that night?  At any rate, we found ourselves leaning across the table and yelling a bit.  If the volume of the music could go down a bit, I think that it would have made a unique and special experience the perfect experience.

text:
Yes, I went back. What can I say...I'm a little masochistic when it comes to my restaurant experience and I decided to go back for more punishment. Luckily, or unluckily, this time around, my visit resulted in me actually having a meal at Hai Di Lao.

I had to bump them up to 3 stars for their effort. At least I feel that they are taking the yelp reviews more seriously and are actually doing something about the complaints. We called and the person on the phone spoke perfect English this time around. Our waiter also spoke English and they added an English menu to their iPad ordering system.

The food is crazy expensive and not worth the money. For 2 girls our bill was over $70 and we didn't even order that much food! That's with the $3 additional per person we had to pay for sauce. I have never seen anyone just eat their hot pot bland with no sauce so I'm going to think of it as paying a $3 cover to enter this joint...except there's no dancing (unless you count the little dance the noodle stretching guy does) and no alcohol.

They did go out of their way to be nice. It was so obvious that they had a pow wow about their service and this has all the sudden became their focus. Our waiter was actually genuinely nice and helpful. He also saved me from having soup spill all over the table and myself when I stupidly dumped a plate of crap into my pot all at once. I would have honestly rated them 2 stars if not for him saving my life. Saving my life = automatic +1 star bump up.

I would recommend the ox bone soup because the spicy soup is basically like drinking chili oil. You have plenty of opportunity to spice things up with selection from the sauce bar. The best sauce combination I've concocted consists of sesame sauce, meat sauce, soy sauce, seafood sauce, vinegar, minced garlic, tofu sauce, thai chili, and green onions.

Want to try to eat your money's worth? Take advantage of the Korean pears they have at the sauce station. Those things aren't cheap. Those guys were so lucky I didn't have a ziplock bag handy or I would have definitely stolen some...Asian style.

Conclusion, C for...effort? I still wouldn't come back again to waste my money. I would rather go to Lu Gi for this style hot pot and either Boiling Point or Jackpot for the individual pots. It's much cheaper and tastier.

"Psy goes Bibigo!" This is what the Bibigo branch commercial is saying these days in Korea as Psy is their current spokesperson. Bibigo is a big brand in Korea and they're known for their frozen food and cooking seasoning and sauces.

Bibigo opened a Bibimbap restaurant inside the Century City Westfield food court. The have quite a steady stream of customers so I guess they're thriving pretty well.

I have no problem with the food. You get it Dolsot style, which comes in a hot stone pot. There are varieties of rice, meat, and veggies you can get. They also have a few variety of sauces available for you to freely mix into your rice, although the red chili paste is really the only authentic way to go.

The price point though is a little high. You have to pay quite a lot to add different types of vegetables. I've also had better tasting bibimbap with bigger portions for a smaller price in Koreatown. You can also add an egg by adding more $$.

Overall I would say skip it. There are other great restaurants in that area and Sawtelle isn't far away. If you want bibimbap, it's best to venture to ktown.

text:
Located on 30th street in between Dunedin and Coin Laundry is a tiny alley where you’ll see Atypical Waffle and Freshman Year sharing a space. Plenty of parking in this area.

Since they are sharing a space with Freshman Year, Atypical Waffle is the line on the right and you’re greeted with someone at the counter. Use the QR code to bring up the menu. You order and pay before proceeding on to select your own seats.

We asked for the most popular and got the Number Seven ($8.50) and Chicken and Waffles ($9.50). All the other waffles on the menu are sweet.

We then went to look for seats and this place is so cute! All the furniture are mix matched and you have camping areas and private outdoor rooms. We sat at a table with college stadium seats. You can see the foldable arm table where students used to write on.

Took about 35 minutes for our food to come. At first glance, I’m like “I think I’m still going to be hungry after this”. But I was wrong, it was the perfect portion and so good. The waffles reminded me of when I was in Belgium, eating Belgium Waffles off the street. It has the light, fluffy, crispy, crunch texture combined with a ton of candied bacon wrapped around a scope of avocado. I asked for goat cheese crumble on the side. Every bite was like a dream. I didn’t want it to end.

The chicken and waffle tastes just as good and filling but with juicy chicken fritters. Topped with bacon bits and aioli sauce and maple syrup for that extra sweetness.

I highly recommend this hole in the wall place. Also give Freshman Year a try while you’re waiting for waffles. Their menu seem to change often but they offer biscuits.

text:
*4.5 stars*

I hate nothing more than to admit that I went to a restaurant because of Guy Fieri and it's probably worse that I even watch "Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives," but I've been looking for a decent East Coast pastrami sandwich in SF that can measure up to the greats in New York (Kat's, 2nd Avenue). Miller's definitely delivers. The place is welcoming, the servers are incredibly friendly, and the food is awesome.

--------------
FOOD:

Grilled Pastrami Sandwich =
The grilled pastrami sandwich at Miller's East Coast Deli may not be up to the impossibly high standard of Kat's Deli, but it's pretty damn close, and that's speaking volumes. The rye bread was perfectly grilled, the pastrami was tender and fatty (could've used a bit more though), and the cole slaw gave it just right amount of sweetness. I could eat this sandwich all day.

The Chief Sandwich (Pastrami + Corned Beef) =
Good, but the corned beef isn't as tender and fatty as the pastrami, so it kind of made the sandwich a bit bland. I'm all about the pastrami here though.

Macaroni Salad =
The Macaroni Salad that comes with the sandwich is incredible here. Not too much mayo, perfect al dente macaroni (I can't believe I'm calling the macaroni in a macaroni salad "al dente"), and just perfectly sweet.

Chicken Soup w/ Matzo Ball =
Not a huge fan of matzo ball, but this is definitely one of the better matzo balls I've had in my day. I always found them to be too bland and this is really no exception, but I've definitely had worse.

--------------

I'd say this is the best East Coast-style grilled pastrami sandwich in SF. It's not New York, but it's amazing for SF and that's good enough for me.

name: Roy Chi
text:
Aziza is the most exciting restaurant I've experienced in SF.

It combines high-class quality with an astoundingly-unique flair that is up there with the best of the best in SF. Upon entering the restaurant, you encounter a world that mixes intimacy with darkness and elegance with exotica. It's not a themed restaurant, but you can't help but to think that this not your ordinary fine dining establishment.

Aziza is Moroccan cuisine, fused with seasonal ingredients that are perfectly selected by the chef. According to our waitress, the menu changes every week, and depending on the month you visit, the menu looks vastly different month-to-month.

Our server, Katia, was one of the best servers I've ever had. She was not only completely knowledgeable about every dish, she describes them so well that you feel like eating everything on the menu. She wasn't as much a waitress as she was a storyteller -- providing specific details about the origin of the restaurant and the philosophy of the chef's cuisine. It really does make you enjoy the food you are eating that much more. It makes you feel like you're not just eating food, you're eating a piece of art that has a deeply-rich story behind it.

The drinks at Aziza are incredible. Hand-crafted drinks, delicately concocted with the freshest of ingredients -- unique and flavorful. I ordered the Cilantro vodka drink -- one of the best drinks I've ever had. Subtly sweet and with a strong, fresh cilantro flavor. I tried a few others: the pomelo with bourbon, the grapefruit with gin -- all were awesome.

With our party of 5, we ordered:
(1) the beet salad
(2) flatbread w/ three different sauces
(3) radish
(4) romaine hearts
(5) beef cheek and beef loin
(6) lamb shank
(7) spanish mackerel
(8) duck confit basteeya

Each dish was phenomenal. My favorites were the beet salad, the flatbread w/ sauces, the lamb shank, and the beef cheek and loin. The lamb shank was incredibly tender and flavorful -- not gamy whatsoever. The beef cheek was an interesting texture -- a little tough, but soft at the same time. The beef loin was perfectly cooked. Duck confit basteeya was perfect.

Aziza provided a food experience that was daring, risky, new, strange, unique... and it was all amazing. Definitely one of the best restaurants I've tried in SF and, quite possibly, ever.

I get home to find that the jalapenos were missing from my veggie nachos (a key ingredient for me) and there were a lot of broken/small chips...like from the bottom of the bag. My parents complained their burrito and quesadilla were cold, which they had to place in the toaster oven. Excellent!...Delicious!...Top notch!

I have to start this review by thanking our host/server (Joanna) for making our dining experience a great one!

We started the meal with the burrata along with the polenta & ragu aperitivos.

The burrata is served warm with roasted tomatoes & pesto which complimented each other very well.

The polenta & ragu is served straight from the pot at your table and might be the best ragu I've had! Highly recommended!

Next up was the Porcini Mafaldine Bolognese which was tasty, hearty and well balanced.

To cap off our entrees we went with the risotto which was delicious with it's mushroom and truffle accents! Highly recommended!

Wrapping up the night, Joanna suggested we try the caramel crostata which has an oreo crust and bunch of other stuff that tastes amazing mixed together.

Of course to go along with all the delicious food we had to have some vino! We went with the Seghesio Zinfindel (which isn't cheap at $59 per bottle) but complimented our entire meal very well. Make sure to ask your server which wine will go best with your dishes.

Thanks again for a great night Joanna and to anyone who is considering Davanti......GO GET A TABLE NOW!!!

text:
Always a delicious time when you go to Raku. And there is good stuff to be had by both purists and those that like a little fusion. If you like a variety of kinds of sushi, this place is for you. It's all you can eat, but it is also made to order. So you pay a flat fee, order a few plates at a time (just the way you want it), eat said food (which is super yummy) and then repeat. I have only two minor issues with this restaurant.

1. I can never eat as much as I want. I fill up, and despite the fact that I could eat more, I feel like that guy from Monty Python's The Meaning of Life.

2. Service is not fast. Which is fine if you're not in a hurry. It is also great if you don't want to be rushed out (you never are). But if you are in a hurry to pound some sushi and get to the next thing, this probably isn't the place for you.

Rest of the meal was rather disappointing as I thought the point of the salad bar and the pao de queijo (cheese bread) was to get you to fill up on them instead of the meat -- but they weren't really that yummy so we definitely went for more meat.

I was especially sad about the pao de queijo, the version at Pampas is so terrible compared to what I remember from Brazil and even, frankly, the "Brazi bites" I have in my freezer (which are far too salty, but actually not bad at all compared to the Pampas ones, where none of the texture seems right).

Salad bar highlights: whipped mashed potatoes, pickled cucumber salad, fruit salad (melon, pineapple). And the kids loved the mac n cheese of course.

We hadn't been to Pampas despite many, many years of living nearby, and I'm not sure we'll do it again.

name: Jonathan Marinaro
text:
Pampas succeeds where other Churascos fail to live up to the hype.

I had a delicious dinner with my wife where we had the standard all-the-meat-you-can-eat found at every Brazilian Steakhouse. What we were expecting was aloof service and overcooked, underspiced meats with your usual salad bar. What we received was absolutely phenomenal service from Mario and the staff who quickly and expertly carved the meat onto our plates.

The food: I wholeheartedly recommend the Top Sirloin, the Parmesan encrusted Filet and the pork loin. If you eat these three you'll see the difference between this and its competition. What surprised me was the bacon wrapped turkey, the linguiça and the skirt steak. All of these are cheap cuts, usually come out like shoe leather compared to the first three and are barely edible outside of filling you up before the good stuff comes around. Here they easily surpass the better beef cuts at the competition and would do the same at Pampas if not for the excellent quality of the beef and pork. If there was only one request would be for more variety of pickledpeppers and other veggies to help cut the delicious fat, but I guess that's what a good Cabernet is for.

The service: Mario and his team had us eating quickly and trying everything with them checking on us to make sure we hadn't missed a single cut. Most other places you have to ask them to bring around the good stuff, but at Pampas it hit us first and with full descriptions by Mario and his butchers who were very friendly and helpful. I need to come back again to try the Caiprinha but the beer menu has some delicious deep cuts with a dark Brazilian Beer that you shouldn't miss!

The ambiance: The restaurant is well lit, spotless and well designed with plenty of room for large parties while being intimate for couples wanting to celebrate. I want to come back and see how far back it goes, I believe there's a balcony area and a rear room you could reserve for parties.

All in all, this is my new favorite Brazilian place and is ranked up there among my favorite steakhouses! Shout out to Mario and his meat-cutting team again for the great service, I'll be bringing my whole crew next time, so be prepared!

the server was so friendly and knowledgeable & the manager also very friendly came by our table and they brought us samples of the mealk (milk made from nut meal) really good too! We got 2 things and shared both, good size portions we even brought some home, we will have it for lunch today.
We got the Pasta Chardonnay Alfredo my personal favorite ( definitely recommend both entrees) and the open faced sloppy joe (the nut bread underneath the chili is divine!) the chili so thick and delicious you won’t miss the meat! And the guacamole on top just so yummy makes it over the top, and both had this wonderful cashew cheese, I’m a BIG cheese lover and this is to die for!  Didn’t miss the dairy at all!
If you are Vegetarian or Vegan you Must try this place! “Good wholesome meal” not vegan junk food. And for non vegans a wonderful place to go for healthy change of pace! ( I’m seriously considering going Vegetarian ). And “this will be my new go to” for a night out! 😋

*Oh, I almost forgot, we also brought home some icemealk for later that evening “ made from their famous nut butters & mealk ( our tummies too full to eat it there) we got the figzilla it was amazing, sweet, nutty and satisfying! This place truly is a hidden gem, blink & you’ll miss it, I’m sure it will hold it’s 5 star ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️rating!
OrVeganic: make a branch by the beach, and you will Be rich!$$

text:
The 405 shutdown caused the change of plans that landed me here for valentines day dinner instead of another romantic restaurant in Santa Monica. I have been to a yelp event at Fig & Olive before but this was my first time coming back since.

Fig & Olive is definitely a beautiful restaurant with romantic ambiance. They have a balcony bar area upstairs too with some seating areas in addition to the big bar downstairs.

We were early for our reservation but they were able to accommodate us and we were seated right away. Our table was next to the door to the outdoor seating area so it was a little chilly. Our server was nice and the dishes came out quickly.

I had the crab cake appetizer. It was pretty good although I prefer bigger lumps of crab rather than a lot of shredded pieces. There was a lot of fillers added and there wasn't a whole lot of sauce to go with it.

For my main dish, I had the truffle risotto with mushrooms. The flavor was good but the dish was so rich that I couldn't finish it. I only ate about 2/3 and left the rest. My date had the chicken tajine. I actually really liked the dish. The chicken was tender and the cous cous was delicious. Both of the dishes came in smaller portions.

Their creme brulee cheesecake dessert was also quite different. It came in a small round shape on top of a thin sweet cracker and slices of peach. The cheesecake was small and plain with some roasted sugar on top. I was not impressed.

Parking is definitely not easy to find in the area. Valet parking is really expensive and there's a long wait for your car.

We got there in 20 minutes but from the time stamp of when I placed the call to the time on my receipt, it was 35 minutes. Parking here is really bad. It’s always packed and the spaces are tiny!

We got the Spicy Soy and Sweet & Spicy. Honestly, it doesn’t look like the photo based on the color and it wasn’t spicy. Couldn’t really tell them apart but if I had to guess, one was slightly sweeter than the other. The Sweet & Spicy was like a wet sticky sauce and it was only at the bottom of the box so only parts of the chicken had the sauce. It wasn’t evenly distributed. In the mean time we ordered a pretzel for an appetizer and asked the waitress if she could also find out if the pretzel had dairy in it. About 10 minutes later the waitress came back and informed us the bread had dairy and the fries were made in the same frier as other items with dairy, so cross contamination was an issue. Kudos to the waitress for finding out for us! When you kid gets sick when she eats anything with dairy or anything cooked with items with dairy, you have to be careful. My daughter ended up ordering two of their sliders without a bun and fruit. The manager even came out and made sure our dairy questions were answered. That was nice. After about 15 minutes our waitress came over and we asked when the pretzel was going to come out. She said, "since it had dairy in it I didn't put the order in. We told her that she never told us it did and we still wanted it, we only asked so we could know if she could have it. The waitress asked if we wanted to put the order in now and we said no thinking our food would be out shortly. One hour after arriving we had no food and saw people that came in way after us being served. Our waitress was no where to be found so we flagged down another waitress and asked to see the manager. Our waitress then came over and I complained that we had been there an hour and had not been served. The manager then appeared and made an excuse that it took them longer to make the burger to ensure it was dairy free. My daughters two tiny burger patties were burnt and inedible. We order the smoked tri tip sandwich. It didn't taste smoked and it was fatty. Very disappointing. I complained to the manager about my daughters burger and the service. They did take my daughters meal off the ticket and give us 25% off our meal. Maybe they were just having problems that day, but I would expect a lot better. text:
Located near the corner of Fern and 30th, there was plenty of street parking around 5pm on a Friday. If you park at the meters, it’s free after six.

They have a few tables outside on the sidewalk and a few tables in their patio. Be warned that you’ll most likely be bitten by mosquitoes or flies landing on your food. We sat out in the patio but then moved indoor when my legs got devoured by mosquitoes and popped up like hives.

We ordered:
Dynamite wings
Samosa slim
Curry fries
Curry mac n cheese
Chicken masala
Butter chicken

All the curry tasted the same. Sorry to say but it’s like me making curry in the Instapot and slapping it on the waffle fries, Mac, and wings.

The samosa had potato fillings and came with a tamarind and chutney dip. The butter chicken came with a few pieces of shredded chicken while the masala was something I’ve never seen before. The pieces of chicken were on a plate with the masala sauce in a bowl in the center. I had more sauce than the masala. So it made it dry when the chicken is not in the sauce. For some reason the basmati rice was not good either. It was just plain.

We spent a total of $95 and I didn’t feel like we got our monies worth when everything was just average. The service and ambiance was nice.

It might have been different if we were able to add spice levels. The best item would be the garlic naan. My drink was a mojito and usually I ask for something sweet but all their drinks are on the sweeter refreshing side so can’t go wrong. The mojito was actually too sweet for my liking.

It’ll be best if you can go during happy hour to try the same thing but less on your wallet.

text:
Best fish sandwich I’ve had in California.

I spent a few years trying to find the best fish sandwich in Florida and in that process I tasted so many amazing ones. From a list of about 100, my gold standard will always be Steamers restaurant in Cedar Key, FL with their epic grouper sandwich.

Since moving to CA, I’ve been trying to find anything that satisfies my obsession. The Solana Beach Fish House smoked salmon sandwich is now #2 on my all time list.

- fabulous seasoning. Robust. Full of flavor.
- perfect level of hot smoke cooking but served chilled so the fish has a buttery and firm consistency
- ideal pairing with sliced sourdough bread that holds up well structurally while adding complimentary flavor
- simply world class tartar sauce. Perfect balance with the mildly spicy seasoning and smoke of the salmon. I cannot overstate how important this is to a good fish sandwich
- A+ cole slaw side. Creamy and mid level sweet. None of the bitterness of some slaws.

I’ll be back here often.

text:
In Sausalito/Marin City and Mill Valley there is  not an abundance of places that serve Brunch, and even less that serve a really good one. Searching  and trying every place in Southern Marin for about a year I finally came across the Bayside, that was 20 years ago when my wife and I moved across the highway from Mike's Bikes  on  top of the hill,  over looking the area  that used to be the Marin City flea market,before they (Marin County) shut it down and developed the Marin City shopping Center.
Since that time I have found some really decent places over the years, but they don't seem to last for one reason or another. The Bayside has stood the test of time, and  remains Rock Solid.
I moved over 10 years ago from Mill Valley  to Northern Marin. I will drive  from Novato to Sausalito to eat there. Why ??? Because in my opinion they are one of the best in  Marin County. Definitely in the top 3 in my opinion.
They have an incredible menu and  the prices are very reasonable. This is a family owned business and the whole family works there, everyday they are open.
The service is fast, and getting seated right away  is usually not a problem. They are very busy most of  the time especially on the weekends. Large parties should call to make reservations, there tables and booths seat  4-6  people depending on the people. I know they did a remodel and added additional seating off the back around 10 + years ago, but should consider doing  another one if possible to do so.
I am very  critical of restaurants and the food service industry, as a whole, so for me to give 5 stars is  a huge deal for me ,so I hope you the reader keep that in mind.
The average life span in Marin for a restaurant is measured in weeks/ months if you are lucky, so for the Bayside Cafe to have stayed in business for 20 + years has got to say something  about the place, the family, and  the employees.  There must be a whole lot of people who share my opinion and love this place as much as I do because numbers don't lie.

First of all, make a reservation. Second of all, show up on time. We were 15 minutes late and the host promptly pointed that out while informing us that we may still have our reservation as long as we get up in an hour and 15 minutes or less. I can't say that I have ever experienced this at any other restaurants before.

Our service was a little slow. The waiters were too busy fighting about which tables belong to who. This is also another first for me. I think they were trying to be subtle but they really weren't.

All this is very unfortunately because the restaurant has a great ambiance and the food was quite good. My favorite has to be the brussels sprouts salad. I could just dig in with a big spoon and be completely content with that. The dressing was super delicious.

We had the original Bacu, which is a sandwich with a fluffy bread folded into a half circle. It was excellent. The meat had great flavor and the bread was soft. The Waffle Rilette, on the other hand, was average at best. The duck wasn't as flavorful as I would have liked and the waffle was almost at room temperature.

They have a good wine selection. They come in short glasses and they really don't give you a whole lot. We had a 2 glasses each and all 4 selections were excellent.

The check took forever to come. Parking is a pain. We ended up paying for parking in the lot across the street.

text:
Opens early at 730 am for that I can't wait gotta have hot broth for breakfast kinda day. Specially good when the weather turns cold or cloudy and rainy all at once.

Cambodian cuisine, mostly of the wet or dry noodle variety. My wife  ordered the dry noodles after its namesake, Phnom Penh.  It had on top of a heap of steamed noodles, I assume steamed from the same broth, but without the broth. Garnished on top, with slices of meat balls, beef brisket, and pork liver, and it was tasty. Some cilantro and slivers of spring onion on top.

I ordered the beef stew noodle soup. I did not expect that star anise and tomatoe broth went together. I had mixed feelings about it. It is not off putting, but I was expecting a clear broth.

Choices of type of noodles, if you want, or leave the choice to the chef.  Order dry noodles and they also give you a small bowl of broth with a bone on the side.  The broth comes with side garnishes, as in a Vietnamese pho noodle house. Broth is a tad on the sweet side. But had a great taste.

The fried donut like bread is very good and is a must try, they are big. My wife tore pieces of the bread and dipped them in the broth, delicious!

Parking is street side. So prepare to look even early in the morning.

name: Roy Chi
text:
Coqueta is a solid restaurant, but it is definitely overpriced and over-hyped.

Everything about it was great -- the location, the ambiance, the service, the food -- except for the prices. Just to be clear, I'm more than happy to pay $150+ a person for a Spanish tapas restaurant, but there has to be a reason why a dish is so expensive -- a Celebrity chef shouldn't automatically skyrocket the price of 8 slices of grilled pork to $38. The pork should taste like it's $38, or maybe at least $30 with an $8 "Celebrity chef" tax.

Honestly, though, as long as you know that you will be overpaying and you are content with knowing that you will be overpaying, Coqueta really is a solid Spanish restaurant in SF. There are many millionaires in SF who use $100 bills like Charmin Ultra sheets, so there will definitely be people who don't care, and for those people, Coqueta is great.

----------------
FOOD:

Pluma (Grilled Pork with Honey) =
Nicely grilled, but definitely under-seasoned without the honey. The honey gives the pork a wonderful, subtle sweetness, but the pork itself just isn't worth $38 for 8 slices. I don't care if there was an incredible scientific breakthrough that managed to reincarnate Julia Child and zombie Julia Child cooked up this meal for me, no celebrity chef should be charging this much for 8 pieces of bland pork that has to be drenched with honey.

Serrano Ham w/ Manchego Cheese Pintxo =
Good ham, good cheese -- the bite was the size of a tic tac, but it was a satisfying bite.

English Pea Croquettes =
Delicious chicken pot pie croquettes -- nicely fried with a strong, creamy flavor.

Paella =
Very good paella -- excellent texture of the rice, subtly spiced, and with lots of crispy rice to give it a great overall consistency. Goes amazingly well with the peppers and aioli they give you on the side.

Grilled Octopus =
The octopus was a bit too mushy, and not tender like how grilled octopus is supposed to be. The fingerling potatoes were tasteless -- I think this dish would go better with a puree or at least something with a bit more flavor.

Fig Tart with Blue Cheese Ice Cream =
Fig tart was just okay -- tasted like a stale pop tart. BUT the Blue Cheese Ice Cream was INCREDIBLE. Honestly, we spent about 10 minutes contemplating if we should try the Blue Cheese Ice Cream, because it sounded horrific but it definitely piqued our curiosity. Best decision of the night. Subtle blue cheese flavor, but the perfect amount of sweetness that ended with a satisfying end. This is one of my favorite ice cream flavors ever and I wish the fig tart wasn't there in the way.

Churros =
Perfectly fried churros. The chocolate sauce wasn't strong enough to do anything of substance, but the churros themselves were excellent. Again -- not sure if it's worth the $8 price tag, though.
----------------

Coqueta is an excellent addition to the Embarcadero and it definitely has its spectacular moments (Blue Cheese Ice Cream, Paella) but I was just expecting more, given the prices and the hype.

HOW MUCH DID IT COST:  With tip, it was a little under $50, but I went with someone else.  For dinner, it was $18 per person, and the drinks were like a dollar something or whatever.  So if you went by yourself, it would cost probably around $25 including tip.

WOULD I GO BACK/RECOMMEND THIS PLACE:  Yes and yes.  The food is rotated out pretty frequently, the variety of food is pretty fair, the servers are friendly and the place is pretty clean.  And really, everything tasted pretty good.

This review is strictly for the speakeasy-like bar in the bar of Cafe Stella. Dimly lit and upbeat, I stepped into a room full of wonder and excitement. I was digging the music they were playing, which seemed to be straight from my Pandora playlist (hint: Bonodo station all the way). There's even a DJ booth area for when the place wants to get extra hype, I guess.

It was my first time at this establishment last night. I was there for a friend's birthday celebration and features your typical 'first come, first serve' seating area.

Because my friend doesn't drink alcohol, we asked Jesse, one of the bartenders (he wears black eyeglasses) to make a nice non-alcoholic drink. What he ended up making my friend blew all of our minds away. I come to find out that it's their cocktail Sea Archer without the alcohol. It was AMAZING and I highly recommend it virgin or with booze. Extremely refreshing with a hint of ginger taste to it.

The one thing I wouldn't necessarily order is their old fashioned. They do not do it well. The balance is extremely off and it's way too strong. I'd rather take my whiskey neat than to have it mixed w/whatever they put in their old fashions. It literally tasted like gasoline was in my mouth. Be warned!

Got the Scramble with Chicken Sausage & Avocado and it was okay. The crispy potato medley was good though and nice switch from your typical white potatoes. The swedish pancakes were just okay too -- nothing special.

The $7 "Millionaires Bacon" was ridiculously overpriced and shamelessly promoted like I was at some grungy hotel/casino off the Vegas strip. It tasted EXACTLY like the "Korean Pork Jerky" that you can buy at Costco -- actually I may even prefer the Costco jerky to this. I'd promote their side potatoes over this.

Anyway, Sweet Maple isn't a bad spot by any means -- the food is good enough to satisfy your brunch needs. But given the long wait and the heaps of other SF competition, Sweet Maple just really isn't worth it during weekend brunch hours.

text:
Trust me, I love big chunks of stewed meat more than anyone. I just can't accept having to pay over $25 for a tiny bowl of it. I can't say that I will be returning to Seongbukdong any time soon for that kind of price.

Seongbukdong is in the same plaza as Dan Sung Sa and Gaam Karaoke. They are actually the only business that validates so you can pay $1 for valet instead of $2. They're known pretty much solely for the galbi jjim, or a slow cooked beef rib in a dark sauce. We have a similar dish in Thailand but we use pork instead. The Seongbukdong meat is tender but I find the sauce to be a little too sweet. One order can cost you almost $30.

They also have a few other dishes on the menu. We ended up getting braised mackerel too and found it to be very unimpressive. The side dishes were pretty good though. The service was alright and the food came out quickly.

If you like galbi stew, I would recommend going to Ttu Rak instead. Their spicy galbi jim is much more afforable and I personally like the taste a lot more.

name: Roy Chi
text:
Honestly, the last time I had a $100 per person dinner at a Chinese restaurant was... never. For that reason, I was REALLY skeptical about Hakkasan. I mean, Chinese food is at its very best when it's dirty and grungy, cooked homestyle by an old Chinese man with a long hair twirling out of the penny-sized mole on his neck or by an old Chinese lady with a voice that sounds like she'd been smoking since birth.

I knew Hakkasan would look and feel amazing (which it does), but would the food justify the $$$$? After having dinner here, I would have to say that although it's still debatable, it definitely comes pretty damn close to being justified.

I'm actually quite surprised at how much they did with so little space and with such low ceilings. The ambiance is incredible -- definitely one of the nicer restaurants I've been to in SF. Naturally, it's filled with business professionals and super wealthy Silicon Valley icons, which could make tech nerds starstruck (we saw Gurbaksh Chahal sitting next to us).

---------------------------
FOOD:

Steamed Dim Sum Platter:
- Very well-done dim sum with the perfect amount of chewiness of the dumpling skin and interesting flavors. Is it worth $26 for 8 little dumplings? Probably not, but it was still pretty good.

Braised Kurobuta Pork Belly:
- Hands down the best dish of the night. Hakkasan's braised pork belly might just be the best of its kind that I've had outside of Asia. The thick layer of fat was perfectly cooked, the meat was fall-apart tender, and the sauce was delicious without being overpowering. I would come back just for this.

Truffle Oil Duck:
- So disappointing. It had so much going for it: the skin was perfectly crispy and how can you ever go wrong with truffle oil? Unfortunately, the duck was overcooked, so it was tough and lost all of its fattiness. If the duck was just cooked a bit better, the flavors would've made this dish awesome.

Hakka Noodles:
- Definitely not worth $12. The noodles were good, but it was just nothing special whatsoever. The flavors were a bit bland and it wasn't very satisfying. In fact, I had to drench it with chili sauce and chili oil to give it any pop of flavor.

Chocolate Orange:
- Incredible dessert for chocolate lovers. The dish comes with a round chocolate shell that breaks gently when the waiter pours the molten lava-like chocolate sauce on top. There's a scoop of chocolate ice cream on the side, on top of this delicious mixture of nuts, cocoa crumble, and... Pop Rocks (or at least it felt like pop rocks because SOMETHING was fizzing and popping on my tongue). Everything about this dessert was great.

---------------------------

All in all, Hakkasan was a good, memorable dining experience, with an excellent ambiance and great service. The food was a hit or miss, but when it hit (like with the Braised Pork Belly or Chocolate Orange) it DEFINITELY hit it out of the park.

It was the first time I ever thought to myself: "Hmm, maybe paying $100/pp for Chinese food isn't so crazy after all..."

The service was spot on and the ambiance was quiet and comfortable. It was a Wed night so it wasn't crowded. We love the fact they don't have a corkage fee here. We've collected some nice wines over the years and hate to bring them out with us when we have to pay an additional $15-30. You pick your fish (they have about 10-15), how to cook it (grilled, macadamia encrusted, Cajun, etc), and choose a coupIe of sides. I ordered the Ono encrusted with macadamia which comes with a delicious orange ginger butter sauce. I added the grilled zucchini and garlic mashed potatoes. We split a yummy dinner salad. My Ono was cooked perfect leaving it tender with plenty of juices. The mashed potatoes were some of the best I've ever had, sorry mom. These potatoes don't have chunks they're whipped creamy with plenty of consistency. The flavor was so tasty. We were celebrating an anniversary so our waitress was kind enough to offer us a free dessert which we chose the chocolate cake. Wow! The cake was moist the texture and flavor were spot on. Can't say enough about our meal. Can't wait to come back!

name: alice chung
text:
I can't believe I've been passing by Du Par's all this time and never realized what existed in front of my eyes!

Voted #1 pancakes by many publications such as Esquire and LA Weekly, I had to finally try the beloved restaurant and did so this past weekend. What a great decision I made.

I ordered a short stack (3) of their buttermilk pancakes with just plain ole' syrup and melted butter (which sits at the bottom of the cakes). Upon first bite, it was fluffy buttery caramel with a nice crisp at the bottom. It was perfect. I was in pancake heaven. WOW! Every bite thereafter tasted like it was the first. AMAZING!

In addition, if you are a fan of banana cream pies, Du Par's has one that is tough to beat at other eateries. With any pie, the crust is always the important factor. Well, for me, at least. And the crust here, along with the amazing banana cream, was wonderful. Just typing this is making me salivate.

They also have an awesome happy hour menu, which includes cocktails, etc. Look them up for details!

FYI - this location has AMPLE parking in a lot behind the establishment.

My recent experience was not very good, but the saving grace (and the reason I still gave it 3 stars) is that, for regular pancakes, this place hands down serves the best. name: ben der
text:
If I could describe the food at Du-par's in one word, it would be 'bland.'  I went to eat here last night and had the crab cakes appetizer, the meat loaf entree and the banana cream pie for desert.  To wash it all down, I had the fresh-squeezed (and it WAS fresh-squeezed on the spot) orange juice.

Sad to say, the OJ was the best part of the entire meal.  The crab cakes were mediocre and soggy inside and tasted more fishy than crabby.  The meat loaf, as well as the mashed potatoes and veggies that came with it, were incredibly bland; there was no seasoning put on anything.  The meat loaf itself looked like it was from a TV tray dinner.  And finally, the banana cream pie tasted like anything but banana.  The strongest taste that came from that pie was the whipped cream, which was very disappointing.

Suffice to say, I will not be eating again at Du-par's, which set me back about $44 for the entire meal (not including tip).  This long-time running diner may seem like an LA institution on the outside, but unfortunately it's all a facade.  The food served at this diner is more at place in an underfunded school cafeteria.

10 Stars!
Clayton’s is the ideal corner breakfast spot. The cozy environment, amazing staff, and flat out perfect food make it a must. There are not a lot of seats, but the workers hustle like no place else, so turnover is quick and we had very little wait time despite the line outside. The breakfast menu is chock full of so many options that everyone is sure to find something yummy. The carnitas and chorozo hash is just plain ridiculous good. Perfect balance of ingredients and just the right amount of food. The staff is friendly and attentive - sitting at the counter, my coffee was never less than half full. Be prepared to be tempted by a display of fresh baked pies and other treats, and bring a big appetite. I haven’t yet tried it, but the fried chicken and waffles looks delicious.

They open at 6am daily, but if you just want coffee, they have a walk up window on the side that opens at 5am - this also lets you skip the dining line if you just want to grab a cup and go.

First, i must start with their bread basket policy, which ,had me flabberghasted.There were 2 of us eating,  and the waitperson brought us a bread basket with 2 teeny round  slices of bread, ,(the width of a slice from a skinny baguette) ,and no butter. Granted, the bread is fresh, and possibly made on site, but gee, after 2 bites  each of our tiny slices were gone. When we asked for more bread we were told that's the policy--one slice person!
Also, in the past, you could make minor substitutions, such as asking for pasta on your dinner instead of steamed vegetables side, but not now. Everything is pre assembled, pre-made, measured, etc.
As for the meal, do not come hungry. The ravioli dinner was pretty skimpy, as were the 2 thin slices of eggplant parmigiano.  And the flavor of the food is definitely nowhere near as good as it used to be...I've eaten there many times in the last 20 years.
Well. If the owner is insistent that each customer get just one 2 bite slice of bread each, this restaurant must be in dire financial circumstanes , so they can only afford to give the customer one tiny piece! That's unheard of; the bread basket in Italian restaurants is usually full, and refills are no problem. In the end, a different waitperson came to tell us sorry, your waiter is on his first day, but in fact, they are told by the owner to give one slice only to each customer. The owner is not new so what would cause him to become so stingy, unless the restaurant is in financial trouble?
I sure don't recommend them. The only place i like in Santa Cruz for Italian food is Lilian's, but they rarely offer eggplant, my favorite dish. Guess I'll just have to stay home and make my own!

Went here for the first time this morning after a coworker constantly said they have the best breakfast burritos. Person taking our order was very friendly. Many people came in and out as we were waiting for our order, so we knew it had to be good. Only problem was that after waiting for 30 minutes, people that had placed orders after us started getting their food before us. When the folks that ordered immediately before and after me asked where their orders were, the staff started getting confused. One person was told the cashier was new, another was told their order would be right out. I was told the kitchen didn't know their printer was out of paper and this is why my order wasn't done, but my order would be ready in 10 minutes. Another person asked if their order was ready; it had been for a while, but they were calling the number and not the name; this person ordered over the phone and gave them a name, but was not given a number. We finally got our order an hour after we paid. Food was good, but not so good that I'd be willing to wait an hour again. Not sure if it was due to the cooks having to speed cook to get orders done, or if this is how it normally tastes. Food would be maybe 3 or 3.5 stars, the wait bumps it down to 2 stars, but I'm giving 3 stars because the staff didn't panic and held their cool with the 5 people in their faces about why their orders weren't ready and more people placing orders in person and over the phone.

text:
My first time dining here.
I was so excited... maybe going on a busy night like NYE was not a good choice.

We had reservations @ 7:45pm they were running behind *(we didn't mind). Decided we would have a glass of wine in the bar area while we waited. We got lucky, and found a seat and our server was very sweet. Didn't appreciate the 3 trays of dirty dishes on  jack stands along the wall that never were removed and it kept growing! They just kept piling them on.

We were sat in the back dining area about 8:15pm.  Our server was Sean. He was the only server in the entire room and it showed. We sat for at least 5 minutes before we were greeted by his busser *(he was pleasant) and brought us bread. Sean came to our table a few minutes later.

I am not going to get super long on this, tho I could. If the manager wishes to have a conversation I am more than willing.

Few key points.
1. Too much room not enough server.
2. Server seemed to be very rushed and rushing us.
3. Ordered another glass of wine, he walked off we had to call him back *(So he would know what I was drinking).
4. Said glass of wine shows up *(wine glass had just been washed, completely wet with water and some lipstick, had not been dried off).
Note: **Had appetizers, main course, then dessert.
We ate our appetizer (Caesar Salads) and then received our main courses about 9:00pm
5. 9:20 - Your Servers in their uniforms are now sitting two tables away from us, doing their checks, eating food, one has laid her head down taking a little nap ? *(mind you there are still 3 paying tables seated in there including us and we haven't finished eating yet).
Another server comes out with voice raised, asking "oh my gosh do you have the stapler"?
6. 9:30pm. Music in the restaurant is turned off !?  - we inquire to our server- who has been hovering..why has the music gone off. He states it's been a very busy day and it's coming to an end. He disappears.
We decided to ask the busser for togo boxes take the rest of our dinner home.
7. We order dessert. Chocolate Lava Cake with ice cream. Which arrived, looked beautiful but was luke warm :(  We took about 3 bites and that was it. This cake needs to be hot.
8. Sean dropped the check when he delivered the dessert.
9. And those same 3 trays of dirty dishes along the wall area in the bar were still there when we walked out.

Okay longer than I wanted but honestly I just couldn't believe all of this.

So disappointed.

I now realize that Gullivers choose to close at 9pm on New Years Eve.. I guess because it was a Monday ??? And their staff obviously wanted to get out and go party.
Given the price increase incurred on the menu because it was NYE, the lack of service, execution and cleanliness.
And need to rethink your timeline as well.
Poor choices were made it seems and it showed.

I laughed at the idea of Cravings by 99 Ranch thinking that they can compete with Costco. My husband and I, we walked aisle by aisle trying to find some cool stuffs to buy, NOTHING. We couldn't find ANYTHING that worth to buy. If you're looking for instant noodles, this is the place. They have like 50 types of noodles. From China, Korea, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia... You name it, they have it. Lol. Prices are mostly higher than regular 99 Ranch, from seafood to meat to vegetables to fruits...  Is this a joke or what? You can get cheaper at markets nearby like Aldi, Sprout, Smart and Final... Just name a few.
Bored with warehouse, we walked over to the food court to check out Shominoods Ramen Bar. I ordered a CALIKATA ramen, it's Hakata Tonkatsu ramen with 1 SLICE of belly pork and green onions. It tasted awful. Noodle was undercooked, pork belly was nothing but a piece of fat. Yuck. My husband got a Spicy Miso Ramen. Same awful taste of soup with a bit of spicy sauce and his noodle was overcooked, so soggy. We couldn't finish it although we were hungry. Beside, it took us 30 minutes to get these nasty taste noodles. What a waste of 30 minutes of our life.
I think I'll stick with Shinsengumi if I ever craving for a REAL ramen.
I understand they try to make this place looks hip with modern decor, BUT, they failed big time. Food is overpriced, yet, they gave you CHEAP disposable chopsticks and spoons. I have never been in any places that give you cheap usetensils like this place. Beside, tables were dirty. Imagine it's only open for just a week? I don't think I will be back.

The ancient style of using charcoal is by far the most flavorful way ( in my opinion) to cook seafood cause it leave the outside perfectly charred and the insides juicy as ever! I recommend getting the CHOOSE 2 items or CHOOSE 3 items, you have a varied selection of fish to choose from along with a delicious plethora of sides from Mac n cheese to cheesy potatoes, which you should get btw. They start at 25$ , but if you want the premium items like Alaskan halibut and premium steak it’s only a couple bucks more per item so no big deal . Delicious food is a wise investment for yourself to truly experience life, after all you only have one, so spend your time wisely investing in the best food available to YOU! text:
Mama's Lu Dumpling House is a popular one among locals and neighboring cities. So much that they usually have long lines during lunch and dinner if you do not arrive at the right time.

The right times to arrive to avoid a line is around 1030am for lunch and 6p for dinner if you don't want to wait for an hour. Another PRO tip: They DO NOT seat you until your entire party is present because they have to be mindful of others waiting. Their space is small but please be respectful and have your whole party there.

My family and I love coming here to eat because they have yummy dishes, of course (not because we love the lines). Dishes like the PEA SHOOT veggie dish, fish pan-fried dumplings, and onion pancake (to die for). These are my top dishes here.

The salted cod fried rice (an all-time Chinese favorite) was TOO salty for our taste, unfortunately. If you like salt, go for this dish.

Parking is ample in the lot behind, which is shared with the rest of the plaza.

text:
I've been waitingggg for a Poke place that specializes in poke and I'm super happy that this place popped up!

So the concept of this place is a build your own poke bowl. Similar to the assembly line that you'll find at a Chipotle and Subway :)

They have an assortment of fishes from spicy tuna, salmon, yellow tail, regular tuna, octopus, and shrimp! You can make it as spicy as you want and have either greens, brown rice, or sushi rice as your base.

The staff is very friendly and try to get you your food as quickly as they can.

Since this is a concept that all of NorCal has been waiting for it does get crowded, and the lines are out the door! If this is the case, you can expect it to take about 20 minutes to get from the end of the line to payment (depending of course if the people in front of you are ordering for themselves or are ordering for multiple people)

There is limited seating and all the seating is actually outside of the restaurant.

The quality of the food was decent, but I've had better, but I will say that this is the best since it's one of the very few in the area that specializes in this.

I would recommend!

name: Jonathan Marinaro
text:
Poki Bowl takes the now tried-and-true assembly line method of making food (see Chipotle or other taquerias) and applies it to Hawaiian poke, a mixture of fresh, sushi-grade fish, onions and cucumbers, and sauce with a selection of toppings.

The shop is small, with an occasional table set up inside on cold days, and is better suited for those grabbing food to go rather than dining there, as all the outside tables are comparable to that you can find at a local park. This makes the ambiance feel much closer to how you'd get poke if you were in Hawaii, as it feels like something you picked up with a bottle of pog at a local market.

The line, while usually long enough to extend out the door and along the walkway, moves very fast as the only food that needs to be 'cooked' is the rice. The speed of the preparers is impressive as you can get from rice to register in about five to six minutes.

The food is broken down into the bowl's base, a choice of brown rice, sushi rice or salad mix (you can mix these as well, I personally prefer rice on the salad for a well-rounded bowl!) the fish mix and the toppings. The fish mix has cubed bluefin tuna, yellowfin tuna and salmon (all raw) along with cooked shrimp and octopus. There is also an option for spicy tuna, but that's spooned on top of the rice without the sauce mix. From there you can get onions and cucumbers added before the sauce station. A mixture of sauces including some sweet soy and chili oil ranges from mild to spicy and is mixed with the fish and poured on top of the base. Then toppings are added including a shredded imitation crab, avocado and more.

All in all it's a cheap meal, coming out to about $12 per person with bowl, drink and tax, and provides a great fast meal for those willing to eat something raw once in a while!

Koi Palace also has locations in Milpitas and Dublin but I've not visited them nor have I been for dinner. name: Lourdes Lopez
text:
There are several locations in the area including one in Oceanside where we were staying.  However, we wanted to go to the original one on the 101.

It is a quaint,  typical SoCal beach town restaurant.  They have some indoor seating, lots of seating outside in front of property, and some outdoor side seating.  The side area is the one we sat at.  It was overcast, a bit windy and cool, but this worked great for us.

My husband and I opted for two of their Specials.  I had the Lobster Eggs Benedict; he had the Hanna Banana Peanut Butter Oatmeal.  My choice was delicious.  The eggs were perfectly done.  The hollandaise sauce was creamy and flavorful. The lobster tasted very fresh and not a bit tough.

The real winner here was the Oatmeal.  There was about two spoons of peanut butter in the middle of the oatmeal.  It also included sliced bananas, sliced apples, and walnuts.  The combination of all, was fantastic.  I had a little taste because my husband wouldn't share more than that.  For the record I kept offering my breakfast to him.  He took a bite of mine and liked it; but he adamantly expressed the Oatmeal was exceptional and was very glad he got it.  A local very nice lady was having the oatmeal as well near our table.  She said that this is all she's ever had at Swami's and orders it every weekend.

They also have a great selection of self serve coffees.  We tried the blueberry coffee thinking we wouldn't like it and could get something else. It  turned out it was smooth, not too sweet,. simply delicious.

We will definitely return next time we are in the area.  Might try the one in Oceanside.  Other reviews indicate that the food is pretty consistent for all locations.  But this location is so unique odds are we'll be back to the 101 one.

text: I have been coming to Tu Lan for over 20 years. The food is always great even though I always get the same thing (#18 beef and rice noodles). There is the usual beef/pork/chicken/veggie entrees on offer so you will definitely be able to find something delicious. This is the 1st place I ever had Sriracha sauce all those years ago. Now it is an accepted condiment on our US tables. There is a counter downstairs if you are just dashing in for a quick bite, several tables and booths on the 1st floor, and even an upstairs dining area. Overall though, this is a pretty small restaurant. The waiter was super nice and easy-going. He even laughed at our table's jokes! My wife always celebrates her birthday here, and they even remember who she is because as I mentioned, we've been coming here for years. Even though the quality of the food is very high with fresh ingredients to please your palate, the overall cost is very reasonable. My favorite #18 used to be somewhere in the $5 range and now it is up to $9 something, but that is OK. San Francisco is friggin' expensive so whatevs! Holy crap, this place is hoppin! We went to Jjan for round 3 on a Wednesday and the place was filled with young Koreans. I can't imagine what it's like on the weekends.

The service was amazing here. They respond super fast to the bells. They forgot one of our dishes and when we nicely asked about it, she went and got it for us right away for free.

They have this really interesting frozen beer. The foam on top is thick and super cold. It really keeps the beer cold for an extended period of time. I was nursing my beer for over half an hour and it was still nice and cold.

I haven't tried too many of their dishes but the kim pi don was good. Kim pi don stands for kimchi pizza donkatsu. It's fried sliced pork, topped with this tomato and kimchi sauce then topped with melted cheese. They also have other variety of meat other than donkatsu. I saw this is Kdrama recently so I guess it's a thing in Korea right now.

They also had hot cheetos topped with nacho cheese. For $10, it's kind of a rip off but the nacho cheese really works with the hot cheetos. Eating all of that with chopsticks just feels so right.

I will be back again for sure to try their other dishes although I'll probably try to stick to weekdays so it's not too crowded.

Tried Little Jewel of New Orleans for the first time last night and it was yummy for the most part. The food was great and the store itself is great, too. They sell items from New Orleans that you probably cannot easily find here. They're soda game is on point, having seen a variety of different root beers, ginger beers and other sorts of beverages. They also sell containers of cold brew coffee that you'd enjoy.

But back to the food....

PO' BOY SANDWICHES: Any po' boy is tasty because the seasoning in the batter is great. You cannot go wrong with the shrimp po' boy or catfish po' boy sandwiches. Both are fantastic. If you're loving oyster and shrimp, go with half & half po' boy for just $16. ANY po' boy is 10 inches long so please consider sharing w/someone if you don't eat a lot.

The popular CRAWFISH MAC 'N CHEESE is good but not great, in my opinion. Definitely worth a try but given the size of the sandwich and side orders, I wouldn't order this dish again but glad I tasted it. The portion is quite hefty and can be shared between 3-4 people.

DESSERT: the bread pudding w/ whiskey sauce was a treat indeed. Not overly sweet and served hot-warm. YUM.

Parking Pro Tip: if you're arriving past 6pm (Mon-Sat), there is a yellow loading zone right in front where you can park for FREE. In addition, there's another yellow loading zone around the corner. Otherwise, standard metered street parking is available.

I'll be coming back for sure to try other dishes!!!

text:
Sad, I have lost a good old friend... I have been a vocal fan of cheesecake factory over the years, date nights, family nights, colleagues get together, cheesecake factory was always our constant. I somewhat feel bad that I had not a written a 5* review all those times I received a great service from great folks who were more than eager to make sure I was having the perfect time. Tonight I believe it was the breakup dinner, and I so tried to attribute it to the Christmas eve chaos. I walked in at 7:45, asked for a table for seven and was told that it would be 55-70 minutes, all making sense till that point. I went back home (8-minute drive) picked up my 80-year old parents, my 3-year old, looking to join a few friends at the restaurant. We got back at 8:50, a little towards the end of the promised window but feeling confident that we would get a table shortly. I checked in with the hostess and she gave me a lecture about having pinged me multiple times and not hearing back from me. I apologized and mentioned I was back within the window she promised me. The hostess then told me that our table was almost ready and they were waiting for the folks who had already paid to leave. I thanked her and joined my party on the side to wait for the imminent call (buzz). After about 20 minutes of waiting standing (my poor parents weren't complaining yet but I could see them moving from foot to foot), I approached the hostess counter and inquired about our wait. The same hostess was unapologetic, almost didn't look me in the eye, and said that the previous party was still at the table. And of course the lady again mentioned that we had missed our first chance of getting seated. At this point I told the hostess that if she knew we were not going to get seated within 10-15 minutes, it would completely be fine just that our party was too fragile and tired to wait while standing. I was ignored. Finally we were seated at 9:40 when I mentioned (to a different hostess) that our young child didn't need a seat and we could fit into a 6-people booth.

Our server was greasy with black stains all over his white apron. I asked for bread and a specific appetizer and was was told bread would take 15 minutes and they were soldout of the appetizer. I was really really bummed at that point.

It doesn't look like Cheesecake Factory cares about the service level as they used to. I liked the food and the warmth and service, but they have gone south. Take care Cheesecake Factory.

text:
Unlike its sister outlet at the San Jose Westfield Oakridge shopping mall, this particular branch handles the flow of seating its customers more efficiently.   As a result, there is not much of a long waiting time to get seated at a table.

Furthermore, the interior design of this branch is more conducive to a delightfully enjoyable eating experience and nice conversations due to the long row of huge glass windows running along the length of the wall facing the outdoors.  The restaurant's interior space looks less congested and less confusing than that of its Westfield Oakridge counterpart because of the floor plan's layout that extends the main dining section through the length of the floor space all the way to the rear and ends with the restroom area conveniently at the very back of the restaurant.

The food and service are expectedly exceptional as is typically the standard case for Cheesecake Factory restaurant outlets.  Nevertheless, I feel that this Santa Clara Cheese Factory restaurant has a slight edge within the South Bay area, second only to its other sister outlet at the Hillsdale Shopping Center in San Mateo.

name: Mariane Curti
text: Well, previously I'd rated this Cheesecake Factory 4 stars, but after my last visit there, I decided to change my review and the rating. The first issue was with the food. I ordered the Farfalle w/ Chicken but I was so disappointed when I received my plate. This plate was supposed to have some toppings (chicken, pancetta, tomato, mushroom and peas) but it was basically all pasta and no toppings, the quality was so poor for a $17 plate. The second issue was concerning the service. I could not believe when the waiter approached me while I was chewing my food (no, I had not called the waiter) and asked me if I was going to finish my entire plate, or if he could bring me a box or put my food on the box for me. YES, HE DID THAT, WHILE I WAS STILL EATING MY FOOD! Just don't come here on a weekend if you expect a quiet scene.

Aside from the bar scene, they have great food too...I've only ever had the pizza, but it is always good and reasonably priced. Make a night of it!

name: Jennifer Hunker
text:
WHAT IT IS
A fairly standard chain restaurant with a twist--BJs prides itself on its brewery.

WHAT YOU SHOULD ORDER
Beer and mixed beers.

AMBIANCE
4 stars

While I love the *look* of BJs, its popularity combined with its open concept makes it a very loud, lively place. If you're like me and prefer intimacy at your restaurants, this is not for you. The bar especially tends to get raucous during happy hour.

FOOD AND DRINKS
3 Stars

I don't know what it is about this particular BJs, but every time I've come something has gone wrong with my orders. I'm not the sort to usually send things back, but this restaurant holds the honor of being the only one that has ever served me a RAW hamburger. The hamburger's toppings themselves were great, but the patty was hardly lukewarm in the middle and was clearly uncooked. Really scary. I've also ordered their salmon and received it overcooked and dry. Unpleasant, to say the least.  :(

With the burger, my server DID make it right, however, and the second burger was perfect. That's why I've awarded 4 stars--mistakes happen, but good service and friendly servers really do make a difference.

On my last visit I ordered the roast beef dip, which was a standard beef dip--a welcome surprise. Unfortunately we were also seated next to a table of 30 who were pretty rowdy (and who insisted on standing around their table as though they were at the bar). Again--I don't know what it is with this particular BJs.

Their beer, however, is phenomenal. They have a number of beers ranging from very light to very dark, so there's definitely something for everyone. I especially like their mixed concoctions.

NICE SURPRISES
The Chili and Sriracha Queso dip was a really fun spin on the classic queso dip. The servers are also really pleasant at this location.

OVERALL
If you're looking for some interesting beers and mixed beers, give this place a try. Just don't come at peak hours--it gets crowded and the kitchen at this location has a tendency to over or undercook food. Both times I had trouble here (the undercooked burger and overcooked salmon) were during dinner service--my stops for lunch or early dinner (around 4PM) resulted in a quieter restaurant and much better food.

text: We did an overnight trip to Turlock, CA just to see what was in the area. After checking in our hotel, we decided Italian food sounded good. We were given a list of suggested restaurants in the area when we checked in. Who would have thought Turlock, CA would have one of the best Italian restaurants we have ever ate at! The restaurant stands alone in a kind of residential neighborhood. It's a small restaurant, but it is very quaint, well decorated, and a great setting for dinner. They had a kids menu for my daughter so, I give any restaurant bonus points when I see that. As far as Italian food goes, they have just about anything you could want on their menu. I wouldn't say prices are high, but you will pay between $12-$18, depending on what you order. The food presentation was visually pleasing and the food tasted incredible! I judge how well I like a meal by how my plate looks at the end of that meal. If the plate has very little food left on it, to incude sauces, I loved it. Needless to say, it was hard to tell my plate ever had food on it, after this meal! So, if you ever find yourself in Turlock, CA and you are looking for a good meal, I would highly recommend you stop by Villa Napoli.

name: Roy Chi
text:
*4.5 stars*

I traveled to Buenos Aires last year and I've been craving Argentine food ever since. Lolinda is definitely the closest I've ever had outside of Argentina. Sure, the beef isn't as good as in Argentina, but the flavors here are absolutely on point.

I really love what they've done to what was once the tacky and grimy Medjool. The decor is great, the atmosphere is bustling, and the service was incredible (thanks to Mia).

------------------
FOOD: (Best to worst)

Ojo de Bife (Rib-eye):
- Oh man, this is definitely one of the best steaks I've had in SF. The flavor, the perfect medium-rare, the globs of fatty goodness -- everything about this steak is wonderful (other than the fact that it's not Argentine beef). I would choose this slab of steak over Bobo's or Ruth's Chris or Alexander's any day.

Bone Marrow:
- One of the best and tastiest bone marrows I've had in SF. With the subtly sweet chimichurri, this bone marrow is perfectly cooked and well-seasoned. A bit too oily at times (don't put on too much chimichurri), but delicious nonetheless.

Ceviche Mixto:
- Fresh ceviche with an addicting corn fritter.

Sweetbreads:
- I'm not a huge fan of sweetbreads, but this was cooked very well. Excellent juxtaposition of the crispy exterior and the soft interior.

Pork Belly:
- Good crispy pork belly, but a bit overdone. Great flavor though.

Tres Leches (Dessert):
- A bit too sweet, but the tres leches flavor explodes pretty significantly. I loved the combination of the milky cake with crispy madeline.

Corn Empanadas:
- A bit bland (could've used a stronger flavor), but definitely a good empanada. Compared to the ones I've had in Buenos Aires, though, these don't even compare.

Blood Sausage:
- I was really mixed on this one. I feel like there wasn't enough blood in there to give it the pasty, grainy texture that blood sausage should have. Instead, it tasted a bit too mushy and wet, as if it was undercooked. In fact, it had the consistency of beef tartare. Went decently well with the bread though.

----------------------

All in all, Lolinda is a very refreshing and welcome addition to the SF tapas community. I will definitely come back for this rib-eye.

text:
Love this new Pho place. It's in the same area of Superior Market. Plenty of parking and close to 60 Fwy. Very modern and CLEAN, CLEAN, CLEAN, specially, its RESTROOMS. Lol. How many times can you say that to an Asian restaurant? (Don't get me wrong, I'm also an Asian, just telling the truth. Lol). I like the concept of ordered and paid at the counter. They'll give you a number to place at the table and food will serve quickly after that. After finishing your meal, just get up and go. So convenient. It saves lots of time compare to a traditional Asian restaurant, whereas, you have to flag down someone for the bill and then again, to pay for it. Especially, when you have to hurry get back to work after lunch.

Food taste AMAZING. My husband got a Beef Salad while I got a Chicken salad. Very generous portions. Both beef and chicken were tendered and tasted soooo delicious. Nothing can beat the taste of lemongrass that comes with it. IMO. Egg roll is also good, so crispy and perfect to taste. No need for dipping sauce, and best of all, IT'S FREE. FYI, it comes with every entree. Thumbs up Pho Shack. Its Passion fruit juice is so refreshing!!! One more cool thing here is its COCA-COLA Freestyle fountain. You can mix a variety of flavors of your choice, as much as you'd like because it's FREE REFILL too. Last, but not least, its Vietnamese coffee tasted awesome.

Service is attentive. While we were here, Kevin, the manager came out to greet customers, he carefully listened to our feedback regarding of food, service, cleanliness... He seemed to genuinely care about customers feedback. With good location, nice and clean, good food, good service, good management, and affordable price... what could go wrong??? Give it a try, I guarantee you won't be disappointed.
We'll definitely come back to try its Pho next time. Highly recommend this restaurant to everyone.

text:
(Translated by Google) HALAL CITIZENS IN SAN FRANCISCO

In California, there are good eateries, especially in the cities of Los Angeles and San Francisco, which specialize in burgers, but it is not very easy to find places that have halal meat on the menu.

In San Francisco, there is Ziggy's Burger, which offers halal burgers worth trying.

The place is very central near Union Square and right by the ferry port. The decor is nice and the selection is wide from breakfast to dessert.

We limited ourselves to trying their specialty, which is burger. The choice ended up with lamb burger with goat cheese, where we also got french fries next door.

Prices are reasonable. One burger costs about $ 10, which equals $ 70, but the lamb burger was slightly more expensive than the others ($ 14 = $ 97).

Ziggy's Burger is a recommended eatery for burger lovers looking for great taste, friendly service and clean surroundings.

(Original)
HALAL BURGER I SAN FRANCISCO

I Californien findes der gode spisesteder, især i storbyerne Los Angeles og San Francisco, som har specialiseret sig i burgere, men det er ikke særlig nemt at finde steder, der har halal kød på menuen.

I San Francisco findes Ziggy's Burger, som tilbyder halal burgere, der er værd at prøve.

Stedet ligger meget centralt i nærheden af Union Square og lige ved færgehavnen. Indretningen er flot og udvalget er bredt fra morgenmad til dessert.

Vi begrænsede os til at prøve deres specialitet, som er burger. Valget endte på lammeburger med gedeost, hvor vi også fik pommes frites ved siden af.

Priserne er rimelige. En burger koster omkring 10 USD, hvilket svarer til 70 DKK, men lammeburgeren var lidt dyrere end de andre (14 USD = 97 DKK).

Ziggy’s Burger er et anbefalingsværdigt spisested for burger-elskere, der søger efter god smag, venlig betjening og rene omgivelser.

If you're looking to adopt a cat, some of the ones here are up for adoption, so if you find a match you might be able to take it home. And if you're not looking to adopt, spending time with cats is still wonderful, and the cost goes to supporting the cats and helping this place stay in business and shelter the cats who do need adoption. You get to play with cats, support their wellbeing, the cats get to be played with and petted, and the cats who need adoption have increased chances over being unseen at a shelter. It's a win-win-win-win!

name: My Le
text:
This place is beautiful at night! Small parking lot but you can see the blue LED lights surrounding the edges of the building from afar.

We got on the waitlist and received a text 40 minutes later for a party of 4 adults, 3 kids, and a dog. We got seated in the patio which had heaters above and very dim lighting that it was difficult for the kids to  color. The tables weren’t spaced apart but had the clear  glass between tables. Inside seating had distancing and tons of cocktail and spirit products on the floor that you can purchase.

It’s a four page menu and three of them were all sorts of spirits. Would have been four stars but knocked one off due to too much ice in my cocktail. I ordered rum mojito and was asked if I wanted it from the bar or canned. I said bar and had a choice of classic rum, pineapple rum, or black rum. Over 90% was all ice.

All the food were average and decent. I think it’s more about the atmosphere and drinks.

Crispy chicken wings - choice of habanero  Buffalo sauce or barrel aged rum mustard  bbq sauce. We got the latter.

Mushroom and leaks Flat bread - fontina cheese, lemon cream sauce, mushrooms, leeks, arugula. Already feel healthy ordering this dish.

Chili spiced pork chicharrons  - came with gaucachili sauce which didn’t taste spicy to me.

**Charred sugar snap peas with burrata - crunchy and sweet. Another healthy dish.

**Red pepper umami Bread - OMG this was my favorite dish of the night. The bread was so good! Soft and moist. It’s gojuchang sourdough bread with cutwater bourbon shoyu honey butter flavor. Gojuchang is a Korean chili paste but it wasn’t spicy at all.

Smoked pork belly mac & cheese - I’m not a Mac and cheese gal but this was alright. Not too cheesy because of the white cheddar. The pork belly was smoked not braised so it didn’t really melt in your mouth.

We ordered all appetizers and one main dish as family style and ate between 4 adults. The three little kids shared a grilled cheese sandwich from the kids menu.

Great prices, great quality. I wish there was a Donuttery location in Los Angeles.

Donuttery has amazing doughnut flavors in yeast and cake. They are most famous for their blueberry cake doughnuts (and also my favorite). Other cake flavors are strawberry, red velvet, salted caramel apple and lemon glazed blueberry doughnuts. The cake flavors are most popular because they are unique and diverse.

Are you vegan? No problem. They also make vegan blueberry cake flavors (but sells out fast).

They don't charge you an arm and a leg for these delicious desserts, either. They are awesome for offering flexible price packages if you were looking to get a dozen (mix and match). Depending on who is helping you, they usually throw in a few FREE doughnuts on the house.
