(Translated by Google) 800 GRADERS NAPOLİTANSK PİZZA İ LA

If you fancy a Neapolitan pizza while in Los Angeles, one of the options is to take a walk past 800 Degrees Pizza, which has 5 branches in the city. We chose to try it in Westwood, which is located between Beverly Hills and Santa Monica.

The concept is very cool. You can even make your own pizza from a Margherita, where the ingredients such as flour, tomato and mozarella come from Italy and are of the same quality as in Naples.

The pizzas get ready in 90 seconds in a stove that gets 800 degrees hot.

The shop has a nice decor with a good atmosphere where you can follow how your pizza is made in open kitchen.

The prices are very reasonable. A Margherita costs $ 10 ($ 10) and each accessory can be added for $ 1 ($ 1).

800 Degrees Pizza is a recommended pizzeria that makes good Neapolitan pizzas. Especially the dough, which was nice airy, like in Naples.

(Original)
800 GRADERS NAPOLİTANSK PİZZA İ LA

Hvis man får lyst til en napolitansk pizza, når man befinder sig i Los Angeles, er en af mulighederne at tage en tur forbi 800 Degrees Pizza , som har 5 afdelinger i byen. Vi valgte at prøve den i Westwood, som er placeret mellem Beverly Hills og Santa Monica.

Konceptet er meget fedt. Man kan selv opbygge sin egen pizza fra en Margherita, hvor råvarerne som mel, tomat og mozarella kommer fra Italien og er af samme kvalitet ligesom i Napoli.

Pizzaerne bliver klar på 90 sekunder i en brændeovn, der bliver 800 grader varmt.

I love Isaan food. In case you don't know, that's Northeastern Thai food that mostly consists of sour and spicy salad of some nature (e.g. papaya salad, larb, etc), grilled meat with dipping sauce, and sticky rice. When I heard that a joint called Sticky Rice opened in Grand Central Market, I was dying to try it.

When I saw that the Tiger Cry was $15, I was a little reluctant to get it but I'm so glad I did. So it is a little expensive but it's the best Thai grilled beef I've had. Th quality of the meat was magnificent and it was perfectly cooked to medium rare. They give you this delicious dipping sauce, a bag of sticky rice, and some papaya salad. The portion on the papaya salad is small and it wasn't too flavorful.

They don't have a large variety on their menu but there is a specials board off to the side. I believe that the specials menu is constantly changing. I will definitely come back to try their grilled chicken, which is listed on their regular menu.

The wait for the food was quite long. I had to wait close to 20 minutes for my order. They do take credit cards. You can park in the adjacent structure for free as long as you get a validation.

text:
This place is good and has a large menu including lunch food.  The coffee tastes good but as one reviewer noted, comes in a small cup.  Fortunately I was there when it wasn't crowded so refills were quick.  I had the chicken fried steak and eggs with home fries:

The chicken fried steak: Excellent.  Loads of good gravy on top and with lots of sausage pieces.  Not sausage bits, not just pepper, honest sausage pieces.  The steak was good with the right amount of breading and fried crisp.  Really delicious.

The Home fries: Thinly sliced, fried potatoes, fried crisp on the outside of the pile and tender and warm inside.  Very good, not too greasy and just the right amount of fried.

The eggs: I requested over easy but they were a bit overdone as some of the yolk had congealed.  I prefer the yolk completely liquid.  So only a grade of "fair" on the eggs.

Service was excellent.  Prices were a bit high but not outrageous.  I will be back again.

text: The bathroom is way too small, and poorly ventilated for the amount of people using it. There's no paper towel dispensers in the bathroom at all, they offer air dryers only. There's no Pilot/FJ hot food here. The food store is very small. The selection is poor, and the prices are high. The Bacon Breakfast Burrito was $7 and it was mostly potatoes, double-wrapped gummy tortilla, and powdered eggs, I didn't see, or taste any bacon in it at all. There's not much going on within walking distance except a Burger King. The shower didn't have a fan, and the shower exhaust was poor, you can't open the door a crack because most shower doors are on the main hallway everyone from the lot uses. The employees are super nice, and yet most drivers seem to hate this place. I watched a trucker dragging a soiled mattress, and gleefully place it next to a trash can. The dutiful employees just grabbed it with the trash as if it was just a another normal day for them. When you enter the lot you have to take a ticket from the automated machine to get the entry gate to open. Don't lose that ticket, there's a ridiculous penalty for lost tickets, and the first 4 hours are free. If you buy 75 gallons, or buy $50 worth of goods inside the store you get Free Overnight Parking, otherwise it's $15 a night to park. If you do meet those requirements to validate your parking you have to bring the receipts inside the food store, or to the service shop with your entry ticket to get it validated. The guard shack at the exit gate will NOT validate your entry ticket even if you have your receipts with you. That must be done inside the food store, or the service shop prior to exiting. The guard shack at the exit gate ONLY takes Visa, MasterCard, and American Express. The guard shack does NOT take cash, or any fuel card as payment. In the morning turn on your CB, and plan on wasting some time in line trying to get out of the lot as drivers yell at the exit guard. Also leave plenty of room in front of you while you're in line as somebody is always trying to back out from the guard shack so they can park and go back inside the food store to get their parking validated, or pay with cash. This is a loud daily drama played out around a window of 5am on the CB several times in the morning, every weekday morning as drivers try to thread the needle of appointment times, beating bay area traffic, and saving their 14 hour clock. Stop honking your horn driver, you should have left earlier. If you can stay outside of town the night before at the Trucks Stops in Fernley, NV definitely do it. Don't stop here if you don't have to.

text:
Being a drunk that I am, I made sure to get my money's worth of the bottomless mimosas during brunch at Equator. For only $10, you can choose from lychee, apple, or orange mimosas and there are several "premium" flavors you can select from for $5 additional. Once you pick your flavor though, you are committed to it because they won't let you change it around.

I got the lychee and it was delicious. The apple and the orange was not very good at all. I saw other people drinking different premium flavors and they look pretty good, especially the blue one.

They have a regular menu, which consists of appetizers, salads, sandwiches, and a few American dishes. During brunch though, they have dim sum for $3 each. I liked the baked bbq pork buns and the shrimp shu mai. I didn't care for the other items much but the flavors were definitely authentic. They make each one to order so it does take some time to come out.

Our waitress was so nice and patient. We were there for a long time and she didn't rush us. She was on top of bringing us everything we need and kept checking up on us. In fact, she kept the mimosas flowing to the point where we had to ask her to give us a little break because we couldn't drink it fast enough.

The restaurant itself is hidden in the alleyway where Jake's and Three Dog Bakery is in Old Town. They do have a few outside seating. I would recommend parking at the structure on Green and Fair Oaks. It's 90 minutes free only though.

This was a great place to go for a dinner to celebrate my mothers birthday.  We brought all the kids with us so it was quite the crew.

Two of the kids saw Mac and Cheese on the happy hour menu while we waited in the bar and locked in on that.  Problem was they didnt offer mac and cheese as a kids meal in the dining room.  The waiter was very accommodating though, he had them ring it up as the chicken tenders kids meal and substituted the mac and cheese.

The oldest kid decided he only wanted to eat appetizers so we got a few extra, but they didn't fill him up since everyone was sharing them.  Fortunately they were happy to allow him to share bowls of chili and soup from the salad bar that came with each of our four adult entrees.

I had the shrimp scampi and it was great.  I loved the salad bar, and tried several different combos.  The only salad I didn't like was the Asian chicken salad, which didn't taste quite right.

The kids were amazed by the views and wanted to look out the window all night.

Overall this was a very enjoyable first dining experience at Orange County Mining Company.

text:
There's no better sandwich shop in the Loma Linda area than Angelo's! Weather you want a turkey and avocado on squaw, a truly delicious roast beef on wheat or the world's best meatball sub, this is the spot you need to try.

Angelo's has been serving some of the best food at the same location for over 30 years. As the restaurant has been passed down from father to son, so has the tradition of excellent food with quality ingredients. I can proudly say that I've been eating here for over 20 years.

My personal favorites are the meatball sandwich on a grinder roll or the pastrami on sourdough. The garlic rolls are a taste that you will never forget and they will also leave you with a craving for more. I am happy that I am now a father and bring my wife and children to the same location that I've been enjoying for so many years. I highly recommend that you bring your family to see what people from Loma Linda have been raving about for over three decades.

text:
-WHAT DID I GET:  The shrimp fried rice and the fried dumplings and a coke.

-HOW WAS IT:  The side dishes at this place are legitimately some of the best side dishes I've had at any Korean restaurant.

Unfortunately, I can't say the same for the main dishes.  The fried dumplings were somewhat bland and the filling was soggy, and the shrimp fried rice was really mushy and also bland.

I asked them to make my fried rice spicy, and this request seemed to perplex the staff; they genuinely had no idea how to make something spicy.

I asked them, "Don't you guys have any sort of peppers, or some Korean spices or anything?"

They nodded.

"Then add some of that in to make it spicy, please," I said.

Yet still, my fried rice came out bland.

The service was friendly, though.

-HOW MUCH DID IT COST:  Including tip, it cost me $29.50.  I should say this, though - they give you A LOT of food.  Like...they gave me two meals worth of food.

If I had one suggestion for this place, it would be to reduce the portion size and price of their dishes.

-WOULD I COME BACK/RECOMMEND THIS PLACE:  Probably no to both.  There are simply better Korean restaurants out here in Korea Town for the same price or cheaper.

name: Roy Chi
text:
*4.5 stars*

Lers Ros Thai may or may not be the best Thai food in the city, but it's definitely the most exciting. It's like homecooked Thai food amped up ten-fold -- there are Thai dishes I've never seen on a menu before, and there are variations to typical Thai staples that will blow your mind. The pungent flavors and fire-hot spiciness here are phenomenal, packing punches harder than with any Thai food I've had outside of Thailand. After my first visit, I was absolutely hooked, and now when I feel like eating Thai food, I'm essentially saying that I feel like eating Lers Ros.

------------------
FOOD:

Crispy Pork Belly = It's weird, this dish lacks consistency, even within the same plate. When the piece is done right, it's possibly the best crispy pork belly in the city. The spice, the intense flavor, the ultra-crispy skin, the tender meat -- it all just blends together perfectly. However, within the same plate, there are also pieces that are too tough, too dry, and too overcooked. There are also other pieces where the skin is soggy rather than crispy. It's really strange and somewhat disappointing. But because I know how DELICIOUS the good pieces are, I always keep ordering this dish and will probably continue to order this dish for as long as I eat at Lers Ros.

Yum Koh Moo Yang (Pork Shoulder Salad) = Tender pieces of pork shoulder that go incredibly well with the salad.

Papaya Salad w/ Grilled Prawns = My vote for the best papaya salad in SF. The spice level here is through the roof, making this a dangerous dish for people who can't handle their peppers. The prawns are well-cooked, the papaya is nice and crunchy, and everything just works together excellently.

Fried Quail = Pretty good. This dish rides a dangerously-thin line, since it could easily be tough and overcooked. I had pieces that were, for sure, but when it's done well, it's delicious.

Green Curry = Very good. Green curry is one of those dishes that's tough to get wrong, and Lers Ros definitely doesn't get it wrong. Again, the intense spice is what makes this a winner.

------------------

Lers Ros Thai breathes unique and exciting life into your typical Thai fare. With Basil Thai and Marnee Thai, among others, there's tons of great Thai food competition in the city; but Lers Ros is definitely the one that stands out for its ingenuity and boldness.

name: Solomiya Lyshenyuk Williams
text:
I like this place. They have a great selection of cheeses, craft beers and all kinds of sodas you never heard of, which always gets me excited :)

We had a "french" sandwich: T-Brie-D, and it is a bomb. Second, we had a "pork" sandwich: Banh Mi Oh My, and it is okay. Just okay. We also had a bowl of tomato soup.

T-Brie-D (french) is a "must try at least once" kind of meal.
Banh Mi Oh My (pork) is the kind of sandwich you can never have again in your life and you would be okay with it, but if you happen to have it again you'd be okay with it too.
Tomato soups falls in that same category as the "pork" sandwich.

Despite all of my liking of this eatery, 2 negatives (not a deal breaker, but every place has some, and it wouldn't be fair not to mention them):

1. It's a little pricey. We had 2 sandwiches, 1 bowl of soup and a soda for lunch and our bill came out to be $52 (including taxes and a 15% tip). I don't know, maybe I am wrong for saying it's expensive. I just compare it to the "opportunity" value of these $52, and in our restaurant adventures, $52 usually will also entail lots of leftovers, which is good for the next day lunch/dinner. So, in truth, $52 converts to $13/meal (2 people, 4 meals total), and in this case it came up to be $26/meal (2 people, 2 meals total).

2. Really cramped. Looks like they have a lot of interest (demand) and not a lot of space (supply), which is probably an explanation for higher prices. Tables are located very close together, which is obnoxious for waiters (not to mention the customers), because they have to ask customers to move every time they want to get to the table in the corner.
From a pure business prospective, your overhead cost per customer will go down if you expend. And that's because it looks like you will have more customers (demand) than the increase of some overhead cost (like rent, wages, and amortization), which in turn will allow for retail prices' reduction, which will bring even more customers. Not to mention that a bigger place will attract more customers because it won't be cramped anymore. Do your math :)

text:
Roka Akor is one of the most solid restaurants I've been to in some time. The decor is incredible (bright lights, neo-contemporary deisgn, huge open kitchen), the food is delicious, and the service is impeccable. It's an upscale restaurant, but injects a casual feel that makes it perfect for anything from anniversaries to business meetings to catchups with friends.

What stood out for me was what they did for my friend for her birthday. We wrote down that it was her birthday on our Open Table reservation and, upon our arrival, she was greeted with a glass of complimentary champagne and a warm "Happy Birthday." When our dinner ended, she was presented with a complimentary dessert and candle, with a personal rendition of Joe Cocker's "You Are So Beautiful" sung by our incredible server, Carlos. THIS is how birthdays should be celebrated at a restaurant (are you listening, Atelier Crenn?!?).

The food at Roka Akor was phenomenal for the most part, although there were a few misses here and there:

BEST =
- Beef Tataki w/ Truffles
- Pork Belly
- Butterfish Tataki
- O-Toro Nigiri

GREAT =
- Uni Chicarrones
- Miso Black Cod
- Prime Rib Eye
- Sweet Corn

OKAY =
- Soft-Shell Maki w/ Kimchi Aioli
- Robata Scallops
- Gulf Shrimp Tempura

For dessert: the Cheesecake was excellent, the Warm Chocolate Cake was delicious.

It was a pricey meal, of course ($410 after tax/tip and a bottle of $70 wine), but for the incredible food, ambiance, and service, it was worth every penny.

text:
My partner and I took a day trip from SF to Half Moon Bay (typical, right?). She made it a point to mention this nook along the sandy coast. This reminded me of my cousin who often says that she's willing to drive two hours for some good food. Luckily, I only had to drive out under an hour.

We had just made it on time before close since I had the bright idea of having French Toast and Greek coffee right before. (This is a habit I picked up from the aforementioned cousin). From sweet, we made our way to savory.

I'm not fond of cow burgers, so I opted for the mushroom sandwich and cucumber soup. I asked for coffee but they had begun their cleaning process and coffee was already out. "No problem. I know you're about to close", I said.

[Side note: Don't be the jerk who insists on having coffee less than 10 minutes before close. Three bros that popped in after us did so. This is someone who likely has never worked in the service industry. I would have chargned them for the entire pot and poured cups for the other clients on his tab. But that's just me. Scott Clark was much more gracious about it. Anyway, back to the food.]

Pro Tip: DO NOT UNWRAP THE SANDWICH! The best part is at the bottom wherein all the juices have concentrated and make for a mouthwatering last bite.

As a newb, I undid the wrap and had to eat it like a caveman. Though, I left no drop or crumb behind. The tang, the texture, the sweetness of the cucumber soup felt like a breezy beach volleyball game on my pallet. Moreover, a spike of flavor hit as I bit into a leaf of fresh basil served with the soup. (Cavemen wished they could eat like this!)

On top of this Scott came out and served us with the biggest smile this side of Half Moon Bay. I suppose having worked at Saison makes him jaded when it comes to handling douchey bros. But I would have loved to sip that cup of joe on that dude's tab.

I love it when I can try out a small business in Poway and actually like the food. Please continue to support your local small business!

I actually never knew this place existed. It’s wedged between Five Guys and Little Ceasars. What attracted me was the oversized big banner that referenced 19% off entire bill.

I ordered for pick up: Tonkotsu ramen ($11.48), shrimp tempura udon ($10.98), and a lunch bento box that came with rice, salad, miso soup, 2 piece CA rolls, 4 tempura, 2 gyoza, a small drink and a protein ($9.98). I got chicken teriyaki.

They packaged the bag very tightly and neat. I was afraid of the udon and ramen broth spilling but they put a small piece of card board at the bottom of the bag for support.

The udon and ramen noodles where kept separately in a container and the broth was still super hot. Both broths were good but udon tasted like what you can make from the store. The tonkotsu broth was yummy and creamy. The ramen was tasty and had texture and chewy. I would order the ramen again but the udon.

The bento box was well worth the price. I wish the chicken had more teriyaki drizzle because it was a bit dry. Can’t go wrong with tempura and they gave a huge container of sauce to dip. It was all veggie but the udon came with one shrimp tempura. I was also surprised that the lunch bento prince was offered on a weekend.

Please don’t forget to tip more since 19% discount was given.

text:
Fat Angel is a craft beer gastropub that is the perfect blend of artisan fanciness and casual garage grunge. It's difficult to describe, but very pleasant to experience.

The list of craft beers, both bottled and on tap, is phenomenal. Being an avid IPA drinker, I was blown away by the IPA selection here -- ordering three different IPAs and loving each one. I can't wait to try all of the beers here; challenge accepted.

The food is definitely better than your average gastropub, but nothing amazing.

--------------------
FOOD:

Flatbread w/ Mushroom & Truffle Oil: This is a dish that's excellent upon first bite, but gets progressively worse as time cools the cheese. I mean, you can't really go wrong with mushroom and truffle oil on anything, so the taste was definitely there. When the cheese hardens, however, it just tastes stale. Sidenote: I spread some duck liver mousse on it and it was incredible.

Pretzel: It was okay. I wish there was another sauce than mustard.

Cheese Plate w/ Duck Liver Mousse: The duck liver mousse was excellent. When spread upon the bread (or the flatbread), it gave me a faint glimpse of what I loved most about foie gras before the ban.

--------------------

Fat Angel is an excellent joint for beer enthusiasts. If you love craft beers, then you really can't go wrong with this place. Even if you're a craft beer newbie, the knowledgeable and friendly bartenders here will lead you in the right direction. If you're not a beer lover and you're looking for excellent gastropub fare, you may be disappointed.

Endless mimosa and delicious brunch menus. The Table is a must go. Granted the lines are long, but wake up earlier so you can start the festivities earlier. There is a parking garage nearby, but it does fill up (thus go early).

They have a wide variety of drinks and food options so there definitely is something for everyone. We were lucky they still had their special monkey bread left so we nabbed one of the last ones!

I’ve sat at the bar and sat on tables. Must say, if you have just 2-3 people, sitting at the bar next to the kitchen is not a bad option. You get seated faster and you get to watch the kitchen staff prepare all the food.

The waitresses are all super nice. No matter how busy they are, they always spot an empty coffee mug or mimosa glass (they always fill it up to the brim).

Overall, if you want a local place to go. This is it. Good food fun times await.

name: Natalie K
text:
The best frickin deal in Mexican food ever. No wonder there is always a crowd here at Salsa & Beer.

Compared to their sister location in North Hollywood, which is significantly more on crack, this Salsa & Beer in Lake Balboa is much more mellow and the wait time is a lot more reasonable. When it's cold out, there is usually no wait to sit on the patio outside.

They give you unlimited chips and this cheesy bean dip when you dine in. There is a guy who keeps coming around with new baskets of chips and bowls of bean dip without you having to ask. There is also a salsa bar for you to help yourself to. I love their green salsa and the avocado sauce.

I usually get the California burrito here although everything else is good. The burrito comes with chicken, steak and shrimp. It is then covered in this amazingly delicious melty cheese and served with beans and rice. It's less than $10 and I usually get 3 meals out of it.

The service is great. There is a waitress there who helped us the last few times. She always makes conversation even though they're busy and is super friendly.

name: Roy Chi
text:
Ike's Place has just been dethroned.

The Boca sandwich is the prime example of what sandwiches should be: a generous portion of delicious corned beef pastrami and brisket, held together by warm, aromatic French bread and an addicting Board Sauce (much like the Dirty Sauce at Ike's). Each bite packs a wallop of flavor that renders you speechless for a minute or two. Add in some spicy peppers or the habanero hot sauce, and you'll have yourself one of the best sandwiches that SF has to offer.

The BG is also incredible -- filled with their tender brisket, cheddar cheese, spicy peppers, and the Board Sauce. Due to the peppers, this one definitely brings some heat, and the flavors mesh together perfectly. Get this if you're not as much of a corned beef fan, and you'd like to stick to traditional brisket.

Yes, the sandwiches are a bit pricey at around $11 each, but the quality of the ingredients, the size of the sandwiches, and the explosive power of the flavors make it one hell of a deal.

Think of Deli Board like a mature adult version of Ike's Place. Ike's is colorful and fun -- delicious flavors, but the ingredients are just good enough to get by. Deli Board adds in freshness and quality to the mix, while still being incredibly delicious. When all is said and done, Deli Board is just plainly far superior.

name: Roy Chi
text:
*4.5 stars*

I felt like I was reaching the end of my rope with Contemporary-American-French cuisine. Restaurant after restaurant, it just seemed like the same old dishes -- roasted chicken (or quail), braised short ribs, or grilled pork chop with some kind of tart fruit glaze. It got to the point where I started to never crave anything that was "Contemporary-American-French." In fact, without foie gras, I feel like French food (at least in SF) has become boring in general. Tasty, perhaps, but boring. That is until I came to Bouche.

Now, there were some small misses here and there, but honestly, the food at Bouche breathes so much new creative life into the SF food scene that it's worth those small flaws to enjoy a meal that actually makes Contemporary French exciting again.

--------------
FOOD:

Scallops:
I loved the intricate and subtly sweet flavor to this dish. The dish is a cold dish, which kind of caught me off guard, but the scallops were insanely tender.

Marinated Salmon:
This was one of my favorite dishes of the night. The salmon meshed perfectly with the crunchy (equivalent of a) bird's nest and the creme fraiche. I've never had anything like this before and it was an incredible first.

Lamb Shoulder:
I normally don't like lamb due to its sour gaminess, but the lamb shoulder is cooked to absolute perfection. It tastes like a very tender braised beef short rib, which is awesome for those who normally hate lamb. What really makes this dish, though, is the sauce -- a sweet marmalade with crunchy almonds-- that really brings out the flavor of the lamb shoulder. I could've done without the tangy sorbet-like carrot coriander puree, since there was so much sweetness in the marmalade already. Perhaps a more subtle puree, like turnip or potato, would complement the marmalade better.

Veal:
The veal had an amazing flavor, but it was a bit too well-done. Whatever flavors they used though, worked very well.

Creme Fraiche Panna Cotta:
This dessert was a bit too boring and tasteless for me, except those moments when all you have in your mouth is salt (not enjoyable either). The caramel sauce was a nice touch, but it just needed something else to really make this panna cotta memorable.

--------------

Bouche has an intimate, hidden atmosphere that really brings out a rustic, underground Paris ambiance. It's actually pretty cool. Kind of reminds me of the upstairs section of Gitane.

Shane, our server, was on point. Our water was always filled, our wine glasses were never empty.

All in all, what I love most about Bouche is that it really pushes the envelope when it comes to discovering wildly inventive flavors. Most of what I ate tonight brought flavors and textures that I've never had before, and it was incredible to experience. I'm impatiently looking forward to a return visit.

We were seated right away and our server gave us a few minutes before asking for our drink orders. We got a large bottle of cold sake. Very delicious.

For food, we got a cod clay pot, a radish wrap, a beef wrap that was fried, a braised pork belly, sashimi plate, pizza, agedashi tofu, and fried chicken. My favorite was the braised pork belly. It was sweet and the meat fat melted away. But it did not leave me feeling oily. I definitely would recommend it. The other dish I would recommend is the chicken wings. It is not like any fried chicken I’ve had before. The batter was light and crispy. I would have hoped the chicken had better batter to meat ratio, but that’s not really the fault of the restaurant. Was just a skinny chicken.

Overall, definitely recommended!

WAYFARE BURGER 'le grande': Good. No Chez Maman burger, but I have tried and tried again to find another burger as good (it hasn't happened, but I continue on my quest). It was solid.
ICED TEA: Great. I'm all for cute little pitchers. It came with a syrup to sweeten, never figured out what it was, but I told myself it was a cranberry syrup. It was a little sour and sweet.

The popovers were worth the visit, the service was excellent, and while neither entrée blew my mind, I feel certain there is something on the menu that would. I'll be back.

text:
*2.5 stars*

Papalote is really ALL about the salsa. When it comes to Mexican food, however, great salsa is awesome, but it's definitely not the make-or-break factor. Papalote has amazing salsa, but that's pretty much all it has going for it.

When you're a hole-in-the-wall Mexican restaurant in the Mission, then you've got to have some pretty incredible food to even be in the competition. Papalote is okay, but definitely not even close to what's available in the Mission.

I got the carne asada super burrito, and including being more expensive than El Farolito or La Taqueria, it was also much more subpar. The meat was tender, but it was lukewarm. In fact, everything was just lukewarm. The rice tasted strangely old. I mean, it was okay, but definitely nothing special.

The chips they provide are horrible. Overly crunchy and overly fried, they were pretty bad for a Mexican joint in the Mission. The guacamole was flavorless -- just a bowl of avocados mushed together.

I did get a jar of their salsa to go (yeah it's really THAT awesome) but the food itself was just lackluster all the way through. Unfortunate.

I started with the Moscow Mule - sobieski vodka, angostura bitters, ginger beer.  This was really good.  Nice tart ginger flavor.

For entree, I had the Beer Battered Fish & Chips - true cod, union secret sauce, sea salt, kennebec fries.  I have it before and its always good. ARTICHOKE AND CHEESE TART
This was the star of the meal. It was fantastic.

HAMACHI CRUDO WITH MEYER LEMON GELEE

HAZELNUT AND HONEY ENCRUSTED RACK OF LAMB
The lamb was good. Not great. The red quinoa and asparagus were very good. Call me crazy, but I felt that the minted pea puree that came with my husband's scallops was a better match for the lamb than the tomato olive ragu that it came with.

SEARED WILD SEA SCALLOPS, MINTED PEA PUREE
Again, scallops were good, not great.

TIRAMISU
Delicious, creamy, not too rich.

PROFITEROLES
I thought I would like the mint ice cream, but these convinced me that classic vanilla is the best match.

BASIL GIMLET
I ordered a Basil Gimlet, but I think I got a standard Gimlet. It was very good, but not a Basil Gimlet.

My husband had a cocktail he really enjoyed as well, but I can't recall the name.

The service was friendly and helpful. Overall, the only 2 items that I would order again are the Artichoke and Cheese Tart, and the Tiramisu. The food was good, not great, which was a little disappointing (at this high price point, I would choose Evvia over SMA in the future).

text:
This is a letter I sent to the management after my last visit on 2/17/14, they need to make some staffing changes:

I have frequented your establishment many times since you have opened and for the most part the food and service has been great. Unfortunately my last visit there, on Monday February 17th was the most awful customer service I have received, with the exception of the bartender who ended up acting as our server.

When we arrived there was a short wait so my guest and I sat at the bar and ordered a drink and appetizer as we waited for a Tepanyaki table to open up. We were then seated. There was one other couple sitting at the table, and then the last few remaining guests seats were filled. Our order was taken, soup and salad served immediately, and then there our whole table sat. Never getting checked on once, and we ended up waiting almost a complete hour with no service and no chef in site. A table behind us that was seated well after we came had a chef before us, while they were still receiving their appetizers. I had to go to the bar just to get a water refill and to order additional cocktails.

Finally one of the other guests at our table located our server to ask where our chef was, she snapped at him and he was told he is right there on his way. It took all we had for us to all not get up from the table and leave, and I didn’t even know the party next to us but they were just as upset as my guest and I. Even after I had brought to the bartenders attention that we were not getting any service, our server still did not come and attend to us. I had to clear my own cups and bring them to the bar so we would have room at the table.

When the server did finally appear after the food was prepared, there was no apology, just “do you need a container?” This is by far the worst customer service I have ever received and the first time in my life I didn’t tip a server. I did however go out of my way to thank the Bartender for all her help and we tipped her since she did most of everything. She was very apologetic for the experience we had, which was sad as she was awesome.

There are plenty of choices of Japanese Restaurants in this town, and unfortunately you will no longer be one that me or my guest will be going to. You have Edo-Ya within a couple of blocks of there, and although they are an older establishment, I have never been treated poorly there. I just thought you should be aware of the service that I received. I am attaching the receipts from our visit as well.

text:
This is hands down good food. Possible the best BBQ I have had in California thus far. I was greeted with a warm friendly smile walking in the door and was not rushed to order. Pretty simple concept, place the order at the counter and take a buzzer to any open table. It goes off and your food is hot and ready at the pick up counter.

The beer list was impressive. About 15  different drafts on tap to choose from plus a big bottle selection.

The bbq was more impressive than the beer selection as the brisket sandwich I ordered was perfect.  Had a California twist on it with the ciabatta roll but everything else was southern at heart. The brisket was by far the best I have ever had. It was not too fat but perfectly moist with every bite. A touch of bark around that perfect pink smoke ring from a real fire smoke pit, not gas.

If you go you have to try the cornbread. Not don't think granny's dried up rock of cornbread, or aunt susies sweet as sugar bread, this was cornbread cooked properly, soft, and mosit. I must have they recipe. ;)

A+ experience.
A+ food

I would take family here and will see drive out of my way for this food. Like way out of my way to find this food.

Good luck and great job y'all.

text:
Made a reservation the day before our meal and was lucky to nab a good time! We arrived 15 minutes before our reservation. Valet is $11 without tip. There was lots of people that day so finding a parking spot was hard to find.

The hostess checked us in and we waited about 15 minutes as our table was set up. We were seated right on time. The decor is eclectic and dark (literally the restaurant is dim). Allow your eyes to adjust or you might walk into a wall.

We got a Wild Thing and Surf and Turf a la cart for 4 of us. A la cart came with salad (chef or spinach), cheese fondue, grill, and then the chocolate fondue. We went with a mushroom fondue with truffle oil. It was pretty good! They had bread, picked veggies, normal veggies, and fruits that can be dipped in the cheese fondue. After that came the grill. For the Wild Thing, there was exotic meats like ostrich, boar, venison, alligator, etc. I did hope they could have little tags, I could not remember what I was eating. Although all good especially with the butter and the 6 yummy dipping sauces.

It’s safe to say that although we were stuffed, we were not going to let dessert go untouched. There is an assortment of things to dip (fruits, candy bars, cake, etc) all of which you can ask for more of.

Definitely a very worth it meal. The bill with tip and tax came out to be about $500. We did have 2 half bottles of wine plus a glass of champagne.

Overall - would go back again to celebrate special occasions any time!

text:
Hit or miss. We came here for happy hour because we were in the neighborhood.

The service was friendly and capable.
THE FOOD... some was good, some was not very good.

**CEBICHIN MIXTO** Spicy, but not too spicy. Citrusy. It was a great cebiche.

**CAUSA LIMENA** Really good. Crab sitting atop a beautiful little potato. The sauces and purees were also great compliments. Get your own you won't want to share.

**PANCITO CON CHICARON** This is a tough one for me. The pork belly was deep-fried, it was crispy on the outside and creamy rich on the inside, but the slice was too thick. The result was fat running down your hands and when you took a bit, and a fat coating your mouth. If there was any way for them to cut the pork belly thinner (1/4 to 1/2 the thickness), I think this would be a winner, but as it stands it was too rich, too indulgent, too fatty. We ended up dipping the sando in the remaining cebiche sauce to cut the richness of the pork belly.

**FRIED CALAMARI** Terrible. Fishy, and overcooked. Tough, dry, and the flavor was awful.

**CHICHARRON DO POLLO ANTICUCHERO** Fried chicken thigh meat. It was good, not great. Sauces were lost on the fried coating, and their flavors were not strong enough to stand up to the breading.

The drinks were the same. Some good, some ok.

**PRICKLY PEAR MARGARITA** the winner of the bunch. Hands down.
**PISCO PUNCH** good, very limey, but good.
**PASSION DAIQUIRI** I really don't like maraschino (which is a key ingredient in daiquiris). It wasn't listed on the cocktail menu as an ingredient, so I thought I'd give it a whirl. I am pretty sure there was maraschino, I should have known better. My fault, but I didn't care for this drink.

Would we go again? Maybe if we were in the area for happy hour.

text:
I've been to Mastro's Ocean Club and I loved it.  I haven't tried the steak at this location but I have it on very good authority that it's pretty damn delicious.  The other evening while having dinner across the street, Chris K. and I decided that we wanted dessert but not just any dessert.  We wanted butter cake from Mastro's.  Yes, ooey, gooey, butter cake with ice cream and fresh whipped cream.  Again, I'd never had it before and I've heard it was really good.  You never know unless you try it, right?  So we walked across the street from Pizzeria Ortica and made our way into Mastro's.

We asked for a table for 2 and they escorted us to a dining room with dim lighting.  We ended up in a half booth which was perfect.  It's dark and romantic but who were we kidding, we were there for just dessert.  Do tell the waiter that you just want the dessert menu to avoid wasting his time and yours.  We perused the list but butter cake was our objective.  It's $15 and worth every penny.  This portion can easily feed 4 people after a massive steak feast.  Since it was just the two of us we polished off a good amount before admitting defeat.  The cake is definitely gooey in the center but the outside was a little crumbly and dry.  The ice cream and fresh whipped cream worked really well.  They even garnished it with a few strawberries too.  Delicious.  Even if you're not there for steak, you can still have dessert.

text:
I really believe that Seasons 52 is one of the best new restaurants in town.  Why?  Because their menu changes with every season and they have a weekly menu that changes every week of the year so as to use the freshest ingredients available.  Plus, I love that everything on their menu is 475 calories or less.  Knowing that small fact helps me indulge a tiny bit when I come here.  The place is dimly lit with luscious wooden booths and tables.  It would be a great place to have a celebratory dinner or a business dinner with folks from out of town.  Granted, being a part of South Coast Plaza, it does have a fair amount of foot traffic.

Last night I met some friends for an early dinner and we ordered up a small feast.  Despite having a full bar, they do not carry Land shark lager.  This didn't deter me from trying out their chocolate & espresso martini and sangiovese wine.  The martini was delightful and the wine went well with my dinner.  We tried the shrimp & crab stuffed mushrooms, steak & cremini mushroom flatbread, Maui tuna crunch salad, green salad, BBQ chicken salad, yellowtail tuna rolls, cedar plank salmon, filet mignon, rainbow trout, & chicken.  Wow that was a lot of food.  I split the tuna salad and tuna rolls with my friend.  We thought it was really delicious and the serving was quite generous.  I tried a bite of the salmon which was perfectly cooked and moist, yet flavorful.  The filet mignon was also perfectly cooked as well.  The carrots it came with were a little too crunchy for my taste, but the asparagus and potatoes were perfect.

We even tried the mini indulgence desserts that come in shot glasses.  There were quite a few to choose from.  I tried a little bite of the peanut butter chocolate swirl and it was delightful.  I chose the pumpkin pie since it was in season and it was so delicious.  I hear that the key lime pie & meyer lemon poundcake were just the right touch of sugar and spice.  They have something for everyone and if someone took a flavor you wanted, they have extras to bring out.  Just the right size to have after an amazing dinner.

The service was superb.  Our server, Andrew B., even handed us a business card, so that we could request to be seated in his area during our next visit.  As we exited the restaurant, I noticed that the restaurant was bustling and most of the tables were full.  I would suggest making a reservation during the busy hours or you can stop in while on your next shopping trip at SCP.

text: King Taco is one of those LA institutions you visit when you have late night cravings or are headed to a football game at the Rose Bowl.  For me, we were headed to the Rose Bowl.  We didn't want to tailgate so we did the next best thing.  We ordered burritos.  To order, just wait in line and order at the counter.  They have 2 registers and almost everything is made to order.  I ordered an al pastor combination burrito with everything and hot salsa.  The red 'rioja' salsa is incendiary.  Talk about burn your mouth hot.  I can still feel its effects days later.   The burrito had a lot of meat, beans, rice, onions, salsa, and cilantro in it.  I also ordered a sweet 'dulce' tamale.  This was pulled out of whatever warming pan they had and was steaming hot but unfortunately overcooked.  It was dry and kind of gross after I started to pick at it.  Go for the burritos, tortas, and tacos but maybe pass on the tamales.

Their prices seem to be the same for lunch as for dinner but they offer happy hour specials for sake.  There's a check-in deal for a free drink which is nice but I just wanted water during my meal.  I'll just save it for another day.  There wasn't anything during my meal that was spectacular nor was it bad.  It was just ok and that's fine with me.  They offer a variety of items on their menu in case you didn't want shabu but with shabu in the name, one would hardly come for anything else.  It's nice to have options though.  They also have booths and a private table area enclosed with a curtain in addition to the bar seating.  They are located on Irvine Center Drive and Jeffrey by the Papa Johns.

text:
Grace C. and I tried to get a table on the patio with our dogs but sadly, R&D Kitchen will not serve you if you have your canine friends with you.  We opted to eat next door at Pain du Monde instead much to the chagrin of our wallets.  However, I had on good authority that the carrot cake at R&D Kitchen was to-die-for so we had to try it.  I was able to order it at the bar to-go.  They were really busy that Saturday morning but managed to bring me a healthy slice of carrot cake but forgot any plastic utensils whatsoever.  #FAIL  I was able to grab some from Pain du Monde, again saving the day for us.

The verdict: their carrot cake is good.  But was it $8 good?  Oh heck, no.  I did enjoy the whole toasted walnuts that decorated the exterior of the cake.  The cake itself was moist and tasty.  The frosting was light and creamy but in no way the right texture.  Grace didn't like it as much as I did but then again I was enamored with the walnuts not the cake itself.  I might come back to try the rest of the menu just without my dog.

name: Trina D.
text:
I've been craving Hainanese chicken for weeks.  Weeks, I tell you.  There's something about that ginger-spicy dipping sauce that has been gnawing at me.  So finally after denying myself, I dragged my parents here to have what else, their number one special. Of course everything on their menu is chicken.  My mom ordered pho with chicken.  This pho wasn't your typical chicken pho, it had stuff like livers, and well other chicken parts that you may not enjoy but it's a cafe in Westminster, you're going to get the weird stuff too.  My dad and I both ordered the number one Hainan chicken with rice.

My mom noted that the chicken is brought out cold, but deboned.  How nice of them to debone it for us!  The skin is left on but the fat has melted away in the cooking process.  If you don't like chicken skin then this place is probably not for you.  The whole point of this dish is for you to eat the chicken with the skin, and I suppose you could eat just the meat.  But what would be the point?  It's really up to you.  My mom was surprised that my dad and I cleared our plates.  It was that good.

The sauce is set out for you as well and it's up to you to put the ginger in the sauce or set up a dipping station for yourself.  I prefer to add the ginger to the spicy sauce.  I didn't go with the soy sauce but they give that to you also.  The rice is piping hot infused with chicken broth and fat.  It's so freaking delicious.  It quelled my craving too.  I know I'll be back the next time I want Hainanese chicken with rice.

name: Trina D.
text:
3.5 stars.  My cousin Vanessa D. and I decided to walk over to Haute Cakes Caffe from her apartment for brunch on Sunday.  I arrived at her place around 11:40 am so by the time we got there it was close to noon.  There was plenty of seating and they were still serving breakfast items.  I guess seating can be scarce during peak hours but we didn't experience that while we were there.  Also, there was a sign up stating that they don't serve lunch menu items on Sunday, possibly because most people come for Sunday brunch.

We both ordered the Haute combination ($9.75) which includes pancakes or french toast, your choice of bacon or sausage, fresh fruit, and 2 eggs any way you like it.  We both upgraded ($2) to blueberry cornmeal pancakes and orange ricotta pancakes respectively.  I also ordered a medium sized fresh squeezed orange juice ($2.25; think Naked, not Tropicana) and she had a medium sized iced tea ($2.50).  I ordered my eggs scrambled and my cousin had hers over easy.  The food took a while to come out.  We were starving.

The food was definitely pleasing to the eye when it arrived and tasty as well.  The orange ricotta pancakes are very soft, due to the ricotta cheese and my blueberry cornmeal pancakes reminded me of cornbread, which I loved.  The orange ricotta pancakes also come with macerated fruit in addition to syrup.  I'm just wondering if maybe they forgot mine?  It would have definitely heightened my star rating for this place had I received extra fruit for my pancakes.  The bacon was crispy and the fruit varied from plate to plate.  I had watermelon, pineapple, and an orange slice while Vanessa got a sliced peach, watermelon, and orange.  The food is good, maybe above average but definitely overpriced.  I might be persuaded to come back to try other items off of the menu, but not for awhile.

name: Trina D.
text:
I went to HH with a few friends and tried their tacos out for the first time.  Let me say that I wasn't impressed.  I tried 3 tacos: duck, pork belly, and ghost chili.  All were bland!  The pork belly was up first and I liked it the best.  I didn't put any hot sauce on the first bite because I wanted to try out the flavor first.  The meat was tender but on the dry side or really fatty.  That went for every taco I tried.  I did like that the pork belly was sort of like a Vietnamese sandwich in that it was stuffed with daikon, carrots, and cilantro.  Bravo on the flavors but it needed salt.

The duck taco was just ok.  The meat was probably the most tender of the 3 tacos I tried but still bland.  The brie and chips on it were an interesting way to salt the taco.  It didn't work.  The ghost chili was hot spicy but I still put more ghost chili hot sauce on it.  I didn't finish all of it because I had one giant piece of fat in my taco disguising itself as meat.  Gross.  I get what they are trying to do and I love supporting local establishments that have responsible sustainability in mind but I wasn't impressed with the tacos.  Especially for the price.  I also know that it's better to put salt in rather than it being too salty but I was expecting more flavor and was disappointed.

The nice thing about happy hour is that the beers on tap are $3.  I tried to order the Belgian Ale but they were out of it.  The bartender did mention that they were out of some of the beers on tap and that she could recommend a similar beer to me.  Bummer.

My friend, Drew, ordered an agua fresca (the flavors change from time to time).  That day it was blueberry-cucumber-mint.  That was probably the best thing I had at Taco Asylum.  Sad that it wasn't a taco.  I may return to check out the grilled octopus and short rib tacos but other than that, it's a solid 3 stars for now.

name: Trina D.
text:
The food here is extraordinary.  My date and I had each ordered from the tasting menu.  I had the seasonal menu, while he ordered the traditional one.
Seasonal Menu:
First dish ~
Fresh Wild Seabass Ceviche on a Wonton Crisp with Sweet Soy & Micro Greens.  Paired with a 2009 Kung Fu Girl Riesling, Washington State.  The seabass ceviche was delicious with the microgreens and sweet soy sauce.  The plating was beautiful, but I did not hesitate to dig in.  It's a good thing I took a photo beforehand.  The wonton gave it a nice crunch.  The riesling rounded out the sweetness of the dish providing a dry note to the whole experience.  I was very pleased with this dish.  4.5 stars.

Second dish ~
Proscuitto Wrapped, Panko Crusted Fried Green Tomato & Fresh Sweet Creamed Corn, Garnished with Queso Fresco.  Paired with a 2009 Tintero Moscato d'Asti, Italy.  This was absolutely AMAZING.  I was blown away by the simplicity. yet complex arrangement of flavors and textures in this dish.  The crunchiness of the panko with the soft, sweet corn brought a slight tear to my eye.  I was in HEAVEN.  The salty proscuitto paired with the sweet corn and Moscato d'Asti made a little party in my mouth.  By far my favorite dish of the night.  5 stars.

Third dish ~
All Natural Quail on a bed of White Bean Puree with Spanish Chorizo, drizzled with a Strawberry Balsamic Reduction.  Paired with a 2008 Castillo de Monjardin Tintico, Navarra Spain.  This was delicious but I wasn't as enamored with it as the other two dishes.  The wine was spicy which brought about an interesting addition to the quail and puree.  Again it was good, but not my favorite.  3.5 stars.

Final dish ~
Fresh Baked Oatmeal Raisin Cookie with House Made Vanilla Moscatel Ice Cream.  Paired with a N.V. Adega de Favaios Moscatel do Douro, Portugal.  This was a small bite but very indulgent nonetheless.  The warm cookie with the ice cream when well with the moscatel wine.  It was so GOOD.  4 stars.

Traditional menu:
First dish ~
Sautéed Sea Scallop on a nest of Crispy Fried Yucca finished with Tarragon Chardonnay Sauce.  Paired with a 2006 Frogmore Creek Chardonnay, Tasmania.  My date really enjoyed this.  I'm not a fan of scallops in general, possibly because I've never had great scallops.  But these were delicious!  They were cooked perfectly with a beautiful caramelized sear.  They were sweet and succulent. The dry chardonnay rounded out the sweetness of the scallops nicely.  Very good.  4.5 stars.

Second dish ~
Handmade Fettuccini Pomodoro garnished with Aged Pecorino Romano Cheese.  Paired with a 2008 Castelvero Barbera, Piedmonte Italy.  This fettuccini pomodoro was delicate and tender.  It went well with the barbera wine.  My date liked it but said it was just ok.  4 stars.

Third dish ~
Four Ounces of All Natural Filet Mignon & Crispy Fried Onions with Bleu Des Basque Demi Cream Sauce.  Paired with a 2008 Maipe Cabernet Sauvignon, Argentina.  This was by far the best dish on the menu.  The steak was so tender that with just a butter knife, it gave way so easily.  The crispy onions were so good with the filet.  The cabernet rounded out the dish nicely.  5 stars.

Final dish ~
Grandma's Cheesecake, Wild Berry Puree.  Paired with a NV Ferreira Ruby Port.  A wonderful end to a great menu.  The cheesecake was the perfect size to finish off the meal.  It was slightly rich but paired with the puree and fresh fruit, it was delicious along with the port.  4 stars.
We had a fantastic meal.  I'm amazed at the quality of the food, service, and ambiance.  This is definitely one of the BEST restaurants, if not a best kept dining secret in the OC.

text: I have to say, I'm a fan of these elevated dining food courts.  I love the concept and I'll definitely eat at them before going to a fast food joint.  My venture to 4th Street was a mixed bag.  There's plenty of parking at the structure adjacent and there are a lot of offerings.  There's Wagyu Chuck, PFC, Dough Exchange, Recess, Ink Waffles, Noodle Tramp, Front Porch Pops, Chunk N Chip, Dos Chinos, and so much more.  It's like being a kid in a foodie playground.  The dining options are excellent and it's not as busy as the Anaheim Packing District.  Cheers to 4th Street sticking around for a long time.

The Jasmine green tea is brewed strong.  Definitely a favorite bakery in the neighborhood.

text: It's been ages since I've eaten at L&L Hawaiian BBQ but it's still pretty much the same.  Meat + Rice with a side of macaroni salad.  I should have told them to hold the macaroni salad because I really despise mayonnaise from a jar.  I've made the fresh stuff and I know that what they have back there is jarred.  I ordered the mini beef bowl to go because I wasn't sure how much I'd be able to eat there.  It was actually the perfect size because I ended up eating it all, except for the macaroni salad.  I also grabbed one of the Hawaiian juices from the beverage refrigerator.  The meal was fine but I wished that their plastic cutlery were better quality.  This stuff was flimsy and could barely cut through the meat.  Service was great and the food was cooked to order or reheated.  I'm not completely positive but either way, it was fine.  The beef was cooked well done and I wished it wasn't.  Oh well.

text: It was slightly disappointing to be here. It looks great but it's very very noisy with music and the Acoustics there. The menu does not correctly identify the ingredients in the dishes. We ordered something that listed the protein as beef, but there was also a variety of seafood and other things in there that one might be allergic to and could get sick from. The service was great but they seem to be very disappointed if you don't order the large barbecue. In their defense though the gay very great service but I thought that it was a bit expensive for what is received.

name: Trina D.
text:
A bunch of usmet up over the weekend at the Buena Park location of Kang Hodong Baekjeong KBBQ for a post Thanksgiving meal.  I have been to the KTown location before so I knew what I was in for.  Kang Hodong is one of the best places to KBBQ in SoCal.  Chris C. organized the whole thing and we were settled in the back of the restaurant with 2 tables and 4 grills.  We arrived before the busy fray of dinnertime customers but were still met with excellent service.  We ordered the large beef but received some cuts that were off menu as well.  Let me just say that do not come here for AYCE.  You won't find it.  Everything here is purchased a la carte.

They have combinations that are well worth the money and so are the cuts of meat.  It's quality over quantity and you'll definitely find it here.  They have two different types of grill plates along with charcoal in with the gas burner to give the meat a chargrilled aroma.  Everything was delicious.  We had brisket, boneless short rib, marinated beef, and a few sides brought out.  The japchae was steaming hot from the kitchen and oh-so-good.  We even tried the beef tatare with Asian pear.  That was the best!  It was tender and delicious with the pear.  I would not have thought to eat it that way but I'm a believer now.  Our servers were fantastic.  Kudos to Isaac and our other servers who I did not catch the names of.  The meal was pretty gut-busting but well worth it.  I still think the cheesy egg and cheesy corn are weird additions to KBBQ but it makes people happy.  Thanks for showing us a good time.

The pub is small with a patio on the side and an upstairs area that can be reserved.  Our group was in the upstairs area where Chelsea was our server.  She was great!  She learned our names and took everyone's orders after they perused the menu.  I ordered a Blackthorn Cider ($5) and my friend ordered a soda.  The place was still lively after the football game and only got more rowdy as the night went on.  We only had about an hour on the meter so we didn't stay too long.  They had Jeopardy on the speakers so that was pretty cool.  It was great to see some of my LA friends who I hadn't seen in a while in such a cool setting.  Lucky Baldwin's is a chill spot for food and beer.

A 7oz serving costs $4 for your puppy.  We sat on the patio and enjoyed the people watching.  The waitress even brought her some water.  I ordered the pumpkin gratin ($9) off of the snacks menu.  It's a new item that I noticed for fall.  A lot of my blogger friends posted about it a few weeks ago.  I also utilized the Yelp check-in for 50% off the snacks menu. name: Trina D.
text:
There's this Thai Kitchen in Costa Mesa that goes by the name of MaDee.  It's small unassuming but has a lot of heart in its dishes.  It is a fast casual cafe setting so despite the modern industrial feel, you will still experience the full spectrum of Thai food here.

The flavors are of Northern Thai so you get a lot more of the Burmese, Chinese and Laotian influences from that region.  My friend Drew M. introduced me to this place because he knows that I love all things spicy.  We tried the larb, Kao Soi, and the chow mein.  Everything was cooked to order so we waited a few minutes for our order to come out.

The larb was deconstructed and really disappointing.  I have had better and although it's a fresh dish that is light (think lettuce wraps), I was not impressed by the flavors.  I was looking for that combination of sweet, sour, savory, and spice.  It was lacking.  However, I did love the spiciness of the chow mein and the Kao Soi was so amazing.  The Kao Soi is crispy noodles in a yellow curry soup.  It's so good.  I would definitely order this again.  The spice was perfect and the coconut flavor very pronounced.  They do not skimp on spice if you ask for it.  I was quite pleased with the other two dishes.  3.5 stars rounded up.

name: Trina D.
text: I'm not sure why this place is so popular.  Every time I pass by there's a wait.  Could it be that it's just nicely furnished?  The food is so-so.  The portions are large.  I think Honda-Ya in Tustin has a better offering.  I was not impressed.

name: Trina D.
text:
Mokkoji has opened a new location in Arcadia!  I was out in Pasadena on Saturday for the UCLA-USC game so we were in the area and in the mood for Shabu.  Mokkoji popped up in our search and we called to see how late they would be open.  We made it there shortly after 10 pm and sat down.  Our server had worked at the Irvine location too!

The menu has a little bit more on it than its sister location, but I ordered the Fatty Toro beef ($12) and my friend had the Wagyu regular ($17.99).  They also offer an additional broth flavor at this location.  I tried the spicy miso broth instead of the original.  The flavors were great.  The fatty toro they brought out was indeed fatty and I would not normally eat this stuff everyday but for a cool, brisk evening, this meal definitely hit the spot.  We thoroughly enjoyed our meals.  They also offer porridge instead of soup at the end here but I enjoy the soup more than porridge generally.  The porridge is worth a try if you've never had it.  Service was great and the tables they have with the induction burners are fancy.  I'm really happy to see that Mokkoji is expanding to other cities.

name: Devan Maingot
text: This was the best dining experience i've had in years - possibly ever. Chef George was FANTASTIC. Not only did his preparation routine go over perfectly, he was also hilarious and the food was absolutely incredible. The steak was so tender I could just about cut it with a spoon. I ate two full plates of food, and even though I'm about to burst, I'd eat more if there was any left. The bartender/server, Brett, made sure that we never had to ask for anything. Our plates and drinks were always full, and the service was timely throughout the night. Seriously - check this place out. I can't remember the last time I had so much fun.

name: Trina D.
text:
Initially I tried to make a reservation but unfortunately, they had another large party coming in so they told me to either choose an earlier time or a later time.  Since we had a large group, I had to double-check with the group if this was ok.  I had a friend call in and make the reservation.  Lo and behold, he was able to get us a reservation for the time we wanted for teppan.  When I called, they didn't give me the choice and I'm assuming the other large party was for the sushi area.  So definitely specify when you make a reservation!

Our group wanted teppan so we happily snagged the 7 pm slot.  The restaurant is located on PCH by this motel and parking is valet but you can try your luck parking on PCH.  Once inside, I went to the back bar to meet my friends.  Free shot with Yelp Check-in!  The night was off to a good start.  Apparently they have all night happy hour on Mondays and Wednesdays, double score for us.

As far as teppan was concerned, we saved $10 off with the happy hour special of pick 2 (any combination of NY steak, chicken, shrimp, or calamari).  I opted for the NY steak (medium rare) and shrimp.  With our meal, we also received salad, soup, fried or steamed rice, vegetables and noodles.  It was a lot of food and I was starving.  They even accommodated my friend's request not to mix her seafood with meat as she has some food allergies.  The food was delicious, but maybe it's because I was starving.  I also tried some of my friend's Nigori cold sake and ordered a Kirin for myself.  I thought I had ordered the draft but out came a bottle instead.  No big deal since it was happy hour pricing.

If you've never been to a teppan show, you're in for a treat.  Our chef and server kept us entertained throughout the evening.  Our group had a great time.  I can see how this place can get rowdy on the weekends but when we were there, it was quieter.  It definitely depends on the clientele.

name: Trina D.
text: This place has pretty good Dim Sum.  The carts move fast but they remember you the next time around, if they don't have what you want the first time.  We went here for lunch for a coworker and the service was pretty fast.  The prices for lunch are decent if you order the lunch specials.  We also had 10% off our Dim Sum order today.  Maybe it's a Wednesday thing?  I don't know for sure but it was stamped on our check, "10% off Dim Sum."  That beats paying full price.  It's about $10 or less per person depending on what you order.  We ordered a dish for everyone (served family-style) and ended up having leftovers to take home too.

name: Marlon Ade
text: Quality dim sum spot! Carts could be more frequent though.

name: Ulises Herbert
text: For me, shabu is all about the sauce and this place has the best sauce. They have great quality meat and good size options. At other places I hate running out of meat and having to order a side that's too much.

name: Trina D.
text:
On cold autumn nights, like last night, I tend to want some warm soup to soothe my soul.  Enter California Shabu-Shabu.  My friend Seta S. met me here to catch up and dine in Asian pop style.  This was my first time at Shabu-Shabu and I'm definitely a fan.

The place was busy for Friday.  There's a sign-in list at the door where they call your name when there's space available.  There's a lounge area where it just looked like they served drinks, no food.  The Shabu-Shabu pots are on induction plates in front of you.  There's a plate of veggies, tofu & noodles per person.  You get a choice of white or brown rice.  There's also ponzu sauce & sesame miso paste for flavoring should you want it.  Believe me you'll want it.  I also asked for spicy chili oil to be added to my ponzu sauce.  The wait staff is very busy but attentive and fast.  No one server is assigned to you; they all take turns seeing if customers need anything as they pass by.  There's a list of menu items you can choose from.  I went with the beef and chicken combination.  It was plenty since the veggies and noodles made up for the thinly sliced meat.  I did have to ask for a separate soup bowl.  They had forgotten to give them to us when we sat down.  The soup bowl comes with soup base ladled inside.  I'm no amateur when it comes to cooking my own meal and I must say shabu-shabu is pretty fun.  My friend and I had a great time.

California Shabu-Shabu is located in the plaza adjacent to the Shark Club.  Parking is scarce but you can always valet or find it nearby.

name: Kenneth Macias
text: This place is worth visiting. They serve large portions for reasonable rates. Consistently well kept and with great atmosphere. Will visit here again.

name: Trina D.
text: I stopped by for happy hour. Who can beat $3 sangrias and $5 taco plates?!!  The ambiance is laid back but hip. My bartender was prepping the mint for the evening. Music was pulsating with a Spanish vibe. A great place in the midst of the Santa Ana art district. Fun for a date or just drinks with friends. Happy hour is 3-6:30 pm Mon-Fri and they also have $5 taco plates after 10pm Mon-Fri. The sangria hit the spot with its ice-cold fruity notes.  The carne asada tacos are fun with cliantro, onions, salsa served on-the-side.  Slightly on the chewy side, but for $5, not bad.  Up next, the duck fries were covered in cheese, green tomatillo sauce and yummy goodness.  We also ordered the banana bread pudding which is fried in a skillet.  It's topped off with whipped cream and blueberries.   Each bite was like a little taste of heaven.  The mojitos are every bit as refreshing as you can imagine.  Definitely a great place to hang out with some friends.  Worth a trip for happy hour.

name: Rajesh Patil
text: The food is really good..i liked the Tom yum soup....the flavors are amazing..i would really recommend this to everyone....

name: Trina D.
text:
There are very few Thai places in the area that I'd absolutely rave about and this place might be one of them.  First of all, no corkage fee.  AWESOME.  Secondly, fellow foodie friend, Drew M. has been talking non-stop about Mint Leaf Thai since he discovered it on the Balboa peninsula last year.  He loves that they will make dishes "legitimately" spicy for him.  Both of us detest places that say they will make it spicy but hold back because they think the customer can't handle the spice.  If we are asking for an 11 on a scale of 1 to 5, give us an 11!!  Anyway, I finally made it down to Mint Leaf with Drew M., Mike M., and Lindsay M., feeling a little left out because my last initial isn't M but we had a great meal.

We ordered:

Appetizer Sampler:  ($10.95) Combination of lady fingers, veggie crispy rolls, fried wontons, and cheese puffs.  Typical fried fare.  This was just ok.

Pumpkin Curry with chicken spice level requested was 6 but it came out a 4: ($10.95) Red coconut curry made with tender pieces of pumpkin, tomato, basil, and bell peppers.  The curry was barely spicy but the flavors were so delicious I kept coming back for more.  The pumpkin was perfectly cooked with a creamy bite to it and the coconut gave it a very rich satisfying flavor.  Delicious!

Larb with pork spice level requested 6 but came out a 5: ($8.95) Seasoned minced meat with basil, onions, roasted Thai chili and tossed in a lime dressing.  There's so much flavor in the dish that I absolutely loved it.  It's served with lettuce leaves and you can essentially make a lettuce wrap with it.  The balance of spice and citrus is spot on.  So good!

Mint Leaf Thai Noodles spice level requested 6 and it came out a 6: ($10.95) Stir-fried egg noodles with chicken, shrimp, cashews, onions, carrots, celery, and dry Thai chili tossed in the house sauce.  This was by far the spiciest dish we had at the table and it was just what I wanted in a noodle dish.  I love noodles.

Lindsay who loves very mild dishes ordered the Mongolian beef ($9.95) which was really tasty.  We also had a large serving of white rice ($3.00) but they do happen to serve brown rice or sticky rice if you prefer it.  We also had the Tempura ice cream which was a special of the day type of dessert so I don't remember how much it was.  For the four of us it ended up being less than $20 per person with tip included.  Not bad at all for Newport but pricier than other Thai places I've been to.

I have to say though that they do take their time.  Service is not their forte but the fact that there is no corkage fee helps out a lot.  Bring your own bottle of wine and they will provide wine glasses and a wine opener for you.  That's pretty cool if you're not in a hurry to eat.   Otherwise pick out your entrees if there's a wait and immediately order food once seated.

text: Just ate here last night (party of two at the bar) and cannot wait to return. Not many places are near capacity (bar seating only) at 9pm on a Sunday. After having eaten here, i completely understand why. Exceptionally good. We started with drinks... i had their house Old Fashioned which had a unique smokey quality with applewood smoke and lardo infused bourbon. We shared a few smaller plates, all of which i recommend: (1) lamb belly (only available on Sundays), which was delicious with a mediterranean flair; (2) calamari; (3) chicken liver pate (so darn good!); (4) veal tartare. Following the small plates, we wanted to try the pasta and got the spagetti with dungeness crab... perfectly al dente and delicious. Next, we shared the whole branzino which was perfect with a wonderfully crispy skin. For desert, (1) the maple fritters and (2) bar au chocolat tarte.

name: Natalie K
text:
I tried so many times to get a reservation at Bestia and they are way booked ahead of time. I ended up making a reservation 4 months out to secure a spot for me and 5 of my friends. I heard that you can get away with no reservation if you are willing to dine at the bar but you have to arrive quite early for that.

The restaurant itself is located in the most unexpected area of LA. There's also no real safe place to park your car close by so I highly recommend utilizing their valet.

The restaurant is much more casual for what the price tag is. It's packed even on a week day. The dishes are small and meant to be shared. You can only all your dishes at once. There's no ordering additional dishes later so choose wisely and make sure you order enough food. I personally think this rule is a little extreme but I guess if your restaurant is this popular, you can do whatever you want.

The service was a hit and miss. Our server was not very attentive and even yanked the menu right out of my friend's hand because he was in a rush to attend to other things. It was hard to get someone's attention and even just to get our water refilled.

The food was quite delicious. I was a huge fan of the their bone marrow and the mussels. They encourage you to eat at least 3 dishes per person but I think that's quite a lot depending on what you order. I would say 4-5 dishes for every 2 people is probably good.

I would probably come back some day but with a smaller party and just eat at the bar.

name: Scott in Pollock
text:
Tough call between 3 and 4 stars; I usually reserve 4 for fine dining, but have a warm spot in my heart for this place based on its history.

It has been lousy for years, but new management brings quality food and professional service (something that has been lacking for almost as far back as I can remember).

Menu is huge! and my first try here was a Monte Christo for lunch. A little unconventional in that the sandwich was not deep fried. Instead it was simply surrounded by French Toast; a lighter incarnation, but nevertheless delicious (as was the accompanying cole slaw). Service was impeccable.

Second outing was today for brunch; place was full at 11am mid-week, so it seems the word is spreading. Even full, service was impeccable. Food came out hot, with no delay, and we  were checked on no less than 4 times during our meal; twice to see if everything was alright, and twice asked if we wanted our drinks refilled.

Spinach mushroom omelet and eggs benedict. Both delicious. Real hollandaise and nicely poached eggs (although ham instead of Canadian bacon - which was clearly mentioned on the menu - and was very tasty ham, nicely grilled). Hash Browns were light, crispy, and almost buttery... not dripping in tasteless grease like other places around.

This place is two for two, and highly recommended. So nice to have another "go to" spot in this neck of the woods.

Been a regular here since 1998. Yesterday afternoon I go to pickup my 24 dollar pizza and there is a 8 inch high barrier of slippery, slushy, icy snow around the entire perimeter of the restaurant.

Neighboring businesses have all done this, including the Family Dollar on the other side of the lot. Clearly, this owner has no interest in the safety of his customers carrying their pizzas from his restaurant, and I told him so... and he seemed entirely OK with that.

20 year customer will never return.

text:
Definitely an experience to have at least once whether you live in San Francisco or you are visiting.

We were a party of three, which increased our wait time (we wanted to sit at a table). The people watching (guests and employees) is great. We grabbed some drinks while we were waiting.

Pro tip - Best to come as a party of two, lots more seating options. You can saddle up to the bar and eat there even on busy nights.

Things to know: menu is seafood heavy and traditional.

We had the crab cake entree, Dungeness Crab and Prawns a la Monza, and the Seafood Cioppino.  The food was very good. I would pass on the potatoes that came with the crab cakes... and order double veggies. I wanted the potatoes to be crispier.

The Tadich Rice Custard left a lot to be desired. Total fail. It's a super eggy custard that has rice at the bottom. I was so excited about it, I love custards, I love rice, I love rice pudding... but somehow I didn't love their Rice Custard.

Tiny gripes: tonic in my g+t was flat. This is an old school establishment, not a female on staff to be seen. I know, old school, just roll with it... but... I... can't...

I tried the sour grape and the peach beer cocktail. I can't quite recall the name but the peach was definitely very delicious. It was light and refreshing.

The food is just okay in my opinion but I have a feeling that we didn't order the right items. We tried the Tripel Burger, which has a combination of 3 meats, a sweet spread, and a pretzel bun. The patty was nice and moist but I didn't care for the sweetness. We also had the crab dip, which smelled very fishy. I wouldn't order it again. The garlic fries were pretty good.

A lot of people ordered the mussels and also the creamy chicken dish. They seem to really enjoy those 2 dishes so if I make it back here, I will definitely be giving it a try.

Parking is a total pain. I had to park several blocks away in a residential area after circling around multiple times. They do have some street parking but I went on a Saturday night so they were all taken.

Seating can be difficult. We were seated on a large table with 2 other parties and everything was very cramped. The service is pretty good though. Our waitress was very nice and helpful. She also brought us samples of beers we were interested in so we could try it before we ordered.

Water boy did not understand english. I wonder why they don't have any wall decoration. It took me several minutes to find what was off about the interior.

text:
I had a pretty horrible date at Bru Haus but I still enjoyed my food and drinks. I would come back here for a casual hangout or to watch the game. Their seating options aren't the best. I would definitely recommend grabbing one of the high top tables.

The parking in the neighborhood is nearly impossible. I circled for 15 minutes before giving up. They have valet parking but it is expensive at $5.50 and they usually park it in the front of the restaurant in the loading zone.

They have unique drinks and a decent beer selection. I had their jalapeno margarita. It wasn't very spicy but I could definitely taste a strong jalapeno flavor. They also have great beer on tap and beer flights you can order. You can also make your own beer flight.

I tried both the sweet sriracha wings and the sweet potato tots. I loved both quite a lot. The wings were extra crispy but not breaded and the sauce was tangy and delicious. I could eat about 3 orders of that by myself. The tots were also good and they give you so much. I especially like the aioli and the housemade ranch to go with it.

The service is good and the food and drinks come quickly. The place does get busy and crowded during game time so I would recommend arriving early if you have a slightly larger group.
