There's a large variety of food for all appetites and eating particularities; one member in our group had a lot of dietary restrictions, and she was easily able to find food that fit her requirements. The server figured out fairly early on that we were there for a leisurely meal and she accommodated us quite nicely. We decided to eat family-style because there were so many great looking items on the menu that we could not Each narrow our choice down to just one. This worked out wonderfully! I enjoyed probably the best onion rings I've ever had , a nice ceviche, a steak salad and an Asian salad, pepperoni pizza and a pork belly sandwich. For dessert, we ordered the left side of the menu, haha, and I cannot believe the generous portions that came out! We had the butter cake, the apple and Huckleberry pie, and the s'mores brownie. We barely finished half of each of them, and each one was delicious. I would definitely recommend this restaurant, it is good for large groups and small ones. We sat by a few large tables and saw that they were well taken care of. They do take reservations, fyi.

The meat there is delicious even though it is consistently on the dryer side. I prefer meat that is more juicy. The taste makes up for it. You can ask for slices or for chopped brisket.

I do not like the amount of fat that they include when chopping your meat and weighing it. I don't want to pay for chunks of fat when I buy meat. Also, the outside can sometimes be too tough to eat, but sometimes is flavorful.

The rolls are fantastic. Nice and soft. I spread BBQ sauce on them, put my chopped meat on top, add much more original BBQ sauce, a must have and make little sandwiches.

There are 3 different sauces to choose from. Original, sweet, and spicy. The spicy actually has the whole seeds from whatever peppers they use. A little too hot for me! The sweet is passable, but I like the plain old original. It is so popular that when I last went there, the whole container was empty and I had to go back to the counter to get them to fill my to go containers. The sweet sauce was almost empty and the spicy was the most full.

Though expensive, it is a wonderful treat for carnivores and I recommend going and trying it. I think you will appreciate it.

text:
We went here for a birthday supper and were greeted with a slight wait even with a reservation so be prepared to wait as this place is popular. Fortunately, the wait is so worth it. This place has plenty of seafood options for anybody looking for their seafood fix. One of their specialties is the seafood bucket which is as the name says a bucket of seafood with varying spice levels. We didn't get the bucket this night, but we did get another one of their specialties. Large drinks called "Punch Bowls." This restaurant does have a wide variety of for their alcohol selection, so if a punch bowl is not your fancy, then there are plenty of options.
So onto the best part which is the food. We ordered an appetizer of hushpuppies. They were nice and crisp on the outside and perfect on the inside. They are served with a spicy dipping sauce which I enjoyed. I also ordered the soup flight offered at the Crab Hut and it was delicious. You are given three different soups and I was imagining them to be just little cups, but these were full on bowls and could almost be a meal by itself. The three soups are seafood gumbo, clam chowder, and tomato basil. I loved the clam chowder and tomato basil the most. It should be noted that the soup flight only appears to be offered at the downtown location. The different locations don't all have the same food options.
Our main courses were the spicy jambalaya and the seafood creole. The jambalaya was spicy and packed with seafood and flavor. My girlfriend's dish was great as well. Both were large portions and required take home boxes.
I would certainly recommend this place to anybody looking for some good seafood.

text: My wife and I came to see Billy Currington and had a terrific time. We parked in the underground lot beneath the mall. Extremely easy to get in and a close walk via elevator to the venue. It's $3 and hour, however, if you bring your parking ticket in with you they have a couple of stations that allow you to validate your ticket for 2 free hours. The venue itself is small and intimate making for a great concert experience. There is a large sunken wood floor that's standing room only. Surrounding that is plenty of area for standing room and 2 bars, one on each side. These 2 bars are your go to because everyone thinks the entry bar is the only one and the line is ridiculous. You can order a few different appetizers from the bar if your hungry. I ordered chicken strips and garlic fries which were pretty good. You can purchase an upgrade to the balcony once your in but not sure it's worth it because your already close to the stage. The balcony does have seats so that might be an option. There was a long line when we arrived outside the venue but once they start doing security checks the line goes fast. I highly recommend catching a concert here.

The rice in the roll seemed cold and wasn't good.  Our waiter Ryu was very pleasant and attentive to our needs.  The decor was beautiful and we were immediately seated since we arrived after 9 pm. text:
I'm a burger fanatic.  I love my all-American beef patties.  I like the fact that the Counter uses Angus beef that is not tainted by hormones and antibiotics.  It's worth the extra $$ for that piece of mind.

I was a tad disappointed by the lack of seasoning on my beef burger though.  I must say that they probably are cooking for low-sodium diets because there was definitely no salt in the patty.  They do make up for it by the variety of sauces they offer.  I ordered the build-your-own burger with: roasted red peppers, pepperoncinis, grilled onions, pepper jack, baby greens, maple cured bacon and the garlic aioli sauce.  I was amazed that they got all 6 ingredients onto the burger without it sliding off.  It was a little difficult to eat because everything I ordered slid off the burger.  Even so, it was tasty but not the burger of my dreams.  The "medium" was more pink than I bargained for but the burger was juicy.  The sweet potato fries were very good and we got a healthy serving for two.  The spicy horseradish mayo that accompanied the fries was just ok.  This place reminded me of a pricier Chipotle for hamburgers, from the build your own style, to the steel-minimalistic look of the furniture.  3 stars for the variety of ingredients, taste, and service.  I was not WOW-ed.  Maybe a return visit will attain a better review.

This food truck is one of the better fish taco food truck. They have Taco Tuesday price for $5 for 3 OG fish tacos as well as specials daily.

We spoke to a customer who’s a regular and he said next time, try the OG spicy fish taco.

name: Todd Clemmons
text:
Came here as I've been on the hunt for the top 3 beef BBQ places in San Diego County. From everything I read prior to coming here the Tommy's Tri-Tip Sandwich was highly rated and the best beef BBQ sandwich they had.

The sandwich comes on a soft Kaiser style roll with a good amount of meat, a side of your choice, pickles (on the side), pickled onions (on the side) & a side of BBQ sauce.

For the side I opted for the french fries as I saw them on another customers plate and noticed they were dusted with some type of red spice and looked good. Turns out it was a paprika or cayenne mix of some sort and they were indeed tasty.

Now back to the sandwich. First bite was tasty but the meat was a little overcooked which killed the juicyness even though they still maintained good flavor. Second bite I topped with a little BBQ sauce and after tasting it i knew exactly why they provided it as it complemented the sandwich very well.

While I enjoyed this meal I also opted to have a craft beer (Hazy IPA) which was local and also tasty. Their tap list in fact is pretty well balanced with options for almost everyone.

Overall I would give Cali Comfort a 4.25 rating but since Google doesn't provide that option they get a 4.

I would visit them again as i do like the BBQ sports bar feel but I would most likely try a different dish as Tommy's Tri-Tip Sandwich doesn't get them in my top 3 currently.

name: Roy Chi
text:
*3.5 stars*

Honestly, ANY other burger establishment would've been a welcome replacement to the horrific cesspool that was Burger Joint, so the bar was set pretty damn low for this restaurant space. Upon hearing that Umami Burger was coming in, I must admit that I did groan a little bit -- I tried the original Los Angeles location a few years ago and wasn't impressed at all. But still, much better than Burger Joint -- and since it's so close to where I live, I decided to give it another shot.

I'm still disappointed with the size of the burgers here -- I mean, c'mon, WHO gets full off of these?! Our table actually ordered extra burgers just so we could be full (resulting in a pretty steep final bill), so for the price, one burger is just way too tiny.

Best of the bunch: The Manly Burger. Oh man, everything about this burger was excellent -- the crunch from the toasted bun, the tenderness of the meat, the gooey melted cheese, and the F**KING LARD!! I would get this again in a heartbeat... that is, if my heart doesn't stop beating after eating this calorie-stuffed monster.

The rest of the burgers were just okay -- the Umami Burger was bland, the Truffle Burger just tasted like truffle oil (which I guess is accurate naming, but not really inventive or special in any way). The truffle fries were good; the fried pickles were meh. Finished off with a pecan pie, which tasted like it was bought in the bakery section of the Safeway next door. Service was awesome, though.

Umami Burger is definitely a VAST improvement over the Burger Joint that was here before, but there's just so much more they can do to make it awesome. Since it's a franchise, probably nothing will ever be done though. However, I'll surely be coming back for that Manly Burger (or two, since one is SO DAMN TINY).

This place is called Then Bench for a reason. The place sports communal seating around a long table or at the bar. The idea is to promote socializing. Unfortunately, most people still broke up into cliques and talked amongst themselves, even for two strangers seated right across from each other.

If you're coming here with friends, this is a good place. Otherwise, if you're here by yourself, then you'll feel a bit out of place as most people still kept to themselves.
There are more private firepit tables outside just by the 18th Hole but they required a longer wait.

In spite of the at times chaotic atmosphere, the servers all manage to keep track of everyone and their places. The food served is American/Italian. We had the flat-beard pizza, which was quite good. name: Ryan Bauer
text:
Dining here is an interesting and fun experience. If you have not been to a restaurant like this then be prepared to eat, because the food literally keeps coming your direction. Upon being seated at your table, the waiter or waitress asks if you have been there before and gives you a quick tutorial on how the restaurant works if you haven't been there before.
On your table you will find a circular card that has a red side and a green side. These is essentially a stoplight for the meat portion of your meal. You are allowed to go up to the salad bar as often as you like and it is a sizeable salad bar with a wide variety of items ranging from meats to pre-made salads like potato salads.
Upon flipping your stoplight to "go", the meat starts coming your direction. The staff have big sticks of meat including pork, chicken, beef, and lamb. It is a wide variety and very delicious. The pork sausage, chicken and garlic beef were my favorites. I would certainly recommend this place to anybody looking for an out of the normal style of dining.

Fast Mexican food with prices a bit higher than its quality.

I like El Jalapeno Rojo. Their chimichanga, tacos and burritos were tasty, much better than the standard taquerias, with their carne asada and pollo well spiced, their al pastor juicy with pineapple. Sadly, the bump in quality over the standard is met with a a bit higher price.

The last time I was there, I ordered an al pastor chimichanga and a fish taco along with a big cup of horchata and it came out a bit over $20 after tax. Other local establishments of the same quality would have charged less or offered higher quality fish for the same price.

It's not that it's a bad place, and I'd gladly go if someone else suggests it, but I wouldn't choose it of my own volition.

When the waitress came next she brought us our check without asking if we wanted dessert. I interjected that we would be needing a dessert menu. She brought one and I ordered a chocolate shake and my Wife ordered a pumpkin pastry.  The waitress disappeared and my shake and pumpkin pastry did not arrive. I hailed the manager who apologized for the mistake and comped me the desserts. I still left a big enough tip to cover the desserts. I really wanted good service more than a freebie, but the manager was professional and I appreciate that. During the same times that we were ignored my Wife observed a large table next to us that was given better service by the same waitress. This is the second time I've gotten random service at this location, which is why I took the time to write this review.  Food was ok, service was, well, random. Go here with expectation that it's a roll of the dice how your service will be... Not bad, not great... in-between. Two visits here had great service with a smile, two didn't.

text:
I dined here last night for my first time and was impressed with the food. However, I will warn you now - SAVE ROOM FOR DESSERT. This is the mistake we did last night. We ate too much food and couldn't fit in the most popular section on the menu - the sweet part, which is what they're known for. I'll have to come here just for dessert the next time I stop by, which will be very soon.

Tapas style. Sharing is caring. Recommended: 2 dishes/person. Parking: ample street

We had a group of four so we were able to sample a lot on the menu. My TOP DISHES were:

WILD MUSHROOM BRUSCHETTA: four pieces of perfectly salty, seasoned mushrooms on crispy toasts. YAY.

CRISPY MASHED POTATOES: order this.

FARRO WALNUT: a rollercoaster of flavors.

Dishes I enjoyed and WOULD order again: Brussel sprouts, Mac & Cheese, Stuffed Shells, Fried Cauliflower

Other dishes I enjoyed but WOULDN'T order again: Broccolini, Shepherd's Pie, Sausage & Polenta

Again, don't stuff yourself. MAKE ROOM FOR DESSERT! I'm coming back for ya!

And no, Moby was not there when we dined last night.

If you have seen the Hollywood movies Pulp Fiction and xXx, you have definitely noticed this diner where both movies are filmed.

Pann’s is located in Los Angeles by the Inglewood area and is best known for its breakfast. The place is popular, so you can risk waiting to find a place.

The decor and atmosphere are very good, where you almost feel like in a movie. The service is fine while the prices are moderate.

We ordered pancakes with syrup and banana whipped cream next to it, which cost $ 16.95, which equates to $ 105.

Pann’s Restaurant is a recommendable eatery offering American breakfast. It's an experience of eating at this iconic diner when in Los Angeles.

IKONISK DINER I LOS ANGELES

Pann’s ligger i Los Angeles ved Inglewood-området og er mest kendt for sin morgenmad. Stedet er populært, hvorfor man kan risikere at vente for at finde en plads.

Indretning og atmosfæren er meget god, hvor man nærmest føler sig i en filmoptagelse. Servicen er fin, mens priserne er moderate.

Vi bestilte pandekager med sirup og banan flødeskum ved siden af, som kostede 16,95 USD, hvilket svarer til 105 DKK.

I had almost forgotten how much the little traditions of a  sushi experience matter: oshiburi (hot towel) offered to us before beginning our meal, complimentary edamame and delicious sunomono appetizer served quickly and automatically. But the biggest factor in my impression, and arguably the most important of any sushi review, was the fish. text: I've lived in Orange County my entire life and have driven by this restaurant a million times but this was my first visit. I'm realizing that I've missed out on a ton of awesome meals. This is a casual environment restaurant and anything from shorts and flip-flops to suits and ties. I chose a 3/4 rack of baby back ribs. They were tender, meaty, flavorful and downright tasty. They were so good that they didn't require any additional barbecue sauce. Let's talk BBQ sauce! Their sauce is just about perfect not too sweet not too spicy. I find a lot of restaurants try too hard with their barbecue sauce. With my rack I had to side choices and considering I'm on a low-carb diet my only two options were mashed sweet potatoes and grilled veggies. Didn't love the mashed sweet potatoes but thought the grilled veggies were excellent. Included with the meal is a quarter corn on the cob and a large piece of cantaloupe. I can't say enough about the quality and taste of the ribs and that is the backbone of any barbecue restaurant. My meal was $28 not including a drink. At the price point it's not a place you're going to eat at nightly but certainly an occasional stop will put a fix to any BBQ cravings

name: Ryan Hall
text:
The wait can be a little bit long, even if you got on Yelp and put your name on the waitlist. Believe it or not, it's slower around 5- 6pm, then slows down again after 9pm. Between 6- 9 is the busiest time so avoid that time if you can. Here are some tips:
1. Do not park to the left of the restaurant (if you're facing Manna). There are plenty of signs that warns you not to, and they WILL tow. Park to the side of the bank and Hive bar.
2. Ask for sesame seed oil to mix with your salt to dip your meat.
3. They used to bring them out automatically but now you have to ask for the sliced garlic, the jalapenos, and the ssamjang.
4. The steamed egg is kinda... eh. I don't like how it smells.
5. They changed the menu so that some of the best cut meat are no longer on the A2 menu. Just shell out the extra $5 per person and get the A1.
6. Remember that the entire table has to get the same menu, i.e. you can't get A2 when everybody else gets A1. Decide this before the server gets there and you'll save yourself some embarrassment.
7. If you don't finish youre soju or beer, ask the next table if they want the bottle. I detest wasting alcohol so I always do.
8. Ask them to change out the grill often. You're not bothering them and they'd rather switch out the grill twenty times rather than you create a thick cloud of greasy smoke that wafts through the restaurant.
8. They'll turn down the fire under the grill if you start burning your meat. The controls are below the table so turn it up if you know what you're doing and needs must.
9. Wear clothes you don't mind smelling like burnt meat. If you're going somewhere nice after KBBQ, take an extra shirt and your cologne/ perfume... and keep them in your car or purse.
10. Know what you're ordering before you push the button on the table to call then over. They're busy so they get annoyed if you make then wait... and if you can help it, don't use the button. It's weird, but kbbq servers don't seem to like that sound.
11. It might take a few tries to get everything you asked for. Don't get indignant if it does - it won't help you.
12. Don't yell "Excuse me!" I know it's loud in there but... don't.
13. Yes, that birthday song is kinda cool. But don't lie and say that it's your birthday when it's not. They'll remember that.
14. When you order, ask everyone on the table what they need and then tell your server everything you need instead of pushing the button over and over again.
15. Tip them well and remember your server's name. You'll be surprised by the extra stuff you get on your next visit.

I have never been to Zov's but I've heard great things.  The restaurant is located in a quaint shopping center near Sharkey's and Pomodoro.  We had a reservation for 10 and they accommodated us with a long table in the back.  Our server was cordial and was able to split off my check upon request.  The food is a mix of Middle Eastern, Armenian and Mediterranean with a full bar.  They also serve an angus sirloin and burgers.  There's a wine list, beer list and a cocktail menu too.

Donald S. recommended the golden lentil soup which was a hit with our table.  I also ordered some baba ghanoush ($8.95) to share.  I had the cucumber mint fresca ($11.50) which was really refreshing and delicious.  My entree was the pan-seared bass ($22.95).  My tablemates tried: lamb sandwich ($13.95), spinach & ricotta ravioli, salads, chicken kebob, and filet medallions ($25).  All were good selections since everyone seemed to enjoy their food and drinks.  My bass although "pan-seared" did not have any crispiness to my disappointment.  I did enjoy it with the citrus jasmine rice, asparagus, and tomatoes.  It was good but not great.  The baba ghanoush was ok too.  I did have a bite of my friend's lamb sandwich which was delicious and the filet medallions were very tender.  We even ordered some desserts to share: key lime tart, chocolate bomb, and bread pudding.  Of the 3, I really liked the bread pudding.  The chocolate bomb was good but it was overkill for me.  Overall, we had good food with great service and conversation with awesome friends.  We'll definitely continue our dinner series but maybe we'll move into numbers before restarting the alphabet again.

name: Kimberly R. Kelly
text:
Staying at Evergreen was a pure pleasure. It was so convenient to be able to stay at a property that had all that one could want on site!

Food:
As many reviewers have said, the free Smore‘s every night were such a treat. The food at the Tavern was easily of the best quality in Yosemite Valley and as such reasonably priced, imo. Breakfast in the restaurant did trend a little expensive ($14-$16 per entree plus $4 for coffee/tea), but for a full-service restaurant, I’m not mad at it. Also the portions are huge, so one could easily share a main dish and add a side for a reasonably priced and good sized breakfast for 2. Also, the restaurant has a kid’s portion size option at breakfast, and the breakfast burrito (vegetarian) and breakfast sandwiches (egg, cheese, bacon with tomato chutney) in the camp store are surprisingly gourmet. The laundry room had a shared microwave and toaster, but the electric water kettle (shown in website pictures) was not available.

Lodging:
We stayed in the Custom Camping for the first 3 nights and upgraded to a one-bedroom cabin for the final night. The tents were sufficient and comfortable for a tent. Although it was nice to have a mattress, I’m 5 ft and my partner is 6ft, so I would slide to the middle especially in the sleeping bag, which was a bit slippery. The cabin was Fantastic. Big, comfy, with a deck!

Extras:
We booked a massage with GiGi. I had the stretch massage, which was exactly what the doctor ordered after two days and 30+ miles of hiking. My partner had the hand foot and scalp massage, which he said was very relaxing.

The staff in all interactions were professional and welcoming. Even the slight surliness of the Sunday night bartender didn’t bother us. On the other hand, the Fri and Sat night bartender was a delight. Fun to talk to about local hikes and the area in general.

Overall, we had an extraordinary stay at Evergreen and we can’t wait to go back!

name: Cheryl Peters
text: I was first introduced to the Corky's dining experience at the Rancho Cucamonga location. I was really excited to learn we have one here in Corona!!! Corky's is a classic comfort food destination. I say destination because the menu items are sure to take you back to the days when having a huge slice of pie or slab of meat loaf put a big smile on your face. Corky's has an old school diner bar as well as large over-sized booths and tables to hold your dining choices. The decor is simple country and doesn't take away from the whole point of being there, TO EAT GREAT HOME-COOKED FOOD. Turkey burgers were recently added to the menu and it didn't disappoint!!! For those of you diners who prefer a meatless alternative, you will be pleasantly surprised that the turkey is fresh ground and seasoned like its a next day Thanksgiving Sammich!! It's topped with fresh avocado and mayo. I like dipping it in the Thousand Island Dressing they offer as requested. The fries (not kidding) look they came off a foot long potato. I have yet to get through the whole burger because I usually order a side salad. So basically (for me) its two meals for the price of one. Oh did I mention the pie?? I love the apple pie!! it's so fresh, you can taste the caramelized skin on the Granny Smith apples they use. It's crust is flaky and light. I prefer this to the doughy pies of the local competition rhymes with (Lame Lumper). Im so addicted to it I have yet to try one of their creme pies, which they are famous for. I did try the Brownie with Chocolate sauce and vanilla ice cream. Even with two of us tacking it we could finish it off!! It did however make a nice late night snack the next day!!

text:
Yesterday was my second or third time at the Girl & the Fig and I remember fond memories of the food here. They do not disappoint.

I came with a large group with my team for lunch and sat in the patio. It was a HOT day so it was nice that our table was mostly covered and they had small fans blowing. We had a nice lunch and the customer service was great. Our server was the most delightful woman with an accent.

What I ordered:

Duck liver pâté -  peach butter, brioche toasts ($14): One of the best duck liver pate's I've had in a while. The flavor was deep and rich and and I loved it with the peach butter with was more like a jam. The fluffy brioche toast was also a nice touch. All the flavor married each other well. It was so good my co-worker dipped his finger in the jar and got every last bit out!

Grass-fed steak tartare - traditional, raw egg, caper berries, lavender sea salt ($15): One of my second favorite dishes. Had to get it and it was delicious, fresh and well seasoned. Love the generous amount of capers in it too. Wish the portion size was a bit larger.

Quiche lorraine - seasonal salad, matchstick frites ($15) - I don't usually order quiche but I was hungover and wanted something with egg and on the lighter side. Our server said she doesn't like quiche and this was the best one she had with a souffle consistency and she was right! After eating the other items above, I only finish less than half my meal. The serving size was huge and they really pile on the fries. I had this for lunch today and it was even more delicious than it was yesterday. Maybe it was because I have an appetite today and I'm not hungover anymore lol.

I have a great experience here and I would like to return and try their dinner menu one day.

For food, I had the salmon cakes, which are kind of like an eggs Benedict, but with salmon instead of an English muffin. It was incredible! name: Natalie K
text:
Tatsu Ramen has some seriously legit ramen. I honestly think that this place isn't more popular only because of its proximity to Tsujita Ramen the next block over. Aside from the fact that the wait here isn't as bad as Tsujita, another huge plus is that they are opened till 3am on weekends and 2am on other days.

There are 3 iPads on the wall for you to input your order and pay. There is a separate iPad right next to the door so that you can add tip. Once your order is in, take your receipt and find a seat. Someone will come check your order and eventually bring out your food.

The place is small. They have mostly bar seats and one big table that you can share with others.

I had the "Soul Ramen", which is a combination of their broths. I absolutely loved it. The ramen had the perfect texture and the broth was so flavorful. They have these raw garlic and garlic mincer. I would probably suggest about 3 cloves at most. I'm a little crazy and had 6 cloves. I liked it but most normal people would find my broth disgusting.

Parking is valet only. You can drive around the neighborhood looking for parking. You may find one if you're lucky. If you go late enough though, the valet guys are gone and you can park in the lot for free.

I took my family here for Mother's Day.  My parents had never been here so I thought it might be fun for them to check it out.  We were also celebrating my brother's birthday as well.  I used OpenTable to make the reservation.  There was a $20 voucher via OpenTable too if you used the "PAY" feature in the OpenTable app at the restaurant.  It would have allowed me to view and pay the bill while dining at the restaurant.  In theory, had it worked, it would have been great.  But they must have forgotten to check me into my reservation so I was unable to pay via the app.

Although we had reservations, we still waited 10+ minutes to be seated.  There were large groups of people also waiting.  I heard them give someone a 2-3 hour time-frame which I was glad that 10 minutes was all we had to wait.  The chef was pretty good but not as lively as I expected him to be.  We ordered the 6-course meals.  I had the hibachi steak and shrimp.  My mom had the filet mignon and lobster tail while my dad had the filet mignon and shrimp.  My brother ordered just the hibachi steak.  Everyone had the chicken fried rice.  Our meal also included hot green tea, mushroom soup and a house salad with miso dressing.  We also received a shrimp appetizer along with grilled zuccini and onions.  There was ice cream at the end but we all passed on it because we were stuffed.  It was a good meal but in comparison to other teppan places, it was lacking in value.

text:
Mama's is a wonderful breakfast and lunch restaurant in the heart of the Telegraph Hill neighborhood.  The atmosphere is cute and charming.  The food is fresh and delicious.  Mama's is a tourist hot-spot and local favorite.  Perhaps that explains the unbelievably long lines that form during the weekends.  Unless you arrive before opening time, expect to wait for a while in line (typically ~1 hr in my experience, but sometimes longer).  This is the only reason I couldn't give Mama's 5 stars.

Be sure to arrive as early as you reasonably can on weekends.  Parking is also a bit challenging, as there is only street parking nearby.  But if you're willing to wait, the experience is worth it.

name: Trina D.
text:
I had been lusting over some foodie photos taken at the Federal Bar in Long Beach for months.  Then one day, I saw a LivingSocial deal for brunch.  Of course, online coupons can be hit or miss but all those blog photos can't be wrong.  I bought the deal which included 2 entrees and bottomless mimosas.  I don't know about you but I'm not going to pass up bottomless mimosas.  No way.

So last Sunday, my friend Julie B. and I went to the Federal Bar for brunch to celebrate her birthday.  She was super excited because she had no idea what we were doing for brunch.  We walked in to give our name to the hostess and we're ushered into the large, spacious dining room.  The Federal Bar is located inside an old bank so it has high ceilings and a gorgeous art deco interior.  The staff is dressed up in 1920s clothing circa the Great Gatsby.  This place would be awesome for a party!  Our server came by and took our orders for the mimosas and my LivingSocial certificate.

I ordered the red velvet waffle sandwich but was informed that they had run out of waffles.  TRAGEDY!  Especially since they had just been open an hour when we walked in.  The waitress suggested the breakfast burger which also had the sweet and savory combination I was looking for.  Julie ordered the omelette with short rib.  Our entrees came out shortly after and I have to say their food is so delicious!  The burger was perfectly cooked to order.  I asked for medium.  The maple aioli was a nice touch and I loved the heirloom tomatoes.  The French fries were covered in parmesan and parsley but so tasty.  Julie really liked her omelette as well and ate the entire thing.  My mimosa glass was constantly refilled to the point where I had to ask her to stop filling it because I had to drive.  I'd definitely come back here for brunch.  It's a shame that it's so far away from me though.  I'll also come back to try out their dinner menu as well.  They have a full bar with a few craft cocktails that sound interesting.  I'll definitely be back.

name: Trina D.
text:
Vanessa D. and I met for brunch here today.  Finally, I get to try this place out and see what all the hype is about.  My cousin is all about healthy eating and this place is right up her alley.  We tried to make reservations but apparently, they don't take reservations for parties less than 8 people.  We arrived at 11:50 am and waited about 10 minutes for a table.  Not too bad.  However, as we were seated, I noticed that there were quite a number of tables in a section that were open.  Maybe that's the section that they use for reserved parties.  The restaurant is designed with an open kitchen feel.  It's airy, bright, and very modern.  The place screams healthy.   The salt and pepper grinders on the table were a nice touch as well.

We ordered the cucumber kumquat skinny margarita and the medicine man drink to start.  For an appetizer we ordered the onion tart.  The tart was more like a flatbread with bits of roasted garlic, caramelized onions, figs, and cheese.  It was delicious!  Despite being a small portion, it was perfect with the sweetness and saltiness of the ingredients married together with each bite.  I ordered the vegetable scramble and V ordered the Greek frittata.  Both dishes were vegetarian, but so good that we didn't miss the meat.  My scramble was chock full of vegetables.  The sweet potato hash was incorporated into the dish as were bits of red onion.  Our waitress brought out a dish of chili paste per our request so that we could spice up our food as we saw fit.  I finished every single bite.

For dessert we opted for the flourless chocolate cake, with the ice cream on the side since V can't eat ice cream.  More for me!  The chocolate cake was the size of the small cupcake but every bite was decadent, especially in the caramel sauce and ice cream.  I was a happy camper.  True Food serves delicious food in small portions.  I'd say the right portions since we shouldn't overeat.  Don't expect Claim Jumper portions, but rather the right portions for your money.  This place will not cause obesity.  It's healthy food, done right.  I like the philosophy and it's about time SoCal got an infusion of healthy, responsible, delicious food.

name: alice chung
text:
Extremely affordable for amazing homemade tortillas and unique, delicious flavors.

I've tried pretty much all the flavors here. My favorites are the chorizo, quesadilla, mole poblano (chicken), cochinita pibil (pork) and tinga de pollo (chicken). The pescado (fish) and camarones (shrimp) are good but not great. I stick to my favorites.

The ones I stay away from are the chicharron (texture disgusts me) and spicy items such as chuleta en chile verde (pork), bistek en salsa roja (steak) and steak picado (steak).

IF YOU'RE NEW: get the SAMPLER PLATE (6 tacos) because this will give you a chance to try out the different flavors offered here. The sampler gives you the first six flavors listed on the menu. If you wanted to substitute one for another, you can -- just let them know!

text:
First time here since the renovation and change of ownership, which gave it a new kitchen, and knocked out that raised seating platform. I'm pretty disappointed in what Sam's has become.

Food isn't what it once used to be, which is weird considering it's now back in the hands of the original family. Still good, just different. Also disappointed that the pickle barrel is gone! You now have to ask for them, as they're behind the counter.

Service has also gotten worse. The previous workers used to be very friendly and engaging. The ones we encountered didn't talk, and acted like they had other places to be. Not friendly at all. There were four of us ordering food. The first two went thru the line relatively quickly. Next was myself and another; we each ordered a French dip. They made my sandwich, and started to carve the next. The patrons after us asked a question. The two line workers called for a manager, and waited and watched as that manager spoke with that customer. Meanwhile, two of us were left waiting for our food. After about 5 minutes, one guy gave me my sandwich, minus au jus. I had to ask for it. He asked if I had ordered a French dip, twice. I said yes, twice. He seemed irritated while reaching to grab the black toothpick thing to stab into the bread, and as he was getting my au jus. We had to wait an extra few minutes for the other French dip to be served. The two people in our party ahead of us had already paid, sat down, and began their lunch by the time we sat down.

Not being accustomed to the new layout. we asked a lady behind the counter for to-go containers. She snapped at us and pointed to the containers as she irritatingly said, "YOU GET THEM YOURSELF. THEY'RE RIGHT THERE."

So, 3 stars for food, two for service. Very sad that this place doesn't have the same charm it did before the renovation.

text:
The newest Fogo De Chao location takes over former Roy's Hawaiian establishment in downtown Los Angeles. It's so new that they did not have their liquor license to serve alcohol when I dined there this past Friday.

Last time I dined at Fogo De Chao was about 8 years ago at the Beverly Hills location. It didn't impress me but I didn't want to write the restaurant off just after one try.

Decided to dine there again and the results were the same. Quality of meats were okay at best. I would prefer ordering one tender, well cooked filet mignon, steak or lamp chop then to have unlimited amounts of decently cooked meat.

While both my experiences in food quality at Fogo De Chao was "okay," I will have to say that the customer service at this new location was TOP NOTCH AMAZING! Loved the staff and our waitress.

text:
I kind of don't want to review this place because it's the best kept secret of the east bay. The food is always good. Their special events offer great wine pairings and they always blow me away with their veg and fish options. I normally don't like fish but they cook it with such a perfect mix of sweet, sour, salty and spicy. It's never too much of anything but just the right amount of everything. The portion sizes are just right to be able to have a starter the main and desert.

Now to the service. They are a small place that has a staff that's loyal, which is a good sign. They always seem to really love the dishes because when you ask their mouth waters! The service is wonderful! They are attentive, know when to come fill your glass and when to pickup the plates.

From the outside it doesn't look like much but the experience is like being at home with family eating fresh seafood of the coast of some little Italian village you are passing through but never want to leave!

Great place for a small group. You can call ahead and put your name on the wait list, they don't take resos.

Rainbow Salad 5/5
I LOVE this salad. It's light, refreshing, but substantial. 22 ingredients!!! Four types of noodles, green papaya, onions, and ... with a tamarind dressing

Samusa Soup 5/5
It's amazing, and vegetarian! Samusas, falafels, lentils, cabbage, and onions.

Platha and Dip 5/5
Flaky deliciousness.

Mango Chicken 5/5
Stir fried chicken breast with fresh mangos in a light chili sauce. So good!

Sesame Chicken 5/5
Slices of chicken breast lightly fried in a sweet and tangy sauce.

Mint Chicken 4/5
Minced chicken, mint, cloves of garlic, cilantro, and jalapenos. Reminds me of Basil Chicken at Thai restaurants.

Walnut Shrimp 5/5
Shrimp lightly fried and tossed with a sweet sauce. Topped with roasted walnuts and sesame seeds. For those that like Walnut Shrimp at Chinese restaurants, this will not disappoint.

Garlic and Chili Shrimp 4/5
Wok tossed shrimp in our garlicky infused oil with jalapeños and topped with toasted garlic & cilantro. Honestly, I like the Walnut Shrimp better.

Sesame Beef 5/5
Strips of beef lightly battered and fried with a sweet and tangy sauce. Topped with sesame seeds. A friend wanted to order this, I was on the fence, but pleasantly surprised.

Then it took another 40 minutes for them to bring out our entrees. Though I don't come here for fast food, for a business lunch, we had to shovel the entrees down because we were out of time from the food taking so long to come out. Then to top it all off, when the wait staff came out to finally give us the bill, they knocked the glass water bottle off the table breaking on top of my foot. I have never had a bad experience here but this was far off the mark. Essentially lunch took almost 2 hours and the food just wasn't what it had been in the past.

name: Jack Lau
text: There is the baseline: McDonalds. One level up is In and Out. In an entirely separate realm outside of the fast food are these type of places that serve burgers in their own signature way. That's the part that fails to make Nom Burger special. They have specials, but it's more like a strange fusion of throwing things on a burger and turning it into an entirely different meal. It sounds cool, but in reality makes for a very poor combination of flavor profiles. There's a place for NOM burger in downtown Sunnyvale. I don't expect it to go anywhere. I also want to recognize their commitment to using local and hand craft patties. In this burger era, it's hard to stand out from the crowd. Even the average place can be good enough.

name: Kelly Moran
text: Great food, service, and atmosphere. I had the signature burger with an appetizer of sweet potato waffle fries and left feeling satisfyingly full but not overstuffed. The burger patty was well seasoned and juicy, and the waffle fries came with sides of garlic aioli and ketchup. I liked that the bun squished down when I bit into it and wasn't too dense and bready. My husband had the pulled pork nachos, which are made with taro chips instead of corn. I tried a taro chip and it had a very mild, almost undetectable starchy flavor which I thought was good for a nacho chip. They also seemed to stand up well to heavy, wet toppings. All in all it was a wonderful meal out.

Soft boiled egg does not come standard in some of the ramen so be sure to include it if this is a necessary addition to your ideal bowl (does cost a $1 extra). I would say its worth it because they do marinate it and it does taste more awesome.

The space itself is a bit cozy, so large groups (greater than 8) maybe a bit difficult (although possible) to accomodate.

They played Reggae as the background music to the restaurant not sure if this is common but me and my girl loved the tunes (who doesn't love Bob Marley while you chow down on some Ramen! haha)

Great spot we'll be coming back here whenever we're in the area!

Here, they have the classic schweinshaxe, jager schnitzel, knodel, assortment of bavarian sausages, and German beer on tap. It is no doubt that the food is authentic because all I could hear was him speaking German. The inside is kept furnished in its old school style. A main course comes with bread and butter, a small side salad and a cup of soup - none of which is mentioned on the menu so it's a nice surprise although I almost ordered other items to make sure I had a balanced meal. The service was fairly slow but the place is run almost entirely by an elderly German couple with no additional waitstaff so just know you're not going to be in and out in under an hour. The traditional food is very good and worth a bit of a wait, especially since the bread etc will arrive faster. The restaurant is rather brightly lit and decorated with various German (and other?) knick-knacks. There is seating available on an outside patio but it was too cold to use during this visit.

name: Roy Chi
text:
State Bird Provisions is a shining example of why I love the food culture in San Francisco. The entire restaurant experience here is top-notch; definitely one of the best dinners I've had in the city. State Bird Provisions introduces a dim sum-style ordering process to unique, fresh, and flavorful concoctions, all of which were absolutely delicious.

The large open kitchen in the front of the restaurant is definitely a nice welcome. You see a dedicated league of chefs preparing a countless number of intricate and interesting dishes.

There are a few shared plates on the menu, and plenty more that they bring around the room on trays and carts. I love this process because you can see the food before you decide to take it, and you can ask questions with the dish right in front of you. I've never seen anything like this before at an American restaurant, and it really is genius. Be aware though: you will probably end up spending way more than you expected to, because it's pretty difficult (at least for me) to reject any of the dishes they bring around. They all looked phenomenal, and the vast majority of them were.

----------------------------
A group of 3 of us had the following:

Serrano Ham w/ Persimmon: Fresh & tasty. I could eat these all day.

Pan-seared Trout = Excellently-cooked trout.

Beef Cheek w/ Bone Marrow Vinaigrette = Delicious. The Bone Marrow vinaigrette is incredible and the Beef Cheek was nice and tender.

Flatbread with Oxtail and Curried Lentils = Warm & flavorful. Loved it.

CA State Bird w/ Provisions (Fried Quail) = This was my favorite dish of the night. The fried quail was PERFECTLY fried and the meat was unbelievably moist. This is how poultry should be fried.

Cavatelli w/ Dungeness Crab = Interesting flavor that really grew on me with each bite.

Kimchi Pork Belly w/ Yuba Noodles = Very good take on the Korean flavors. The kimchi flavor is faint, but works very well in the broth. Pork Belly was nicely crisped.

Duck Confit w/ Cornbread = The cornbread is phenomenal. The duck confit was good, but I wish they utilized something different with cornbread (ideally something like foie gras).

Duck Neck Dumplings = Little dumplings that had a distinct duck neck flavor, but the dumpling skin was a little too doughy. Still good, though.

Clam Sliders = The bun for the sliders were great, although I wish the clams were hot instead of cold.

Goat Cheese w/ Vegetable Crudite = The goat cheese was great -- not too overpowering but still had a strong flavor. Goes well with the vegetables.

Grand Total: $61.00 per person, including an ice-cold IPA (and tax & tip).
----------------------------

For a brand-new restaurant, State Bird Provisions blows many SF establishments out of the water. It serves up incredibly fresh, unique, and tasty dishes at decent prices. Make a reservation now and be prepared for an amazing night out.

The server mentioned something about salmon, not the vegan dish, and I corrected him. It was 40 minutes total before the vegan dish came out, after I had already informed the host we would be leaving for another restaurant without the entree. Then a food runner came with the entree and I informed him, again, that we would not be paying for that but we would pay for the 3 drinks and the app. It came to $63. This year, (2019) my mother chose to go to Pacific Catch, in Mount View, Ca.. It was kind of hard to find at first; and the construction didn't make things easier! It's nestled away in a brand new Hidden Cove type of Plaza thats sooo sophisticated there's really not too much room to maneuver your vehicle, and then the parking set up is absolutely horrible! It was so hard to find parking that I ended up being late and my mother was mad at me! When I finally made it inside, there was hardly anybody there.The restaurant looked very new and had a nice decor but our waiter did not match this environment at all! I was very upset by his attitude, demeanor and professionalism and I wanted to complain so bad about a few defferent things; but my mom was very adamant that I not say anything, and she continue acting as if she enjoyed herself. I had a very hard time because I'm the type of $on that wants nothing but the best for my mother! Especially on a day like this!! When I finally received my food, I was disappointed! I was sooo frustrated, I didn't know what to do! I feel like this restaurant is overpriced and overrated; but it does have the potential to raise it's ratings one day, once it works out all it's little kinks.

This is my favorite place to go in Downtown Palo Alto. It's the only place that has both good food and good beer.

My co-workers and I come here pretty often for lunch since they have multiple community tables that can accommodate more people. We usually don't have too much of a problem getting a table. I have come once for dinner, and it's a little more difficult to get a table without a reservation.

The food quality is amazing and tastes fresh. I really like the turkey club. Good portions are pretty generous; maybe even too generous for me for lunch (I either end up taking some home or stuffing myself).

Beer selection here, while not overly extensive, is very good. There are a decent number of beers of different varieties on tap and a similar number in bottles. The wine list is also fairly long, and my co-worker (who generally drinks wine) seemed to enjoy her wine here, though I can't personally vouch for it since I don't drink wine very often.

The ambiance here is also really nice. I love that the skylights allow a lot of natural light; it feels like you're sitting outside. There are also a few tables by the sidewalk that can be good if you're in a smaller group or by yourself.

Highly recommend!

name: Trina D.
text:
One of the best KBBQ places I've ever been to.  There was a line at 11:15 am on Easter morning and they opened at 11:30 am.  The place is not AYCE.  You order off of the menu whatever you want.  Jonathan Z. and Grace C., joined me for brunch.  Grace ordered the 3-4 person combo ($89) for the 3 of us.  The quality of the meat was excellent.  We had brisket, short rib, marinated short rib, soup, rice, lettuce salad, and baekjeong salad.

They had kim chi set out for us as well as egg in a side pan that cooked from the heat of the grill.  What I found to be really strange was the corn with shredded cheese.  My friend who is Korean-American said that she'd never seen anything like that at a KBBQ place either.   We received the soup before the meat came out but that's ok.  I did notice that all the other tables had received their meats before us but maybe that's because we had just ordered.  The servers do cook for you.  If you're flipping something over or trying to cut it, if one of them walks by, they will take the tongs and scissors from you to help.  That's a nice extra service that they offer.  There's a bell you can ring should you need service immediately but it seems that they walk by often enough that you don't need it.

We had to ask for sesame oil for the salt.  I guess it's not something they put out but you can ask for it.  Grace asked for another bowl of rice and was told that we'd be charged for it.  But when the bill came out they had forgotten about her extra rice.  We had asked for extra bowls to divide the soup into but that never came and I felt bad about sipping the soup with my spoon when we could have been sharing it.  Turns out I liked the soup better than the rest of the group because it was spicy.  Win for me.

My favorite meats were the short rib and marinated short rib.  It was wonderfully marbled.  They also switched the grate quite often.  They had a wire one for the fattier, thicker cuts and a flat, slotted grate for the brisket.  They also had 2 pieces of charcoal in with the fire so that even though we used a gas burner, the meat was still enhanced with a little charcoal smoke.  I enjoyed the house sauce that had bits of onion, jalapeno, and wasabi in it.  The baekjeong salad was interesting too.  It was full of hot sauce which was great.  The dining experience here is pretty much what you'd expect from KBBQ.  The quality of the meat was probably the best part of the meal.  They don't take reservations and there probably will be a wait if you go on the weekends or during prime dinner time.  It's only worth the wait if you think it is.  That's why we went when it opened.  4.5 stars.

name: alice chung
text:
My boyfriend got lucky and landed a same day reservation on a Friday at 7:30pm via Opentable - prime dinner time. Outside of luck, expect at least a month-long wait for a decent reservation of your preferred date and time. The couple next to us made reservations that much in advance. We definitely lucked out.

Heck, after realizing reservations were so hard to come by I decided to keep my 12:30pm brunch reservations in case we loved dinner that much that we wanted to come back the next day. Did we?

The popular restaurant is set in a dim lit, chatty setting with the attractive hostesses and waitresses making sure to highlight their assets with skin tight attire.

As a foodie, I did my research beforehand and had an idea of what I wanted to order. Their popular CHEDDAR BACON BISCUITS came out first, which did not disappoint. Although, I will have to say that it cannot contend with The Hart and the Hunter's signature biscuits, which are to die for. But I digress.

The rest of the dishes we ordered were superb with the exception of the POMEGRANATE COUSCOUS that we could have passed on. On the fence would be the brussels sprouts, which were good but not fantastic and especially not something I would crave again.

The stand out choices were the WHITE OAK GRILLED SKIRT STEAK (perfectly cooked medium rare slices of goodness all thanks to the red chimichurri sauce) and BRAISED LAMB NECK (tender chunks of flavored filled lamb perfectly paired with semolina gnocchi).

Overall, our dinner experience was extremely satisfying. And to answer your question (mine, rather), yes, we did return the next day for BRUNCH, which comes with another review.

We ordered the biscuits again because they were delicious and one can eat biscuits for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Any time of the day!

We ordered the ricotta stuffed FRENCH TOAST and TRUFFLE LACED HONEY FRIED CHICKEN, both of which are their popular items. The French toast was underwhelming and didn't offer anything special, in my opinion. It was more like a sandwich with ricotta in the middle.

The fried chicken was good but the flavors remained only on the surface - the skin. As you cut deeper into the chicken, it becomes bland white meat ... and lots of it. On the flip side, the side of coleslaw was amazing and probably the best I've ever tasted. I could get a jar full of that stuff.

In the end, I wish I had ordered the BLUEBERRY LEMON SKITTLE CAKE.

Dinner was fantastic and brunch was lukewarm. It makes sense as to why dinner reservations are so coveted while brunch reservations are easily obtained. You know what I'll be coming back for...

text:
(Translated by Google) POPULAR FISHING RESTAURANT IN MALIBU

On the Pacific Coast Hwy in Malibu is a very popular fish restaurant that has been the location of several famous movies. The most notable is The Fast and the Furious, where the final scenes of the film are filmed this place.

The restaurant is called Neptune's Net and is located just above County Line Beach. The place is best known for fish dishes, but we just chose to try their french fries.

The service is very friendly and the atmosphere is pleasant even though it is crowded with guests. Neptune's Net has its own parking lot, which is an advantage in the Los Angeles area.

Prices are reasonable. French fries cost 5.5 USD, which is equivalent to 33.5 DKK.

Neptune’s Net is an eatery that is above average and close to being recommendable. The fritters have a nice taste for the price and the atmosphere makes the experience better, but the place is far from the center and is not worth the trip just to eat fritters.

(Original)
POPULÆR FISKERESTAURANT I MALIBU

På kystvejen (Pacific Coast Hwy) i Malibu ligger en meget populær fiskerestaurant, der har været lokation for flere kendte film. Den mest nævneværdige er The Fast and the Furious, hvor de sidste scener i filmen er optaget dette sted.

Restauranten hedder Neptune's Net og er placeret lige over County Line Beach. Stedet er bedst kendt for fiskeretter, men vi valgte blot at prøve deres pommes fritter.

Betjeningen er meget venlig og atmosfæren er behagelig, selvom der er overfyldt med gæster. Neptune’s Net har sin egen parkeringsplads, hvilket er en fordel i Los Angeles-området.

Priserne er rimelige. Pommes Fritter koster 5,5 USD, hvilket svarer til 33,5 DKK.

Neptune’s Net er et spisested, der er over middel og tæt på at være anbefalingsværdigt. Fritterne har en fin smag til prisen og atmosfæren gør oplevelsen bedre, men stedet ligger langt fra centrum og er ikke turen værd kun for at spise fritter.

I'm not a huge fan of other Roy Choi's establishments to begin with so I'm not surprised that I didn't find Sunny Spot to be spectacular either. I would recommend this place for drinks but not the food.

You pretty much seat yourself here. You get a choice of either the bar area tables or the patio outside. The ambiance is actually really nice inside. It would be the perfect place for date except for the fact that it's extremely loud inside.

I enjoyed their cocktails. I had the rum punch and it was tasty but not too sweet. They also have a little bit of a wine selection. I tried a glass of the malbec and it was disappointing.

The food was the most confusing. We had the mofongo and heirloom tomato salad for appetizers. The heirloom tomato salad was quite good. It has a spicy kick and the goat cheese was delicious. The mofongo, however, was almost soupy. I didn't enjoy the texture or the flavor.

My cuban torta was also disappointing. It was definitely not one of the best cuban sandwich I've ever had. It's served with a flavorless sour slaw and yucca fries. The yucca came with this dipping sauce that I quite liked. Unfortunately the dipping sauce was the best part of the dish.

The service was pretty good. Our waitress was extremely friendly. They have valet parking for $3.

I've dined here many times and have always received great customer service. The "who's who" in the entertainment industry often come here for lunch meetings and dinners. Expect a noisy atmosphere.

The restaurant is conveniently located on the corner of Melrose Ave. and Robertson Blvd. Parking is valet only.

Appetizers
My favorite dish was the Ahi Tuna Tartare. However, the quality have been inconsistent the last few times I ordered this so I stopped altogether, sadly.

I highly recommend the Grilled Octopus, which is cooked just right. You also cannot go wrong with the Burrata, Heirloom tomatoes and avocado dish. Nothing beats fresh burrata - a simple yet tasteful dish.

Entrees
My new favorite dish would have to be the Organic Salmon, which comes with side of broccolini both topped with yummy basil pesto. The skin is perfectly crisped, which adds to the flavor of the fish (without the "fishy" taste).

Another good choice are the pizzas - thin crusted with fresh ingredients.

The lobster spaghetti was disappointing to me, unfortunately. The lobster was overcooked so the texture was pretty tough when paired with al dente pasta. Stay away.

Desserts
I've never had enough stomach space for dessert but you can never go wrong with a good ole fashion tiramisu.

It's currently OC Restaurant Week and I couldn't pass up the opportunity for a $40 prix fixe meal at Steakhouse 55.  We made our reservations for 6 pm on Sunday for 5 people, which was a good thing because when we arrived, someone in front of us was inquiring about a party of 6 and they told him that 9:30 was the next available table.  Ouch.  We let them know that we had arrived and they asked us to wait until our table was ready.  I had to go and ask around 6:10 to see where our table was at.  They promised to let us know soon.  It's Disney dining, I've come to expect a slight wait.

We were seated and greeted by our server shortly after.  They asked if we would like bread and water brought out to which we all said yes.  We perused the menu and decided on our options.  I went with the onion soup, prime rib (medium rare), and creme brulee.  The bread that came out was warmed and served with softened butter topped with thyme.  It was really tasty.

The seven onion soup came out in a gigantic bowl.  It was VERY salty.  I'm not sure who is making this but it contained so much sodium that I had to dunk a piece of sourdough bread in it in order to eat it.  I did enjoy the fried shallots in the soup but  I give the soup 2 stars.

The prime rib came out with potato au gratin and perfectly cooked green beans.  The cut was medium rare as requested.  The au jus was poured into a dish on the plate and there was a creamy horseradish sauce next to it.  First of all, I don't enjoy horseradish at all but this sauce was creamy and not too intense.  It was pretty good.  The au jus was also very salty but I figure they must be putting it into the onion soup at this point.  The prime rib was delicious and juicy.  The potatoes were cheesy and a nice texture.  I give the entree 4.5 stars.

The creme brulee came out without the advertised almond cookie because they ran out.  Instead they gave us a bigger portion of the creme brulee which delighted everyone at our table except for me.  It was the most popular dessert of the evening so naturally they ran out.  But you must realize that our reservation was at 6 pm and we were seated no later than 6:15.  You're telling me that the kitchen ran out of a dessert when everyone ordered the prix fixe at 6?  That's poor planning on their part.  I can't imagine what the people at 7:30 were given.  The creme brulee was pretty good and 4 out of 5 of us had ordered it.  Because it was a larger portion I had to stop myself from eating the entire thing.  I give it 4 stars because of the lack of cookie.

For the most part, service was great.  Our server was attentive but not overwhelming.  The bussers cleared the table of glasses, plates, and even crumbs as needed in timely fashion.  I can only comment on the initial wait before being seated and that wasn't horrible.  I know that the later the time, it would have been longer.  Steakhouse 55 takes the AP discount but not on the restaurant week menu, which was understandable.   They were also able to split the bill over multiple credit cards and validate parking.  Over all experience 3.5 stars rounded up.

text:
Another amazing visit to the Playground, this time for Sunday Supper and it was fantastic.  Compliments to Jason Quinn and his amazing staff.  The Playground is hands down one of my favorite restaurants in OC.  We were full upon leaving and I was so happy to have been able to share it with some of my friends.  Thanks again to everyone who attended and to the wonderful staff at the Playground.  Our Sunday Supper was $40 per person and that already includes tax + gratuity.  They brought out plate after plate of delicious and amazing food.  I couldn't have been happier with my experience and my friends echoed the same sentiments.

We had cauliflower nachos, corn, broccolini, jicama salad, artichoke risotto, blue crab, asparagus, wagyu beef buns, quail, beet salad, fried chicken, pork belly stuffed cannelloni, maple glazed pork chop, grapefruit sorbet, and sticky toffee pudding.  I may have forgotten a dish, but it was all amazing and delicious.  They will bring out more of a dish you can't get enough of but we were so ridiculously full that we cried uncle.  For Sunday Supper, it is by reservation only and the max group size is 10.  They charge your credit card in advance to secure your reservation but it is worth every penny.  Plan it a month in advance for a large party but you might be able to squeeze in a smaller group within a few weeks time frame.  It depends on how full their reservation book is.  Don't forget, there's no corkage fee and you can bring your own wine or beer to accompany your dinner.

name: Jonathan Marinaro
text:
Best Breakfast Burrito in San Jose and a damn good Warm Asian Chicken Caesar Salad!

This place is, by far, the best breakfast burrito in San Jose. The size is right, filling up most patrons. The price is right, costing about $7. The condiments are right, offering a standard red salsa along with the local favorite orange sauce. The ingredients are easy, with a combination of home fries, american cheese, your choice of meat (it's chorizo, right?) and eggs, wrapped in a warm tortilla and then pressed crispy in a plancha.

Oh, and that orange sauce. Ooooh that orange sauce. It's fresh, it's light, it's not sour like some, but it's got a hell of a kick if you want it. It's in my top three versions of San Jose's special sauce, and extra is always brought home for the occasional tamale.

That's not to say the rest of the menu is terrible. Au contraire, the Warm Asian Chicken Caesar Salad is a delightful combination of warm teriyaki-esque chicken on top of a zesty cool caesar salad. It seems weird at first, but the flavors match perfectly and it provides a filling meal for even a guy of my large size!

WHAT DID I GET:  The famed Dragon's Breath dessert.

HOW WAS IT:  The dessert itself tasted like and had the texture of bland Fruity Pebbles cereal.  There was nothing special about it; the flavor wasn't amazing, it wasn't even decent.  Having said that, the only redeeming quality of this dessert is the fact that when you bite into it, smoke comes out of your mouth and nose because of the liquid nitrogen, which is, admittedly, fun.  But ultimately, this dessert is nothing more than a novelty.

HOW MUCH DID IT COST:  $5.43.

WOULD I COME BACK/RECOMMEND THIS PLACE:  I wouldn't come back to this place, but I would recommend this place to others.  The Dragon's Breath dessert isn't amazing taste-wise, but it's worth trying at least once, in my opinion, for the fun of the smoke-blowing.

text: I lived in the area all my life and I am a bit a ways and have not visited a shopping mall in quite a while. I have to go to a workshop there recently and was shocked to see that the whole shopping mall is closing down. The worst thing about it is that Macy's is touting it's liquidation sale which will be over in about a month. Things were 25 to 30% off but when I asked if electronics in the kitchen etc. were covered by warranty or could be exchanged or returned to any other Macy's I was told that they would not do this. It makes no sense to purchase new products there and not be able to be supported at other shops in the area of which there are many and not to have the option of returning an item as normally you would and any other store. 25 to 30% off on a vita mix or other kitchen appliance is not a good deal if you're stuck with it without any recourse by Macy's. Nordstroms had moved out previously so they turned off many of the escalators so that you were forced to walk towards Macy's. It just doesn't make any sense and you still have to pay for parking and the era of brick and mortar shopping centers is clearly quickly disappearing. On principle alone I just won't support Macy's in view of how they are handling the situation of the shutdown and how upset and grouchy and rude the employees were about the whole situation. I know they are losing their jobs but you don't need to be mean and insensitive to people who are simply trying to find out how things are working during The closing of their store and the shopping center.

text:
There was a lot I loved about this place, but sadly there were things I definitely didn't.  I want to give this place 5 stars for all their sides and their amazing kettle corn, the mashed potatoes are some of the best I've had and the biscuit was rustic and crumbly. The sweet tea and horchata slushies were amazing!

Now the reason I'm only giving this place 3 stars was that even though their sides are amazing, the main dishes leave a lot to be desired.

The fried chicken that we were so hyped up about was dry and felt stale and we thought maybe it was twice fried, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, it's just that some parts were burnt and overly breaded. Others it looked like the breading had fallen off.

The steak I had looked amazing, but it was somehow dry, I tried to enjoy it with the lovely mushrooms and onions in the dijon sauce but sadly it was just too overpowering.  I could taste nothing but the mustard so I opted to eat the rest of my steak without it.

The nashville hot chicken sandwich wasn't spicy, though I'm happy to say the chicken on the sandwich wasn't dry and was enjoyable despite us missing the kick.

At their price point I was expecting to be blown away, and while their main dishes fell short on the task, I was pleasantly surprised with all the sides.

Really good chicken wings/drumsticks in countless flavors and even better fries. Their fries are beer-battered and come out with a nice crispy texture, and stay that way even after sitting at the bottom of the basket for 15 minutes. Probably the best fries I've had...
For how busy they are, service is pretty good too; haven't really had any poor experiences and the waiters are all very nice.
I'd recommend the Seoul Spicy (sweet and spicy sauce), or the O.G. (crispy and tasty), but to be honest you can't really go wrong with the any of the flavors. As a side note, when you order the "wings" they actually come with about half wings half drumsticks (so 3-4 of each for 7-8 in total), all very decently sized.
Don't do the BBS challenge unless you're crazy, it's a lot spicier than a lot of other spice challenges offered by other restaurants, and eating a pound of wings (spicy or not) in less than 5 minutes without drinking anything is a feat in itself.

name: Mark A
text:
A fish-lover’s paradise!

Blue Water Grill is worth the wait. Which is good because we waited about 45 minutes to order and find a seat. The line was a few people deep on the sidewalk at lunch time. So, if you have the time, bring a favorite human to chat with. If lacking a human, bring a book. It seems that you can also call-in order for takeout and skip the line.

As an avid saltwater fisherman, my standards for freshness and quality are pretty high. This place is simply as good as it gets. The variety of fresh caught fish is perfect for a place serving lots of fish tacos. +1 for having a selection of different groupers.

The fish tacos are a generous portion and very well balanced. The seasonings applied to fish are not overpowering like some taco places. You can taste the fish. And the fish is delicious. Two grouper tacos with added avacado filled me up and I’m a big eater.

This will be the place that I bring friends from out of town.

We have stayed at the Balboa Bay Resort for years for a yearly conference that we attend.  The amenities are wonderful, so I hate to write this review. Unfortunately an accident was made when booking and the reservation was accidentally made for a day early.  My biggest concern was that my card was charged nearly $300 for not showing up on time but it was never communicated with me when charging the card.  This was never once communicated by the front desk staff and since my receipt was emailed to me I did not become aware of this until returning from my trip.

My biggest issue is the dishonesty and negligence on the side of the hotel staff.  To charge someone $300 without their consent or knowledge seems completely egregious.  More so, the fact that I have spent the past week trying to call and get a hold of a manager is ridiculous.

This is so unfortunate because this is a yearly conference that we attend and we normally have a great experience.  But I am not sure that we will be able to return if it is at the Balboa Bay Resort.  The unprofessionalism and dishonesty is a deal breaker.

Phenomenal Ramen... if you're willing to wait! I absolutely loved Ramen Nagi, but will be waiting for the lines to die down before heading back, that said it's otherwise an absolutely top-notch ramen joint that throws down with the best of them in the area!

My wife and I had the Red King and the Original King, with both shining in their own regard. As you can easily customize everything at Ramen Nagi, I can tell you that the Original King was to the chef's specification and came out rich and delicious without being overwhelming in any sense, a great balance. I had the Red King with a little extra spice added, heavy on the tare (sauce, basically), heavy on the oil and heavy on the garlic with some added pork belly to finish it out. All in all, it had a little kick (I chose a +1 to it's 'included spice') but I'll be knocking that up a notch next time. The broths were both deep and complex, but I prefer the Red King because of just that added garlicky, misoey goodness!

We'll be back.... just probably not until the line's under 30 min.

name: Josh Fearson
text: I've been going there for about 4 years now and I love the place. The environment and the people are upbeat and always chill. Good reggie always playing, and Jay, Woo, and Pete are always there to hang out with. It's the only place where when I was done having my sushi I went bowling with the sushi chef, where else can you find that? It's like a family there and when you come you welcomed in. I love the place so much it's the last meal I have before going to Iraq, and that's been twice so far. It's the first place I stop every time I get back from Iraq. I make it a habit to go at least twice a month. I suggest getting sitting at the bar so you can chat with Jay, Woo or Pete. They will always be nice and talk to you and are happy to answer any questions you have on the sushi that is being made. I would call or arrive early on Friday and Saturday so that way you can get a seat, it's a smaller place and so it gets packed quickly. If you're waiting to get in do what me and my friends do and get a hacky sack circle going (if ya see it happening it's probably me). If you're into getting your drink on they have a selection of beer and saki, and we always do saki bombs every time I go there so ask about them. The prices are average, not insanely high like some places I've been to, I always go with the all you can eat and then get whatever else on the side and usually end up spending about $30 - $35 on myself. I highly suggest having the dragon roll, crunch roll, rainbow roll, and caterpillar roll. The sashimi has always been good, I love the salmon and tuna. I recommend huku to anyone, I've taken plenty of my friends (also marines) who have never had sushi and they love it. I can't wait until I get back from this deployment to go there again it's that good. Several of my friends, one from jersey and the other from vegas and they both said it was the best sushi they've ever had, and there freakn' sushi connoisseurs. To wrap it up the place is freakn' awesome, great food, good environment, awesome chefs and decent price.

text:
They always seem pretty busy but you can park all the way around the building so parking shouldn't be much of a problem. Now, if you're thinking about taking a romantic date there, they usually have some live band (or maybe they just happened to have birthday parties all three times I've gone) so it might be a bit noisy, but hey, less chance for that awkward silence, amirite?

Their chips and salsa are very good which I've always uses as a barometer to measure the rest of what's to come at a mexican restaurant and we weren't disappointed. It's got a good bit of chunkiness, but not overly so, and it has just a hint of that spicy kick without overwhelming your tastebuds. Their aguachile is oh so, so amazzzzing (ask for it raw; it'll still be cooked, just not boiled) and it's a perfect blend of spicy and savory. Their posole was... meh. I mean, it didn't have a bad flavor but... it actually didn't taste like posole. However, the bistec ranchero that I had was excellent and the Cadillac margarita we ordered with which to wash it all down was a great balance of strong and clean.

If you want a little quieter atmosphere,  ask to be seated to seated to the left side of the restaurant when you walk in.

They have rooms to suit any needs whether it be a tent cabin or a nice room with a bathroom, it does not disappoint. The original shack location! Tommy's is just simple, greasy, chili-smothered greatness...the stuff of hipster nightmares. Chili is standard on pretty much everything but the sodas. The way it should be. But don't let it fool you...under all that messy chili goodness is an amazing hamburger that would stand on it's own with great tasting beef and crisp, fresh veggies. That said, you'll never catch me uttering that sacrilegious phrase "hold the chili".

Beware of the countless imitators! If you don't see the shack...take it back!

We were having so much fun that another table joined us.

Jacob was our waiter and he was excellent. He was having fun with us and making the atmosphere very fun.

Now I can't write this review without discussing the food. The food was large portions and it was excellent. My girlfriend had the bacon and bleu fries. Which were topped with bacon and bleu cheese plus roasted veggies. They were delicious. I had the El Chingon Mac and cheese. This dish had carne asada steak marinated in spiced rum plus was topped cheese sauces and had other toppings. It was an amazing experience to behold. A friend of ours was with us and she got the double dipped chicken strips. There was at least 8 strips on her plate! She couldn't finish them all as there were too many. All of the food was amazing and the service was top notch!

I would recommend this place to anybody has the ambience and food is well worth it.
