text:
Updated:
I like the food here. It’s not the best pasta, but it’s enjoyable. But after our experience tonight I will not be returning.

We arrived just after 6 and were seated a little after 6:30. We managed to leave 2 hours later. It took 30 min for our ordered drinks to arrive and that was after multiple reminders. It took 45 min to get our salads. When I was given the wrong salad the waiter made a comment faulting me for it, not a simple apology and correcting his mistake. After over an hour of waiting for our food the waiter said he was going to get it right now. Then proceeded to get two other large tables food. 20 min later the manager happened to walk by and we complained and our food was there in 2 min. So it wasn't a kitchen delay. When the food arrived we immediately asked for our check which took another 30 min.

We all had other things to do than wait that long for what is normally quick food. We also had a small child, and small children really cannot wait that long.

I know there are busy times at restaurants. And I know that things happen. But it's important for the waiters to communicate delays, be reasonably apologetic when there are extreme delays. Generally when you have to get a manager involved twice they offer some sort of compensation for all your wasted time. Nothing was offered. No apologies.

This visit was a disrespectful waste of our time. I will not be returning here and definitely not with children. It is not family friendly. We weren't even given a kids menu. I had to look it up online myself...

This is most definitely an old (but great) Landmark Restaurant! I've been coming to this restaurant off and on throughout the years since I was a kid. My grandparents used to live right around the corner before they passed away. Definitely some old and great memories that I'll keep for the rest of my life!
This restaurant is most busiest and I mean packed in the mornings for a reason! In my opinion that's their specialty. They make French toast like I've never seen it before!! Its sooo big, you better make sure you come hungry and ready to eat!! You're guaranteed to leave this place full!
The only time I've been unsatisfied was the one time I brought a friend with me for his first time and we had a bad experience; though he is a hard critic. This time I tried a dinner plate for the first time, (1/2 spaghetti 1/2 ravioli). It wasn't what i was expecting but still tolerable. My friend tried to keep it basic, (he has a very hard time trusting food places he's neever been to before), so he ordered Fried Chicken! 🤔 Hhhmmm... I was really hoping he was going to like this place! I did not see this coming! 😳 As soon as he cut into the chicken, he made the most putrid face I ever seen him make in my life! 😲 Mind you, he's in his fifties, and, "in all his years" he said, "I've never seen anything like that before"! When he cut into the "fried chicken", more blood came out of it than anything we both have ever seen before! Now I don't know how you can mess that up, but I was really disappointed! My friend never took a bite and couldn't eat anything after that! A manager or maybe even the owner came out aggressively apologized & cleared our tab!
I think they did the right thing! The bad thing is, my friend will never eat here again. 😞 I will though. I just know now to stick with the breakfast.

My mom and I met some friends here for lunch recently.  It was a Saturday and the place was empty.  Not sure how they stay in business.
I guess weekday lunch and evenings are more popular.  Also, the place needs an update.  Lots of stained walls. Old artwork, old furniture.

We started with the Wor Won Ton Soup - Dumplings, snow peas, broccoli, shrimp, chicken and pork.  This was really good.  Lots of veggies and dumplings.  Light flavor.

For entrees, we had the Prawns & Honeyed Walnuts - Prawns crisp-sautéed and honeyed walnuts in a tangy sauce.  This is always my favorite.  Lots of big shrimp, tangy mayo based sauce.  Love the walnuts.

We also had the Sesame Chicken - Battered chicken breast with sesame seeds in a tangy sauce.  We like the sesame beef at the Santa Theresa location but the chicken was good.  Small pieces, easy to eat.  Sauce was a bit spicy.

And we had the Chow Mein - Choice of pork, chicken or beef with stir-fried noodles.  We did the meat combo.  Lots of big pieces of meat, not too many veggies, flavorful sauce.

Nice lunch in an empty restaurant.

name: Jeanne Lam
text:
I haven't been back to Marica for years and I have no idea why it took me so long to return but boy have I been missing out!

It's hard to come across fine dining quality food that's reasonably priced, in a casual, yet intimate environment in the heart of Rockridge. This restaurant is certainly a gem.

Last night, I was in a dinner party of 12 and we had a feast! I was drooling over the entire menu which caused me to be pretty indecisive, but I buckled down and ordered the signature twice cooked Maine lobster claw and tail. The pre-fixe menu with the Canadian salmon was a close call because it was such a deal for $32! But then again, I can say that about the filet mignon, seafood stew, or the rack of lamb I was torn between. See, very tough decisions to be made here. I WANT IT ALL!

Thank you Calvin for the amazing hospitality! We all had a wonderful time dining at Marica's and plan to return very soon!

What I ordered:

COCKTAILS
- Kentucky Sidecar ($9) - Delicious! It was like a dessert in itself and I drank it way too fast and had to go back to my boozier options.
- Makers Manhattan ($8) - Solid. And where the hell am I going to score a decent manhattan for this price?

APPETIZER
- Prince Edward Island Mussels, Pernod shallot butter sauce ($12) - the mussels were nice and plump and I wanted to soak all the broth up with my bread.

ENTREE (highly recommended)
- Signature twice cooked Maine lobster claw and tail, lobster sauce, pancetta, corn risotto (MP $42) - My plate was a perfect masterpiece and the lobster and everything else was delicious. It came in 4 big juicy pieces and paired perfectly with the creamy corn risotto. If I could lick the plate clean I would.

DESSERT (not overly sweet, yay!)
- Dark chocolate souffle with vanilla ice cream ($12) - this required 30 min prep time but it was absolutely worth it and I love how it was hot and fluffy.
- Grand Marnier creme brulee ($8) - sweet, creamy and refreshing because it was topped with fresh blueberries.

Parking: Effortless. Look for residential or free meter parking after 6pm right in front of the restaurant.

name: Roy Chi
text:
When it comes to ramen, I'm definitely a broth guy. Delicious ingredients are great, but the broth is what really makes ramen pop. The broth at Ramen Dojo is just okay -- it has a faint pork bone flavor, mixed with tons of additional oil that makes every bite way too salty and way too oily (and not natural pork bone oil like it's supposed to have). Also, there's way too little broth in each bowl.

I will give it credit for its ingredients, though. The ramen noodles were phenomenal -- a perfect al dente. The other ingredients (pork slices, pork belly) were tender as hell. I didn't really understand their use of quail egg (it just didn't feel significant at all), so I would definitely add the regular boiled egg if I ever go back.

The chicken wings were actually pretty good too. Nicely fried and very moist inside.

The service was pretty bad, but I don't really care about service that much anyway so it's fine. They rushed us in, rushed us out (we got our check before we took our second bite) like we were intruding on their home. This would be fine if the food really was THAT good, but it's not, so then it just seems a bit arrogant.

Not sure exactly what everyone sees in Ramen Dojo, because I think it's pretty mediocre, especially for the long wait. It's DEFINITELY better than Santa Ramen and most ramen joints in SF (San Francisco is the absolute worst city for ramen, by the way), but Ramen Dojo definitely needs to work on its broth in order to compete with the best.

I would probably consider coming back if there was no wait, but since there always is, it really isn't worth it.

name: Marcella Nichols Eastin
text:
We came to visit for the same reason as a lot of folks- we heard it was a frequent dining destination for Walt Disney.  The food was excellent.  We started with the shrimp cocktail (the sauce was delicious, and I personally detest cocktail sauce) and a caesar salad.  I had a small bowl of macaroni and cheese as my main entree, which was the perfect amount of food.  My husband ordered the prime rib, which was pretty good but not outstanding compared to other restaurants.

However, the service here is the only thing holding it back from a full 4 or 5 star rating.  Perhaps stereotypically of LA, the service was quite curt and dismissive.  Some orders were forgotten when the dishes arrived, and my husband's salad came out with the wrong dressing.  We had to ask for drink refills multiple times. Our waiter had a habit of racing past our table with a quick glance, barely stopping to listen to our requests or see if we had any issues.  He literally walked away even as a member of our party asked for a drink refill, after another member had reminded him of a missing order.  He seemed annoyed with us, even though we were calm about the issues.  We are easy customers, and never make a fuss, so the fact that we had to ask for so much says a lot.  Due to the service we experienced, we likely would not return or recommend it to others.

My previous review is below. I decided to give Summit House another try, but in person. Let me tell you I am so glad I did. We ordered the exact same food to make a fair assessment and everything was so good. We were able to enjoy drinks this time and they were tasty as well as strong. (My previous review)
Please note I placed an order for pickup during COVID-19 so I cannot speak to the quality or flavor of the food when ordered in the restaurant.

I placed an order for my anniversary dinner after reading reviews online. I ordered the following:

Lobster bisque
House salad
Prime Rib - with creamed corn and creamed spinach
Filet Mignon- with creamed corn and mashed potatoes
Chocolate torte
Bread pudding

All around the food was very bland. The salad was not worth ordering at all. The filet mignon was great quality meat and was cooked to perfection but was not very flavorful. The mashed potatoes again were very bland. The creamed corn was surprisingly delicious. The bread pudding (they give it to you cold with at home heating instructions) was quite dry, tasted a bit stale and again was otherwise bland.

My fiancé loved the lobster bisque, prime rib and the chocolate torte. Neither of us cares for creamed spinach so I do not feel it fair to provide an opinion on that.

All in all for the price point, Summit House take out falls FAR short of quality food.

The CABEZA is tender, so flavorful and even more delicious. Cabeza means cow head. I know, it doesn't sound very good but forget what it means and just order this. You won't regret it.

The GOAT, however, was a bit too dry for me. Still flavorful but required a lot of chewing.

The line can extend down the aisle but know that you can easily cut everyone by walking up to an available server to order. They don't discriminate on line cutting and just serve whoever shows up.

name: Leslie Liu
text:
Our family went for my daughter's birthday; she wanted sushi and we thought we'd upgrade from our usual place. We regretted it. I'm not sure if it was because we had kids (7 and 4), but the service was pretty bad and the food didn't make up for it.

We were seated at the table closest to the entrance, which was ok, but I wondered if it was because we were a family and not the usual corporate crowd on a weekday night. The server was cold (my daughter really wanted to tell someone it was her birthday, but she wasn't friendly enough for us to offer that at any point in our interactions); I had to ask twice for hot tea; when we were told they were sold out of an appetizer, I asked for the menu to see if I might order something else, but it was never brought; and when our items were placed on the table the server pushed some appetizer plates rather abruptly aside with the incoming plates. And oddly, the server didn't seem very familiar with sushi (I asked if they served inari sushi and she responded "what is that?")

Between that, and the appetizers being quite disappointing, we won't be back. We ordered the "Kushiyaki Mori," described as rib eye beef and chicken skewers "served with a hibachi grill at your table." The rib eye was overcooked and hard to chew, and it was not served with a hibachi grill at the table; we didn't get an explanation as to why. We thought the kids would enjoy that part so that's why we ordered it -- I saw another table using a mini grill.

The highlight was the nigiri sushi -- quality was a notch better than the usual places -- and the rolls we tried were also quite good.

text:
We have a goal: visiting 1-2 Michelin rated restaurants a year. Sometimes we meet our goal and sometimes we don't. Hubs had a birthday, it was the perfect excuse to go grab dinner at a special restaurant. Often with these restaurants you are having an experience, sometimes it's one that you treasure but don't necessarily need to repeat, sometimes it's one that you treasure, and would gladly repeat. Boulevard offered us an experience we will happily repeat.

We thought (eeeeek... sorry Boulevard) that it might be stuffy and over-rated. We were wrong, so wrong. Boulevard delivered. The interior is beautiful, in a way it's like a stage set, but a real-life working one. I like the open kitchen concept, it's nice to see the kitchen working away. Another plus, the chef de cuisine and the chef/owner are women, and there were women in the kitchen. Our server was very professional, but without pretension. She was warm and friendly, and offered fantastic recommendations upon request (sorry I don't have her name, she was young blond, awesome, working near the kitchen on Friday 7/11/14). And then there was the food. The food was so very good.

We had:

Scallops: 5/5 stars
Delicious, perfectly cooked, perfectly seasoned. As the offerings in the restaurant are seasonal, the accompaniments will change, but the scallops I will still be perfect.

Corn Ravioli with truffles: 4/5
The corn was wonderful, the ravioli dough was a little too much.

Pork Chop: 5/5
This was the best pork chop I have ever eaten. Ever. Perfectly cooked, we ate every last bite. It was divine.

Sea Bass 5/5
Poor sea bass. You were excellent, but you had to go up against the pork chop. Honestly, the sea bass was wonderful, that pork chop was just. so. good.

Butterscotch Pudding 5/5
Delicious. If I ordered it again, I'd hold the chocolate.

Cheese Plate 5/5
Hubs ordered The Bomb and something else. They were both wonderful.

Thank you Boulevard for such a spectacular meal.

Don't get me wrong, there are plenty of amazing restaurants in the bay area that are not rated which are amazing and we love them too.  It's fun to get out every now and then to see what all the fuss is about. So far we've been to six Michelin rated restaurants. Boulevard is one of two rated restaurants that we would go back to (Aziza is the other).  The whole experience was wonderful.

text:
Obviously, the fact that this place is really wonderful is no secret.

Atmosphere. It's cozy. Tiny-cozy. Cozy-tiny. Really best for 2 people. You can sit at the counter and watch the restaurant work, your server making his way past the cooks, your cooks making your delicious meal. Or you can sit at the table outside, or the nook inside. But really the counter is where it's at.

Service. I love our server (we're usually there for lunch). He's always perfect. Not too friendly, or un-friendly, just a great server who knows his craft. We've been for dinner, and while I love the fella at lunch, he's only one notch above the lovely fella at night.

name: Jonathan Marinaro
text:
An interesting take on American Contemporary, Willard Hicks is notable for its steaks, cocktails and warm vibe.

The Ginger-Ponzu Ribeye, garnished with shittake mushrooms and onion strings stole the show, as the marinade/glaze complimented the beef well. While not as tender as a traditional Ribeye, the wood grilling was easily tasted through the ponzu, and was a delicious choice altogether.

The sides included a Pancetta Mac and Cheese, which was tasty but sadly had too much pancetta. While I normally would enjoy it, it made the dish extremely salty and tasted more like a liquid cheese covered pancetta than any variation including macaroni. The second side were the fries, which included about ten very large steak-cut potatoes with a nice and unusual seasoning and sides of ketchup and a garlic remoulade. These were very tasty and the only change I'd make would be to make them a more manageable size to increase the number but keep the portion.

name: Roy Chi
text:
*2.5 stars*

Vietnamese fast food with Chipotle-style ordering process? Sounded interesting, but ended up being nothing special. You can find better Vietnamese food anywhere in the Tenderloin, for much cheaper. The appeal of Freshroll is the customization of your meal, but that can only get you so far.

I got the Lemongrass Pork Vermicelli Noodle Bowl with Peanut Sauce. It was just okay. The lemongrass pork was a little tough and overcooked, but had a good lemongrass flavor to it. The vermicelli here is a bit thicker than it should be, which basically means that you need much more sauce to compensate for the natural blandness of plain vermicelli. I added the fried scallion, which definitely improved the overall taste of the bowl with a nice crispy texture.

Freshroll is watered-down, generic Vietnamese food. If I'm basing it solely on the Vietnamese flavor, Freshroll just doesn't cut it. Great idea and layout, but boring and mediocre Vietnamese flavor.

text:

This building has a lower level and an upper level.
Now onto the food and service for Half Door Brewing, The service was fantastic, and everybody had a welcoming personality to them. Beer flights are offered in sizes of four, five, and six beers. We had a six beer flight, and my favorites were the sour and the buzz lite. The food had an Irish appeal to it and offered things from fish and chips to Bangers n Mash. My girlfriend had the fish and chips while I had the bangers and mash. The fish and chips were cooked to perfection, and the fries had a salt and vinegar taste to them. They were excellent. I ordered the bangers and mash and replaced the mash with brussel sprouts. It was all covered in an onion ale gravy. Bangers are another name for sausage, and these sausages were imported from Ireland. The dish was great. I would recommend this place to anybody looking for a friendly atmosphere to unwind and enjoy great food with an excellent selection of beer or cocktails.

text:
Ramen in SF sucks. Bad. I've been to countless ramen joints in SF and they've all been meh (especially the ones in Japantown). Even Katana-ya's quality has deteriorated over the years. In fact, the best ramen in SF isn't even from a ramen restaurant, but rather an izakaya (Izakaya Sozai).

That's why I wasn't really expecting much from Kirimachi Ramen. Maybe my low expectations helped its case, but I was actually pleasantly surprised by how good the ramen is here. Don't get me wrong, it's nothing like the ramen in the Pennisula (e.g., Ramen Dojo) or the South Bay (e.g., Orenchi), but within the borders of San Francisco, it's pretty good.

The Tonkatsu Ramen had a good pork bone flavor. I wish the broth was a bit more piping-hot and I wish the noodles were a bit more al dente, but it was a good bowl of ramen nonetheless. They included shredded pork rather than pork slices, which is kind of weird, but the pork is definitely tender. The soft-boiled egg had the perfect gooey yolk.

Kirimachi should definitely be open later in the night, since the location is perfect for afterhours grubbing in the North Beach area. I mean, what better than a nice bowl of ramen for after getting dirty lapdances from Chlamydia-infested strippers or dancing all night at ghetto AZN clubs?

text: Went to dinner for 2018 New years eve and it was very nice but, it was FANTASTIC for folks in their 60's and up who packed house for NYE! They were all having a really GREAT TIME! I would highly recommend this place for anyone of that age group who's looking for a fun night out on the town. Its a well preserved time capsule that captures a vibe of an era gone by! This historic landmark is a must if your visiting Santa Cruz and looking for a lovely place to eat! Parking is a top of the hill up above the restaurant and to get dowm to it, You can either take the stairs that descend into a beautifully manicured outdoor forest like green house garden or you can opt to take the fully functioning historic cable trolley car that seats four. The vibe is positive and Zen like. And most important, The food is good! For my appetizer, I had the battered (famous for the area) artichokes, For dinner I ordered a hand tossed pizza with broccoli  minced garlic fresh tomatoes fresh basil minus the cheese drizzled with olive oil! Topped off with not one but two Guava Martini's! I wont be coming back for New Years Eve! But i will definitely be back! xo

text:
Some friends were in from out of town and they wanted to go to Smoking Pig for lunch.  We typically go to the 4th Street location but decided to try this new location on Newhall this time around.  The place is quite larger with a full bar and lots of TVs to watch sports.  Our waitress was attentive, took orders quickly and refilled drinks often.

I got the pulled pork w/ cole slaw & french fries. This was so good.
I added in their mustard based sauce which I love.  Fries were crispy outside and soft inside.  Cole slaw was vinegar-forward and not too creamy.

One friend got fatty brisket with macaroni & cheese. One friend ordered 4 lollipop chicken and a side of mac and cheese. The last friend ordered the 3-meat combo with burnt ends, ribs, and chicken. He also upgraded his side to the Brunswick Stew.  Everyone loved their food.

This location is definitely a lot nicer than the 4th Street location.  Good food and service.  And seems like a great place to watch a game.

Maybe a little too warm (I run hot, so I was really warm, but I heard someone at the table next to me comment about how hot he was).

We ordered:
Stuffed Falafel: AMAZING (one of the best falafels I have ever had)
Shish Taouk (grilled chicken skewers, onion, pepper, rice and hummus): AMAZING (will definitely order again)

text:
I came here for my anniversary dinner and had a lovely and intimate dinner. It was my first time here and it was busy all night. This is not a restaurant that is good for groups.

What we ordered:

Antipasto - Mixed antipasto platter, imported Prosciutto crudo, salamino calabrese, salame toscano, two milk Robiola, Gorgonzola, fruits, honey, crostini, nuts. This was beautifully plated and I loved the combo of the meats, fruit, various cheese and nuts.

Casoncelli - My Mom's lombardian-style stuffed pasta with beef, prosciutto, pork shoulder, imported smoked pancetta ,sage brown butter. I thought this was okay. I don't have stuffed pasta often and was underwhelmed. I felt like the stuffing was dry and the texture of my pasta was hard and chewy.

Maybe I should have went with another pasta. I was also considering the Agnolotti Di Lidia but our server mentioned it was similar to the Casoncelli but with a different and richer sauce. Since my bf doesn't really care for pasta I opted for the less rich option.

Anatra: Seared duck Breast, Sautéed red Treviso, honey, pink peppercorn, smoked cipolline, balsamico Giusti. My favorite dish of the night! I'm a fan of caramelized onions and duck breast. The meat was tender and seared to perfection. It was a nice medium rare, just the way I like it.

Panna Cotta - A nice refreshing end to the night topped with a raspberry sauce. They also comped this because they forgot we were celebrating a special occasion and didn't dress up our dessert. Although I would prefer my Instagram worthy picture, I thought this was a nice gesture.

Overall, I had a pretty positive experience and would like to come back to try the other pasta and other items.

name: Roy Chi
text:
Hands-down one of the very best restaurants in SF. I come here maybe once every month or two, and I've never been disappointed.

The food is excellent -- tender prime rib, uniquely-delicious salad, and even the block of free bread was good. If you're lucky enough to get a cornbread that they make every 30 minutes or so, those are awesome. And if you're not full after your meal, they give you a second serving of a thin slice of prime rib and sides!

The service was impeccable. Last time I went, we waited about 30 minutes (which is actually pretty good considering how packed the place was) and the hostess offered us a free dessert for waiting. And even though we were insanely full, obviously we took her up on the offer and we got a slice of their cheesecake.

Honestly, it was probably the best cheesecake I've ever had. Much better than Cheesecake Factory or any other bakeries I've ever been to -- they could probably create a sister restaurant that revolved solely around their cheesecake. And it's crazy that I'm saying this because I was so full at the time that any thought of food made me sick -- and I still thought this cheesecake was the best I've ever tried.

Now unbuckle that belt, wipe the horseradish off your face, and stop talking about how starting tomorrow you're going to go on a salad-only diet. You have the rest of your life to skip dessert. Don't do it now. You are getting the cheesecake.

Anyways, I love this place!

text:
VIDUNDERLIGE CHEESECAKE OG MORGENMAD I SAN DIEGO

Den meget populære amerikanske kæde Cheesecake Factory tilbyder både dessert, morgenmad og aftensmad til sine kunder.

Vi besøgte afdelingen i San Diego for at spise morgenmad samt deres berømte cheesecake.

Servicen og betjeningen er meget god, hvor vi fik en tjener til at servere for os under hele opholdet.

Vi valgte at prøve deres omelet til morgenmad og som dessert endte valget på gulerodskage.

Priserne er rimelige. Omeletten koster 14,95 USD (94 DKK), mens gulerodskagen koster 9,95 USD (62 DKK). Det skal dog understreges at der bør pålægges drikkepenge til disse priser.

Cheesecake Factory er et meget anbefalingsværdigt spisested, der er tæt på at være enestående. Selvom de mest er kendt for deres lækre cheesecake-udvalg, smager deres morgenmad også meget godt. Vi kunne især lide deres mørke brød, som blev serveret flere gange. Det er absolut et sted man skal besøge, når man er i Californien.

text:
Brenda's is THE brunch location in downtown San Francisco. Additionally, since the recent renovation the decor is greatly improved and the once horrific lines (sometimes close to a 2hr wait) are dramatically reduced.

Things not to miss: the grillades and gravy. The biscuits are the best I've had in the bay area and are always accompanied by amazing homemade jams. Finally, why mostly everyone comes... the beignets! If you want light, fluffy, and sugary beignets, I actually prefer Just For You cafe, but if you want authentic french beignets, Brenda's is for you. The two standouts to me are the chocolate beignet which is made with Ghirardelli semi-sweet chocolate, and the savory crawfish beignet, though I would recommend the full flight of four beignets (which also includes classic sugar coated and a cinnamon/apple filled beignet.)

We were there when they were having a photography take some pictures of their dishes so we were looking at what to get. My friend and I spotted a large dish of Atomic Pasta with chicken breast that looked pretty awesome. We decided to share it (and we didn't even finish it--it was THAT big). The pasta itself is homemade and rather sticks together a bit. It was like thick fettucine with an al dente bite to it. The sauce strongly tasted of bell peppers and spices but very little salt. I think this place is pretty health-conscious because the chicken was not salted at all. Overall, the dish looked better than it tasted but once you put some salt and parmesan cheese over it, it was redeemed. I will come back to try more dishes. Also, parking is a bit difficult since they have limited spots in their back parking lot but there are some meter spots across the street, by the Blue Bus station.

text:
The locals flock come here so they say.  And it is busy. It is very small and mostly counter seating only, with  two tables that are available for seating two or more guests.  Count on waiting if you come late, they open early at 5 am. Monday is farmer's market day at the park a few yards away, an excellent way to eat organic fruits and veggies in season, with free samples.  You can park in the park if street parking is full, or in the Doctor's office next door, behind their building on the weekends they are not open.
The decor in this place is old and has probably been unchanged since it opened pictures of vintage cars, muscle cars, and semi truck cab.  Pretty country curtains and a there is a quaint antique red cash register at the till, my wife pointed out the details.

The kitchen is only a few feet from counter seating. Can't say the food was bad but not great either as some reviewers seem to hint. Tried a veggie omelet it had sliced avocado on top, it was okay nothing to write home about, and went for the biscuit and gravy instead of toast, because of good reviews about it.  We thought the biscuit itself was good, melt in your mouth and the bottom was not hard, but the gravy although it had taste could use some improvement, either a bit more sausage or a pinch more nutmeg per my wife.  It had a creamy texture and not bad at all.  My wife had the corned beef hash with country fried potatoes, and biscuit and gravy also as a sub for toast.  As she says, all were just okay.  The corned beef hash flattened and dry, came like two small patties. Country fried potatoes were crispy outside and soft inside but could use a few chopped fresh onions and chopped bell peppers and diced tomatoes, and seasonings. CASH only by the way, so you know. A little hole in the wall with an "A" rating on the window and they serve breakfast  the old fashioned way, not sure if they serve lunch too. A gem in the city of Bellflower that is worth the visit if you are looking for nostalgia and close to home made feel.  The Wait Staff don't recall her name was nice and friendly. No hype.

We stopped in here after a movie. It is conveniently located from the Regal movie theater on Jamacha. It is an Irish pub, so I expected for it to have an Irish theme and to promote Guinness beer. It did not disappoint. It had a very Irish theme and supported Ireland in ways that it wasn't overbearing. Hooleys had a friendly, quiet, and cozy atmosphere. Hooleys has two separate sections one was a bar, and the other was a grill/restaurant section.
The food and service are excellent! The wait time for the food was concise as my girlfriend barely had time to finish her soup before our food arrived. I had the Hooleys half and half pub burger. This burger is half ground corned beef, and half ground beef served with steak fries and whole grain dijon mustard. Be forewarned, the side items for the burger were a la carte and did cause an upcharge. Which is fine for me, but it does deserve a warning for future guests. My girlfriend has the shrimp and chips. The shrimp were massive! There were at least eight large pieces of shrimp and a lot of fries.
Would I recommend this place? Yes! I will be back after my next movie.

Almost perfect.

Strengths:
- Outstanding raw bar (and liquor bar).
- Good menu of spirits and well made cocktails (recommend mojito)
- Such great bar seats. Super comfy. Probably the best I’ve experienced.
- superb staff and service. Attentive, knowledgeable, and friendly
- Deep menu with lots of options for anyone. It was hard to pick
- If you want something simple, get the delicious tuna melt

Weaknesses
(For perspective, I spent two years searching for the best fish sandwich in Florida. This was my first CA fish sandwich after moving here)
- The blackened seabass sandwich had a great portion of fish and good slaw. The problem was the overly soft potato roll. It disintegrated almost immediately. Any high quality fish sandwich should be served on a hearty roll like ciabatta or even sourdough.
- The fries were mediocre. Not crispy and almost a little undercooked.

[I know - people don’t come here for sandwiches. It’s the full menu and raw bar that stand out. But this was my experience on this visit. Willing to try again and definitely would recommend]

text: Great for a big group. Celebrated three birthdays here and it was a nice farm to table experience. No parts of the hog go wasted but my favorite dish happened to be the southern bird, their take on southern fried chicken. But the executive plate also shined featuring smoked andouille, Mexican chorizo, and traditional Austrian kasekrainer. Don't forget the warm Bavarian style pretzel served with spicy hot mustard was a perfect pairing to the sausage. For appetizer the meatballs was a mix of ground pork shoulder with pine nuts, paini and grana and made a good start with the meal. Spicy pork cracklins were nice and crispy and even took some to go. Portions are big, hearty and satisfying. Large beer selection on tap and communal tables give it that German Oktoberfest feel. I highly recommend this spot for any occasion especially if you are hankering for some pork.

name: Jennifer Hunker
text:
They've really fixed this place up!

WHAT IT IS
I've only been to this Marie Calendars, so I'm not sure what the standard layout of their restaurants are. This one has you enter into a large lobby where you'll see the to-go counter/pie area to your left. The bar is on the west side of the building and the dining room is on the east. I prefer this because it keeps the bar noise *AWAY* from the diners, making the dining room a much more tranquil place. This is also the first time I've seen a salad bar in years.

WHAT YOU SHOULD ORDER
Pot pies and pie.

AMBIANCE
4 stars
It's dated, but I rather like it. I've never been opposed to booths and partitions in the dining room--it keeps the noise level down! The carpets are really old and there are a few upgrades they could make to make this place look nicer, but I'd be heartbroken if they ripped down all the walls to follow the "open concept" fad. This is one of the only restaurants in the area where I can go with my husband during the dinner hour with a relative assurance that our dinner will be somewhat peaceful. I'll trade modernity for peace any day of the week.

FOOD AND DRINKS
5 Stars
Their pies are fantastic, but that goes without saying. Actually, everything here has been pretty good. The service is fast, and their potpies are a perfect way to warm up your belly on a cold and drizzly afternoon. This isn't gourmet level or anything crazy or groundbreaking, but it isn't trying to be. It's just trying to give us good, rustic, comfort food, which I want sometimes. On that level, it succeeds with flying colors.

NICE SURPRISES
Free CORN BREAD!

OVERALL
A nice place if you want some comfort food.

name: Roy Chi
text:
Okay, I've never been to Jiro's restaurant in Tokyo, but I imagine that it must be REALLY similar to Ohshima.

Now, I must admit that I was pretty damn skeptical about Ohshima. The city of Orange doesn't really strike me as a city that knows its cuisine, and especially because Ohshima is unfortunately placed in a barren strip mall next to a ghetto tropical fish store. The exterior doesn't really whet the appetite.

And then you walk in and it's like you're transported to one of the sushi joints along the outer rim of the Tsukiji fish market in Tokyo, serving the freshest sushi ever available. I can honestly say that Ohshima is my favorite sushi restaurant that I've tried outside of Japan, and I've tried a ton all over LA, SF, and NYC. Granted I've never had Urasawa, but let's keep this discussion to sushi restaurants that are within the reasonable means of someone who is not ultra-wealthy.

------------------------
FOOD:

I'll make this simple. We sat at the sushi bar and had:

Omakase: (Black Cod, Cherry Salmon, Amberjack, Spanish Mackerel, Scallop, Baby Bluefin Tuna, Hamachi)

Other nigiri: Amaebi, Uni, Toro, Seared Kobe Beef

Hot dishes: Stewed Pork Knee, Uni Spaghetti, Miso Cod

EVERYTHING was delicious -- there wasn't one piece of sushi or one hot dish that disappointed whatsoever. If I had to choose my favorites of the night, though, it'd be:

- Toro Nigiri = One of the best pieces of toro I've ever had
- Seared Kobe Beef Nigiri = Perfectly torched, extremely fatty and tender
- Black Cod Nigiri = Delicious as hell
- Cherry Salmon = Incredibly tender but with a bit of firmness that was perfect
- Uni Spaghetti = Probably the best thing in the world for uni lovers

The one disappointment was that they ran out of Ankimo (Monkfish liver) that night, which is one of my favorite dishes. I will definitely need to come back to try this.

------------------------

Ohshima has everything I look for in a sushi restaurant:
- NO ROLLS!! A sign of fresh fish that can't be masked by eel sauce and mayo.
- No soy sauce (everything is perfectly seasoned)
- REAL wasabi (not the fake green-dyed horseradish paste at 99% of sushi joints)
- And of course, unbelievably fresh fish that won't break the bank

Also, make sure you sit at the sushi bar for the true experience. The chefs will schedule out the pieces of sushi perfectly.

This is the real deal. Whenever I come back to Southern California and I'm eating sushi, Ohshima will be the only place I go.

text:
Excellent Italian restaurant, part of the lovely Casa Madona Hotel.  We ended up eating here 3 times during our 3 day stay, because it was so good.  I had the penne with Calabrian chili sausage, broccoli di ciccio, red onion, and pecorino, which was absolutely delicious.  The bucatini alla amatriciana was also really good -- noodles were cooked perfectly.  My wife had the anatra salad with confit duck leg twice -- I tried it, and the duck was done perfectly!  The salad also had amazing peaches.  Our daughter had a giant pizza from the kid's menu (that honestly would've been filling for a big guy).  Dessert was warm bittersweet chocolate cake
with vanilla gelato (awesome) and tiramisu (nicely done, not overly sweet or boozy).  For breakfast, we had tasty breakfast sandwiches, and our daughter had a great waffle with super-fresh strawberries and blueberries.

Service was impeccable and friendly.  Dining was entirely outdoors, with adequate spacing.  This is definitely a great place to have any meal while visiting Sausalito!

I came in with a friend after seeing some good reviews for Cafe Tropical. The first  thing I noticed when I walked in is that the whole restaurant smells like a dirty restroom. I am usually not the one to be bothered by smell but it smells so bad inside that I had to go outside.

They have cakes, cookies and pastries along with sandwiches. I had the carrot cake while my friend had the dark chocolate cake. Both weren't very moist and way too sweet. The frosting on my carrot cake isn't cream cheese frosting so the whole thing didn't have a good balance of flavor.

My friend got the apple and blueberry turnovers to-go. The crust is way too thick and chewy. Turnovers should be flaky but these are more doughy. The filling is meager.

The service wasn't great. They aren't very friendly. My friend had to ask for her to-go pastries that she already paid for and the girl was attitudy asking "oh you want them?". Of course she wants them otherwise she wouldn't have ordered and paid for them.

With so many great bakeries around LA, I will be skipping this place next time.

name: Edward Burgess
text:
This place is great. The food is fresh, and if you're familiar with how Mongolian BBQ works, you understand the major plot points and can skip ahead.

For those of you uninitiated to the world of MBBQ, it works this way. Grab a bowl, fill it with all your favorite ingredients (for me this usually includes the following: spinach, noodles, chicken, broccoli, pineapple, garlic, etc) and then pour sauces on top - 10 different kinds are available and I encourage you to use many of them in sufficient amount. I strongly recommend no less then 10 ladles.

Next, you hand it to the chef that cooks it up for you. Didn't get the sauce combination correct? No worries! This place is all you can eat. So go back and do another bowl. Yummy!

Also, extremely fresh and satisfying, cause you only put in what you like.

Anyway, quiet and quaint place with a friendly staff and a nice selection of ingredients to add to your bowl.

name: Chantel Menzie-Williams
text:
Phenomenal food!
I was unaware to go to the counter to order; in my defense, I came in through the back, it was crowded, and even after I was told, I had to search for the counter. I was informed by a very enthusiastic patron that it was Taco Tuesday. They have an electronic board that flashes food porn and descriptions; I glanced up, saw Taco Tuesday, but it changed before I could read the rest and didn't scroll back while I was in line. I ordered two tacos and asked for chips and salsa (felt like the right thing to do). The cashier mumbled something, the price was a little higher than I expected, I paid and asked for the receipt. He stared at me, I didn't want to hold up the line and figured maybe the receipt came as they delivered the food to make sure they had everything, and I sat down.
My two tacos came and I reminded the server about my chips and salsa. My friend moved hers over to share. Another friend's food came and again I asked for my chips and salsa.... Never received.
The tacos were as appealing on the plate as the pictures on the screen, and my taste buds were not disappointed. I never got MY chips and salsa. I saw a menu later and realized what the cashier was mumbling was an item on the regular menu that had the two tacos.... And the price fit... But I didn't get the sides the menu had. Live and learn. I do plan to go again, hopefully not at a busy time, and pay attention to what I am ordering, paying for, and receiving. All the food I sampled was worth giving this place a second chance.

Sip hot cider outside on brisk winters day, listen to the country music surrounding you while you shop authentic Indian jewelery, amd leather goods.  Be captivated by this cottage of a town while it wraps you with it's charming people and livestock all around you.  The petting zoo for the kids I very entertaining while the animals climb over one another for a bite of feed from their little hands.  Fun pony rides make for big smiles too!

Alfredo's! A classic family owned, family style Italian restaurant that has been a jewel in the heart of San Bernardino for over 30 years...

I personally have ate at this location for 30 years... They have all of the feel good dishes you could ask for... from deep dish lasagna, stuffed pasta shells, fettuccine alfredo, chicken parmagian, spaghetti and meatballs and of course... Pizza!

The staff is courteous and prompt. The restaurant is well maintained and very clean. They get busy every night of the week, so plan accordingly. If you want to stop by for a quick lunch, try the Peasant Special...it consists of a split French bread loaf with sauce and melted cheese, top it off with a salad and you're good to go!

Come hungry and leave happy... That's the Alfredo's way.

The breakfast sandwiches are good, my personal favorite is the ham and cheese. The pastries are good. They are better in the morning because they are fresh. The ice tea's are great, my favorite is the ice green tea unsweetened. I would also suggest any of the tea's with half lemonade.  My all time favorite drink there is a venti double blended caramel frappuccino with nothing on top. It's a great drink on a hot day. Treat yourself to a frappuccino today.

The rice has lots of saffron that really improves the flavor. Rather low price for what you get. Calling ahead for reservation is recommended because it's a small restaurant. The falafel was not overcooked but very soft with lots of flavor. Baklava was not too sweet and covered with walnuts ( both good things). I will definitely return. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!

name: Russell Towne
text:
Everything I've ever gotten here was a delight. I work nearby, so it's easily accessible. Parking in the area can be a bit tricky, but it's near a neighborhood with free parking if you're ok with a short walk.
It's a bakery and a restaurant.  No reservations, as it's a counter walk-up. and as fro seating, although there's a good number of tables inside and out, it's usually pretty packed and hard to get a spot,   There are two lines: one for the restaurant, and one for the bakery.  Both lines are usually long, but Porto's has a large staff, so the actual wait time doesn't seem long. Also periodically a member of the staff will walk around the lines with samples of something delicious.  If you're in the area, definitely check it out. (There's also one in Glendale--the original location)

name: Jose Aleman
text:
There is nothing at Porto's that is subpar.  The potato balls and savory baked treats are delicious.  The sandwiches are also good, but I have only had the media noche and cuban (essentially the same sandwich just on different bread).   The salads are big and the drinks are fresh made.

If you want to place a big order, call it in at least a day in advance and not only will you save money (about half price vs a walk in order), but you can skip the HUGE line and go to the pickup line.

The food was ok nothing really extraordinary the calamari appetizer was disappointing it had an interesting texture the sweat potatoe fries where good. The main course consisted of the shrimp scampi with a mango salsa and mozembique rice it was done nicely just not impressed by it.  The seafood Curry was also done nicely again not impressed by it. The other guests ordered the peri peri chicken pops the presentation was really nice they enjoyed it. Seafood platter for 2 was enough for 2 or 3 people they also did not enjoy the calamari and the other seafood was ok. The drinks where nice with lots of variety I enjoyed the mozembique mojito nice berry sweetness to it the Oaxaca mule was interesting made with tequila nice twist to it. The other guest enjoyed the spicy watermelon drink it does have a spicy kick to it. The atmosphere is really nice the live band was good. They played a nice variety of classic to current hits with a reggae twist to them.

Great spot to grab a bite and some beers if you're exploring the rails of So Cal. They have a great po' boy sandwich and a decent selection of beer.

Oyster bar is located inside the Anaheim Regional Transportation Intermodal Center, which is just a fancy way of saying train station. The building itself is a strange and unique structure and worth the time to investigate. Plenty of info online about this building for the geeks that are into that.

This was our starting point for a day trip down to San Juan Capistrano. This station is serviced by Metrolink and Amtrack. Metrolink offers great weekend rates, $10 for all you can ride, but is limited on the number of stops and does not run late. Amtrak is more expensive, but has a lot more stops, runs way later, and sells booze on the train so the party doesn't have to stop when you're rolling.

text:
Huge casino two levels.
Ample parking. You get some nice perks by joining club Serrano depending upon your tier  level you get free hotel  room stay and other plusses like an ambassador who welcomes you and can offer you a cappuccino or Figi water or Voss water.
A host is assigned to you and this person can also make your trip worth while by adding points to your card for the giftshop or adding points to be redeemed like food credits at the Bear Springs Hotel. It is accessible by car at a short distance less than 10 minutes away. There is no shuttle at the moment but that is also a nice feature. It was a really great place to stay and it comes with a great Bistro. The bistro food is very good. Loved the seafood omelet and the ribeye steak. Also the French vinegarette on the side salad which was elevated by the crunchiness of the deep fried carrot strips. Like eating it with bacon but healthier.

Chingon a George Lopez restaurant within the casino, offering Mexican fares. They have a very good pork prepared Al Pastor style in a burrito or taco prepared fresh to order.  You can see the meat with the pineapple on top on a vertical skewer revolving around this electric flamed grill. They also offer carne asada beef, rotisserie chicken  or vegetarian as fillings with black beans and salsa. The churros are a great sweet treat.

Other restaurants are closed at the moment. A twenty four hour food service is available in the first floor.

Tuesday and Wednesday is 5x points. Great for earning drawing tickets and it adds up too on your points.

You maybe eligible for certain drawings having  accumulated enough points.

Everyone was very nice and helpful. I lost but I also won some jackpots
and even won free play money.

Overall a fun and a good place to visit. Many machines to choose from. The dragon links are very popular.

Safety concierge abound throughout the casino and they clean the machines as they are vacated and ensure people wear their masks properly.

text:
Wow this place is amazing! I've never had Burmese food before, but I'm glad I was able to have enjoyed it here! I enjoyed the food so much here! And it got me curious about other places that serve Burmese food!

Overall the restaraunt experience was great! The service was quick and attentive and they had great suggestions! The place is also very cozy so you'll probably closer to other parties more than you may want. It is also a bit noisy so you may have to speak a little louder than you are used to.

Now to the food! We had the pleasure of enjoying the Tea Leaf Salad, which was amazing! We had non-salad eaters at the table and they found themselves to enjoying it! For our entrees we get the Garlic Noodles with Roast Duck, Coconut Rice, Walnut Shrimp, Country Beef (curry), and Chicken Kebate all of which were amazing! My personal favorite of the above were noodles, shrimp, and coconut rice!

We paired all the above food with a 4 person shared Scorpion Bowl! They were generous with the pours of rum!

Wonderful experience here and it was all very affordable especially for Palo Alto!

Definitely coming back when I get the chance!
